We prove that the oscillatory integral operator \begin{equation*} T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}}f(x):=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}} e^{\dot{\imath} \left(a_{1}x^{{\ell}_{1}}_{1}y^{m_{1}}_{1}+\dots +a_{d}x^{{\ell}_{d}}_{d}y^{m_{d}}_{d} \right)}f(y)dy,\;\;\; x\in \mathbb{R}^{d}, \end{equation*} satisfies the restriction estimate \begin{equation*} \|T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}}f\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})}\lesssim \|f\|_{L^{p}(\mathbb{R}^{d})}, \end{equation*} for each $1\leq p\leq 2$, whenever $(\frac{\ell_{j}}{m_{j}}-\frac{1}{m_{j}}+1)\frac{2}{p^{\prime}}\geq 1$, for every $j\in Γ$, and \begin{equation*} \mathcal{E}:=\min{\left\{\min_{1\leq j\leq d}{\frac{m_{j}}{{\ell}_{j}}},\,\min_{1\leq k\leq d}{\frac{d-1}{\sum_{j\neq k} \frac{\ell_{j}}{m_{j}}+\frac{2}{m_{k}}}}\right\}}> \frac{2}{p^{\prime}}. \end{equation*} We also give counterexamples that show that the condition $\mathcal{E}\geq 2/p^{\prime}$ is necessary for this restriction inequality.
VEM-bubble discretisation and iterative coupling algorithm for a fluid induced seismicity model with rate-and-state friction
El Hadi Zerga; Roland Masson; Jean-Paul Ampuero; Pierre Romanet

This work addresses the discretisation and iterative coupling algorithm for an induced seismicity model accounting for fault reactivation and slip driven by subsurface fluid injection. The model couples single-phase Darcy flow in both the porous matrix and the fault network with a quasi-static poroelastic mechanical response in the bulk and fault slip governed by a rate-and-state friction law with radiation damping stabilisation leading to a quas-dynamic formulation. The contact mechanics problem is discretised using the Virtual Element Method with bubble stabilisation of the facewise constant Lagrange multiplier. It is combined with a Hybrid Finite Volume scheme for the mixed-dimensional Darcy flow model. The time discretisation is implicit and the nonlinear system is solved at each time step using an iterative coupling algorithm which iterates between the Darcy flow, the frictional contact-mechanics, and the state differential equation. The contraction of this iterative coupling algorithm is established with a smallness assumption on the time step independent on the mesh size. This proves convergence of the fixed-point as well as well-posedness of the system. The frictional contact-mechanical model is solved using a semi-smooth Newton algorithm based on a local nonlinear inversion of the friction rate-and-state law and a block Gauss--Seidel preconditioner exploiting the structure of the VEM-bubble-$\mathbb{P}^0$ mixed discretisation.
Branch Obstructions for Area-Minimizing Currents and Flat Critical Points of Weakly-Conformal Maps

We study two problems motivated by the local geometry of conformal $φ$-curves. First, let $T$ be a $k$-dimensional locally area-minimizing integral current in Euclidean space, with $k\geq3$, codimension at least two, no boundary, and a locally conformally flat induced metric on $\operatorname{reg} T$. We prove the following branch obstruction: at any rapid-decay branch point whose planar frequency differs from $2$, every nonzero cyclic component of every cylindrical normalized tangent function has repetition multiplicity at least two. Consequently, the nonintegral-frequency points of densities $2$ and $3$ in the rapid-decay branch set have Hausdorff dimension at most $k-3$. On the full branch set, they have zero $\mathcal H^{k-2}$ measure. These conclusions apply to Euclidean image currents of conformal $φ$-curves with locally conformally flat domains, provided the image currents satisfy the stated hypotheses.
 Second, for $C^j$ weakly-conformal maps between smooth Riemannian manifolds, with domain dimension $k\geq3$ and $j\geq2$, we prove that all derivatives of orders $1$ through $j$ vanish at every critical point. As a consequence, for smooth weakly-conformal maps with connected domain, we establish a curvature condition under which the map is constant or has no critical points. The flatness and continuation results apply in particular to conformal $φ$-curves with the corresponding regularity and curvature assumptions. Finally, we examine the Borůvka cone, which illustrates the role of regularity and the distinction between critical points and branch points.
The symmetric Gaussian isoperimetric problem in the plane

We resolve the symmetric Gaussian isoperimetric conjecture in the plane: every minimizer of Gaussian perimeter among centrally symmetric sets of prescribed Gaussian measure is a centered ball, a symmetric strip, or the complement of one of these sets. A quadrant-reflection argument reduces the problem to unconditional sets. The planar structural results of Barchiesi, Cagnetti and Julin then leave only a noncircular strictly convex stationary oval. We exclude this oval by an explicit volume-preserving and perimeter-decreasing linear deformation, which geometrically corresponds to an "unconditional squeezing". More generally, without requiring any symmetry assumptions, we show that any noncircular closed embedded $λ$-self-shrinker is always unstable via linear deformations. We also record a reduction to the unconditional case in dimension three, using an orthogonal equipartition theorem of Musin.
A capillary logarithmic Gauss curvature flow and the capillary Minkowski problem

We study a logarithmic Gauss curvature flow of strictly convex capillary hypersurfaces in the Euclidean half-space. For an acute contact angle and an arbitrary positive smooth prescribed function, we prove that a suitable initial dilation yields a global solution which converges smoothly after a horizontal translation with a uniquely determined constant velocity. As an application, we provide a logarithmic flow proof of the capillary Minkowski problem, previously established by Mei-Wang-Weng [Adv. Math. 469, 110230 (2025)].
Exact local spectral thresholds for loose and tight Hamilton cycles in $3$-graphs

For an $n$-vertex $3$-uniform hypergraph $H$, let $σ(H)$ denote the minimum adjacency spectral radius of its vertex links. We determine the exact thresholds for $σ(H)$ that force loose and tight Hamilton cycles for all sufficiently large admissible orders, and give constructions showing that each bound is best possible. The loose threshold is $(1+\sqrt{13})n/8+O(1)$, with two forms according to $n$ modulo four. The tight threshold is $2n/3+O(1)$, with four forms determined by $n$ modulo three and, when $3\mid n$, modulo nine. The resulting spectral conditions and the corresponding minimum vertex degree conditions do not imply one another. For loose cycles, we combine fractional packing stability and absorption with exact completion near a space barrier. For tight cycles, spectral stability and rooted sampling reduce the problem to three extremal configurations. We resolve these configurations by controlling the spectral loss caused by missing triples and constructing short paths that extend to Hamilton cycles, including in the presence of exceptional vertices.
A proof of the Theta conjecture
Haojun Bai; Feng Gu; Zhuowei Lin; Dun Qiu; Minhao Zhang

We prove the touching refinement of the Theta conjecture of Interdonato and Iraci, giving a formula for $Θ_{e_\ell}Θ_{e_k}\nabla E_{d,j}$ as a weighted sum over parking functions with decorated rises and valleys and touch number $j$. Summing over $j$ gives the Theta conjecture. As corollaries, we prove the valley Delta conjecture of Haglund, Remmel, and Wilson and its generalized version proposed by Qiu and Wilson. Our proof compares algebraic and combinatorial recurrences using an extension of the plethystic substitution $X\mapsto(q-1)X$ to quasisymmetric functions. The algebraic recurrence follows from an endomorphism constructed by D'Adderio, Interdonato, Iraci and Pagaria on the Dyck path algebra of Carlsson and Mellit. The combinatorial recurrence is obtained by introducing signed labels and deleting the main diagonal. The two recurrences have the same initial conditions, which identifies the corresponding generating functions.
Renzo Cavalieri; David Klompenhouwer; Paolo Rossi

We effectively compute all intersection numbers of the form $λ_gψ^d$ on moduli spaces of genus $g$ admissible covers with one point of full ramification and two additional branch points with arbitrary profile. We encode these invariants in appropriate generating functions, which we relate to the Hamiltonians of the KdV hierarchy.
Unique continuation property for $\bar\partial$ with $L^{2n}$ potentials
Guokuan Shao; Ziming Shi; Jujie Wu

We establish the sharp unique continuation property for the Cauchy--Riemann operator $\bar{\partial}$ in higher dimensions. Let $0\inΩ\subset \C^n$ be a domain. Suppose $u \in W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1,2}(Ω; \C^N)$ satisfies the differential inequality
 \[
 |\bar{\partial} u| \leq V |u| \quad \text{a.e.~on } Ω
 \]
 with $V \in L_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2n}(Ω)$. If $u$ is $L^2$ flat at the origin, then $u \equiv 0$ on $Ω$.
Total variation error bounds for Schrödinger-Föllmer samplers

Sampling from high-dimensional, multimodal target distributions plays a fundamental role in scientific computing, statistics and machine learning. Recently, the Schrödinger-Föllmer sampler (SFS) has been proposed by Huang et al. (IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory, 2025) as an efficient sampling algorithm that transports the degenerate distribution at $t=0$ to the target distribution at $t=1$, without relying on long-time ergodicity. In this paper, we establish non-asymptotic error bounds for SFS in the total variation distance by deriving regularization estimates for the associated Kolmogorov equation via the Bismut-Elworthy-Li formula. When the drift can be computed exactly, a convergence rate of order $\mathcal{O}( h|\ln h|)$ was obtained under certain smoothness conditions on the drift with a uniform time step-size $h>0$. When the drift is approximated by Monte Carlo methods, we obtain a convergence rate of order $\mathcal{O}( h|\ln h|+ 1/M)$, where $M$ is the number of samples used in the Monte Carlo approximation. This yields a sharper dependence on $M$ than the existing bound $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{M})$ in the $L^2$-Wasserstein distance in the aforementioned paper, by turning the total variation error to the weak error analysis in the setting of non-smooth test functions. Numerical experiments are presented to illustrate the convergence rate with respect to the time step-size $h$ and the Monte Carlo sample size $M$ and the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.
Sampling Colorings on $G(n, d/n)$ via Glauber Dynamics

We study the mixing time of Glauber dynamics for sampling uniformly from the proper $q$-colorings of sparse Erdős-Rényi random graphs $G(n,d/n)$. Our main result establishes that with probability $1-o(1)$ over the draw of $G$, Glauber dynamics is rapidly mixing for every $q\geq d+d^{1/2+\varepsilon}$, given any fixed $0<\varepsilon\leq1/2$ and any sufficiently large fixed $d$. In particular, the surplus of colors above $d$ is sublinear and close to $\sqrt{d}$. The achieved color range therefore approaches the tree uniqueness threshold and improves over the previously best achievable number of colors $q > 1.763 d$ due to Efthymiou, Hayes, Stefankovic, and Vigoda [SODA 2018]. Moreover, our mixing-time bound is $O(n^{2+o_d(1)})$, and hence almost quadratic as $d\rightarrow\infty$.
 Our proof is based on establishing a spectral gap for block dynamics resulting from a suitable decomposition of $G(n,d/n)$ into blocks and singleton vertices, ensuring that every high-degree vertex is encapsulated within a block. Our main technical contribution is a novel way of establishing rapid mixing of block dynamics via an integrated Bochner-Bakry-Émery approach, which we expect to have applications beyond sampling colorings. We further devise a new block decomposition of $G(n,d/n)$ that strengthens and simplifies similar constructions used in previous work. Finally, to compare block and Glauber dynamics, we establish a novel recursive separator decomposition of tree-like blocks, together with a coupling argument that avoids the need for nearly uniform color marginals at vertices adjacent to hubs. This comparison argument might be of independent interest.
Nontrivial Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function and Its Derivative
Chuancun Yin; Xianghua Zhao; Zuolu Hao; Zhongyang Sun

The nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function lie at the heart of analytic number theory. Through the explicit formulas, they govern the distribution of prime numbers: the closer all nontrivial zeros lie to the critical line $\Re(s)=\frac12$, the more uniformly the primes are distributed. The Riemann Hypothesis-asserting that all nontrivial zeros satisfy $\Re(s)=\frac12$-is equivalent to the optimal error bound $O(\sqrt{x}\log x)$ in the Prime Number Theorem. Beyond number theory, the zeros of $ζ(s)$ and its derivative $ζ'(s)$ are deeply intertwined: the horizontal distribution of $ζ'$-zeros near the critical line encodes information about the spacing of consecutive $ζ$-zeros. This paper establishes some results concerning the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function.
An Algebraic Foundation of Rate-Product Style Quantity Calculus

Using the new notion of a scalable (right) monoid-heap, the quantity calculus in [1] is generalized to include quantities that may not be possible to multiply as well as both (weak) rates and products of quantities. Several examples are given of applications in metrology and physics
Physics-informed neural networks in the small-data regime: A controlled comparison with classical PDE surrogates
Kirill Katsuba; Oleg Rudenko; Egor Bugaev; Alexander Tarakanov

Neural surrogates for engineering models are often trained on large collections of simulated solutions. We investigate whether physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) can achieve accurate predictions from scarce labelled observations by incorporating governing equations and prescribed initial and boundary conditions. We introduce hierarchical loss weighting (H-PINN) and its gradient-direction-aware extension (HO-PINN), which adjust the emphasis on physical constraints according to higher-priority losses. Hierarchical PINNs are compared with Vanilla PINN, tuned gradient boosting, support-vector regression, and Gaussian-process regression on a heat equation and three heterogeneous two-phase-flow benchmarks. Experiments use 20--1000 labelled states and ten paired seeds. Each label is one coordinate--state observation, not a complete simulation. At least one PINN variant achieves the highest mean primary-target \(R^2\) in each interpolation and equation-assisted forecasting comparison at 20 and 50 labels. The advantage for water saturation persists across all tested budgets. Hierarchical weighting reduces variability across runs in selected settings. These results demonstrate that known physics can support accurate neural surrogate predictions from very few solution observations, at substantially higher fitting cost than the tested classical regressors.
Positive solutions of power equations in planar corner domains
Hongtao Hu; Zhouyu Long; Hongzhe Tao; Qiaoran Wu; Wenming Zou

We study positive solutions of $Δu=λu^k$ on bounded planar corner domains with zero boundary values away from the vertex. For negative-power absorption we identify the admissible interval of Martin masses and prove uniqueness at the minimum mass. Along the ordinary boundary, we identify the weak Hessian endpoint and its sharp tail when the set of zero inward derivative has positive length. For superlinear sources we prove attainment of the largest positive Martin mass in the subcritical range. At criticality we construct a family of singular solutions with zero Martin mass and distinguish its members by their second logarithmic coefficient and the endpoint integrability of their Hessian differences. Above criticality an angular eigenvalue governs the Morse index away from its zero threshold. We also give sharp physical-Hessian asymptotics for finite-mass remainders and joint corner and side estimates for negative-power sources.
Holomorphic integer-graded vertex operator superalgebras are purely even
Chongying Dong; Kaiwen Sun; Haowu Wang

We prove that a simple, self-contragredient, rational, $C_2$-cofinite, integer-graded holomorphic vertex operator superalgebra of CFT-type has zero odd part. We first show that a hypothetical nonzero odd part would be a simple current of categorical dimension $-1$ over a strongly rational pointed VOA with four simple modules. We then prove that every nonvacuum simple current of a strongly rational VOA has strictly positive lowest conformal weight. This leads to a contradiction with Dong-Jiao-Xu's theorem on the positivity of categorical dimension.
Vladimiro Benedetti; Daniele Faenzi; Simone Marchesi

We describe the module of logarithmic derivations along the discriminant of a stable polar representation of a reductive algebraic group. It splits into derivations along the fibres of the quotient map and a free summand lifted from logarithmic derivations along the associated branch divisor. This gives a uniform extension of previous results on full adjoint discriminants. We prove that, for visible stable polar actions of semisimple groups with finite generic stabilizer, the discriminant is a free divisor. For stable periodic gradings of arbitrary order with semisimple degree-zero group, we construct explicit Saito matrices from the infinitesimal action and the gradients of basic invariants, which yields determinantal equations for several exceptional discriminants. In particular, starting with exceptional Lie algebras, we provide examples of free discriminants of degrees 60, 120, 126 and 240 for inner gradings and a degree-72 example for an outer one.
Singularities in leaf closures on complex surfaces

We prove a geometric and dynamical criterion excluding minimal sets contained in the regular locus of a holomorphic foliation on a compact complex surface. In particular, we prove that every Jouanolou foliation of degree at least two has no exceptional minimal set. We also give an explicit lower bound, growing linearly with the degree, for the number of singularities in every regular leaf closure of a Jouanolou foliation. This bound persists under small perturbations, as does the existence of a nonempty open saturated set whose leaves accumulate at all singularities. Under finite pullback unramified over the singular set, the bound is multiplied by the degree of the normalised component over the base leaf. Together with a general persistence theorem, this yields nonempty analytic open sets of foliations on every smooth projective surface with arbitrarily large uniform lower bounds on the number of singularities in their regular leaf closures. On double-plane K3 surfaces, we obtain foliations with ample canonical bundle and explicitly describe and count their singularities.
Data-Driven Conservation Laws for Newtonian Systems: Physics-Informed Neural Networks and Eisenhart-Duval Geometry

We introduce a Physics-Informed Neural Network approach for the data-driven reconstruction of the symmetries and conservation laws of Newtonian dynamical systems, based on the geometrization of the dynamics through the Eisenhart-Duval lift. Within the Eisenhart-Duval lift, the symmetry conditions reduce to the linear Killing or Conformal Killing equations of the extended metric. We combine a Hamiltonian neural network, which reconstructs the potential function from the data, with a random-feature neural network, which solves the symmetry conditions for the collineations of the extended geometry. From the learned vector fields we construct the Lie algebra and, through Noether's theorem, the corresponding conserved quantities, while the derivation of the curvature invariants for the extended geometry provide allow us to perform an independent consistency test. We apply the method to the one-dimensional Ermakov-Pinney equation and to the one-dimensional harmonic oscillator, with and without a quartic perturbation, by using different level of noise in the phase-space data. For the Ermakov-Pinney equation, the three Killing vectors of the flat extended plane, and the corresponding nonlocal conservation laws, are recovered for, while for the harmonic oscillator, the ten conformal Killing vectors which form the $so(3,2)$ Lie algebra are determined for noise levels up to $10\%$. When the quartic term is added, the broken symmetries are identified as approximate symmetries.
Linear disjointness and values of Mahler M-functions

Wen Huang; Song Shao; Hui Xu; Xiangdong Ye

In this paper, we show that every totally minimal system admits a point whose orbit along the primes is dense. Moreover, assuming the Dickson-Hardy-Littlewood conjecture, we show that in any totally minimal distal system, the orbit along the primes of every point is dense.

In this article, we connect the local Lipschitz geometry of a normal surface singularity with a rational homology sphere link to the analytic semigroup $S_{an}(\tilde{X})$ associated with a convenient resolution. A central objective in stochastic mechanics is to separate deterministic physical behavior from the probability laws governing uncertain inputs. Inspired by the spirit of VRFs, this work establishes that, for a fixed physical system, uncertainty propagation is described by a law-invariant operator mapping input realizations to responses, governed by the underlying physics and the deterministic parameters of the system. We establish this law invariance under complete, invertible coordinate transformations and develop complementary, Fourier, fixed-reference polynomial-chaos (PCE) and finite element method (FEM) transfer formulations. Fourier captures nonlinear cross-frequency interactions and recovers the classical VRF in the appropriate linear limit, PCE describes coupling among stochastic modes, while FEM expresses the deterministic inverse-stiffness action. Neural approximations of these deterministic operators are investigated through analytical and finite-element benchmarks, examining cross-law generalization, the influence of training distributions and stochastic excitation, and the prediction of response fields and statistics. The results demonstrate the potential for reusing learned physical operators across different stochastic laws without retraining, while highlighting the importance of adequate training coverage and the challenges of accurately estimating low-probability events.

Recently, Currier, Moore, and Yip developed a general framework for constructing colorings avoiding prescribed monochromatic arithmetic progressions in Euclidean Ramsey theory. Writing $\ell_m$ for an $m$-term arithmetic progression with unit spacing, they proved $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,\ell_{20})$ and $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,α\ell_{6889})$ for every $α>0$. We refine and simplify their framework, proving $\mathbb E^n

This paper is devoted to a uniform spectral Silverman-Meadows rank condition for the nullcontrollability of coupled systems of heat equations with time-dependent diffusion, coupling and control matrices. The proof relies on an adaptation of the Lebeau-Robbiano strategy combined with uniform finite-dimensional observability estimates associated with each Laplace eigenmode.

In unrestricted smooth one-parameter families, the generic event is a single evolution fold on a continued orbit. We introduce PDEViBench, a benchmark of 290 tasks in six equation families that traces each passing program to the computation behind its output and reruns unclear programs on changed data. A Codex agent (GPT-5.2) passed 80% of 1,450 runs, yet about one pass in ten returned the exact solution without solving the equation. Once the prompt forbade the shortcut, every pass was a numerical solve, and on tasks without a closed-form solution passing programs stayed correct on changed data. In this context, Colbourn posed the following open problem, which concerns upper bounds on the reliability coefficients in terms of cycle-basis lengths: For all-terminal reliability, is it true that if $G$ has a cycle basis containing cycles of lengths $c_1,\ldots,\allowbreak c_{m-n+1}$, then $H_i \le\sum\limits_{\substack{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m-n+1\},|I|=i}}\prod\limits_{j\in I}(c_j-1)$? We study the asymmetric simple exclusion process on the half-line with particle insertion and no particle removal at the boundary. We point out that there exist two distinct multiple contour integral formulas for the transition probability between two finite particle configurations containing the same number of particles. We recall one of these formulas from the literature and prove a second, new formula by showing that it satisfies the evolution equation using a coordinate Bethe ansatz calculation and verify that the initial condition is implemented by the contour integrals. As an application we sum this formula over all final configurations and obtain an integral formula for the probability that the number of particles is conserved up to a given time. The proofs use symmetric rational functions and their properties together with contour deformations.
Real quadratic fields and finite quantum dilogarithms II: traces of quantum modular cocycles
Stavros Garoufalidis; Danylo Radchenko; Campbell Wheeler

We study traces of quantum modular cocycles at fixed points of hyperbolic elements $γ\in\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, formulate an algebraicity conjecture for these traces, and prove it for the cocycles associated to 1-dimensional state-integrals. In addition, we analyse a finite TQFT associated with $γ$ and conjecture that its invariants for 3-manifolds agree with the traces of their $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ quantum modular cocycles. The finite TQFTs predict a yet-to-be-defined motive with cohomology equipped with a $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-degree grading and a $\mathbb{Z}$-weight grading coming from a version of the Riemann hypothesis, which suggests a similar grading should exist for an extension of the Kauffman bracket skein module, for the framed $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ Floer cohomology of Abouzaid--Manolescu, and for the quantum modular cocycle. This leads to surprising additive identities among algebraic units, which we confirm for the complement of the simplest hyperbolic knot $4_1$, as well as for $S^1 \times Σ_g$ for a closed genus $g$ surface.
Certified finite-precision readout for $p$-adic kernel aggregation

In non-archimedean numerical analysis, a verified $p$-adic approximation can determine an absolute value, and hence downstream probabilistic rankings and classification decisions, with mathematical exactness long before the underlying number is fully resolved. We turn this observation into rigorous finite-precision certificates for norm-based readouts of amplitude families. For a common error radius, a nonempty resolved set already fixes every exact maximizer, ties included, at the sharp integer absolute precision $v_*+1$, and conditioning on that set yields an exact total-variation identity separating unresolved $p$-adic mass from real rounding error. For aggregates of $p$-adic exponentials, we give a centered-moment certificate with an explicit remainder bound: on rational data it runs in exact rational arithmetic without individual exponential evaluations, attains its minimal bound at an active phase, and resolves every nonzero aggregate at high order; we also obtain an aggregate perturbation bound free of summand-count factors. For multiclass $p$-adic classifiers that decode by minimizing the norm of a class discriminant, we prove a necessary and sufficient certification condition and show that the sharp common precision threshold is $v^{(2)}+1$, governed by the second-largest discriminant valuation, so the winning discriminant need not itself be resolved. We apply these certificates to discrete $p$-adic path-integral actions on uniform affine chains, deriving explicit action centers and proving exact output-independence at zero effective quadratic coupling. Pseudocode and a reproducible reference implementation accompany the theory.
Fundamental Outage and Diversity Limits of Fluid Antenna Multiple Access Under Correlated Nakagami-$m$ Fading

Existing analytical studies of fluid antenna multiple access (FAMA) are largely confined to Rayleigh fading, independent-port assumptions, or asymptotic selection metrics, leaving the fundamental outage behavior under realistic fading and spatial correlation conditions uncharacterized. This paper fills this gap by presenting the first exact and asymptotically tight outage analysis of interference-limited FAMA systems under spatially correlated Nakagami-$m$ fading. By explicitly modeling the joint statistics of the desired and interference powers across fluid-antenna ports, \textcolor{black}{we first formulate the outage probability in terms of the joint desired-signal and interference distributions and then derive an explicit integral expression under a tractable single-reference-port spatial correlation model.} Building on this result, we establish a rigorous diversity-order characterization revealing that the achievable diversity is jointly dictated by the fading severity and the spatial correlation rank imposed by the finite antenna aperture, rather than by the nominal number of ports. To enable accurate and tractable performance evaluation beyond the asymptotic regime, we further introduce a Gamma-matched outage approximation that preserves both the exact diversity order and the array-gain constant. The resulting closed-form expression provides an accurate characterization over a wide range of signal-to-interference ratio (SIR) thresholds and offers clear physical insight into the role of spatial correlation in FAMA systems. Extensive Monte Carlo (MC) simulations confirm the tightness of the exact analysis, the sharpness of the asymptotic results, and the accuracy of the proposed approximation.
Odd realisation numbers of rigid graphs
Sean Dewar; Anthony Nixon; Ben Smith

Determining the number of realisations of a rigid graph for a specific choice of edge lengths is a fundamental problem in discrete geometry. Gortler, Healy and Thurston showed that the number of real realisations of a generic framework is always even or equal to one. Despite being rare, there do exist graphs whose number of complex realisations is odd and not equal to one. In this article, we exhibit two necessary conditions for a rigid graph to have an odd realisation number other than one. We also provide an infinite family of rigid graphs with an odd realisation number other than one.
Cube tilings, partition counters, and the Calkin--Wilf and Kepler trees
Jarosław Grytczuk; Andrzej P. Kisielewicz; Krzysztof Przesławski

A tiling of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ by translates of the discrete cube $K_d=\{0,1\}^d$ cuts every translate $K_d+x$ into subcubes. We study the function $\ell(x)$ counting these parts. Its sum over every translate of $K_d$ equals $3^d$, for an arbitrary translation set. For lattice tilings with a triangular basis we obtain a dimension-reduction formula, and we describe every cocyclic lattice by a single normalized congruence. Along a cyclic generator, the counter of a signed bidiagonal lattice is a row of Stern's diatomic sequence; pairs of counter values realize the Calkin--Wilf tree, and complementary binary words realize the Kepler tree. For the binary lattice, the translated counter labelings of the cube carry generating face partitions, supplied by the tiling itself, which force the levels of the Kepler tree, and every nontrivial face partition has a unique lamination direction. Using finite Fourier analysis we prove that the ordered cyclic profile determines a standard cocyclic cube tiling lattice up to coordinate reflections. For lattices tiling by discrete boxes we determine exactly when the analogous statement holds.
Multi-Target Tracking via Mean Field Feedback Control
Changming Lei; Junhao Dai; Donghua Shi

Cooperative tracking of multiple moving targets requires a swarm to continually adjust its deployment. Existing methods often rely on repeated agent-target reassignment or updates to position-dependent partitions, which can complicate coordination as swarms grow. This motivates us to seek an approach with a lighter coordination burden. Specifically, we formulate multi-target tracking as a time-varying density-tracking problem, with the targets' tracking and sensing demands encoded in a task-demand density. From an Onsager-type variational formulation, a closed-form mean-field feedback law is derived to make the swarm density track this evolving density, and the resulting closed-loop system is shown to be well posed. Under the stated assumptions, a Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence analysis establishes exponential KL convergence under ideal feedback and conditional robustness to feedback mismatch under estimated. Numerical experiments demonstrate effective tracking of multiple moving targets and show smaller density errors at comparable applied control energy compared with an existing density-tracking feedback method.
Mitigating the BICM Loss in MIMO Receivers with Correlation-Informed Logits

Bit-interleaved coded modulation (BICM) is widely used in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) wireless systems. However, separating MIMO data detection from channel decoding and only exchanging per-bit soft information discards correlation information among the bits within each transmit vector. We show that the resulting information loss limits the performance of practical one-shot receivers. Even though iterative detection and decoding (IDD) can recover most of this loss, IDD significantly increases receiver complexity and latency. In order to reduce this loss, we propose COrrelation-Informed Logits (COIL), a soft-output format that combines per-bit soft information with pairwise coupling logits for correlated bits. We show how to incorporate these coupling logits into a conventional belief-propagation-based channel decoder, which enables correlation-aware decoding in a one-shot receiver without IDD. We evaluate COIL in a MIMO-BICM system with a conventional low-density parity-check code. For a 4x4 MIMO orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) system, a one-shot linear minimum mean-square error (LMMSE) receiver with COIL outperforms a conventional one-shot unbiased LMMSE receiver by 1.3dB and operates within 0.8dB of four-iteration IDD, while requiring only a single pass through the data detector.
Generation of semigroups for vector-valued pseudodifferential operators on the torus with space-dependent symbols
Bienvenido Barraza Martínez; Robert Denk; Jairo Hernández Monzón; Max Nendel

We consider toroidal pseudodifferential operators with spatially dependent, operator-valued symbols of positive order and finite regularity. For an arbitrary complex Banach space $E$, we prove that the negative of the closure of a parabolic operator on $C^\infty(\mathbb T^n,E)$ generates an analytic semigroup on $W_p^k(\mathbb T^n,E)$, where $1\le p<\infty$ and $k\in\mathbb N_0$, provided the symbol has sufficiently many spatial derivatives and discrete differences. The proof combines uniform estimates for parameter-dependent kernels with right and left parametrices. It does not require the UMD property of $E$. Real interpolation gives corresponding resolvent estimates on $B_{pq}^s(\mathbb T^n,E)$ for $0<s<k$ and $1\le q\le\infty$. The induced semigroups are strongly continuous for $q<\infty$ and on the little Besov spaces when $q=\infty$.

Heffter arrays are combinatorial structures that can be used to construct orthogonal cyclic cycle decompositions of complete graphs. A square Heffter array $H(n;k)$ is a partially filled $n \times n$ array with $k$ filled cells in each row and column. Its entries are distinct and nonzero, form a half-set of the group $\mathbb{Z}_{2nk+1}$, and sum to zero in every row and column. If the natural orderings of the rows and columns of an array are simple, the array is called globally simple. The globally simple property guarantees the orthogonal cycle decompositions constructed from the Heffter array consist of simple cycles. While existence results are known for most congruence classes of the parameters $n$ and $k$ modulo 4 for square globally simple Heffter arrays $H(n;k)$, the existence for $k \equiv 2 \pmod{4}$ has remained largely open. In this paper, we present a construction for globally simple integer Heffter arrays $H(n;k)$ covering all admissible values of $n$ when $k \equiv 2 \pmod{4}$. This settles the existence question across all congruence classes.
A criterion for the set of subsums to be a Cantorval for a certain class of multigeometric series
Mykola Pratsiovytyi; Yaroslav Vynnyshyn; Oleh Vynnyshyn

The paper studies the topological structure of the set of subsums (incomplete sums) of multigeometric series of the form $\frac{k_1}{s} + \frac{k_2}{s} + \ldots + \frac{k_m}{s} + \frac{k_1}{s^2} + \frac{k_2}{s^2} + \ldots+ \frac{k_m}{s^2} + \frac{k_1}{s^3} + \frac{k_2}{s^3} +\ldots$, where $k_1, \ldots, k_m, s \in \mathbb{N}$. In terms of graph theory, necessary and sufficient conditions are established for the set of subsums of a given series not to be a finite union of closed intervals, as well as necessary and sufficient conditions for this set to contain an interval. As a consequence of these statements, a criterion for the set of subsums to be a Cantorval is obtained. An example of applying the criterion to a series whose Cantorval property was previously unknown is given.
 A more general object of study of topological properties is the set of numbers whose representations in a numerical system with a natural base and a redundant alphabet are subject to restrictions on the use of digits. It is for this object that the above statements are proved.
Branch points and natural boundaries of Poincaré functions and of solutions of nonlinear functional differential equations

In this paper, we study the singularity structure of the analytic continuation of solutions to the equation $g(λw)=R(g(w))$, where $|λ|<1$ and $R$ is a rational function. We show that the analytic solution \(g\) near zero is branched, and that its analytic continuation yields an infinite-sheeted Riemann surface with various patterns of branch points. In one specific pattern, some branch points are delayed: they appear only when the analytic continuation reaches a particular Riemann sheet. Using this functional-equation framework, we extend the study to first-order nonlinear functional differential equations. We show that the continuation of certain special solutions near an attracting fixed point yields either single-valued or multivalued functions, with the unit circle as a natural boundary on every sheet.
On operators with many spectral components

For a complex Banach algebra $\mathscr A$ with unit and $n\in\mathbb N$, let $\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$ be the set of all elements whose spectrum has at least $n$ connected components, and let $d_σ(\mathscr A)=\sup\{n;\;\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)\neq\varnothing\}$ be the spectral depth of $\mathscr A$. We characterize nonemptiness of $\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$ in terms of orthogonal idempotents, compute $d_σ(\mathscr A)$ for finite-dimensional algebras, and show that every class $\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$ is open. For operators on an infinite-dimensional complex Banach space $X$ these classes are dense in $\mathscr B(X)$, which implies that $\mathcal C_\infty(\mathscr B(X))$ is a dense $G_δ$-subset of $\mathscr B(X)$. By contrast, we exhibit a commutative Banach algebra whose spectral classes are all nonempty and none of which is dense. For self-adjoint operators on a Hilbert space, we obtain sharper perturbation results, with positive semi-definite perturbations of prescribed rank producing spectra with exactly $n$ components. We show that a quasinilpotent weighted forward shift $S_w$ on $X$ admits a nilpotent rank-one operator $F$ such that the spectrum of $S_w+αF$ has infinitely many components for every nonzero $α$.
Geodesic connectedness of globally hyperbolic spacetimes with a causal Killing vector field

We characterize the existence of a geodesic joining two prescribed points of a globally hyperbolic spacetime $(M,g)$ admitting a complete causal Killing vector field $K$ and a complete smooth spacelike Cauchy hypersurface $S$. We prove that two points $p,q\in M$ are joined by a geodesic if and only if there exists an $H^1$ curve $γ$ from $p$ to $q$ such that $g(\dotγ,K)$ is constant almost everywhere. The statement is intrinsic and allows $K$ to be timelike at some points and lightlike at others. A global splitting induced by the flow of $K$ is used in the proof, but no global bounds on the metric coefficients are imposed. The proof relies on stationary perturbations of $(M,g)$, whose relevant compactness properties follow from global hyperbolicity of $g$, and on uniform estimates based on an integral admissibility condition and a Glaeser-type inequality. Two examples illustrate geodesic connectedness and the obstruction detected by the characterization.
Minimum cumulative power divergence estimation with applications to copulas

Parametric inference based on distribution functions is useful when a model is naturally specified through its cumulative distribution function or when a tractable density is unavailable. We study minimum cumulative power divergence estimation, obtained by comparing a parametric distribution function with its empirical counterpart. For a fixed positive tuning parameter and a fixed finite integration measure, we establish the existence of a consistent sequence of local solutions to the estimating equations and derive its asymptotic normality. The resulting covariance has a sandwich form whose components involve derivatives of the distribution function and the covariance kernel of the multivariate empirical process. We specialize the construction to copulas using Lebesgue measure on the unit cube, and distinguish estimation with known margins from estimation based on ranks. In the latter case, the covariance incorporates the effect of estimating the marginal distributions. The relationship with the copula divergences of Eguchi and Kato is made explicit: the power loss is closely related, whereas the integration measure determines a different estimation criterion. A simulation design for Gumbel, Clayton, and Frank copulas examines the estimation of Kendall's tau under correct specification, family misspecification, and contamination by independence. The simulations show competitive clean-data accuracy but no general robustness advantage over the empirical-copula-weighted alternatives under independence contamination.
Pascal Fong; Matilde Maccan; Ludvig Modin

We give a criterion for the contracted product $E \times^G X$ to have a singular Picard scheme, where $E$ is an elliptic curve, $G \subset E$ is a finite subgroup scheme, and $X$ is a projective $G$-normal curve, in the sense of Brion. We show that every smooth projective surface with a singular Picard scheme and a positive-dimensional automorphism group scheme arises in this way. We also illustrate the criterion by constructing two new families of surfaces with singular Picard schemes, arising from $G$-normal curves $X$ for $G = \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and $G = \boldsymbolα_p$, respectively. As a special case of $G = \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, we recover Igusa's classical example. Finally, we compute all infinitesimal group schemes which appear as $\operatorname{Pic}^0_S/(\operatorname{Pic}^0_S)_{\mathrm{red}}$ for all (quasi)-bielliptic surfaces $S$. This completes the description of the singular Picard schemes of smooth projective surfaces of Kodaira dimension zero.
Hilton's Conjecture on Uncomplemented Incomparable Families
Yuejian Peng; Zilong Yan; Cheng Zhao

A family ${\mathcal A}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ is \emph{uncomplemented} if it contains no set together with its complement. Families ${\mathcal A}_1,\ldots,{\mathcal A}_t$ are \emph{strongly incomparable} if every set in one family is incomparable with every set in another family.
 In 1976, Hilton conjectured that if ${\mathcal A}_1,\ldots,{\mathcal A}_t\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ are uncomplemented and strongly incomparable, then $$\sum_{i=1}^t |{\mathcal A}_i|\le 2^{n-1}.$$ We confirm this conjecture by a matrix rank argument that encodes incomparability and uncomplementedness in the same matrix, which is quite different from the earlier methods on this problem.
 We also study weak incomparability, in which the same set may occur in different families. Goldwasser, Hilton and Zheng conjectured an upper bound in this setting and claimed that their conjecture is equivalent to Hilton's conjecture. We give counterexamples to their conjecture for every $t\ge3$ and identify the error in the claimed equivalence. We then propose a replacement conjecture and confirm it when $t$ is large.
 The upper bound $2^{n-1}$ in Hilton's conjecture can be attained if some families are allowed to by empty. It is natural to consider the maximum size of $\sum_{i=1}^t |{\mathcal A}_i|$ for uncomplemented and strongly incomparable families ${\mathcal A}_1,\ldots,{\mathcal A}_t\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ when all families are required to be non-empty. Denote this maximum number by $M(n,t)$. We show that \[ 2^{n-1}-1\le M(n,t)\le 2^{n-1} \] for $n\ge3$ and $3\le t\le n$.
Negative normal degree and holomorphic sectional curvature pinching

We obtain an upper bound for the local holomorphic sectional curvature pinching of a Kähler manifold containing a smooth rational curve of negative total normal degree. As an application, we prove that a compact Kähler surface with positive holomorphic sectional curvature and local pinching constant at least $1/9$ is biholomorphic to $\mathbb{CP}^2$, $\mathbb{CP}^1\times\mathbb{CP}^1$, or the first Hirzebruch surface $\mathbb F_1$. For pinching strictly greater than $1/9$, only the first two possibilities occur, confirming a conjecture of Yang and Zheng. We also determine the optimal local pinching constants on $\mathbb F_1$ and $\mathbb F_2$.
Amortized Transport-Map Likelihoods for Hierarchical Inverse Problems with Application to Wetting

Hierarchical Bayesian models pool measurements, but with the forward model in the likelihood every posterior evaluation costs one forward solve per cell. To reduce this cost, we introduce a simulation-based inference framework in which a triangular transport-map likelihood, trained once per design, serves every cell. We apply it to infer wetting properties from photographs of a stable hole in a thin liquid film. The hole's radius depends, through the nonlinear Young-Laplace equation, on the contact angle and capillary length. One photograph gives rank-one information about them, so we pool many in a hierarchical model whose cells, each a substrate at one volume setting, share the apparatus geometry and the noise scale. A design fixes the number of substrates, the volume settings and the photographs per cell. The map's posteriors agree with direct sampling of the forward model in the wetting properties at a synthetic validation design, and less closely at a larger synthetic scaling design. At the validation design, simulation-based calibration detects no departure for any parameter. There, the map needs several hundred times fewer forward-model evaluations than direct sampling with a gradient-free ensemble sampler for a single posterior, and about five orders of magnitude fewer over a calibration study of 200 posteriors. On real photographs its posterior agrees with direct sampling and is consistent with the measured radii. Trained offline, the amortized map turns new photographs into a posterior with no forward solve. It is thus a major step toward measuring wetting properties in situ without disturbing the liquid.
The multiplicity bound for near-group fusion categories of type $\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z+k$

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a near-group fusion category of type $\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z+k$. We show $k\in\{0,3,4\}$, which then gives a complete characterization of near-group fusion categories determined by $\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$.
Involution-Preserving schemes through constrained mesh motion: a novel Arbitrary-Lagrangian-Eulerian framework
Sacha Cardonna; Elena Bernardelli; Walter Boscheri

We introduce a novel structure-preserving finite volume method that exploits mesh motion to enforce differential involutions arising in hyperbolic systems of conservation laws. The key idea is to leverage the geometric degrees of freedom of an Arbitrary-Lagrangian-Eulerian (ALE) framework to construct a constrained mesh motion that is intrinsically compatible with the involution constraints embedded in the governing equations. The method is developed within a cell-centered formulation on moving quadrilateral meshes, where discrete divergence and curl operators are constructed from vertex-based differential operators. Particular care is devoted to the consistent evolution of the mesh geometry and the satisfaction of the Geometric Conservation Law (GCL). The proposed framework is applied to two representative hyperbolic systems featuring distinct involution constraints: the ideal magnetohydrodynamics equations, endowed with the divergence-free condition on the magnetic field, and the hyperbolic Euler-Heat equations, subject to a curl-free constraint on the thermal impulse. Second-order accuracy in time is achieved through a Runge-Kutta discretization, with the geometric constraints consistently enforced at each stage. A comprehensive set of classical benchmark problems is presented to assess the accuracy and effectiveness of the method. The numerical results demonstrate that appropriately constrained mesh motion provides an effective mechanism for preserving differential involutions, establishing a novel connection between mesh geometry and the structure-preserving discretization of hyperbolic systems.
On Relative Smoothness in Dually Flat Geometry

We study the geometric meaning of relative smoothness on dually flat manifolds and its implications for the convergence analysis of mirror descent. Our main result yields one-sided counterparts of the classical Levi--Civita characterizations of Lipschitz Riemannian gradients, each equivalent to relative smoothness. We further investigate the stationarity of mirror descent iterates for possibly nonconvex objectives and show that relative smoothness alone does not guarantee convergence of the Riemannian gradient norm to zero. We identify a one-sided condition on the cubic tensor that ensures such convergence and yields an $O(1/N)$ stationarity bound. Examples based on the negative entropy potential illustrate the role of metric variation.
Whitney-Type Real-Analytic Approximation on Banach Spaces I: The $C^0$ and $C^1$ Cases

The classical Whitney theorem on real-analytic approximation is a fundamental result in finite-dimensional analysis and geometry. Extending this theory to general infinite-dimensional Banach spaces involves longstanding open problems. This paper is the first part of our study of Whitney-type real-analytic approximation on Banach spaces, focusing on the $C^0$ and $C^1$ cases.
 We prove that a real Banach space admits a separating polynomial if and only if it admits a polynomial topological embedding into a real Hilbert space. We also introduce classes of mappings that locally factor through polynomial maps into finite-dimensional spaces and develop methods of real-analytic approximation for these classes. Using these tools, we establish fine $C^0$ and $C^1$ real-analytic approximation theorems for broad classes of Banach spaces, including nonseparable ones.
 As applications, we resolve several open problems, including those concerning Whitney-type extensions with real analyticity off closed sets, real-analytic approximation preserving Lipschitz constants, and the real-analytic equivalence of diffeomorphic open subsets of Hilbert spaces.
From Frobenius seeds to self-orthogonal modules over symmetric algebras

We construct finite-dimensional symmetric algebras admitting nonprojective self-orthogonal modules from Frobenius algebras equipped with a module satisfying explicit stable and homological conditions. The resulting modules have complexity three, and their stable endomorphism algebras are isomorphic to the algebra of dual numbers over the ground field. The construction combines a variable input with a fixed auxiliary factor carrying the required twisting, and preserves the input through specified quotient and corner constructions. The proof combines derived induction, an obstruction to perfect factorization, and a cone construction over a Gorenstein triangular matrix algebra. For a symmetric algebra and a self-orthogonal generator, we describe the derived category of the opposite endomorphism algebra through a recollement with a two-term $2$-symmetric dg algebra. For our counterexamples, it is formal and quasi-isomorphic to an explicit four-dimensional dg algebra. Applications to cyclic coverings of a quantum exterior algebra yield connected examples with explicitly determined numbers of simple modules. The construction works over every field containing an element of infinite multiplicative order.
Functions with finite energy on the Sierpinski gasket

This paper develops a systematic framework for constructing finite-energy functions on the Sierpiński gasket using Lipschitz maps and various classes of contractions. Several properties of the constructed functions are investigated, including the min--max property and bounds for their energy. Several examples of finite-energy functions, along with their graphical representations, are provided to illustrate the functions constructed using the proposed framework. It is further shown that finite energy does not necessarily imply membership in the domain of the Laplacian. The framework is then applied to a class of fractal interpolation functions on the Sierpiński gasket, for which necessary and sufficient conditions for finite energy are established under suitable contractivity assumptions.
Scalar curvature deformation of isoparametric tubes

We resolve Ge's local scalar curvature rigidity conjecture for spherical isoparametric tubes. The conjecture fails throughout its stated radius range for families with at least two distinct principal curvatures, via arbitrarily small smooth deformations supported in any regular annulus. Geodesic balls of radius less than $\fracπ{2}$ are locally rigid under $C^2$ smallness. We also prescribe sufficiently small smooth nonradial scalar-curvature increments with fixed compact interior support, under antipodal symmetry for families with 2, 4, or 6 distinct principal curvatures and without symmetry for families with 3 distinct principal curvatures.
A Rooted Structure Theorem for $5$-Connected Graphs and $K_6^-$-Minors

Jorgensen conjectured that every $6$-connected graph with no $K_6$-minor is apex. For a $6$-connected graph containing a $K_4$ on vertices $a_1,\dots,a_4$, being apex is equivalent to $G-a_i$ having a planar embedding with the other three roots on a common face for some $i$, so that for such graphs the conjecture becomes a rooted planarity statement. Robertson, Seymour, and Thomas showed that the failure of the corresponding three-rooted planarity is witnessed by a legless tripod. We introduce a four-root structure, called a frame, that extends this certificate, and prove a structural theorem: every $5$-connected graph containing a frame rooted at four prescribed vertices contains a subgraph of one of five explicit types, denoted $A$--$E$. This theorem does not depend on the edges among the roots. As an application, we show that when the four roots span a $K_4^-$, each of the five configurations yields a $K_6^-$-minor. Together with a planar argument for the case without a frame and an induction based on a theorem of Kawarabayashi, this gives a proof that every non-planar $5$-connected graph contains a $K_6^-$-minor. This statement also follows from a recent theorem of Lo; our proof is independent and is driven by the rooted structure theorem, whose method we expect to apply to Jorgensen's conjecture with other target configurations.
Convergence of finite element exterior calculus for the Hodge-Dirac and Hodge-Laplace problems on closed Riemannian manifolds

We prove that the finite element exterior calculus (FEEC) approximation to the Hodge-Dirac and Hodge-Laplace problems on any closed oriented Riemannian manifold converges. Its approximate solutions, together with their exterior derivatives, converge to the continuum solutions for every source, and at the rate of the mesh size when the source and its codifferential are square integrable. We use Licht's estimate for the FEEC approximation of forms with one square-integrable derivative by finite element forms. We combine this with a new abstract error bound for approximations of Hilbert complexes. This bound uses a version of Di Pietro and Droniou's third Strang lemma. To apply these estimates, we show that every closed manifold admits a family of arbitrarily fine triangulations whose shapes stay uniformly under control.
Same Physics, Different Gradients: A State-of-the-Art Report on Differentiable Physics Simulation

Lei Shu; Zizhou Huang; Yunuo Chen; Yifei Li; Tao Du; Minchen Li; Tuur Stuyck; Miles Macklin; Kui Wu; Bo Zhu; Yin Yang; Ming C. Lin; Alberta Longhini; Rika Antonova; Leonidas Guibas; Gordon Wetzstein; Jeannette Bohg; Chenfanfu Jiang

Differentiable simulation propagates derivatives through a physics simulator, turning animation, system identification, control, and computational design into gradient-based optimization. Engines differ in the physics they model and, less visibly, in which mathematical object they differentiate. We separate two questions the literature conflates. The referent is which object the returned derivative belongs to: the finite computation that executed, the converged equation it approximates, or the continuous dynamics. The realization describes the organization of the backward pass: automatically generated differentiation, an equation-level adjoint solve, or a custom adjoint. The referent defines the target against which exactness is assessed; the implementation determines how accurately that target is approximated. Cost depends on the realization together with how the states needed by the backward pass are retained or recovered. Crossing the axes places every method and engine we classify in a cell, separates claims the literature merges, and shows that the apparent trade-off between exactness and memory follows from how methods have been built rather than from a constraint. A second, orthogonal taxonomy covers contact, where the map is non-smooth. We then ask whether a correct gradient helps. Four mechanisms by which useful gradients are lost are cataloged and measured on one testbed, where the advantage of the exact derivative over the equation-level adjoint depends on where the fitting target comes from as much as on the solver budget, and we review the evidence that zeroth-order methods can outperform simulator gradients in the regimes where those mechanisms act. The model classes, systems techniques and applications are surveyed through this lens, and we close with a reporting checklist, a released diagnostic that computes it, and a research agenda.
The balance between feature learning and collapse in dynamical systems-based generative models
Julian Brandon; Bruno Loureiro; N Alex Cayco-Gajic; Arthur Pellegrino

Over the past decade, a growing body of work has established that implicit biases in learning dynamics fundamentally shape the solutions found by neural networks, governing their learned features and generalisation performance. However, despite these strides in deep learning theory, far less is known about representation learning in generative models based on dynamical systems, from normalising flows to diffusion. Importantly, empirical evidence suggests that continuous-time generative models can be prone to mode collapse, yet a learning theory explaining such biases remains elusive. To address this, we use tools from dynamical systems and operator theory to express the gradient flow of a general class of stochastic differential equations as a composition of linear operators, allowing us to relate collapse to low-rank biases in generative models. In variational inference and flow-matching tasks, we show that this bias can manifest in two different mechanisms: i) where collapsed models are stable fixed points of the gradient flow, or ii) in sequential feature learning, where smaller modes take progressively longer to be learned, producing an effective collapse for a fixed training budget. Together these findings point to a trade-off between feature learning and collapse, suggesting an operator view as a step towards a unified framework for understanding the learning dynamics of dynamical systems-based generative models.
The strong cylinder conjecture over prime fields

Let $p$ be prime and let $S\subseteq\mathbb F_p^3$ have $p^2$ points, with every affine plane meeting $S$ in a multiple of $p$ points. We give a self-contained argument that $S$ is a union of $p$ parallel lines.

Let $χ$ be a quadratic Dirichlet character and let $Λ(χ, s)$ be its associated completed $L$-function. Nowadays, there are different medical imaging techniques to collect data about the progression of

Good colorings of doubled triangles and a conjecture of Schwartz

Let $p$ be prime. For the weaker requirement of a $2$-factor, Enomoto et al. [J. Graph Theory 9 (1985) 87--95] proved that every $2$-tough graph of order at least three has a $2$-factor and that the toughness threshold $2$ is best possible.
