These results establish local Fatou invariants and 2-adic ergodic averages for $f(z)$, leaving open whether every $n_0 \in \mathbb{N}^+$ lies in $\bigcup_{k \ge 0} f^{-k}(B(O_{1,2}))$.
Stabilization of an Euler--Bernoulli beam equation with distributed damping and interior time delay
Ben B. J. Siriki; N'Guessan F. Alla; Adama Coulibaly

In this paper, we investigate the effect of a fixed time delay on the internal stabilization of an Euler--Bernoulli beam clamped at one end with distributed damping. Under appropriate assumptions on the feedback weights, we first establish that the problem is well-posed using semigroup theory. Furthermore, using the multiplier method combined with a suitable Lyapunov functional, we prove the exponential stability of the system.
Polar foliations on the Cayley plane
Miguel Domínguez-Vázquez; Ricardo A. E. Mendes; Marco Radeschi
We classify polar foliations on the Cayley projective plane, completing the classification of polar foliations on compact rank one symmetric spaces.
Exponential stabilization of an Euler--Bernoulli beam via internal feedback under distributed time delay
Ben B. J. Siriki; Droh A. Behi; N'Guessan F. Alla; Adama Coulibaly

In this paper, we investigate the internal stabilization of a closed-loop system which consists of an Euler--Bernoulli beam subjected to a structural damping mechanism with a distributed delay into the domain. Under appropriate assumptions on the weights of the delay term and internal damping, we first prove the well-posedness of the system by a semigroup approach. Then, by constructing an appropriate Lyapunov functional and utilizing the multiplier method, we establish the exponential decay of the system energy.
The sharp bound on the distance between the centers of mass of a convex body and its boundary
Sergii Myroshnychenko; Dmitry Ryabogin; Kateryna Tatarko; Vladyslav Yaskin

We prove that the distance between the centers of mass $c(K)$ and $c(\partial K)$ of a convex body $K$ and its boundary $\partial K$, respectively, does not exceed $ D_n$ times the width of $K$ in the direction of the vector joining $c(\partial K)$ and $c(K)$. The constant $D_n$ is optimal and coincides with the sharp constant in the problem of bounding the distance between the orthogonal projection of the centroid of a convex body onto a hyperplane and the centroid of its orthogonal projection onto that hyperplane.
Predictive Neuromorphic Control of a Scanning Mirror System: An Event-Centric Framework
Changrui Liu; Robin Wroblowski; Anil Alan; Shengling Shi; Rodolphe Sepulchre; Bart De Schutter

Organizing control around events can reduce sensing and actuation demands while directly linking control decisions to the occurrence and timing of desired system behaviors. This paper proposes a novel event-centric model predictive control (MPC) framework that unifies event sensing, event prediction, and event regulation. Events define the feedback information, prediction horizon, and event-timing objectives, placing them at the center of predictive control design. The framework is developed for a scanning mirror system equipped with a baseline neuromorphic controller composed of spiking neurons that supports sparse actuation. The control objective is to achieve prescribed zero-crossing times and a desired scanning range while minimizing the mechanical energy transferred between the actuator and the mirror. A sampling-based algorithm is presented to obtain suboptimal solutions of the event-centric MPC optimization problem without requiring an explicit event-to-event prediction model. By grounding predictive optimization in events, the proposed framework opens a new direction for MPC design and its integration with neuromorphic control.
Simple algebraic groups with good reduction, the genus problem, and unramified cohomology

We obtain a number of new results on the arithmetic of linear algebraic groups over higher-dimensional fields. In particular, we resolve some key open questions over 2-dimensional global fields, such as the finiteness of the genus of spinor groups of quadratic forms of dimension $\geq 10$. We also extend various finiteness results to new classes of fields, including function fields of $p$-adic surfaces. Our arguments rely in a crucial way on new finiteness results for unramified cohomology.
Geometric Endpoints, Global Trajectories, and Teichmüller Projection for the Möbius-Invariant Willmore Flow

We study endpoints and conformal projection of the Möbius-invariant Willmore flow in the round three-sphere. Under uniform nonumbilicity or an integrable weighted condition, image-measure transport yields a unique finite-time integral-varifold limit. Reduced Hopf trajectories have unique anchored finite-time profile and marked conformal endpoints at arbitrary energy. Every smooth global reduced trajectory converges smoothly modulo reparametrization to an elastic profile, with quantitative rates and finite dissipation length. We compute the differential of the conformal-class projection along reduced trajectories and prove that its maximal rank persists at every finite time when it holds initially. Near the Clifford torus, Hopf tori with the same marked conformal type can have noncollinear projected velocities, ruling out a common autonomous Teichmüller equation even after positive time recalibrations.

We study product-one invariants of finite metacyclic groups, with particular attention to metacyclic $p$-groups. For semidirect products $C_n\rtimes C_m$ such that $\operatorname{ord}_n(\ell)=m$ and $\operatorname{ord}_q(\ell)=m$ for every prime divisor $q$ of $n$, we give a short proof of the known formula for the small Davenport constant and determine the exact value of the $η$-constant. When $n=p$ is prime, we use Vosper's theorem to obtain a growth result for products of non-trivial conjugacy classes contained in $C_p$, from which we derive a block-saturation principle for product-one sequences.
 For split metacyclic $p$-groups, we determine the small Davenport constant in terms of the order and the exponent, and obtain bounds for the $η$-constant and the Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant. The Davenport bound is also extended to finite nilpotent split metacyclic groups. Our approach relies in part on a general quotient-lifting principle for the three invariants $\mathsf d$, $η$, and $\mathsf s$. For non-cyclic metacyclic $p$-groups, this principle applies through the Frattini quotient, which is isomorphic to $C_p^2$. We further establish upper and lower bounds for the Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant of arbitrary metacyclic $p$-groups, and show that both bounds are best possible within this class.
 The lifting method also provides a short proof of a known theorem of Han and Zhang for groups $C_m\ltimes C_n$ with $m\mid n$. Finally, we determine the Olson constant of the dihedral group $D_{2p}$, for every prime $p>3$, in terms of the Olson constant of $C_p$.
Sparse Fault Detection in Linear Systems: Equivalence of GLR Tests and $\ell_1$-regularized Least Squares

This paper studies the detection of an impulsive fault of unknown time and input channel in a linear system with unknown initial state and Gaussian measurement noise. First, we show that the generalized likelihood ratio test, after the initial state is eliminated by projection onto the parity space, is the zero-solution test of a weighted lasso with an unpenalized nuisance block; the regularization parameter is the test threshold, and for unknown noise variance the same holds for the square-root lasso. Second, we show that the null distribution depends on the system only through a Gram matrix, so that the threshold is computed exactly and offline, and we compare it with closed-form bounds. Third, we characterize the fraction of a fault that survives the projection: we give it in closed form through observability Gramians, we show that it converges to a geometrically decaying profile for strictly stable systems, and that, for systems with unit-modulus modes, it grows linearly with the fault time as a fraction of the record length. Numerical studies, including a two-input, two-output example, illustrate the results.
Karhunen-Loève Transforms of Autoregressive Windows Based on Matched Symmetry Groups

The Karhunen-Loève transform of a window of a stationary autoregressive process of any order $p$ is described through its poles, extending the Algebraic Diversity framework, which selects a transform by the matched group. For simple roots every basis vector is a sum of at most $p$ sinusoids, at the frequencies where the spectrum equals the eigenvalue, plus modes decaying from the ends. The window covariance differs from a member of the class diagonalized by the type-II discrete cosine transform by a closed-form matrix of rank $2p$, exactly when no pole is zero, so the eigenvalues interlace spectrum samples on the cosine grid, and the coding-gain loss of the cosine transform is an exact function of that matrix with computable bounds: for the $8\times8$ Markov block of image coding at pole $0.95$ it is below 1.2 percent. By Kronecker's theorem the rank is at most $2\max(p,q)$ for rational spectra; a moving-average window departs in its Hankel corners, and an integrated (ARIMA) window departs by low rank from the type-VII sine class, exact for the random walk. The exact symmetry is generically the reflection and contains a wreath product for interleaved windows; the dihedral group of the even extension is matched approximately, the dominant pole's sign choosing cosine or sine. The two groups give the transform a fast form: a parity fold, half-length cosine cores and a cascade of at most $p$ first-order Cauchy stages, exactly $p$ for a minimal AR($p$) model. The first-order case recovers results obtained by other means.
When Strategies Do Not Determine Play: Infinite Hat-Guessing Games on Subsets of the Reals

We study infinite hat-guessing games indexed by linearly ordered sets $S\subseteq\mathbb R$, where players guess sequentially using information determined by the order. While well-ordered standing sets admit the naive, recursive definition of play, we found a surprising example showing that this approach fails for non-well-ordered ones, where local decision rules do not determine a unique global outcome. By requiring uniqueness of play, we aim to provide a natural framework for hat-guessing games on arbitrary standing sets.
 For the classical visibility model, it was previously known due to Glivický that at most one incorrect guess can be guaranteed when $S$ is well-ordered. We prove the same result for backwards well-ordered sets, even in the case when $S$ has no first element.
 In the full-visibility version of the game, Glivický proved that at most one incorrect guess can be guaranteed if the standing set has a first element. We extend this result to arbitrary nonempty standing sets.
A Talenti-type rigidity theorem and P-function constraints for the Pompeiu--Schiffer problem in every dimension

Schiffer's conjecture asserts that the ball is the only bounded domain, with boundary homeomorphic to a sphere, carrying a nonconstant Neumann eigenfunction of the Laplacian that is constant on the boundary; for such domains it is equivalent to the Pompeiu problem. In 2026 it was disproved in the plane and in many higher dimensions by computer-assisted and analytic constructions. We study what survives. Our main result is a Talenti-type theorem valid in every dimension $N\ge2$: if the eigenfunction $u$ stays strictly below its boundary value $c>0$, then $kR^*\ge j_{N/2,1}$, where $k^2$ is the eigenvalue, $R^*$ the radius of the ball of equal volume and $j_{N/2,1}$ the first positive zero of $J_{N/2}$; equality holds only for the ball. We compare this threshold with the unconditional bound $kR^*\ge 2^{1/N}j_{N/2-1,1}$ given by the Krahn--Szegő inequality. Using Payne's P-function $P=|\nabla u|^2+λu^2$ we prove that every Schiffer domain satisfies $\max|u|>\sqrt N\,|c|$, together with pointwise and distance bounds. We correct the shape-optimization approach of an earlier work by computing the optimality condition of the associated boundary functional with an adjoint state. Using the transcendence of the zeros of Bessel functions of integer and half-integer order, we prove the infinitesimal rigidity of the ball, in every dimension, both for the Schiffer problem and for the Berenstein problem. Finally, we reconstruct numerically the convex four-dimensional counterexample of Guo and check the above statements on it.
Division ring extensions and the realization of Coxeter diagrams $I_2(n)$

For each integer $n\ge5$, we construct a hereditary artinian ring of finite representation type with Coxeter diagram $I_2(n)$. Both of its diagonal division rings are two-generated over the field $\mathbb{Q}(ζ)$, where $ζ$ is a primitive root of unity of order $n-2$. The construction is based on a chain of quantized Weyl relations and a shift automorphism. We give one-sided bases for the corresponding division ring extensions and compute the right dimension sequence of the bimodule. The resulting ring has exactly $n$ isomorphism classes of indecomposable finitely generated right modules.
A Talenti-type result for the Pompeiu-Schiffer Conjecture

Schiffer's conjecture asserts that the ball is the only bounded simply connected domain carrying a Neumann eigenfunction of the Laplacian that is constant on the boundary; it is equivalent to the Pompeiu problem. In August 2026 it was disproved in the plane by computer-assisted constructions. We revisit the shape-optimization approach of~\cite{Se24} in the light of these counterexamples. We first show that the vanishing of the material derivative on the boundary, assumed in~\cite{Se24}, never holds, and we compute the correct optimality condition, involving an adjoint state, for the associated functional $J_2$. We prove that every planar Schiffer domain satisfies $\max|u| > \sqrt{2}|c|.$ Our main result is a Talenti-type theorem: if $u < c$ in $Ω$ , then $kR^* \geq j_{1,1},$ where $R^*$ is the radius of the disc of equal area, and equality holds only for the disc. Finally, using Siegel's transcendence theorem, we prove the infinitesimal rigidity of the disc for the Berenstein problem.

We prove the maximal existence conjecture for pluriclosed flow on Kähler backgrounds. This leads to a priori generalizations of the Aubin-Yau and Calabi-Yau theorems, and resolves the question of connectedness of generalized Kähler structures on Calabi-Yau backgrounds.
Lift Height and the Structure of Classification Failure

We introduce a framework for measuring the depth of classification failure relative to a chosen invariant. A \emph{shadow map} records visible structure while suppressing finer information; lift packages recover this information in successive layers, and lift height measures the depth through which classification ambiguity persists. Canonical reduction removes redundant stages and yields an essential notion of lift height. For nilpotent groups, the lower central series provides a natural commutator lift tower, with lift height controlled by nilpotency class and decreasing under refinement of the shadow. The associated graded structure gives a Lie-theoretic interpretation of the successive commutator layers.
 The main examples show that classification depth is genuinely unbounded. Over any field of characteristic different from two, and for every positive integer, there exist nilpotent Lie algebras with the same fixed four-dimensional abelianisation whose commutator lift packages agree through the prescribed number of layers but differ at the next layer. Moreover, such separation can occur at arbitrarily large degree even when the complete underlying lower-central graded vector space is fixed. Thus neither a fixed shadow nor the dimensions, or even the underlying vector-space structure, of the lower-central graded object impose a uniform bound on the depth at which new commutator information may appear.
The Canonical Family of Reduced Row Pivot Echelon Forms and the Induced Lexicographic Canonical Algorithm for Linear Programming
A. G. Paraskevopoulos; D. A. Patsouras

A complete canonical family of uniquely normalized, row-equivalent representatives of an $m\times n$ matrix is introduced and termed the family of Reduced Row Pivot Echelon Forms (RRPEFs). All RRPEFs represent the same row space, with the standard reduced row echelon form, renamed the Upper RREF (URREF), and the Lower RREF (LRREF) as its extreme members. A reformulation of Noether's Complementary Subspace Basis Theorem yields normalized bases of the row space that coincide with the nonzero rows of the corresponding RRPEFs. Constructively, each RRPEF is obtained by multi-index Gauss--Jordan reduction of a nonsingular transition submatrix. Factoring the admissible pivot-index sets by equality of their associated RRPEFs yields a quotient set in canonical bijection with the set of distinct RRPEFs. This bijection transfers the strict lexicographic order to the distinct RRPEFs and induces a finite chain from the URREF to the LRREF. The resulting structure gives rise to the Induced Lexicographic Canonical Algorithm (ILCA). Lexicographic confinement and singular-transition skipping restrict the candidate domain, whereas RRPEF reuse and scalar-equivalent transition bypassing avoid redundant Gauss--Jordan reductions while retaining the corresponding basic-solution tableaux. Strict lexicographic progression prevents cycling, while the traversal proceeds independently of objective improvement under degeneracy-induced stalling. ILCA terminates when a feasible tableau satisfies the standard optimality conditions and otherwise completes the finite traversal, including for Tucker- and Cunningham-type totally degenerate configurations.
Receding horizon control with sensor-induced positive semidefinite state penalization

This paper develops and analyzes a receding horizon control (RHC) framework for the stabilization of infinite-dimensional nonautonomous continuous-time systems with an infinite-horizon control objective. The considered stage costs penalize only a finite-dimensional component of the state and are therefore positive semidefinite with respect to the full state. Without imposing terminal costs or terminal constraints, we establish exponential stability and derive suboptimality estimates under suitable stabilizability and detectability-type assumptions, together with an online selection of the sampling times. In the linear case, we extend the framework to output-feedback RHC by combining it with a Luenberger-type state estimator based on finitely many sensors, and establish closed-loop stability using an augmented Lyapunov functional. The abstract state-feedback results are verified for a nonlinear Schlögl parabolic equation around an unstable steady state and, in the output-feedback setting, for nonautonomous linear parabolic equations. The control and observation realizations involve finite-dimensional actuation and sensing, including localized boundary controls and spatially localized state-penalization operators. Numerical experiments support the theoretical findings and illustrate the performance of the proposed RHC schemes.
A geometrical approach for obtaining exact analytical solutions for a scalar field in a one-dimensional dynamical cavity
Maxwell F. de Araújo; Odemar Julião do N. Neto; Stanley S. Coelho; Jeferson Danilo L. Silva; Alessandra N. Braga; Danilo T. Alves

The dynamical Casimir effect was first predicted by G. T. Moore in 1969, who considered a real scalar field inside a cavity with a moving mirror in ($1+1$)D, satisfying Dirichlet boundary conditions. Moore wrote the general solution for the field in terms of a function that satisfies a functional equation nowadays known as the Moore equation.In the literature, exact analytical solutions to the Moore equation form a rather small set, restricted to specific classes of laws of motion. Cole and Schieve (1995) developed a geometrical approach that yielded a general formula for the solution of the Moore equation for cavities initially at rest. However, its application has always been done through numerical calculations, and their approach has therefore long been regarded solely as a numerical method. In this work, we show that their method can also be employed as a powerful method for deriving exact analytical solutions, and show the applicability of this approach to deriving analytical solutions to the Moore equation. We obtain original exact analytical solutions for an expanding cavity with a uniformly moving mirror, a contracting cavity with a mirror that approaches the static one asymptotically, and, in addition, we recover the first analytical solution to the Moore equation for a resonant mirror motion, originally obtained by Law in 1994. Moreover, we extend the Cole-Schieve approach, showing that exact solutions can be constructed from any spacetime region where the Moore function has already been determined. We show that this extended geometrical approach allows us to expand the set of known analytical solutions to the Moore equation from the few classes of motion reported in the literature to an infinite set, as it enables the treatment of new classes of laws of motion obtained by combining those presented here with each other as well as with previously known classes of trajectories.

We study CFT four-point functions of identical scalar primaries as their dimension $Δ$ grows for fixed $0<z, \bar z<1$, and call them liberated if they grow at the same exponential rate as those of a generalized free field (GFF), as is the case for heavy free particles propagating along geodesics in AdS. We show that the correlator is liberated at the crossing symmetric point if and only if the light spectrum is sparse, and that liberation then holds wherever $z$ and $\bar z$ lie on the same side of $1/2$. If the low twist states are also sparse, liberation holds everywhere except in an explicit band around $z+\bar z=1$. In particular, if the primary twist gap lies above $\sqrt{2}Δ$, then the correlator is liberated everywhere. For twist cutoffs below $Δ$, composites of two spinning generalized free fields fail to be liberated in a region that fills the band near the double lightcone limit. In two dimensions, Virasoro primaries cannot be liberated unless the central charge grows faster than $Δ$. The same framework sharpens the universality of large-$c$ torus partition functions of two-dimensional CFTs.
Kronecker coefficients of large degree and Littlewood-Richardson inequalities

We prove that Kronecker coefficients are uniformly asymptotic to $f^λf^μf^ν/n!$ when all three irreducible dimensions are at least $\sqrt{n!}\,e^{-A\sqrt n}$, for any fixed $A>0$. This strengthens a conjecture of Pak, Panova and Yeliussizov. For triple staircase and triple square partitions, we obtain relative asymptotics with respective limiting factors $e^{-1/24}$ and $e^{-1/3}$. For Littlewood-Richardson (LR) coefficients, we bound the sum of the three dimension deficits by the LR coefficient deficit times $O(\log n)$, proving their Conjecture 5.5 and extending it to arbitrary fixed size proportions. We also construct vanishing LR coefficients with three Plancherel dimension sequences and determine the exact stabilization threshold of the largest LR coefficient with one input size fixed.
Discrete Distributions and Their Limit Theorems in the Surreal Numbers

We extend the discrete uniform, hypergeometric and binomial distributions to the surreal numbers, allowing infinitely many outcomes, chips and trials. A uniform distribution on $\mathbb{N}$ gives each outcome probability $1/ω$; on the eventually periodic sets we define the needed sizes explicitly, obtaining a probability that is regular and strictly monotone. For an urn with infinitely many chips and finitely many draws, the hypergeometric distribution is within an infinitesimal of the binomial. With infinitely many trials, and under a hypothesis on factorials of omnific integers that we show can be satisfied, we prove a surreal de~Moivre--Laplace theorem, and we show that the hypergeometric distribution with infinitely many draws is locally normal with a finite-population correction. Near its center, it is relatively close to the binomial distribution if and only if the sampling fraction is infinitesimal, an exact form of a familiar rule of thumb. For rare successes we prove, without any hypothesis on factorials, a surreal Poisson limit theorem and describe urns with finitely many red chips, where the binomial approximation fails beyond the first success.
Pierre Colmez; sally Gilles; Zhenghui Li; Wiesława Nizioł

We prove the étale-de Rham direction of the $C_{\st}$-conjecture for compactly supported cohomology of smooth partially proper rigid analytic varieties over local fields of mixed characteristic. More precisely, we recover filtered de Rham cohomology and (under a finite-rank assumption) Hyodo--Kato cohomology from compactly supported $p$-adic pro-étale cohomology as derived Hom (in a category of Arithmetic Topological Vector Spaces) with values in $\B_{\pdr}$ and $\B_{\pFF}$ respectively (period rings related to $\B_{\dr}$ and $\B_{\st}$ whose higher Galois cohomology vanishes).
 The proof uses, via the geometrized basic comparison theorem, Poincaré duality for Hyodo--Kato and (filtered) de Rham cohomology, explicit extension calculations for period sheaves, and fully-faithfulness of the passage from Galois equivariant perfect complexes on the Fargues--Fontaine curve to Arithmetic Topological Vector Spaces.
Probabilistic Weapon-Target Allocation Models for the Critical Infrastructure Protection

This paper analyzes methods for solving optimal resource/weapon allocation problems for the protection of critical infrastructure. It examines nonlinear discrete "Attacker-Defender" and "Weapon-Target Allocation" models, incorporating criteria based on the difference in expected losses and risk-related constraints. Methods are proposed for solving these problems by reformulating them as mixed-integer linear programming problems.
Robust Gaussian process regression: posterior contraction
Ismaël Castillo; Paul Egels; Riccardo Lazzarini; Botond Szabó

Gaussian processes form a popular and flexible class of prior distributions with principled uncertainty quantification, but the Gaussian likelihood on which the corresponding posterior relies makes them highly sensitive to outliers and contaminated observations. We study Gaussian process regression when among the $n$ observations, $m$ of these are possibly contaminated. A generic framework to obtain posterior contraction rates in this setting is considered, from a frequentist perspective as the sample size $n$ and the number of corrupted observations $m$ grow. We adopt a generalized Bayes approach in which the log--likelihood is replaced by a robustified version; we discuss various choices thereof, such as one recently proposed by Altamirano et al. that preserves conjugacy. We investigate the minimax rate of estimation under adversarial contamination in terms of the Sobolev smoothness $β$ of the regression function and $m$. The question of building adaptive procedures to both $β$ and $m$ is investigated, and we show that a polynomial loss for adaptation must be paid in general. We instantiate our results for Matérn Gaussian process and deep ReLU network priors. Numerical experiments for existing and new robust algorithms are provided, illustrating the practical applicability of our results.
Recursive Pricing and Incumbent Subtree Column Generation for Solving Optimal Classification Trees
Tengmu Hu; Chen Chen; Theodore T. Allen

Solving optimal classification tree (OCT) problems is computationally challenging because branching, routing, and leaf-assignment decisions must be optimized jointly. We develop an incumbent subtree column generation algorithm (ISCG-OCT) that exploits the recursive structure of classification trees. We first introduce a mixed set-packing and set-partitioning formulation (MSSF). We then construct a restricted master problem whose columns represent feasible subtree patterns. Unlike conventional dual-based column generation, our incumbent-centered pricing evaluates objective improvements relative to the current solution. We establish a recursive decomposition in which fixing a branching decision separates the remaining pricing problem into independent subtree subproblems, enabling exact dynamic programming. We also develop threshold-based variants that trade optimality guarantees for computational efficiency. Computational experiments on 27 benchmark datasets demonstrate competitive training and testing accuracy and substantial reductions in solution time on many instances. When initialized with a CART solution, ISCG-OCT can certify global optimality faster than warm-started mixed-integer programming solvers on selected instances. These results demonstrate how recursive pricing and structured subtree optimization can improve the computational efficiency of exact classification tree methods.
No regular icosahedron has a rational point on every face: a proof checked in Lean

We prove that no regular icosahedron in $\mathbb{R}^3$ has a point with rational coordinates on each of its twenty closed faces, in every position, size and orientation, reflections included. This answers a question of I. Bogdanov on MathOverflow. A field automorphism of $\mathbb{C}$ that sends $\sqrt5$ to $-\sqrt5$ reduces the problem to the following statement: for every complex orthogonal $3\times3$ matrix $T$ some real linear combination of $\mathrm{Re}\,T$ and $\mathrm{Im}\,T$ separates ten intervals determined by the faces. We prove this statement by a computer-assisted case analysis over rational parametrizations of rotation frames, in which every inequality is an exact polynomial bound over $\mathbb{Z}[\varphi]$, $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$; no floating-point arithmetic and no Lipschitz estimates are used. The whole argument, including the $48$ certificates, is formalized in the Lean 4 proof assistant with Mathlib and checked by the Lean kernel; the main theorem depends only on the standard axioms. The mathematical argument and the formalization were produced by AI systems (OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude) under the direction of the author; see the statement at the end of the paper.
Representations of the Weyl algebra modulo $p^2$

Let $\mathbf{k}$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$. Let $R=W_2(\mathbf{k})$ be the ring of Witt vectors of length $2$. In this note, we are concerned with the study of representations of the first Weyl algebra that are finite-rank free $R$-modules ($R$-lattices). Our main result shows that given an $R[x]$-lattice $V$, it admits a left module structure over the Weyl algebra (equivalently, an $R$-linear connection) if and only if all of its indecomposable summands have the form $R[x]\otimes_{R[x^p]}N$, where $N$ is an indecomposable $R[x^p]$-lattice of rank divisible by $p$. We also classify, up to isomorphism, all lattices over the $p$-Weyl algebra (defined by $[y,x]=p$) for which the action of $x$ modulo $p$ is regular nilpotent.

A natural number $n$ has the $Δ$ property if some difference of complementary divisors of $n$ is the sum of two such differences; equivalently, if some split graph has a factor graph containing an $n$-simple triangle. In additive terms, $n$ has the $Δ$ property exactly when the positive part of the factor-difference set of $n$, introduced by Erdős and Rosenfeld, is not sum-free. The set $\mathbb{N}(Δ)$ of such numbers is closed under multiplication by squares, and it was conjectured that it contains infinitely many $Δ$-primitive perfect squares. We prove this conjecture, and show that these squares can be chosen to avoid any prescribed finite set of primes but $3$.
A rank-zero $2$-converse to the Gross--Zagier and Kolyvagin theorem for elliptic curves with abelian two-division field

Let $E/\mathbb{Q}$ be an elliptic curve with abelian two-division field. We prove that finiteness of ${\mathrm Sel}_{2^\infty}(E/\mathbb{Q})$ implies $L(E,1)\ne0$. The proof follows the quadratic twist deformation approach of OpenAI: Beilinson--Kato elements are interpolated over the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_2$-extension and over families of quadratic twists, and congruences in the resulting group ring transfer non-vanishing from the twists to $E$. The integral control of this interpolation is governed by one cohomological $μ$-invariant, which depends only on $E[2]$ and vanishes for abelian two-division fields. Together with Kato's cyclotomic divisibility and the fixed lattice in his construction, it bounds the denominator by a fixed power of $2$, independently of the twisting primes and the family dimension. Congruences among coefficients of a half-integral-weight form, in the style of Ono--Skinner, construct the required twist families.
Multiparameter counting of numerical semigroups by Frobenius number, genus, and multiplicity

A numerical semigroup is a subset of the nonnegative integers, closed under addition and with finite complement. The size of the complement is its genus. The problem of counting semigroups by the largest gap got very important through the so-called Frobenius problem, first documented in 1884. Accordingly, the largest gap is called the Frobenius number. In the last two decades, counting by the genus has become a subject of even more intense study, mostly because of the non-solved conjectures on its monotonic and super-Fibonacci growth.
 It is known that the number of semigroups of each genus grows asymptotically with the genus like the Fibonacci numbers and that the number of semigroups of each Frobenius number grows asymptotically in such a way that each number doubles the previous but one. We prove a formula for the number of numerical semigroups of each Frobenius number, genus, and multiplicity (first nonzero nongap), under the assumption that the multiplicity $m$ and the Frobenius number $F$ satisfy $m\geq\frac{F+1}{3}$. It has been proved that asymptotically almost all semigroups satisfy this condition. From this formula we prove multiparameter recurrence relations. They give, under the required restriction, a multiparameter exact version of the increasing behaviours previously mentioned. Indeed, we prove that the number $n_{F,m,g}$ of semigroups with Frobenius number $F$, multiplicity $m$ and genus $g$ satisfies $n_{F,m,g}=n_{F-2,m-1,g-1}+n_{F-2,m-1,g-2}$ and that the number $n_{F,m}$ of semigroups with Frobenius number $F$ and multiplicity $m$ satisfies $n_{F,m}=2n_{F-2,m-1}.$
Comparability for quadratic forms with space-dependent singular measures

This paper investigates quadratic forms $\mathcal{E}^Γ$ generated by configurations $Γ$ and families of measures that are parametrized in the space variable and singular with respect to the Lebesgue measure. A first basic result is the construction of corresponding integro-differential operators in divergence form. These operators are obtained by symmetrizing the family of singular measures. The main result is the comparability of the quadratic form $\mathcal{E}^Γ$ with the quadratic form $\mathcal{E}^s$ which is associated with the fractional Laplacian $(-Δ)^s$. Comparability of $\mathcal{E}^Γ$ and $\mathcal{E}^s$ implies Hölder regularity and a weak Harnack inequality for solutions to integro-differential equations involving these operators.
Linear bound for commuting matrix algebra II
Caihua Luo; Xu Song; Yilin Zeng

Let $\mathbb{F}$ be a field, and let $A_1,\cdots,A_m$ be pairwise commuting $n\times n$ matrices. For $m\geq3$ and $n\geq2$, we prove \[
 \dim_{\mathbb{F}} \mathbb{F}[A_1,\cdots,A_m]
 \leq \left\lceil C_m(n-1)\right\rceil \quad\text{with}\quad
 C_m=\frac{Γ(m)}{Γ((m+1)/2)^2}. \] In particular, three commuting matrices generate an algebra of dimension at most $2n-2$.
Universal Critical Relations and Nonuniversal Scaling in Inverse-Square Ising Chains

For ferromagnetic Ising chains with $n^2J_n\to B>0$, the critical excess magnetization in a field inversely proportional to spin separation determines the connected correlation. Their slowly varying profile has finite logarithmic integral exactly when the ordered thermal slope is finite. For any finite nonnegative core, an exact tail gives inverse-logarithmic correlations and a square-root cusp. A relative correction $c/\log(n+e)$ with $c>1$ gives continuously varying logarithmic powers and a linear cusp. A lower bound on its disordered susceptibility excludes the usual Kosterlitz--Thouless law.
Suboptimality of Gaussian quadrature for Freud and logistic weights in weighted Sobolev spaces

We study the worst-case error of Gaussian quadrature for integrals over the real line weighted by Freud weights $\exp(-|x|^β)$ with $β>1$, and by the logistic density $\mathrm{e}^{-x}/(1+\mathrm{e}^{-x})^2$. The integrand functions are assumed to live in the $ρ$-weighted $L^2$-based Sobolev space of smoothness $α\in\mathbb{N}$.
 We prove that any linear quadrature using the $n$ Gaussian nodes, irrespective of the choice of quadrature weights, has a worst-case error bounded from below by a constant times $n^{-α(1-1/β)}$ for the Freud weights, and by a constant times $(\log n)^{-α}$ for the logistic weight. Our proof is based on three simple observations. First, the worst-case error of any linear quadrature is bounded from below in terms of the number of its nodes in a fixed interval. Second, the number of Gaussian nodes in such an interval is bounded from above by means of Christoffel functions. Third, Christoffel functions admit sharp lower bounds on such an interval. For the Freud weights with even integer exponents and for the logistic weight, all steps are proved in an elementary and self-contained way; for the logistic weight, we use explicit recurrence coefficients of the corresponding orthogonal polynomials. Our results provide a theoretical explanation, for integrands of finite smoothness, of the slow convergence of Gauss--Logistic quadrature observed in the literature. In contrast, for the logistic weight and for the Freud weights with even integer exponents, the Möbius-transformed trapezoidal rule attains the optimal rate $n^{-α}$. This rule does not depend on the smoothness $α$ and requires only point values of the integrand and the weight.

We prove versions of (variations of) Erdős sumset and $B+B+t$ conjectures asked by Kra, Moreira, Richter and Robertson for semigroups equipped with pairwise commuting non-algebraic definable Keisler measures. Our results use model-theoretic methods involving the existence of \emph{many} coheir independent tuples in every definable relation of positive density.
On Słociński-type decomposition, BCL model and unitary extension of commuting Banach space Wold isometries
Swapan Jana; Sourav Pal; Saikat Roy

The adjoint of an operator plays the central role in Hilbert space operator theory. In particular, dilations of Hilbert space contractions, extension of commuting Hilbert space isometries to Hilbert space unitaries, orthogonal decompositions of contractions and functional models for commuting isometries are heavily dependent on the presence of adjoint. In this paper, we develop a theory of Banach space Wold isometries with right-complemented ranges by showing explicit constructions of Berger-Coburn-Lebow model and unitary extension for such isometric tuple without the help of adjoint. We also show that a Słociński type decomposition is possible for such a commuting tuple of Banach space isometries. Each of our results generalizes the corresponding result in the Hilbert space theory.
SU(2) Yang-Mills: Spectral Bounds, Vacuum Concentration, and Criteria for the Continuum Limit

A continuum mass-gap argument must preserve nonzero renormalized states and a positive spectral estimate while the spatial cutoff is removed and physical volume grows. We develop quantitative results that separate these requirements. Gauge reduction, reflection positivity and attributed strong-coupling estimates give physical-transfer bounds with nontrivial local sectors. At fixed spatial cutoff and positive coupling, we construct subsequential infinite-volume physical-time dynamics from local history correlations, with nonconstant gauge-invariant observables. For finite spatial boxes, explicit bounds apply to the entire physical vacuum complement; finite-matrix criteria include all omitted representations. Vacuum concentration gives extensive entropy bounds, quantitative fidelity obstructions for hard electric cutoffs, and necessary growth of retained representation spaces. A sharper local comparison yields complete bounds on fixed discarded-link sectors, while collective projection and Schur estimates isolate the additional input needed for a volume-uniform gap. The work also certifies a finite three-link conditioning functional through Wilson coupling 0.354, with its physical interpretation conditional on the stated block-comparison hypotheses. Exact blocking, corrected effective-potential theorems and a representation-by-representation two-dimensional benchmark clarify which approximations preserve the relevant observables. Published glueball measurements retain their original attribution; their reanalysis and the reproduced winding-channel and replica studies have explicitly statistical scope. Complete derivations and reproducible calculations support a set of certified benchmarks and continuum transfer criteria. A nontrivial four-dimensional spatial-cutoff construction and a positive spectral bound along it are not established; no exact continuum mass is asserted.
Asymptotic Stability of Planar Viscous Contact Waves for the Three-Dimensional Full Compressible Navier--Stokes Equations in the Whole Space

The asymptotic stability of planar viscous contact waves is established for the three-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes equations in the whole space. The exact evolving planar background is constructed in a companion one-dimensional paper and may arise from a large integrable perturbation. The three-dimensional remainder has small energy, prescribed second-derivative bounds for density and velocity, and a prescribed first-derivative bound for temperature. Its initial temperature lies in a fixed positive interval; its second derivatives need only be finite. A unique global positive strong solution and algebraic decay in the uniform norm are obtained. The wave-strength threshold depends on lower-order planar bounds, while the allowed remainder size may depend on the complete planar datum.
Stability and Optimal Decay of Viscous Contact Waves under Large Perturbations

The stability of viscous contact waves is established for the one-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes equations under large integrable perturbations. A unique global positive solution is obtained, which converges uniformly to a fixed Eulerian contact profile at the optimal inverse square-root rate in time. The wave-strength threshold depends only on bounds for the initial density perturbation in the first-order Sobolev norm, the energy of the initial velocity perturbation, the thermal relative entropy and the total conserved excess, together with positive lower bounds for the initial density and temperature. It is independent of higher Sobolev norms and the common far-field velocity. No square-integrability condition is imposed on the initial anti-derivatives. Derivative and pressure decomposition estimates are also established for the evolving solution.
Bounded Spaces without a Geodesic in the Gromov-Hausdorff Class

We construct two countable complete bounded metric spaces at Gromov-Hausdorff distance $1/4$ with no midpoint and hence no shortest curve between them. The proof uses the local existence of optimal correspondences near a space with finitely many self-correspondences of distortion below a fixed positive threshold, each of which is the graph of a bijection.
A Stability Analysis of AdamW: Unstable Equilibria and Non-Convergence
Baiyu Su; Lizhang Chen; Qiang Liu

AdamW is ubiquitous in deep learning, yet its behavior remains poorly understood. We analyze its dynamics through the lens of dynamical systems and show that AdamW admits an implicit fixed-point objective: its fixed points coincide with the stationary points of a constrained and regularized optimization problem. However, not all of these fixed points are stable under AdamW's dynamics, and stability depends sensitively on curvature, weight decay, and momentum parameters. Even in one-dimensional settings, equilibria may be unstable, and trajectories can exhibit persistent oscillations rather than convergence to them. We further extend the analysis to higher dimensions, deriving sufficient conditions for local stability of the continuous-time dynamics, and propose a convergent modification that preserves AdamW's fixed points. These results clarify what optimization problem AdamW is associated with, when its convergence can be expected, and how its dynamics could inspire more reliable optimizers.
K-PWM: Control-Oriented Structured Bilinear World Models under Partial Observation
Santosh Mohan Rajkumar; Sriram Narayanan; Samuel E. Otto; Debdipta Goswami

World models learn internal simulators of environment dynamics for prediction, planning, and control, yet learning them from limited, noisy, and partial observations remains challenging. While much progress has focused on pixel-based observations, many physical systems instead provide vector-valued measurements that reveal only part of the underlying state. We introduce K-PWM, a probabilistic world model for prediction and control under partial observation. K-PWM couples Koopman-bilinear latent dynamics with a nonlinear observation decoder and performs probabilistic latent-state inference through the learned model via extended Kalman filtering and smoothing, without a separately trained inference network. Its bilinear structure enables exact propagation of the maintained Gaussian belief through the latent transition and efficient rollouts for uncertainty-aware model predictive path integral (MPPI) control. For training K-PWM, we present a generalized expectation conditional maximization (GECM) procedure with closed-form updates for the generators, noise covariances, and latent prior, complemented by gradient-based decoder learning. A Koopman-consistent initialization selects the latent dimension from data and initializes the action-dependent dynamics. With limited training data, K-PWM achieves lower long-horizon prediction error than the evaluated baselines on partially observed Gymnasium MuJoCo systems, while substantially reducing training time relative to the strongest prediction baseline. On high-dimensional MuJoCo Menagerie robots, it achieves competitive tracking accuracy with low per-step computation times, demonstrating potential for real-time deployment. These results support structured probabilistic dynamics as a data- and compute-efficient approach to world modeling and control under partial observation.
Induced-Minor-Free Graphs Admit a Star-Based Separator of Size $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{n})$
Arnold Filtser; Nikolai Karol; Hung Le; Florian Lehner

Given an $H$-induced-minor-free graph $G$ with $n$ vertices, we construct a balanced separator of $G$ consisting of $\tilde{O}(|V(H)|\sqrt{n})$ star subgraphs. Our result is an induced-minor-free analog of the famous separator theorem for $H$-minor-free graphs by Alon, Seymour, and Thomas [J. Amer. Math. Soc., 1990]. A key idea in our construction is a new decomposition of $H$-induced-minor-free graphs, analogous to the cop decomposition for $H$-minor-free graphs by Andreae [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B, 1986]. We also discuss several algorithmic applications of our result.
Does Merge Form a Hopf Algebra? Coproducts, Traces, and the Prospects of Algebraic Minimalism

Marcolli, Chomsky, and Berwick (2025; henceforth MCB) formulate the Merge operation of Minimalism on a Hopf algebra of Connes-Kreimer type, and claim that language and physics obey the same algebraic structure. This paper separates their program into the working hypothesis H, that Merge on workspaces can be described as a Hopf algebra, and the claim P placed on top of it, that language and physics obey the same principle, and examines the validity of H. MCB employs two coproducts in formulating Merge, corresponding to two different translations of movement (Internal Merge): $Δ_d$, which deletes the lower copy, and $Δ_c$, which leaves a trace. MCB uses the former in syntax and the latter at the syntax-semantics interface, but $Δ_d$ is not coassociative, and $Δ_c$ is not connected under the gradings MCB gives and, moreover, not coassociative as long as the labels of traces are retained. Consequently, MCB's algebra is not a Hopf algebra, and the Birkhoff factorization is not a consequence of the Hopf-algebra theorem but of a weaker statement that requires neither coassociativity nor connectedness. There are four ways to recover a Hopf algebra, but none of them can distinguish different traces, and hence none is compatible with Heim-Kratzer-style formal semantics, which reads traces as indexed variables. Thus H does not hold at present, and under the current formulation, making Minimalism a Hopf algebra and preserving its connection with formal semantics are mutually exclusive. Finally, we indicate three directions in which algebraic Minimalism may proceed.
Compression of Sources with Memory and Private Random Access
Venkat Chandar; Aslan Tchamkerten; Shashank Vatedka

Private local decoding imposes a stringent constraint on compression: the codeword bits used to recover a source symbol must reveal nothing about the remaining symbols beyond what the recovered symbol itself reveals. For memoryless sources, this constraint is known to be compatible with entropy-rate compression. We show that the same holds for any stationary ergodic source over a finite alphabet. Specifically, every rate above the entropy rate is achievable with exact privacy and error-free local decoding on a set of source sequences whose probability tends to one. In contrast, we exhibit non-ergodic sources for which private local decoding incurs a strictly positive rate penalty.

The Einstein equations constrain the transverse Taylor series at a degenerate Killing horizon, but even complete knowledge of that series need not determine a smooth spacetime: a nonzero difference can vanish to every order at the horizon. We show that this ambiguity disappears when the limiting metric on the space of Killing orbits admits a spacelike graph over a compact horizon section. In dimensions $d\geq4$, smooth vacuum Einstein germs with the same marked transverse jets are then locally isometric on a two-sided neighborhood of the whole section. The proof combines a terminal wave-map gauge with energy estimates on the orbit cylinder and yields a finite weighted matching criterion. For unwarped horizons with positive-Einstein sections, a condition on the full Lichnerowicz spectrum reduces the smooth classification to parallel first transverse data. All such data have convergent multiwarped Einstein realizations, including examples whose sections have negative sectional-curvature directions. We also obtain a finite-regularity version for round sections. The continuation argument extends to four-dimensional Einstein--Maxwell theory and gives smooth charged-Nariai rigidity. Finally, rotating Nariai data admit the required spacelike graph throughout the regular branch; an all-order tensor estimate yields smooth Kerr--de Sitter or rotating-Nariai rigidity for $a^2/r_0^2\leq1/8$, without assuming ambient axial symmetry.
A Legendre-Galerkin Method for Kinetic Models of Opinion Dynamics with Quasi-Invariant Consistency

Kinetic models of opinion dynamics provide a mesoscopic framework for describing collective behavior arising from interactions among a large number of individuals. Highly accurate numerical approximation to such Boltzmann-type equations, however, remains challenging due to the nonlinear inelastic collision operators involving multiple integrals coupling opinion variables and random perturbations. To address the difficulties, we develop a Legendre-Galerkin spectral method for a general class of kinetic models with opinion-dependent interaction rules. Our method exploits an exact decoupling of the weak collision kernel to obtain a time-independent tensor representation of the Galerkin collision operator. A recursive construction reduces collision-tensor assembly to one-dimensional quadrature, allowing the coefficients to be precomputed for subsequent use. A rigorous $L^2$-error estimate, along with mass preservation, is established for the fully discrete scheme under suitable regularity and stability assumptions. In the quasi-invariant regime, we derive the limiting Fokker-Planck equation and establish consistency between the exact Legendre-Galerkin operators of the rescaled Boltzmann equation and its limit for each fixed polynomial degree. Numerical experiments support the theoretical results, illustrate quasi-invariant consistency, and capture the formation of opinion clusters under the bounded-confidence interactions.
Sitewise Generator Decomposition and Non-Equilibrium Steady States for Generalized Zero-Range Processes

In this paper we study the generalized zero-range processes considered in [20, 11, 12] with boundary driving. In these processes mass is moved between neighboring sites with rates depending only on the departure site. For a wide class of such models, the equilibrium stationary states are known to be of product form. We show that for such models, the boundary-driven generator can be decomposed into a sum of generators acting on single sites when integrating against (possibly inhomogeneous) products of the equilibrium marginals. We exploit this structure to derive new results for the harmonic models introduced in [15]. In particular, we prove that the propagation of mixture measures in [19] is still valid on graphs with asymmetric edges. On the chain geometry with asymmetric edges, we identify a class of models for which the NESS is given precisely by the NESS of the symmetric harmonic model on the chain. In addition to these results for harmonic models, we also present a new class of asymmetric models on the chain for which the NESS can be found explicitly and exhibits shock behavior. The large deviations for the density profile corresponding to these NESS are stated and proved.
The Lee-Yang property of the Blume-Emery-Griffiths model

The Lieb-Sokal theorem provides a tool for establishing the Lee-Yang property of the partition function of a spin model if the corresponding single-spin partition function has this property and the interaction term in its Hamiltonian is of the form $-\sum J_{ij} S_iS_j$ with $J_{ij}\geq 0$. According to the result of this paper, the spin $S=1$ model with the Hamiltonian $-\sum (J_{ij} S_iS_j + K_{ij}S_i^2S_j^2) + \sum ΔS_i^2$ has the Lee-Yang property for all $K_{ij}\in \mathds{R}$ and $Δ>0$, whenever each $J_{ij}$ exceeds an explicitly computed bound $C(β, Δ, K_{ij})>0$, such that $C(β, Δ, K_{ij})\to + \infty$ as $β\to 0$. The latter suggests that the Lee-Yang property of this model may hold only for sufficiently low temperatures.

The Hölder dimension of a metric space is the infimum of its Hausdorff dimension over all bi-Hölder changes of the metric. Colvin asked whether it can take noninteger values. We show that every metric space of finite upper box dimension has integer Hölder dimension. For a bounded subset of a Euclidean space, the dimension reduction is carried out by a global homeomorphism of the ambient space, built from randomly translated singular functions, which brings the Hausdorff dimension of the set arbitrarily close to its integer part.
On the Complexity of Extending Prescribed Linear Forests to Hamiltonian Cycles in Hypercubes

Let $Q_n$ be the $n$-dimensional hypercube, and let $P\subseteq E(Q_n)$ be a set of prescribed edges. It is known that, for $n\ge 2$, every such set $P$ with $|P|\leq 2n-3$ whose edges form a linear forest is contained in a Hamiltonian cycle of $Q_n$. This bound is sharp for general linear forests. The computational complexity of deciding whether a prescribed edge set of a hypercube can be extended to a Hamiltonian cycle was posed as an open question by Dvořák [SIAM J. Discrete Math. 19 (2005) 135--144]. We prove that the problem is NP-complete even when the prescribed edges form a spanning linear forest with no isolated vertices. We give a polynomial-time reduction from a restricted 3-SAT problem, using local spanning path-forest gadgets for variables and clauses that are uniformly embedded in the hypercube. The same reduction therefore establishes NP-hardness of two versions of Hamiltonian-cycle extension problems for general prescribed edge sets.
A DG method for the pseudostress-velocity formulation of the Stokes-Brinkman eigenvalue problem

We introduce a discontinuous Galerkin method for the approximation of the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of the Stokes-Brinkman eigenvalue problem. The method is based on a mixed formulation in which the pseudostress tensor and the fluid velocity are the main unknowns, while the pressure can be recovered through a post-processing procedure applied to the pseudostress tensor. Using discontinuous polynomial spaces of degree $k\geq 1$, we propose a consistent symmetric interior penalty discretization for the approximation of the spectrum. Relying on the spectral theory for non-compact operators, we establish convergence of the discrete spectral approximation and derive error estimates for the method. A series of numerical experiments is presented to assess its computational performance. On the one hand, we investigate the convergence rates for different polynomial degrees, computational domains, and values of the permeability. Furthermore, we study the influence of the stabilization parameter on the discrete spectrum by comparing different choices of this parameter and examining their impact on the occurrence of spurious eigenvalues.
On Poincaré spaces which are not manifolds

This expository note gives a short derivation of the classical Spivak normal fibration formula for the total space of a spherical fibration over a Poincaré duality space. We review the associated smooth, PL, and topological manifold realization criteria and illustrate them with examples from the stable stems. The principal application combines these criteria with the completed solution of the Kervaire invariant problem to identify the exceptional stems in a specified family of three cell Poincaré spaces.
Local Certificate Repair for Asynchronous Controller Updates in Recommender Systems

We study how to adapt an existing distributed recommendation controller when local dynamics or objective weights change. Starting from a quadratic stability and cost certificate, we construct positive semidefinite corrections with finite spatial support and an explicit residual. A joint admission test allocates the available dissipation margin to these residuals and to interactions among changes and corrections, including pending updates. The test covers complete declared parameter ranges, allowing different operators to progress independently. For a fixed compatible batch, the corrections define a common storage that guarantees exponential stability and bounds the cost accumulated throughout deployment. When the admitted collection evolves, a reservation protocol preserves the certificate and a rate bound on storage increases ensures exponential convergence. Regional linear-quadratic regulator (LQR) design proposes new gain rows for the operators' own users, and a separate residual-based calculation can certify that the final gain lowers the expected cost. A recommendation-network example illustrates the tradeoff between repair depth, data access, and the benefits of deploying an update.
Sharp Rates for Optimal Recovery of Bandlimited Functions from Localized Oversampling

It is well-known that one can recover a function $f$ bandlimited to $[-δ,δ]$ ( $0<δ<π$) from its finite sample data $f(j),-n\le j\le n$, with an approximation error exponentially decaying to zero as $n$ tends to infinity. Various regularized Shannon sampling formula have been proposed to achieve such exponential approximation. So far the best rate has been
 $$
 O\biggl(\frac1{\sqrt{n}}\exp(-(π-δ)n)\biggr).
 $$
 We establish that the optimal recovery algorithm in the worst-case scenario achieves an approximation error $ρ_{n,δ}$ satisfying
 $$
 c_* \frac1{\sqrt{n}}(\tan\fracδ4)^{2n+1/2}\le ρ_{n,δ}\le C^* \frac1{\sqrt{n}}(\tan\fracδ4)^{2n+1/2},
 \quad 0<δ\leqπ,\quad n\geq1,
 $$
 where $c_*,C^*$ are positive constants independent of $n$ and $δ$. This result identifies the best possible exponential rate to reconstruct bandlimited functions from two-sided finite oversampling data. In other words,
 $$
 ρ_{n,δ} \asymp \frac{\tan\fracδ4}{\sqrt{n}}\exp\bigl(-c_δ(π-δ)n\bigr),
 $$
 where $c_δ$ is strictly decreasing on $(0,π]$ and
 $$
 \lim_{δ\toπ^-}c_δ=1,\ \lim_{δ\to 0^+}c_δ=+\infty.
 $$
 We also make the new finding that one can also reconstruct $f$ bandlimited to $[-δ,δ]$ with exponentially decaying error from one-sided sample data $f(j)$, $1\le j\le n$, and the sharp rate of approximation error $ρ_{n,δ}'$ of the optimal algorithm is
 $$
 ρ_{n,δ}' \asymp \sqrt{δ/π}\sin^n(δ/2).
 $$
From Imperfect Information to Controlled Steps: Stochastic Optimization under Heavy-Tailed Noise and Compression

Stochastic optimization relies on information whose statistical quality, availability, and computational cost can vary substantially. Heavy-tailed observations challenge concentration, compression distorts communicated vectors, and generalized smoothness changes how far an algorithm can move. This dissertation studies these difficulties through two linked design decisions: how to construct an informative search vector and how to convert it into a controlled step.
 We first develop high-probability methods under bounded central $p$-th moments, $p\in(1,2]$, allowing infinite variance when $p<2$. Clipped gradient, accelerated, extragradient, and gradient descent-ascent methods come with guarantees for stochastic minimization and variational inequalities, with smoothness and moment conditions needed only where the iterates lie with high probability. For composite and distributed problems, shifted and innovation clipping preserve the fixed point that direct clipping can disturb, while retaining linear speedup.
 We then characterize the value of richer stochastic information: lower complexity bounds quantify when same-sample gradient differences and stochastic Hessian information improve heavy-tailed nonconvex optimization, and normalized momentum variance reduction and Hessian-corrected momentum attain matching or near-matching in-expectation bounds. Separately clipping gradients and their correction terms yields batch-free high-probability methods.
 For compressed distributed optimization, we prove convergence of normalized error-feedback methods under generalized smoothness without a uniform gradient-dissimilarity assumption, and develop parameter-agnostic variants with five momentum estimators. Finally, we extend the estimator hierarchy to linear minimization oracles over arbitrary norm balls, recovering the Euclidean rates under estimator-specific generalized smoothness.
Model-assisted semi-supervised estimation of the Mann-Whitney probability under right censoring

We study semi-supervised estimation of the full-lifetime Mann-Whitney probability under right censoring using finite covariate-only samples from two populations. A model-assisted estimator is constructed by adjusting censored pair comparisons with differences between labeled and auxiliary feature means. Resource weights minimize first-order variance within the working projection class. Under joint independent censoring and regularity conditions, we establish consistency and asymptotic normality through a four-pool influence representation that accounts for censoring distributions estimated from the same labeled records. Consistent variance estimation from all four sample pools yields Wald confidence intervals. The efficiency analysis relates variance reduction to projected comparison signals and auxiliary sample sizes and characterizes the gap to the semiparametric bound. A fixed-horizon extension accommodates half-weighted ties and the terminal mass induced by capping follow-up. Simulations show increasing precision gains with auxiliary sample size under moderate or strong projected signals, with finite-sample losses in some settings with zero or weak projected signals. A five-year Rotterdam breast-cancer comparison illustrates precision gains and variability across label allocations when auxiliary samples are formed by controlled outcome withholding.
Finite soluble groups with Sylow subgroups of class at most two are IYB-groups
H. Meng; A. Ballester Bolinches; P. Jimenez Seral

We prove that every finite soluble group whose Sylow subgroups have nilpotency class at most two is an involutive Yang--Baxter group ($\IYB$-group). This answers a question of Cedó and Okniński \cite{CedoOkninski2025}. The main method of the $\IYB$-structures has been reflected in \cite{MengBallesterJimenez2026}.
Finite models for the order axioms of the Hilbert Plane: Redundancies and Finite Independence Models

Results on the redundancy and on the independence of the order axioms of the Hilbert plane are scattered in the literature, from Veblen's 1904 remark that the independence of the axioms of order can be shown by finite models to the redundancies removed from Hilbert's axioms of order in later editions of the Grundlagen. The aim of this note is to collect them in an organic and self-contained form for the incidence and order axioms as presented by Greenberg. In doing so we single out three redundancies inside the order axioms: the symmetry of betweenness, the existence part of trichotomy, and the second clause of plane separation. Each of them dictates which part of the corresponding axiom an independence model must violate, and we give explicit finite models of three, three, nine and twenty-five points. A model of all the incidence and order axioms, on the contrary, is necessarily infinite, so the independence of any axiom added to them requires infinite models; for two of the order axioms the finite models also give independence from all the remaining axioms of the Hilbert plane.
A Geometry-Robust Nečas-Type Inequality for Stokes Preconditioning
Qi Xin; Xie Yan; Shihua Gong

Pressure mass preconditioners for the incompressible Stokes equations can deteriorate on domains with narrow gaps. We develop a pressure preconditioner that uses the distance to the boundary to account for spatially varying geometric scales. Its application consists of a pressure mass solve and a weighted pressure Poisson solve, with the squared boundary distance as the diffusion coefficient. The theoretical basis is a distance-weighted pressure norm defined by splitting the pressure into an $L^2$ component and a component controlled by its weighted gradient. We prove that this norm is bounded by the negative norm of the pressure gradient on every bounded connected open set, with a constant depending only on the dimension. A reverse bound follows from the boundary Hardy inequality, giving norm equivalence uniformly over families with bounded Hardy constants. Two-dimensional finite element experiments on slender, perforated, and composite domains demonstrate stable performance across the tested geometric parameters and mesh refinements. The smallest eigenvalues of the preconditioned pressure Schur complement remain close to $0.54$, and block preconditioning with algebraic multigrid auxiliary solves requires about 20--30 FGMRES iterations across the geometric sweeps.
Equivalence of finite and infinite survival and sharpness of the phase transition for additive particle systems

Krone's two-stage contact process is an interacting particle system in which each site on a grid can be in one of three possible states: 0 (empty), 1 (young individual), and 2 (adult individual). Only adults can multiply, and their offspring is initially young, before growing up after an exponential time. There are two death rates, one for adult trees, and a higher one for young trees. The process is additive and has an additive dual, but unlike the contact process it is not self-dual. Answering a question of Krone, for the process on the $d$-dimensional integer grid, Foxall proved that survival of finite populations is equivalent to nontriviality of the upper invariant law. Using a completely different method, we generalise this result to processes on countable groups and along the way also establish sharpness of the phase transition for a general class of additive interacting particle systems.
Dlab--Ringel standardization in algebraic triangulated categories

We introduce the notion of derived standardly stratified algebras as a connective dg analogue of standardly stratified algebras. To this end, we extend the Dlab--Ringel standardization method to algebraic triangulated categories and show that every basic proper derived standardly stratified algebra arises from this extended method. We establish Ringel duality for derived standardly stratified algebras using silting objects. More precisely, the Ringel dual is again derived standardly stratified, and the corresponding perfect derived categories are related by mutually quasi-inverse contravariant triangle equivalences. We also show that, over an algebraically closed field, a proper derived standardly stratified algebra is smooth if and only if its derived standard modules are exceptional. Finally, we prove that dg algebras given by finite acyclic graded quivers with arrows of non-positive degrees and homogeneous relations are derived standardly stratified with respect to every total order on the vertices.
Ranks of fibers in random elliptic surfaces

For random integer polynomials $P$ of arbitrary degree we prove that for $100\%$ of elliptic surfaces $y^2=x^3-P(t)^2x$ the average 2-Selmer rank of the fibers is 3. Consequently, for $100\%$ these random elliptic surfaces we establish a lower bound for the proportion of fibers attaining algebraic rank $0$ and $1$.
Singular parabolic Anderson models - From flat space to geometric contexts

However, the known radius rule leading to linear convergence requires unavailable information and is therefore impractical. We use $$z_k\in\arg\min_{z\in\mathcal X\cap\mathbb B(x_k,t_k)}\langle\nabla f(x_k),z\rangle,\quad x_{k+1}=\mathrm{Proj}_{S_k}(x_k-\nabla f(x_k)/L),$$ where $L$ is the smoothness constant of $f$, $\mathbb B(x,t)$ is the Euclidean ball centered at $x$ of radius $t$, and $S_k$ is the line segment connecting $x_k$ and $z_k$. The radius is updated by $t_{k+1}=\max\{\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|,t_k/2\}$. Projection onto $S_k$ requires only scalar clipping. Assuming an exact local linear minimization oracle, each update uses one oracle call. For any positive initial radius, we bound all oracle calls to reach objective error at most $\varepsilon$ and obtain $O((L/α)\log(1/\varepsilon))$ for fixed initialization, where $α=\min\{α_0,L\}$ and $α_0>0$ is the quadratic-growth constant.

The zero forcing polynomial of a graph counts the number of distinct zero forcing sets of every possible size. In 2018, Boyer et al. asked whether the zero forcing polynomial is always unimodal, and provided some evidence that it is. We answer this question by constructing an infinite family of graphs whose zero forcing polynomials are not unimodal. Our construction also shows that the graph polynomials associated with connected forcing and total forcing are also not unimodal in general.
Financial Connectedness: Heavy Tails andResponse Attribution
Zhu Yuzhao; Shao Jiahui; Liu Dongqi; Li Dan; Hu Xiaoxiao

A financial market can appear mainly dependent on its own shocks under a variance account and mainly dependent on external shocks under a cumulative-response account. We establish how these opposite diagnoses arise from the same propagation system. For a given cumulative magnitude, squaring gives greater weight to responses concentrated across sources and time. Source priorities can therefore reverse even in stable Gaussian systems with known parameters. Heavy tails raise a separate question: whether the reported shares have a fixed population basis. One innovation with an infinite second moment removes the full network's finite covariance input. We characterize when normalized shares nevertheless stabilize and construct rank-amplitude connectedness, a cumulative-deviation target without finite first or second moments. It can be consistently estimated under local dependence and identification conditions. With fitted dynamics and rank scatter fixed, changing attribution replaces 3.14 names in the daily Top 10 of forty stocks, selecting recipients with greater external persistence relative to their own adjustment. In five futures contracts, mean external share rises from 28.0% to 55.9%, and 70.9% of recipient-dates switch from own to external dominance.
Extremal graphs for Alon's graph coupon-collector conjecture

Let \(G\) be a finite simple graph without isolated vertices. Starting with every vertex uncovered, at each step sample a vertex uniformly and independently and cover one of its uncovered neighbors, chosen uniformly, if any. Let \(\cc(G)\) denote the expected number of steps required to cover all vertices. Alon conjectured that disjoint unions of \(K_{d+1}\) maximize \(\cc(G)\) among \(d\)-regular graphs of a prescribed order whenever such unions exist. In this paper, we disprove this conjecture for every fixed \(d\ge2\) and give a complete characterization of the extremal graphs for \(d=2\) at every order \(n\ge3\). In particular, all but at most six vertices of any such extremal graph lie in four-cycle components.
On quantitative aspects of ideal membership certificate and GCD inequality for polynomials evaluated at almost units

In this paper, we obtain an effective bounds for the ideal membership certificate in polynomial rings over almost all rings of S-integers, thereby generalizing results of Aschenbrenner and Evertse and Gyory. We also establish an effective refinement of a result of Xiao, building on earlier work of Levin and Corvaja and Zannier. In particular, we provide explicit bounds for both the number and the total degrees of the exceptional hypersurfaces arising in an inequality that bounds the greatest common divisor of multivariable polynomials evaluated at almost S-units under consideration. As an application of our results, we obtain an effective refinement of a theorem of Corvaja and Zannier: Let $(F_n)_n$ and $(G_n)_n$ be two linear recurrence sequences and $\mathcal{N}$ be the set of positive integers $n$ such that $F_n/G_n$ is an integer. Hadamard quotient theorem, conjectured by Pisot and proven by Van der Poorten states that if the set $\mathcal{N}$ coincides with $\mathbb{N}$ then $\left(F_n/G_n\right)_n$ is itself linear recurrence sequence. Corvaja-Zannier proved that if $\mathcal{N}$ is infinite set, then there exists a nonzero polynomial $P(X)$ such that $\left( P(n)F_n/G_n\right)_n$ agrees with a linear recurrence sequence for all $n$ in a suitable arithmetic progression. We give an explicit bound $C$, depending explicitly on the parameters of the recurrence sequences such that, the conclusion holds if $\mathcal{N}$ contains at least $C$ elements.
Gamma classes, central connection matrices, and tt* geometry

We review the gamma class of complex projective space, but from the point of view of topological-antitopological fusion. We deconstruct the central connection matrix which appears in the work of Dubrovin, Galkin-Golyshev-Iritani, and Cotti-Dubrovin-Guzzetti.

Risk-sensitive optimal stopping is useful when poor stopping outcomes carry substantial costs, as in option exercise, sequential medical treatment, and safety-critical control. A natural objective is Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) of the stopped reward. We develop a theoretical framework and algorithm for CVaR deep optimal stopping. The framework and algorithm address four difficulties in applying risk-sensitive reinforcement learning to optimal stopping: state augmentation, score-function pathology, blindness to success, and dependence on auxiliary networks. We isolate three structural properties of optimal stopping: single-point reward, action-independent dynamics, and sum-zero gradient. We exploit these properties to establish Markov optimality without state augmentation and derive a pathwise gradient estimator. Under bounded policy derivatives, the pathwise estimator has bounded second moments near deterministic policies, avoiding the divergence that can occur with score-function estimators. Building on this framework, we propose DIOS (Distribution-Informed Optimal Stopping) to address the remaining two difficulties. A per-time-step soft penalty combined with tail-level annealing mitigates blindness to success. Estimating the reward quantile directly from each batch removes the need for an auxiliary critic. For a fixed tail level, we establish a finite-time stationarity guarantee under regularity assumptions along the training iterates. Across the 24 main Bermudan max-call configurations, DIOS achieves the highest mean CVaR and the shortest recorded training time among the tested CVaR baselines.
Harmonic functions and comparsion geometry for noncompact 3-manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature

In this paper, we establish several sharp comparsion results for noncompact 3-manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature and with a compact, connected boundary under a boundary mean curvature condition. Then we apply these gradient estimates to establish a Cohn-Vossen type bound for the average of the scalar curvature. This generalizes the work of Colding-Minicozzi \cite{Cold4} and Oronzio \cite{Oro2}.
Approximation by subsequences of matrix transform means of Vilenkin--Fourier series

In this paper we study the rate of approximation by matrix transform means of a special subsequence of partial sums of Vilenkin--Fourier series in the spaces $L_p(G_m)$ $(1\le p<\infty)$ and $C(G_m)$.
Monk and Pieri rules for forest polynomials
Haojun Bai; Shu Xiao Li; David G. L. Wang

This article gives Pieri rules for forest polynomials and Monk rule for double forest polynomials. We construct binary relations $\lessdot_i$ and $\prec_i$ based on the local Tamari moves on indexed forests. These relations are explicit and constructive. For ordinary forest polynomials, the $h$- and $e$-Pieri rules are given by all chains of a fixed length along the cover relations, with certain restriction on the left or right endpoints. For double forest polynomials, our Monk rule shows every off-diagonal degree-one structure coefficient is always a single positive root, whose weight is also controlled by Tamari moves. Additionally, we introduce an insertion algorithm on positive injective words that yields a Monk rule for the corresponding slide polynomials. Regrouping this rule along Sylvester classes gives an independent Monk rule for ordinary forest polynomials.
Ricci pseudo symmetric Anisotropic Fluid Spacetime admitting Hyperbolic solitons with Ricci vector field

This work focuses on an anisotropic fluid spacetime with these unique forms of the stress-energy tensor associated with radial pressure and a transverse pressure p.
