We study the standard form Integer Programming problem (IP) parametrized by the imbalanced circuit packing number. This number is $0$ if and only if $A$ can be transformed to a totally unimodular matrix by row operations, in which case (IP) is solvable in polynomial time. We show that if the constraint matrix represents a graphic matroid, (IP) is fixed-parameter tractable when parametrized by the imbalanced circuit packing number of the matrix. The proof combines an Erdős-Pósa property for edge-colored non-monochromatic cycles with a reduction to mixed-integer programming using few integer variables. In contrast, by a reduction from the parity potential problem, we show NP-completeness of feasibility of (IP) when the constraint matrix represents a cographic matroid, even if kernel of the constraint matrix is $2$-regular and imbalanced circuits pairwise intersect.
Jacobi fields and Jacobi sections for semisprays on Lie algebroids: transverse variations and equivalences
Misael Avendaño Camacho; Jhonny Kama Mamani

We study the relationship between Jacobi sections and Jacobi fields associated with semisprays on Lie algebroids. First, we characterize compatible transverse variations in terms of Lie algebroid morphisms. This characterization leads to a variational description of Jacobi sections: a section along an integral curve of a semispray is a Jacobi section if and only if it arises as the infinitesimal variation of a compatible transverse variation of a dynamical variation satisfying a suitable condition on its image in the base. We also investigate the relationship between Jacobi sections and Jacobi fields through the anchor map. We prove that every Jacobi section projects to a Jacobi field, and establish a converse when the corresponding base variation is contained in a single leaf of the characteristic foliation.
Iterative Interference Cancellation for Near-Field XL-MIMO Networks with LoS Channels
Nayyab Haider; Rodrigo C. de Lamare

In extra-large multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) systems, near-field users experience spherical wavefront propagation, offering higher spatial resolution than far-field plane-wave models, but complicating signal detection and interference cancellation. Under line-of-sight conditions, we propose a weighted-rate successive interference cancellation (WR-SIC) scheme whose ordering metric exploits the enhanced spatial degrees of freedom of near-field propagation to prioritize users with stronger channels. An iterative detection and decoding (IDD) scheme with LDPC coding is then developed. Simulations in hybrid near- and far-field deployments show that the proposed WR-SIC and IDD schemes improve bit-error and sum rates over existing schemes
Quadratic Bendixson criterion for delay systems: a numerical implementation

We present a software implementation (as a Python package) of approximation schemes for verifying frequency inequalities arising from the quadratic Bendixson criterion for systems of delay equations (with a single delay in the linear part). In applications to dissipative nonlinear autonomous systems, such inequalities ensure global stability. The theoretical foundations of this approach were developed in our related work. In particular, it was shown that the transfer operators involved into the frequency inequalities can be represented as integral operators with bounded kernels of the Hardy--Volterra type. Here, we use this representation to construct approximation schemes based on finite-dimensional truncations of the transfer operators. Examples of using the package are provided.
A constrained mixed variational formulation with Legendre-dual defects for incremental irreversible thermodynamics

We present a constrained mixed variational formulation for incremental irreversible thermodynamics. A single augmented action combines a linearized contact-increment penalty, equilibrium and dissipative Fenchel--Young defects, a storage--transport functional, and multipliers enforcing the constitutive increments. Under frozen-coefficient and boundary assumptions, stationarity yields the linearized contact condition, the Tisza relation, the Onsager flux--force law, and the implicit balance equation. An exact-elimination theorem shows that the contact and multiplier fields can be reconstructed algebraically from a solution of the reduced weak balance problem. We also prove off-shell invariance of the equilibrium--storage--multiplier sector under an equilibrium-sector partial Legendre transformation; invariance of the full augmented action is not claimed. For Fourier heat conduction, we derive a weighted drift identity and a per-step energy-drift bound for the energy-representation three-term incremental functional. In one spatial dimension, a small-time-step estimate yields a uniform $H^1$ bound and a discrete $L^2(0,T_f;H^2)$ bound, leading to cumulative $O(δt)$ drift over fixed time intervals. A conservative mixed discontinuous Galerkin (DG0)--Raviart--Thomas (RT0) discretization with fully implicit conductivity $κ(T)=1+T^2$ preserves discrete energy to roundoff. A separate lumped-mass piecewise-linear benchmark reproduces the predicted finite-step drift.
A Beltrami Mode in Extreme Fractional Hydrodynamics under Stochastic Forcing

We construct an exact stochastic solution of the extreme order endpoint of adaptive fractional Navier Stokes (AFNS) hydrodynamics on the three-dimensional periodic torus. A helical Beltrami eigenfield reduces the nonlinear vector equation to a scalar Ornstein Uhlenbeck process when the white-in-time forcing is aligned with that eigenfield. The resulting invariant Gaussian law yields explicit formulas for the stationary energy, its fluctuations, temporal correlations, circulation, and helicity. Under the same forcing, the corresponding classical Navier Stokes mode has a stationary energy that diverges as the Reynolds number tends to infinity, while the Euler limit exhibits linear growth of the mean energy and has no invariant probability law. The construction isolates, without a cascade hypothesis, the statistical effect of the finite fractional dissipation retained at the extreme endpoint of AFNS.
Neural Networks with Local Converging Inputs for Solving the 3D Stokes Equations on Unstructured Meshes: Novel Techniques and Advances
Farjana Siddiqua; Haoxiang Huang; Weiming Ding; Haotian Sun; Vigor Yang; Yingjie Liu

Neural-network surrogates for fluid-flow PDEs usually learn the solution globally, which requires large networks and many high-fidelity training simulations. Neural networks with local converging inputs (NNLCI) instead work locally. They predict the high-fidelity solution at a point from two converging coarse-grid solutions sampled near that point, which keeps the network small, needs little training data, and generalizes across geometries. Here, the two low-fidelity meshes, LF1 and LF2, have on average about 300 and 730 tetrahedra, compared with about 155,000 in the high-fidelity mesh (HF). In this work, we develop an NNLCI framework for three-dimensional Stokes equations on unstructured tetrahedral meshes and introduce two techniques for building local inputs near complex curved boundaries. First, input patches may extend beyond the boundary, with the outside values obtained from a local least-squares fit, so that every high-fidelity point can be predicted, including those next to the wall. Second, the local mesh spacing is estimated from neighboring centroids, which sets the stencil size consistently on unstructured meshes. For pipe flows with one to three bumps, including a circumferentially rotated bump, NNLCI reduces the relative $L^2$ error of the finer low-fidelity solution by $90\%$ to $94\%$, evaluated at all high-fidelity points. Both techniques carry over to other NNLCI problems with smooth solutions on point-cloud discretizations.
Monitoring One Channel Is Not Communication Control: Causal Evidence for Adaptive Reallocation of Joint Message--Route Codes

Monitoring a visible channel can change how learned agents communicate without removing why communication is useful. We test this distinction in an end-to-end game where a sender and receiver learn a discrete protocol and route policy without communication supervision. In two independent 20-seed batches, 20/20 and 19/20 protocols form. Online partial coverage increases shadow-route share over no monitoring by .701 [.574,.826] and .575 [.412,.737], while task accuracy remains .905/.913 and signed frozen message contribution remains .592/.563. Complete coverage removes most selective migration without removing communication. Frozen interventions, including a fresh pre-outcome confirmation, show that route is semantic: joint message--route shuffling changes .668 of receiver predictions and route alone retains .388 accuracy versus .25 chance. A corrected explicit-silence cost makes 18/20 policies fully silent and lowers mean sending to .050, but its strict complete-suppression gate fails because two seeds retain communication. Failed semantic-evasion and operational gates further bound the result. The evidence supports adaptive reallocation of a joint message--route code under partial monitoring, not open-world route discovery, emergent encryption, or a universal defense.
Reliability Analysis for Ground-Air Cooperative Wireless-Powered Internet-of-Things
Xingyu Huang; Zhican Zhong; Yulei Wang; Yalin Liu; Yongqiang Cui; Di Bai

Battery-constrained Internet of Things (IoT) devices face significant challenges in maintaining long-term uplink data collection, especially in network-limited scenarios. This paper investigates a Ground-Air cooperative Wireless-Powered IoT network (GA-WPIoT), where ground power beacons (GPBs) provide radio-frequency energy supply and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) serve as flexible aerial access points for IoT data collection. Unlike conventional UAV-enabled wireless-powered solutions, GA-WPIoT decouples energy transfer and data collection, reducing the hardware and energy burden of UAVs. To capture the device-level performance variations among IoT devices, we develop a stochastic geometry-based analytical framework, where UAVs are modeled by a Matérn hard-core point process, IoT devices by a Poisson point process, and GPBs by a finite annular binomial point process. The conditional success probabilities of the GPB-device link (for energy transfer) and the device-UAV link (for data collection) are characterized, and device-level reliability distributions are obtained through the Meta-Distribution based analysis. Numerical results under suburban and urban environments reveal the impacts of UAV altitude and annular GPB deployment on reliability distributions, providing useful guidelines for GA-WPIoT.
On the average eccentricity of Eulerian and bipartite Eulerian digraphs

Let $D$ be an Eulerian digraph of order $n$ and minimum degree $δ$. We prove that the average eccentricity of $D$ satisfies $\avec(D) \leq \frac{3n}{δ+1}$, and that $\avec(D) \leq \frac{2n}δ+2$ if $D$ is bipartite. We show that both bounds are best possible apart from an additive constant and the $δ+1$ versus $δ+2$ gap (resp.\ the $δ$ versus $δ+1$ gap in the bipartite case), where the average eccentricity of the extremal examples shows that $\avec = \frac{3n}{δ+2}-2$ in general and $\avec = \frac{2n}{δ+1}-\frac{5}{2}$ in the bipartite case for $δ\geq 2$. We further conjecture that these values are the true maxima up to an additive constant (for $δ\geq 3$ in the bipartite case).
Forward and pullback attraction under worst-case and ergodic exponents in a predator-prey model with bounded random refuge
Ever F. Cruzado-Quispe; Javier López-de-la-Cruz; Paulo N. Seminario-Huertas

We consider a predator-prey system with logistic prey, Holling type II response and a prey refuge fluctuating randomly within a band, driven by a bounded transformation of an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process. Bounded noise yields a deterministic compact set attracting forward uniformly in the realisation, alongside the random pullback attractor, and we compare the two. The smallest such deterministic set, the minimal uniform attracting set, is the kernel of the control system in which the accessible fraction is any measurable band-valued function, and it meets the coexistence region exactly when the upper worst-case invasion exponent of the predator is positive, whereas the pullback attractor is governed by the ergodic invasion exponent, which decides the predator's fate pathwise. When the predator becomes extinct, the closure of the union of the fibres of the pullback attractor equals the minimal uniform attracting set if and only if the upper worst-case exponent is nonpositive, and otherwise the inclusion is strict and the latter is invariant under no realisation. When the predator persists, the essential closure of the union of the fibres contains, for every frozen environment in which the predator invades, the equilibrium or a periodic orbit of the frozen system, and every state the control system can reach from them. The predator is uniformly persistent when the lower worst-case exponent is positive and almost surely not when it is negative. The ergodic exponent lies below its deterministic counterpart by an amount comparable to the curvature of the response times the variance of the accessible fraction.
César Ismael Corral Rojas; Vinicius de Oliveira Rodrigues; Victor dos Santos Ronchim

We determine the least cardinality of a set of reals that is not a weak $λ$-set, proving that it is $\max\{\mathfrak b,\mathfrak s\}$, where $\mathfrak b$ and $\mathfrak s$ are the bounding and splitting numbers. We prove that if $\mathfrak s<\mathfrak b$, then every first countable weak $λ$-space is a $λ$-space. We also show, relative to the consistency of $\mathsf{ZFC}$, that the existence of a weak $λ$-set that is not a $λ$-set is independent of $\mathsf{ZFC}+\mathfrak b=\mathfrak s$. In particular, we show that in the model obtained by adding $ω_2$ Cohen reals over a model of $\mathsf{CH}$, every weak $λ$-set is a $λ$-set. Finally, we construct an almost-normal MAD family under $\mathsf{CH}$ and show that no such family exists under $\mathsf{OCA}_{\mathrm T}+\mathfrak{ap}>ω_1$. Thus, the existence of an almost-normal MAD family is independent of $\mathsf{ZFC}$.
A uniform lower bound for logarithmic Trudinger-Moser suprema in dimension $N\ge3$
José Francisco de Oliveira; João Marcos do Ó; Raoní Cabral Ponciano

Let $B$ be the unit ball of $\mathbb{R}^N$, $N\ge2$, and let $\mathrm{MT}_N(α_{N,β},β)$ denote the critical Trudinger-Moser supremum of Calanchi and Ruf for radial functions in the Sobolev space with logarithmic weight $(-\log|x|)^{β(N-1)}$, $0\leβ<1$. We prove that $\mathrm{MT}_N(α_{N,β},β)>(2N-\frac25)|B|$ for every $β\in[0,1)$ and $N\ge 3$. This lower bound is uniform in $β$ and lies strictly above the upper bound $|B|\big(1+e^{1+\frac12+\cdots+\frac1{N-1}}\big)$ for the concentration level obtained by Carleson-Chang for $β=0$ and, for $β>0$, by Roy for $N=2$ and by Roy and Nguyen for $N\ge 3$. As a consequence, we prove that $\mathrm{MT}_N(α_{N,β},β)$ is attained for every $β\in[0,1)$ and $N\ge3$, which was previously known only for $β>0$ small enough. For $N=2$, the existence of extremals for every $β\in [0, 1)$ was recently obtained by de Oliveira.
Cylinder spectral curve and 1-cut Matrix model

For a random matrix, with eigenvalues in a one-body potential $V(x)$ and a 2-body interaction $R(x,x')$, it is known that the resolvent converges in the large $N$ limit to an analytic function in the complex plane minus cuts, called the spectral curve. In the 1-cut case, a two-sheeted neighborhood of the cut is a cylinder with two simple ramification points. We describe these spectral curve data by boundary integral operators and generalized cycles. Vice-versa, given a 2-branchpoints spectral curve in a cylinder, there exists a formal random matrix model that corresponds to it. The goal of this article is to show the method to recover a formal random matrix model, with its potential and 2-body interaction, from the geometry of the spectral curve.
The stochastic phase field crystal equation with conservative space-time white noise: well-posedness, regularity and existence of a density

We study the phase field crystal equation $\partial_tu=Δ[(1+Δ)^2u+u^3-\varepsilon u]+σ\partial_x\dot W$ on $[0,π]$ with the boundary conditions $\partial_xu=\partial_x^3u=\partial_x^5u=0$ at $x=0,π$, perturbed by a conservative space-time white noise. This sixth order equation is the standard model for crystal growth at atomic length scales and diffusive time scales, and the conservative noise is the form of thermal fluctuations used in the physics literature. We prove that for every initial condition in $H^1$ there exists a unique global mild solution, continuous in space and time, which preserves the mean and whose supremum has finite moments of all orders. We determine its Hölder regularity: away from $t=0$, it is Hölder continuous in time with any exponent smaller than $1/4$, and $C^1$ in space with a spatial derivative which is Hölder continuous with any exponent smaller than $1/2$. Finally, using Malliavin calculus and a localization argument, we prove that for $σ\neq0$ the law of $u(t,x)$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure for every $t>0$ and every $x$. A specific feature of the model is a second neutral mode of the linear operator, besides the constant mode, which requires a separate treatment in the a priori estimates.
The Herzog--Schönheim Conjecture for Solvable Groups

The Herzog--Schönheim conjecture states that if a group is partitioned into finitely many, and at least two, cosets of subgroups, then two of these subgroups have the same index. We prove the conjecture for all solvable groups, finite or infinite. Sun's bound on unions of cosets, applied in a quotient, is combined with divisibility restrictions on local indices relative to the subgroup generated by the $p$-elements, where $p$ is the largest prime divisor of the order of a minimal counterexample. These restrictions are obtained by counting fixed points in a primitive solvable quotient. This suffices except at the prime $7$, where the counting bound narrowly fails and an additional overlap argument is needed. The proof has been formalized in Lean~4 with mathlib.
Frequency shifts: non-soficity, absence of specification and intrinsic ergodicity

For $p_c\in(0,1)$, the frequency shift $Σ(p_c)\subset\{0,1\}^{\N}$, introduced by Becker and Baraviera, is the closure of the shift orbits of the set of sequences in which a symbol $1$ is followed by $1$ exactly when the density of ones up to that position does not exceed $p_c$. We show that $Σ(p_c)$ is never sofic and never has the (weak) specification property. For $p_c=\frac{k}{k+1}$, with $k\ge1$, we describe $Σ(p_c)$ completely: $Σ(\frac12)$ is the coded system generated by $\{0^m1^m\}_{m\ge1}$, while for $k\ge2$ the shift $Σ(\frac{k}{k+1})$ is not transitive, but every invariant probability measure is supported on the coded system generated by $\{0^m1^{km}\}_{m\ge1}$. For every $k \ge 1$, the topological entropy of $Σ(\frac{k}{k+1})$ is $\frac{\log2}{k+1}$, and, using the Climenhaga--Thompson criterion, we prove that $Σ(\frac{k}{k+1})$ is intrinsically ergodic.
The random matrix hard edge --- applications, exact PDFs and large $N$ expansions
Peter J. Forrester; Anas A. Rahman; Bo-Jian Shen

A hard edge of a Hermitian random matrix occurs when the eigenvalue density is strictly zero on one side of the edge, and nonzero on the other. Another possibility is that the eigenvalues occur in $\pm$ pairs, which creates a hard edge at the origin for the positive eigenvalues. Both review material and new results are presented for random matrix ensembles exhibiting a hard edge. The review material has two focuses: one is on applications of the random matrix hard edge, while the other is on exact eigenvalue probability density functions. The new results relate to the large $N$ expansion of correlation functions and conditioned gap probability generating functions with hard edge scaling for the Jacobi ensemble. For all even $β$ we are able to show that these quantities admit expansions in inverse even powers of the variable $N_{\rm hJ}':= N - 1/2 + (a + b + 1)/β$. For the $β=2$ Jacobi unitary ensemble, we can relate the leading (next leading) correction to the limit law to a particular second order (fourth order) differential operator applied to the latter. The analogous second order differential operator is found for $β=1,4$, leading then to its conjectured form for all $β>0$.
Higher-order Sobolev stability and temporal decay estimate for the tropical climate model with small $H^1$ data
Hyunjin In; Dong-ha Kim; Junha Kim

We study the stability and temporal decay of solutions to the two-dimensional tropical climate model with Laplacian dissipation in both velocity equations and no thermal diffusion. For initial data in $H^s (\mathbb{R}^2)$ ($s \geq 1$) with sufficiently small $H^1$ norm, we establish a unique global solution satisfying uniform $H^s$ bounds and time-integrated estimates for the velocity and temperature. The smallness is independent of $s$, and the higher Sobolev norms of the initial data need not be small. Furthermore, without additional spatial integrability or negative-order regularity of the initial data, we prove that the $\dot H^s (\mathbb{R}^2)$ norms of the solutions are $o(t^{- s / 2})$ as $t \to \infty$. We also show that this decay rate is sharp: no additional decay factor tending to zero works for all such initial data.
On the connected zero forcing polynomial of finite trees

Given a graph $Γ$ with vertex set $V(Γ)$ and a set of colored vertices S, the zero forcing rule is an iterative graph coloring process which states that a colored vertex with exactly one uncolored neighbor forces that neighbor to become colored. If repeated application of this rule eventually colors every vertex of $Γ$, the set $S$ is called a \emph{zero forcing set}. Now, if the induced subgraph $Γ\vert_S$ is connected, then $S$ is called a \textit{connected zero forcing set}. The minimum cardinality of such a set is the \emph{connected zero forcing number} $Z_C(Γ)$. A \emph{connected zero forcing polynomial} of a finite graph $Γ$ is a monic polynomial $Z_C^Γ(x) \;=\; \sum_{k} a_k x^k$, where $a_k$ counts the number of connected zero forcing sets of $Γ$ of size $k$, which we denote by $Z_C(Γ,k)$. In this paper, we find the connected zero forcing polynomial of any finite tree $T$. We then establish sharp lower bounds for each coefficient of the connected zero forcing polynomial, over all trees on $n$ vertices with $p$ many pendant vertices. We also identify a family of trees, which we call uniform trees, and we prove that for any tree on $n$ vertices and $p$ many pendant vertices, there exists a uniform tree on $n$ vertices and $p$ many pendant vertices, whose connected zero forcing polynomial bounds as an upper bound, the connected zero forcing polynomial of the tree coefficient wise. Again for $2\leq p\leq 4$, we establish a sharp upper bound for each coefficient of the connected zero forcing polynomial, over all trees on $n$ vertices with $p$ many pendant vertices.
Holomorphic Isometric Embeddings of the Unit Disk into the Symmetrized Bidisk

We give a complete characterization of the holomorphic isometric embeddings $F:(\mathbb{D},k\,ds^2)\rightarrow (\mathbb{G}_2,ds^2)$ of the unit disk into the symmetrized bidisk with respect to the Bergman metric up to a scalar constant. We show that the isometric constant $k$ can take only the values $k=1$ and $k=3$. For $k=3$, we prove that $(2z,z^2)$ is the unique isometry up to a reparametrization. For $k=1$, we construct an isometric embedding which intersects the royal variety at a single point and does not admit a holomorphic lift to the bidisk via the symmetrization map. We further show that this isometric embedding is unique up to reparametrizations. Finally, none of the isometries are totally geodesic.
Unramified case of Colliot-Thélène conjecture on quadratic forms

The Colliot-Thélène conjecture on quadratic forms asserts that any rationally isotropic nondegenerate quadratic form over a semilocal regular domain with $2$ invertible is isotropic. We prove the Colliot-Thélène conjecture for semilocal regular domains that are geometrically regular over a discrete valuation ring with $2$ invertible. In particular, this includes unramified regular local rings of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$, where $p\neq 2$.

We give a uniform second-order Taylor formula for tensorial Riemannian $H$-structures in Riemannian normal coordinates whose initial frame is $H$-adapted. For a defining multi-tensor $ξ$ with intrinsic torsion $T$, the linear coefficient is $T_q\diamondξ$, and the quadratic coefficient features the covariant derivative of $T$, its iterated diamond action, and curvature. The formula applies componentwise to tensors of arbitrary type and recovers the known $G_2$ and $\operatorname{Spin}(7)$ expansions. We also give the almost Hermitian specialisation and prove that vanishing of the complete second-order torsion contribution forces the intrinsic torsion to vanish at the centre of the coordinates.
DMP-Oriented Anisotropic Mesh Adaptation for SUPG Finite Element Methods for Time-Dependent Convection-Diffusion Problems

We study discrete bound preservation for fully discrete piecewise-linear streamline upwind Petrov--Galerkin (SUPG) finite element approximations of time-dependent convection--diffusion equations on anisotropic triangular meshes. Although the continuous homogeneous-source problem satisfies a parabolic maximum principle, SUPG approximations can exhibit nonphysical undershoots and overshoots. We derive sufficient nodal discrete maximum principle (DMP) conditions that account for the stabilized mass matrix, the combined effects of physical and streamline diffusion, time-step restrictions, and transfer between successive meshes. The analysis identifies a SUPG-effective diffusion tensor and motivates an anisotropic metric aligned with its inverse. We construct a combined metric that retains the effective-tensor geometry while introducing solution-dependent mesh density through recovered Hessian information. The resulting DMP conditions provide a theoretical basis for anisotropic mesh design. Numerical experiments for time-dependent transport problems with isotropic and moderately anisotropic diffusion demonstrate that, under mass-compatible limited SUPG stabilization, the combined metric substantially reduces measured undershoots relative to other methods at matched nominal mesh budgets, although improved bound behavior can carry an accuracy penalty. A controlled tensor--density comparison in the anisotropic transport test supports a contribution from the effective tensor beyond the prescribed mesh density.
Improving Analytic Constants via Interpretable AI-Guided Lean Proof Refinement
Rahul Saha; Alan Li; Anton Xue; Swarat Chaudhuri; Adam Klivans; Pravesh K. Kothari; Raghu Meka

AI agents are increasingly capable of discovering new mathematical results, yet their reasoning and generated proofs can be difficult to understand and verify. We introduce an interpretable framework for AI-guided mathematical discovery, focused on improving quantitative bounds on analytic constants. Our key insight is that existing proofs often contain slack in intermediate lemmas, which can be tightened without reconstructing the entire argument. To exploit this structure, we represent proofs as partially-formalized Lean blueprints: human-interpretable dependency graphs of definitions, lemmas, and theorems. An AI agent then iteratively refines the Lean code while preserving the blueprint's dependency structure, allowing local improvements to automatically propagate to a verified final bound. This interpretable structure allows humans to inspect the agent's refinements and understand how local improvements propagate to the final theorem. For Grothendieck's constant ($\mathcal{K}_G$), we obtain $$ \mathcal{K}_G \leq \fracπ{2\log(1+\sqrt{2})} - 10^{-17}, $$ an explicit numerical improvement over Krivine's 1977 bound. For Korenblum's constant ($\mathcal{K}_K$), we obtain $$ \mathcal{K}_K \geq 0.356565, $$ improving Wang's 2025 bound of $0.3554$. Our experiments demonstrate the potential of both partial formalization and iterative agentic refinement for interpretable mathematical discovery.
A Unified Framework for Robust Blinded Sample Size Re-estimation Based on Nuisance Parameters
Long-Hao Xu; Lei Li; Tim Friede

Blinded sample size re-estimation aims to mitigate uncertainty in nuisance parameters at the design stage while preserving the integrity of the trial. It allows the required sample size to be updated without revealing treatment assignments and thereby reduces the risk of an inappropriate sample size. Although numerous procedures have been proposed for different outcome types, a unified framework is still lacking. We therefore develop a general framework for blinded sample size re-estimation based on nuisance parameters. Within this general framework, we develop robust methods to reduce the influence of extreme observations. The proposed framework combines asymptotically linear estimators for the parameter of interest with robust Z-estimators for nuisance parameters, thereby unifying a broad class of existing procedures through different choices of estimating functions. We also propose a general principle for constructing nuisance parameters that can be estimated from blinded data. The proposed framework is supported by asymptotic theory showing that the type I error rate converges to the nominal level under regularity conditions. Simulation studies demonstrate that the proposed method maintains reliable type I error control across a range of settings, including contaminated data and small pilot sample sizes. Compared with existing blinded and unblinded methods, the proposed framework is more flexible and less sensitive to outliers. A clinical trial application illustrates its practical utility.
Dominant permutations, positive mixed-variable formulas, and product-splitting equivalence for (double) Schubert polynomials

We present new positive combinatorial formulas for triple Schubert coefficients in mixed-variable products of double Schubert polynomials, $\mathfrak{S}_u(x;y)\mathfrak{S}_v(x;z)$, expressed in the $\mathfrak{S}_w(x;y)$ basis, in the case where $u$ is dominant. This result complements earlier results where $v$ was assumed dominant. To generalize further, we introduce a relation on permutations that we call ``domination,'' under which dominant permutations dominate all others. When $u$ dominates $w$, we obtain an explicit positive formula for $c^w_{u,v}(y;z)$, which in particular yields positivity when $u$ and $v$ have separated descents. In addition to these new positivity results, we establish a product--splitting equivalence for double Schubert polynomials, relating triple Schubert coefficients to splitting coefficients. This equivalence highlights structural symmetries and provides reduction methods for computing coefficients that are otherwise difficult to access. Taken together, these results extend the range of double Schubert polynomial products for which positivity can be established combinatorially and yield explicit formulas that can be implemented computationally.
Optimal Sampling and Transmission Policy for Information Freshness in Gossip Networks

We study the optimal sampling and transmission policies for a transmitter communicating with n gossiping receivers with the objective of tracking a source's status over time using a semantic freshness metric: Version Age of Information (VAoI). The transmitter observes the version changes in the source, and can acquire a new information version by paying a sampling cost. The receivers gossip, allowing information exchange among each other without direct transmission. Gossiping can save on transmission cost, but it may propagate stale version information, necessitating transmitter intervention. With imperfect communication links, we formulate an infinite horizon average cost Markov Decision Process (MDP) in order to jointly optimize receivers' VAoIs, sampling and transmission costs in a time slotted fully connected (FC) gossip network. We first solve the MDP using Relative Value Iteration (RVI) algorithm. Then, we prove that the sampling decision has a threshold structure in the transmitter VAoI. Further, under reliable gossiping links, we show that transmission and idling has an VAoI-difference threshold structure with minimum VAoI activation. Numerical results obtained using RVI show that the optimal policy consistently outperforms natural baselines. These results characterize how source sampling, direct transmission, and receiver gossip should be jointly coordinated for cost-aware semantic freshness in gossip networks.
Spectral gaps and mixing rates of primitive matrices

We obtain lower bounds on spectral gap/upper bounds for mixing rate for arbitrary $n$-state (not necessarily reversible) primitive Markov chains which have exponent $-O(n)$ rather than $-O(n^2)$, a significant improvement on the order obtained from classical arguments. Our improvements come from using the irreducibility distance and chainable index (which are at most linear in $n$) rather than the primitivity index (which can be near $n^2$). This also yields corresponding bounds for arbitrary nonnegative primitive matrices.
An Introduction to Applied Probability and Stochastic Processes: Open Lecture Notes

These open lecture notes provide a broad introduction to measure-theoretic probability and stochastic processes, with a focus on applications. Topics include probability spaces, conditional expectation, generating and characteristic functions, Markov chains in discrete and continuous time, convergence of random variables, Brownian motion, stochastic calculus, stochastic differential equations and their connection to partial differential equations, jump diffusions, stochastic control, optimal stopping, and Monte Carlo methods. Most chapters include exercises, and solutions are provided. The notes were written for a two-quarter course for first-year PhD students in applied mathematics, and should also be useful to graduate students in statistics, engineering, economics and finance. The LaTeX source is freely available on GitHub under a CC BY-SA 4.0 license, and readers are encouraged to fork the notes and contribute corrections, improvements, and new material.
Can small transformers learn the language of Coxeter groups?
J. Elisenda Grigsby; Yiyao Huang; Arushi Katyal; Ryan Lin; Pranav Ramakrishnan; Weiya Wang

The field of mechanistic interpretability is well-suited to collaborative projects between mathematicians and AI researchers. This work describes one such project. We trained a small transformer to learn the language of the Coxeter group affine A2, best known as the symmetries of the tiling of the Euclidean plane by equilateral triangles. We then formulated and proved a word-theoretic conjecture about affine A2 after observing the attention patterns of the trained model.
Compact metric spaces as exponentiable metric compact Hausdorff spaces

The class of compact metric spaces (metric spaces which induce a compact topology), despite being an important class of metric spaces, is not closed under many natural constructions. For instance, infinite metric products of compact metric spaces will often fail to induce a compact topology, while on the other hand, the topological product of any family of compact metric spaces is always a compact topological space, evidencing a discrepancy between topological and metric products. The notion of metric compact Hausdorff space -- compact Hausdorff spaces equipped with a lower semi-continuous metric -- provides a class of spaces which keep track of metric data and topological data separately, thereby forming a complete and cocomplete category, while including all compact metric spaces. Our main contribution is that this inclusion can be characterised via universal property: the compact metric spaces are the exponentiable metric compact Hausdorff spaces with respect to a natural monoidal structure on the respective category.
Absolute mod-two gradings on framed real monopole Floer homology

We construct absolute mod-two gradings on framed real monopole Floer homology, for real 3-manifolds such that the image of the fixed point set in the quotient is nullhomologous. This allows us to fix the sign of Miyazawa's degree invariant. Our construction uses a mod-two index-theoretic correction term, the Arf invariant.
Diophantine definitions of nonsplitting for central simple algebras over global fields

For every global field and every fixed degree, we prove that the structure constants defining nonsplit central simple algebras form a diophantine set. We formulate a local witness principle separating reliable localization, exact localization, and local detection. Adapted Kummer and Artin--Schreier presentations provide a common construction of witnesses through a uniform radical formula and ramification matching. This gives an independent proof of the non-characteristic case, which also follows from Morrison's nonnorm theorem, and treats the characteristic-degree case by the same method. We recover prime-degree nonnorm definability and give applications to rootless polynomials, anisotropic quadratic forms in all characteristics, and generalized Severi--Brauer varieties.
Sequential anomaly identification with sampling constraints for composite hypotheses
Aristomenis Tsopelakos; Georgios Fellouris; Olgica Milenkovic

We consider the problem of sequential anomaly identification with sampling constraints, where multiple independent data sources are observed over time, but only a limited subset can be sampled at each instant. The objective is to identify the anomalous sources while controlling the probabilities of at least one false alarm and at least one missed detection below prescribed levels. An identification policy must jointly determine when to stop sampling, which sources to declare anomalous, and how to allocate observations across sources under the sampling constraints. We seek policies that minimize the expected time to decision to a first-order asymptotic approximation as the error probabilities vanish. The observations from each source follow an unknown density belonging to one of two disjoint sets, corresponding to regular and anomalous behavior. Focusing on a nonparametric framework, which allows greater flexibility in modeling regular and anomalous statistical behavior, we establish general conditions for asymptotic optimality and provide a unified characterization of asymptotically optimal policies for composite hypothesis testing under sampling constraints. Simulation results illustrate the performance of the proposed policies, and the robustness of the nonparametric framework.
Positivity Proofs for Third-Order Holonomic Sequences via Differences Scaled by Rational Functions

We study the positivity of sequences $f$ that satisfy a third-order holonomic recurrence $f(n+3)= P_2(n) f(n+2) + P_1(n) f(n+1) + P_0(n) f(n)$ whose coefficients $P_0$, $P_1$ and $P_2$ are rational functions in $\R(x)$. We provide a sufficient condition on $P_0$, $P_1$ and $P_2$ for the recurrence to admit a solution all but finitely many terms of which are positive, and whose positivity is robust under small perturbations of the initial values. This sufficient condition is also a necessary condition for a subclass of the recurrences. By developing the proof of this sufficient condition, for another subclass of the recurrences, we show that it is decidable whether all the terms of a given sequence are positive for any initial values outside an exceptional plane. It is common to construct a positivity certificate, which guarantees the positivity of a solution, to show this kind of decidability. In this paper, we construct a new type of positivity certificate via the $S$-scaled difference $f(n+1) - S(n) f(n)$ for a suitable $S \in \R(x)$. This result partially improves the work by Ibrahim and Salvy.
Vertex splitting, global rigidity and nondegenerate equilibrium stresses

We prove Whiteley's conjecture that every nontrivial vertex split of a generically globally rigid graph preserves generic global rigidity in \(\mathbb{R}^d\), for all \(d\geq1\). We give two proofs of the stronger assertion that the split graph is infinitesimally rigid at every generic coincident realisation of the two split vertices. Both proofs use maximum-rank equilibrium stress matrices and then apply the coincident-rigidity criterion of Cruickshank, Jackson and Tanigawa. The second construction also shows that every generically globally rigid graph admits a nondegenerate equilibrium stress of maximum rank at every generic realisation, establishing a conjecture of Jordán and Tanigawa.
On the Bendixson criterion for attractors of dynamical systems in metric spaces

We revisit the Bendixson criterion for attractors, originally proposed by R.A. Smith for the finite-dimensional case and subsequently extended by M.Y. Li and J.S. Muldowney to Banach spaces. First, we give a concise proof of the criterion for general dynamical systems (semiflows, mappings, cocycles) in metric spaces using Čech cohomology. This approach allows for a significant weakening of previously known conditions while simultaneously resolving existing misunderstandings. Second, for compact invariant sets of semiflows that are topologically one-dimensional and possess zero first cohomology (e.g., attracting a superset with zero first cohomology), we prove that any chain recurrent point within the invariant set must be an equilibrium. In the proof, we construct a global strict Lyapunov function using Whitney-Bebutov sections. Third, we generalize and refine R.A. Smith's theorem concerning the finiteness of the set of fixed points for analytic mappings, as well as M.L. Cartwright's theorems on to almost periodic flows.
An Optimal First-Order Active-Hull Method for Convex Composite Hölder Smooth Optimization

We consider the problem (P): ${\min}_{x\in \mathbb{R}^n}\, f(x)+g(x)$ under the Euclidean geometry, where $f$ is convex and $(M,ν)$-Hölder smooth on $\mathbb{R}^n$, and $g$ is proper, closed and convex on $\mathbb{R}^n$, admits a generalized linear minimization oracle (GLMO), and has bounded domain with diameter $D$. An first-order active-hull (AH) method has access to both the first-order oracle (FO) of $f$ and the GLMO of $g$, and outputs a point that lies in the convex hull of all the past GLMO returns. We propose a new first-order AH method for solving (P), which is based on our newly developed ``recentered homotopy smoothing framework''. We show that in the high-dimensional regime, this method achieves the optimal FO and GLMO complexties simultaneously for all $ν\in[0,1]$.
Quantum synchronizable codes, polynomial and quasi-polynomial shifts
Edgar Martínez-Moro; Miguel de los Ríos de Antonio

Quantum synchronizable codes protect quantum information against Pauli errors and against misalignments of the block boundaries. Almost all known constructions use cyclic codes, because the channel shifts the transmitted block cyclically. We study what happens when the algebraic shift of the code differs from the physical one. When one uses a twisted padding, constacyclic codes synchronize at no cost, and they are the only polycyclic codes with this property for a linear padding. For the other polycyclic codes, we measure the cost of each misaligned position, and we show that the phase damage it causes can be corrected as erasures. Using annihilator duality, we extend the construction to quasi-polycyclic codes, in which the cost is confined to a single block. We prove that the usual quasi-cyclic families have a distance bound that does not grow with the length, and show that quasi-polycyclic codes over repeated-root trinomials overcome it, giving synchronizable codes with larger dimension and distance than the known synchronizable codes of the same length.
Sharp Constants and Maximizers for Weighted Moser--Trudinger Inequalities on the Heisenberg Group
Somnath Kumar; Nguyen Lam; Deepak Kumar Mahanta; Abhishek Sarkar

This article concerns Moser-Trudinger inequalities on the entire Heisenberg group, focusing on sharp constants, maximizers, and applications to subelliptic PDEs. We address several questions on the existence of maximizers in the singular case $0<β<Q$, where the singular weight yields compactness. We first establish an Adimurthi-Druet-type weighted Moser-Trudinger inequality without blow-up analysis and determine its sharp constant. We also prove its equivalence with the critical weighted Moser-Trudinger inequality. For the subcritical inequality of Lam, Lu and Tang \cite{Lam-Lu-Tang-2014}, we obtain two-sided asymptotic bounds near the sharp threshold and prove existence of maximizers in a suitable regime. This inequality also yields insight into borderline Sobolev theory and an asymptotic Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg interpolation-type inequality. We further establish a weighted Moser-Trudinger inequality under inhomogeneous norm constraints and prove its equivalence with the subcritical inequality, thereby characterizing the associated supremum and its maximizers. An improved subcritical weighted inequality is also derived, and its maximization problem is shown to admit a maximizer. Finally, these inequalities are applied to normalized subelliptic equations driven by the $Q$-sub-Laplacian with nonlinearities having singular critical exponential growth at infinity. We prove the existence of nontrivial ground states for every prescribed mass $a>0$, provided the nonlinearity is sufficiently large in a suitable sense depending on $a$.
New lower bounds for even and odd values of the partition function

Let $N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X)$ and $N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)$ denote the numbers of integers $0\leq n< X$ for which the ordinary partition function $p(n)$ is odd and even, respectively. The Parkin--Shanks conjecture predicts that $N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X)$ and $N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)$ are both asymptotic to $X/2$. Bellaïche and Nicolas proved that $N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)\gg \sqrt{X} \log \log X$, while Zheng, building on work of Ono and Swaminathan, recently proved that $N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X)\gg \sqrt{X}$. We improve both bounds simultaneously by proving $\min\{N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X), N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)\}\gg X^{3/4}/(\log X \log \log X)$.
Optimal Byzantine-resilient Federated Learning with User-level Differential Privacy
Ming Xiang; Stratis Ioannidis; Edmund Yeh; Carlee Joe-Wong; Lili Su

Real-world deployment of federated learning (FL) requires resilience against adversarial clients and data privacy. Byzantine fault captures the worst-case behavior of adversarial clients, while differential privacy (DP) provides statistical guarantees against privacy loss. In particular, user-level DP guards a client's entire contribution and provides more realistic protection against information leakage. Despite intensive efforts, the minimax-optimal convergence bound of Byzantine-resilient FL with user-level DP remains open. We establish an information-theoretic lower bound for any Byzantine-resilient empirical risk minimization problem under user-level DP and heterogeneous clients. We propose ByzULDP, a central DP algorithm featuring a two-level momentum across the client and server. Client-side momentum mitigates stochastic gradient variance during robust aggregation. Unlike the fault-free case, naively combining non-linear Byzantine-resilient aggregation with central DP noise can be insufficient to guarantee convergence to a bounded neighborhood of a stationary point. Our key contribution is a server-side momentum that leverages a property specific to user-level DP, where privacy sensitivity depends on how client updates are constructed, to empower convergence. ByzULDP achieves the order-optimal convergence bound for strongly-convex objectives, with vanishing error terms decaying at the optimal $O(1/T)$ and $O(1/\sqrt{T})$ rates for strongly-convex and non-convex objectives, respectively. We corroborate our analysis with numerical experiments on real-world datasets across diverse privacy budgets.
Hypervolume-based column-and-constraint generation for bi-objective two-stage robust mixed-integer programs

Extending column-and-constraint generation (C&CG) for two-stage robust mixed-integer programs from the single-objective to the bi-objective setting is challenging: for a fixed first-stage decision and scenario, the second stage yields an entire nondominated set rather than a single objective value. We develop a C&CG algorithm that uses the hypervolume indicator - one of the most widely studied quality indicators in multi-objective optimization - to evaluate these sets and seeks a first-stage decision maximizing the worst-case hypervolume over a finite set of scenarios. To avoid the nonlinearities of an exact hypervolume formulation, we introduce a slab decomposition of the objective space that yields a linear mixed-integer master problem with an explicit bound on the discretization error. This bound enables a computable optimality-gap certificate and supports an adaptive algorithm that alternates between adding scenarios and refining the decomposition. We prove the correctness of the algorithm and establish sufficient conditions for its finite termination. Computational experiments on two-stage robust selection and assignment problems show that only a small number of scenarios need to be included in the master problem, even when the full scenario set contains 128 scenarios. Moreover, we identify the number of initial slabs as a key factor influencing the running time and develop a simple, instance-dependent rule for choosing the initial slab width that outperforms fixed choices on average for the selection problem and remains competitive for the assignment problem.
Admissible geometries for Talenti's Pólya--Szegő principle

Talenti symmetrization rearranges functions on an open connected set $X\subset\mathbb{R}^N$, endowed with a measure $μ$ with continuous positive density, along the superlevel sets of a given function $f$. Talenti proved a Pólya--Szegő principle for it, provided that these sets are $μ$-isoperimetric, have connected boundaries, and are crossed by straight lines of steepest ascent. We show that, if $X$ is convex, these requirements are very rigid: they force the superlevel sets of $f$ to be either parallel half-spaces, or concentric balls, or complements of tubes around an affine subspace of codimension at least two. This identifies the only geometries in which Talenti's Pólya--Szegő principle can be applied. We also prove a family of weighted isoperimetric inequalities in convex cones, showing that complements of tubes around affine subspaces of every codimension at least two do occur.
Periodic Readout Induces a First-Order Generalization Transition in a Quantum Perceptron
Fabio Benatti; Masoud Gharahi; Giovanni Gramegna; Stefano Mancini; Vincenzo Parisi

Variational quantum classifiers can generate highly structured decision boundaries through the Fourier dependence of observable expectation values on circuit parameters. We show that expressivity can come at a sharp statistical cost, by considering a quantum perceptron whose readout is the simplest periodic classifier, namely a square-wave function of the weighted inputs, and determine its typical generalization in the thermodynamic limit using a teacher-student replica-symmetric theory. Above a critical oscillation frequency, increasing the training load induces a first-order transition from weakly to strongly teacher-aligned phases, resulting in a discontinuous improvement in generalization. At fixed load, however, increasing the frequency eventually drives the equilibrium generalization error to chance level, despite perfect classification of all the training examples. Thus, the same periodic structure that enhances random-label storage can delay the onset of learning. Our results expose a quantitative tradeoff between memorization and generalization generated purely by periodic readout, and provide a benchmark for understanding Fourier-rich variational quantum classifiers.

We prove a generation theorem for the homology of certain Koszul complexes which naturally arise as the $E^1$ pages of the stable Rasmussen spectral sequence of torus links. Combining this theorem with recent work of Ballinger, Gorsky, Hogancamp, and Wang, we compute the stable Khovanov-Rozansky $\mathfrak{gl}_N$ homology of torus links and determine its Poincaré series, resolving conjectures of Gorsky, Oblomkov, and Rasmussen and their $\mathfrak{gl}_N$ analogs, over $\mathbb{Q}$. Using these results, we determine the Khovanov homology of $T(n,n-1)$ and $T(n,n)$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, confirming conjectures of Shumakovitch and Turner and of the first author, which in turn allows us to compute the Khovanov skein lasagna module of $\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$ over $\mathbb{Q}$.
The Brualdi--Quinn conjecture on strong edge-coloring holds fractionally and asymptotically
Rong Luo; Gexin Yu; Xiangqian Zhou

Let $G$ be a bipartite graph with parts $A$ and $B$, and let $Δ_A$ and $Δ_B$ be the maximum degrees of the vertices in $A$ and in $B$, respectively. Brualdi and Quinn conjectured that the strong chromatic index of $G$ is at most $Δ_AΔ_B$. We prove that the fractional strong chromatic index of $G$ is at most $Δ_AΔ_B$, and that the conjecture holds asymptotically: $χ_s'(G)\le(1+o(1))Δ_AΔ_B$ as $\max\{Δ_A,Δ_B\}\to\infty$. The error term is $12(\lnΔ)^{1/2}Δ^{-1/4}$ with $Δ=\max\{Δ_A,Δ_B\}$. Both results rest on a smart partition of edges and Lovász Local Lemma.
A note on Positivity and Rigidity for an Expanding Quasi-Local Energy

We study positivity and rigidity for an expanding quasi-local energy $E_λ$ associated with constantly umbilic initial data $(Ω,g,k=λg)$, introduced in earlier work [ALP26] as an analogue of the Brown-York energy adapted to an expanding flat de Sitter background. Under nonnegative scalar curvature and suitable boundary assumptions, our previous results established positivity for $λ$ below a geometrically determined threshold $α$, while vanishing $E_λ$ at $λ=α$ forced the boundary to be round. In this paper, we strengthen this endpoint rigidity statement by showing that, if $E_λ=0$ when $λ=α$, then $(Ω,g)$ is isometric to a closed Euclidean 3-ball of radius at most $1/λ$. The proof combines the rigidity theorem of Shi-Tam for the Brown-York energy with a strict concavity argument. We also construct an explicit counterexample to the positivity and rigidity conjecture formulated in [ALP26], showing that the energy can become negative beyond this threshold and that vanishing energy need not imply rigidity.
The moduli stack of affine bundles with fixed linearisation type

The goal of this article is the classification of affine bundles with fixed linearisation type over a compact complex manifold $X$. More precisely, let $E$ be a fixed holomorphic vector bundle over $X$ and $\mathcal{E}$ the associated locally free sheaf. We will assume that there exists an effective divisor $D$ on $X$ such that $H^1(X,\mathcal{E}(D))=0$. This condition is always satisfied when $X$ is a projective complex manifold. We define in a natural way the moduli stack of affine bundles on $X$ whose linearisation is isomorphic to $E$, and we prove that this moduli stack is isomorphic to the quotient stack $\big[H^0(X,\mathcal{E}(D)_D)/H^0(X,\mathcal{E}(D))\ltimes \mathrm{Aut}(E)\big]$ of the complex vector space $H^0(X,\mathcal{E}(D)_D)$ by the semi-direct product of the automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(E)$ (which is always an affine algebraic group) by the complex vector space $H^0(X,{\cal E}(D))$. Our isomorphism is obtained by constructing explicitly comparison functors $\mathscr{A}$, $\mathscr{T}$ between the two stacks and explicit natural isomorphisms $\mathscr{A}\circ\mathscr{T}\stackrel{\simeq}{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{id}$, $\mathrm{id} \stackrel{\simeq}{\longrightarrow}\mathscr{T}\circ\mathscr{A}$.
Martingale representations without finite or well-defined mean
Benjamin Côté; Lilian Hu; Ruodu Wang

The classical Strassen theorem characterizes convex order through martingale representations under the assumption of finite first moments. We show that a natural reformulation of the theorem remains true on the real line for distributions without finite or even well-defined means. We further investigate the higher-dimensional setting, where this equivalence fails in general. Martingale representations are nonetheless guaranteed in higher dimensions when every nonzero linear projection of the second marginal has undefined mean.
Superlinear problems related to Fully Non Linear singular or degenerate operators in punctured balls

We study Fully Nonlinear uniformly elliptic equations with a higher differential term degenerate or singular, coupled with a zero order term singular at the point $0$, and an absorbing super-linear term of $p$ power type. We will limitate to punctured balls and positive radial solutions. In the continuity of two previous works in \cite {BDL1}, \cite{BDL2}, we will provide a complete classification depending on $p$ of the asymptotic behaviour of the solutions near the singular point $0$.
Online Imitation Learning for Stabilizing Vlasov--Poisson Plasmas
Xiaofan Xia; Qin Li; Wenlong Mou

We study the problem of controlling instability in the Vlasov--Poisson plasma systems, a fundamental challenge for nuclear fusion control. Motivated by the partial observability of plasma states in practice, we investigate imitation learning algorithms that learn from a fully-observable expert controller, but operate under macroscopic measurements. We theoretically establish a separation between online and offline imitation learning --- even a small behavior cloning error leads to error compounding that exponentially amplifies instability over time. By way of contrast, the online imitation learning loss can polynomially control the stability of rollout trajectories. We then propose a DAgger-style algorithm that learns the stabilizing controller under partial observability. Simulation results on a 1D Vlasov--Poisson system demonstrate that our algorithm can effectively stabilize plasma instabilities over longer time horizons than behavior cloning.
Neural Operator Surrogates for Landweber Iteration in Solving Inverse Problems
Kuo Gai; Marco A Iglesias; Shuai Lu; Frank Werner

Neural operators can accurately approximate well-posed mappings, but for unbounded or discontinuous operators, common in inverse problems, we verify that their network parameters often blow up in architectures such as DeepONet and FNO. To solve inverse problems stably, we use Landweber iteration, which requires only a forward map and the adjoint of its derivative (linearisation). To reduce repeated PDE forward evaluations, we replace the forward operator and its derivative with a differentiable neural-operator surrogate. We show that encoder-network-decoder operators, including generalised DeepONets and fully coupled Fourier operators, approximate both the forward map and its derivative. A modified discrepancy principle ensures decreasing error before finite stopping. With a compact preconditioner, the iterates remain in a compact set where accurate surrogates exist, and the stopped reconstructions converge as data and surrogate errors vanish under a regularity condition. We also relate the theory to derivative-informed training along finite directions, showing that the preconditioner determines which derivative errors affect the Landweber iteration update. Experiments on identifying a reaction coefficient in an elliptic equation show that smoothing reduces late-iteration deterioration for less accurate surrogates but slows sharp-feature recovery, and that smaller derivative errors along training directions do not by themselves improve reconstruction accuracy.
Spectral distribution for biased orientations of random graphs

We study the Hermitian adjacency matrix of the second kind for biased orientations of Erdos-Renyi random graphs. In the model $D(n,p,p')$, an edge is present with probability $p$ and, conditional on its presence, is directed from its smaller to its larger endpoint with probability $p'$. Both parameters may depend on $n$, and biased tournaments are the special case $D(n,1,p')$. We prove a global semicircle law whenever $n(p(1-p)+3p^2p'(1-p')) \to \infty$, for both the centered and the uncentered matrix, and also for the expected empirical spectral measure. Our second theorem gives the exact spectrum of the mean matrix and the limits of the extreme eigenvalues on the scale $np$, under a sufficient density assumption. The main difference from the unbiased random orientations (where $p'=1/2$) is emergence of multiple large eigenvalues. The proofs include the closed-walk counting, control of the moment variances, an explicit diagonalization of the deterministic bias, and the passage from centered to uncentered spectral measures.
Eaton Triples, Polar Representations, and Lie Triple Systems

An Eaton triple consists of a finite dimensional real inner product space, a closed subgroup of its orthogonal group, and a closed convex cone that meets every orbit and satisfies an extremal inner product inequality. In the literature on group majorization and invariant norms it is a standing hypothesis that the triple admits a reduced triple, obtained by restriction to the span of the cone. We prove that this is always the case: the axioms force the span of the cone to be a section of a polar representation, and Gichev's orbit intersection theorem applies. The reduced group is a finite reflection group, crystallographic when the group is connected; Eaton cones are its closed chambers, unique up to the group action; and a compact linear group admits an Eaton cone if and only if its representation is polar with a finite reflection group as Weyl group. For connected groups we construct a Lie triple system on the space, determined by the inner product and the orbits alone, for which the cone is a Weyl chamber; unlike Dadok's orbit equivalence with a symmetric space, it involves no choices.

Given a compact Lie group acting smoothly and freely on a compact connected manifold, we prove that the space of invariant Riemannian metrics whose symmetry group is precisely the group in question is open dense in that of all invariant metrics provided the orbit space is sufficiently large. This strengthens the author's prior results and recovers Ebin's to the effect that trivial-symmetry Riemannian metrics constitute an open dense set. In the process, the discussion also addresses a number of apparent gaps in said sources, pertaining to the rigidity results in question.
A novel Non-Homogeneous Local Representation of the Braid Group

We construct a non-homogeneous local representation of the braid group $B_n$ by tracking the labels of individual strands through successive crossings. Each generator acts through a $2\times2$ block whose position is determined by the crossing and whose coefficients depend on the ordered labels of the participating strands. Starting with the ansatz \[ M_{xy}=\begin{pmatrix}a_x&a_y\\ b_{xy}&c_{xy}\end{pmatrix}, \] for $n\geq3$, the cubic braid relations for arbitrary ordered triples of strands determine $c_{xy}=0$ and $b_{xy}=(1-a_x)/a_x$ in the nondegenerate branch. The moving-label rule leads to an explicit semidirect-product representation, for which we prove the Artin relations and use exact evaluations of the resulting symbolic matrices. In the special homogeneous specialization, where $a_x=a$ for every strand label $x$, the resulting matrix representation is diagonally equivalent to unreduced Burau. We prove that a non-homogeneous specialization of our representation detects Bigelow's explicit nontrivial $B_5$ Burau-kernel commutator. Thus the strand-dependent coefficients distinguish a nontrivial braid that is invisible to the classical Burau representation. This separation provides evidence that the non-homogeneous strand-tracking construction is a promising candidate for a faithful Burau-type representation.
A silting theorem for extended module categories

We generalize the silting theorem of Buan and Zhou to extended module categories. For a $(d+1)$-term silting object $\mathbf{P}$ over a proper $d$-truncated non-positive dg algebra $A$, we construct a $(d+1)$-term silting object $\mathbf{Q}$ over the $d$-truncated dg endomorphism algebra $B$ of $\mathbf{P}$. The $s$-torsion pairs induced by $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{Q}$ yield equivalences of Brenner-Butler type between the torsion class on either side and the torsion-free class on the other. There is also a dg algebra homomorphism from $A$ to the $d$-truncated dg endomorphism algebra of $\mathbf{Q}$, which is a quasi-isomorphism if and only if $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf{P},\mathbf{P}[i])=0$ for all $i\leq-d$. Moreover, we describe Auslander-Reiten theory in ${d\text{-}\operatorname{mod}\!B}$ in terms of that in ${d\text{-}\operatorname{mod}\!A}$.
Efficient SC-Flip Decoding for Polar Codes through Decision-Boundary Normalization
Gulinisha Yiming; Zhongjun Yang; Zhicheng Liu; Zhiming Ma; Xumin Ni; Yuting Liu

Accurate first erroneous position (FEP) identification is key to improving the error-correction performance of successive cancellation flip (SCF) decoding. However, FEP identification remains challenging with a limited number of re-decoding attempts. To address this issue, we propose decision-boundary normalization (DBN) to improve FEP identification and develop a novel DBN-SCF decoding algorithm. DBN normalizes the magnitude of each decision log-likelihood ratio (LLR) by the standard deviation predicted by the Gaussian approximation (GA) for the corresponding bit-channel. This allows a single normalized threshold to be shared across bit-channels within each code configuration, giving it a consistent statistical meaning and avoiding per-channel calibration. DBN-SCF decoding selects candidate flip positions from the information set in the natural successive cancellation (SC) decoding order using a threshold, without sorting. Moreover, DBN-SCF decoding achieves better error-correction performance with a limited number of re-decoding attempts. It also requires lower average decoding complexity than existing SCF decoding methods at a comparable level of error-correction performance.
A high-order structure-preserving ALE--SAV finite element method for moving contact line flows

We develop a structure-preserving arbitrary Lagrangian--Eulerian (ALE) finite element method for incompressible Navier--Stokes flow with gravity and moving contact lines, based on a scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) reformulation. The reformulation expresses the geometric energy quadratically in the auxiliary variable and permits linear treatment of the capillary, wetting and gravitational forces. The method combines high-order isoparametric elements in space with a linearly implicit, second-order Crank--Nicolson discretization in time. Second-order extrapolation supplies the predicted geometry and known coefficients of the linear fluid--SAV system. Mesh motion changes the kinetic-energy inner product and requires a compatible discretization of the time-derivative terms in the ALE formulation. We discretize these terms using an $L^2$-isometric velocity transfer to retain the kinetic-energy balance after the geometry update. We also construct a boundary update that preserves area or volume exactly using only linear solves. The resulting scheme satisfies a discrete SAV energy-dissipation law and preserves area or volume exactly. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions demonstrate high-order spatial and second-order temporal convergence and confirm SAV energy dissipation and area or volume conservation.
Quantum channel bounds for constant-composition codes
Artur Akhiiarov; Peter Boyvalenkov; Danila Cherkashin; Andrei Raigorodskii

We extend the quantum-channel optimization of Alrabiah and Guruswami to $q$-ary constant-composition codes. We study explicit channel and flag constructions that recover selected classical asymptotic upper bounds, including the Ben-Haim--Litsyn, moving-subspace and Horn-channel bounds. We give two equivalent formulations, Gram and flag, and prove stability of the obtained upper bounds under permutation transport and generalized shortening. A hierarchy defined by bounding the output-state ranks within each flag improves strictly between consecutive levels at every composition and every positive distance below the Plotkin threshold. We provide finite matrix parametrizations of these bounds (i.e., the number of variables does not depend on the length of codes under consideration). Numerical optimization rapidly produces improvements over the known asymptotic upper bounds throughout all tested nonbinary parameter ranges. For rational input data, each finite level admits near-optimal feasible rational descriptions of polynomial length. Their feasibility can be checked exactly and their objective values computed to any prescribed accuracy in polynomial time; the associated threshold problem with a prescribed gap belongs to $\mathsf{PromiseNP}$.
Parallel domains in $SL_3(\mathbb{R})$ and the ideal triangle reflection group

For a given positive triple of flags, we associate an open set, called a parallel domain, in the symmetric space of $SL_3 (\mathbb{R})$ whose boundary is parametrized by three spacelike geodesics of the pseudo-Riemannian symmetric space $SL_3 (\mathbb{R})/GL_2 (\mathbb{R})$. This construction is a higher-rank analog of how three points in the ideal boundary of the hyperbolic plane have an associated ideal triangle. As an application, using the fact that positive triples determine a representation of the ideal triangle reflection group into $SL_3(\mathbb{R})$, we show that these parallel domains are fundamental domains for the group action in the symmetric space. Moreover, using the explicit construction and combinatorial properties of the Farey tessellation, we compute the asymptotics for the critical exponent in the symmetric space and the Hilbert critical exponent as the triple ratio of the triple of flags goes to infinity.
Propagation phenomena in spatial periodic bistable reaction-diffusion equations around an obstacle

This paper is concerned with propagation phenomena for a spatially periodic bistable reaction--diffusion equation around an obstacle. It is known that an entire solution emanating from a pulsating front converges to the same front as \(t\rightaroow+\infty\) under complete propagation and an additional technical assumption. We remove the technical assumption and prove that the entire solution coming from a pulsating front converges to the same pulsating front as \(t\rightarrow+\infty\) under the complete propagation.
An explicit basis for the unipotent Specht modules of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$

For each partition $λ$ of $n$ we construct an explicit basis of the unipotent Specht module $S^λ$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$, defined recursively over horizontal strips. Each basis vector is $g\,x_τ$, where $τ$ is a semistandard tableau of shape $λ$, $x_τ$ is obtained from a Steinberg-type vector by alternately applying a permutation matrix and a Fourier sum over a unitriangular group, and $g$ runs over an explicit set of coset representatives. Grouping the basis by the standardization of $τ$ gives exactly $q^{\mathrm{maj}(s^T)}$ vectors for each standard tableau $s$, which is the numerical form of the Dipper-James standard basis problem. The same family is a basis over every field containing a nontrivial $p$th root of unity, including fields whose characteristic divides $|\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)|$, and a subfamily chosen layer by layer gives a basis of the simple quotient $D^λ$. We also give a basis of the $U$-fixed vectors of $S^λ$ and computed values of $\dim D^λ$ for $\mathrm{GL}_n(2)$.
A Low-Rank Augmented Lagrangian Frank-Wolfe-Based Method for SDPs with Unbounded Feasible Regions
Jacob M. Aguirre; Renato D. C. Monteiro; Arnesh Sujanani

In contrast to HALLaR (Monteiro et al. 2026), which is designed for solving problems with a trace-bounding constraint, this work develops a new augmented Lagrangian (AL) method, HALLaR+, for solving large-scale semidefinite programming problems without such constraint. Even though a trace constraint which preserves an optimal solution can always be added, choosing its bound is challenging: a value that is too small may exclude all optimal solutions, whereas one that is too large may substantially increase the computational effort. HALLaR+ is also a low-rank inexact AL method but, in contrast to HALLaR, it doubles the penalty parameter at every AL iteration and its AL subproblems have unbounded feasible regions that are approximately solved by a relaxed unbounded Frank--Wolfe (RUFW) variant. Its analysis relies on a uniform bound on the diameters of the sublevel sets of all generated AL subproblems instead of a bounded feasible set. Assuming that a primal--dual KKT pair exists and the primal optimal set is nonempty and bounded, it is shown that HALLaR+ returns a $\varepsilon$-primal-dual feasible solution in $\tilde {\mathcal O}(\varepsilon^{-2})$ total RUFW iterations. Numerical results suggest that HALLaR+ has very promising competitive performance against current state-of-the-art solvers.
Gradient Estimation for LLM-Embedded Simulation Optimization

Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly embedded in operational simulators to represent context-dependent human decisions, which opens new possibilities for simulation optimization. However, the LLM acts as a black box, so derivatives through its decisions are unavailable for gradient-based policy search. Finite difference estimation can avoid this requirement, but the required paired simulations that sample LLM actions independently often disagree, and such action switches persist under small perturbations, which inflates the gradient variance to order $c^{-2}$ for perturbation radius $c$. To control this variance, we develop a behavioral common random number framework. It first applies maximal coupling to the LLM's action distributions, preserving each simulation's behavioral law while making action switches as rare as possible, which reduces the variance bound to $O(c^{-1})$. It then applies first-switch conditioning, which averages over whether a switch occurs, together with an impact-aware extension that prioritizes influential switches. Under suitable stability conditions, both keep the variance bounded as $c$ shrinks. We further establish improved complexity bounds for projected stochastic approximation. Experiments on synthesized and LLM-embedded simulators confirm the theory and show substantial performance gains.
Holomorphic interpolation and the Levi problem

On a nonsingular locally Stein Riemann domain over a Stein space, we prove that holomorphic forms of top degree interpolate jets of any fixed order on every closed discrete set finite over the base. For unramified domains, this yields jet interpolation by holomorphic functions, answering a question of Colţoiu and Joiţa for nonsingular sources. More generally, we establish a twisted interpolation theorem over weakly pseudoconvex spaces admitting injective holomorphic immersions into projective space. We also give negative answers to the Levi problem over singular Stein spaces: the Coeuré-Loeb space yields a non-Stein locally Stein unramified Riemann domain over a normal Stein threefold, and a related construction gives a relatively compact, non-Stein locally Stein open subset of a normal Stein fourfold. Finally, the punctured anticanonical bundle of Fornaess' ramified surface is a holomorphically separable increasing union of Stein manifolds that is not Stein, answering a question of Vigna Suria.

We show that an additive category is abelian if and only if its functorial nerve is a double décalage of a pseudo-simplicial object in Cat. In this characterization, the canonical isomorphism between the image and coimage is encoded by a coherent pseudo-simplicial identity.
Schauder exponential basis which is not Riesz
We show that there exists a Schauder basis $\{e^{i λ_n t}\}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ with real frequencies in $L^2(-π,π)$ which is not a Riesz basis.
BP-based qLDPC Decoding under Long-range Correlated Noise: Trapping Configurations and Prior Mismatch

We study the robustness of two state-of-the-art BP-based qLDPC decoders, Relay-BP and beam search, designed for independent noise when applied to spatially correlated noise with unchanged single-mechanism error probabilities. We generate correlated errors with a hidden Gaussian Markov random field, which lets us control the strength and range of the correlation while keeping every marginal error probability exact. This setting complements correlation-aware decoding: it asks how existing decoders perform when their assumed joint error model is mismatched. Across multiple tested circuits and code instances that we simulated, we observe that correlations can change logical error rates by orders of magnitude, reduce the finite-size distance advantage, and alter the relative ranking of Relay-BP, beam search, and BP-OSD. On one of the two tested circuits, Relay-BP and beam search become worse than BP-OSD, and increasing relay memory or beam width does not compensate for the degradation. Configuration analysis indicates that correlation primarily increases the probability of trapping configurations that are known to challenge these decoders; at matched error weight, correlated errors still cause decoding failures several times more often than i.i.d. errors. Finally, supplying the decoders with the marginals conditioned on the hidden field recovers most of the lost performance in the tested settings identifying prior mismatch as a major contributor to performance degradation under correlation.
Zeroth-Order Riemannian Optimization on Fixed-Rank Manifolds for LLM Fine-Tuning
