Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization estimates descent directions from function values alone, which removes the activation storage required by backpropagation and makes it attractive for memory-efficient fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs). Existing low-rank ZO methods either parameterize the additive update through Euclidean factors with a non-unique representation, or restrict each finite-difference direction to be low-rank. In this work, we propose to constrain each additive update block to a fixed-rank matrix manifold while keeping the pretrained weights frozen, so the learned update remains rank-constrained throughout fine-tuning. On this geometry, we build a Riemannian ZO gradient estimator that projects a random matrix onto the tangent space, normalizes it to correct the scale mismatch induced by projection, and further propose Zeroth-order Riemannian Gradient Descent (ZO-RGD) and its smoothed variant, ZO-RGD-S. We show that the ambient finite difference matches its retracted counterpart, the normalized estimator recovers the Riemannian gradient in expectation, and ZO-RGD converges under trajectory-regularity conditions. Experiments on LLM fine-tuning tasks show that the proposed algorithms are competitive with strong forward-only baselines across model families and tasks, with gains in several settings.
On the lower bound for the $L^1$ norm of Liouville exponential sums. II
Ben Krause; Jiangpeng Li; Yu-Chen Sun; Hui Wang

Let $λ$ denote the Liouville function, and put \[ I_λ(X)=\int_0^1\left|\sum_{n\le X}λ(n)e^{2πi nα}\right|\,dα. \] In this paper, we prove that \[ \limsup_{X \to \infty} \frac{\log I_λ(X)}{\log X} \ge \frac{1}{3}. \]
Linear structure graphs associated with commuting graphs of Lie algebras

The commuting graph (CG) of a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a field of characteristic zero forgets the linear structure, and a non-trivial center creates redundant vertices. We introduce linear structure graphs (LSGs), whose vertices are the nonzero vectors of a vector space and whose edge set is stable under linear operations. Each vertex generates a finite ascending sequence of subspaces, which defines its LSG-depth; this depth governs connectivity. We characterize LSGs of depth at most 1 and show that the CG of a Lie algebra with trivial center has depth at most 1 if and only if the algebra is a commutative transitive Lie algebra (CTLA). The reduced commuting graph (RCG) restricts the CG to a complement of the center; it is well defined up to LSG-isomorphism, preserves the connectivity, diameter and number of components of the CG, and is compatible with direct sums. Finally, we characterize almost abelian Lie algebras (AALAs) by their RCGs.
A sufficient condition for the Liouville property of solutions to the Euler-Lagrange equations of variational integrals with nonstandard growth in terms of the ellipticity modulus near the origin

We consider entire solutions $u$: $\mathbb{R}^{n}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ of the Euler-Lagrange equation $\operatorname{div}(\nabla f(\nabla u))=0$ with convex density $f$: $\mathbb{R}^{n}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ of nonstandard growth and nonuniform ellipticity. It turns out that the Liouville property can be characterized through the behavior of $D^{2}f(p)$ for points $p\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$ close to the origin: if, for example, $D^{2}f(p)$ behaves as $|p|^{ρ-2}\mathbf{1}$, $\mathbf{1}=\text{unit matrix}$, with exponent $ρ\ge2$ and for $|p|\le1$ then the validity of $n\leρ+2$ together with the boundedness of $u$ implies its constancy.
Euclidean view-obstruction in dimensions eight to ten and the asymptotic deficit

The Euclidean view-obstruction problem asks for the critical radius of balls centered at the half-integer lattice that meet every positive ray from the origin. Writing $Δ_n$ for its square, we determine $Δ_8=8/17$, $Δ_9=1087/1980$ and $Δ_{10}=7/11$ by computer-assisted proofs using Kahlon's seven-dimensional theorem.The upper bounds combine full-support subspace averaging, projected lattice coverings and exact finite certificates; dimension ten also requires a finite search through short integer relations. Explicit directions attain all three values, including a ten-dimensional direction previously listed by Gritsenko, Skoruppa and Zagier. In arbitrary dimension, we express their theta-block invariant in geometric normalization and derive the known bounds $c\log(n+1) \le n/12 - Δ_n \le C\log^3(n+1)$, with repeated coordinates allowed throughout. Thus $Δ_n \sim n/12$, while the deficit tends to infinity more slowly than every positive power of $n$. The supplementary archive contains the executable verifiers, exact certificates and archived verification records.

We combine degree sequence bounds with a supporting tangent plane method to study maximum volume polytopes inscribed in the sphere $\mathbb S^2$. Building on the vertex-star estimates and combinatorial reductions in Wimmer's dissertation, we determine the exact maximum for ten vertices and the unique maximizing combinatorial type for eleven vertices. Moreover, using explicit computational certificates we identify a unique possible maximizing type for polytopes with thirteen and fifteen vertices, and two possible types for sixteen vertices; this approach also recovers Wimmer's fourteen-vertex combinatorial theorem. Finally, we derive a facial inequality which holds for every degree pattern, and prove that the maximum volume for polytopes with thirty-two vertices is $\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{10(5-\sqrt{5})}$, attained precisely by an inscribed realization of the pentakis dodecahedron, which is the convex hull of the regular icosahedron together with its normalized facet centers. Wimmer had already determined this configuration and its optimality within its own combinatorial type. We also obtain a global degree sequence envelope and a universal affine volume bound.

We study spectral Einstein functionals associated with the $J$-twist of the Dirac operator on almost product Riemannian spin manifolds. On closed even-dimensional manifolds, we compute the corresponding noncommutative residue in terms of the Einstein tensor, the curvature of the connection determined by $D_J^2$, and its zero-order endomorphism. For four-dimensional compact manifolds with boundary, we consider two boundary residue functionals obtained by inserting two covariant derivatives in the first factor of the compositions $π^+(D_J^{-2})\circπ^+(D_J^{-2})$ and $π^+(D_J^{-1})\circπ^+(D_J^{-3})$. Under the stated collar and almost product structure assumptions, we calculate their interior and boundary contributions and obtain Dąbrowski--Sitarz--Zalecki type formulas. We also present applications of these results in physics and noncommutative geometry, focusing on spectral actions, spectral distance, and mean-curvature boundary contributions.

We analyze the spectrum of quantum square lattice graph exposed to a homogeneous magnetic field with a rational flux through plaquette, assuming all nontrivial cases of the vertex coupling which is circulant and scale-invariant, with a particular attention to those of them that give rise to a dynamics violating the time reversal invariance. Except for two cases with partially decoupled edges, the remaining twelve split into two spectral classes; the second one offers a hitherto unknown butterfly pattern.

We construct almost perfect nonlinear (APN) functions $G_{λ,M}(x)=g(x)+M(x)+λ(x^{q-1}-1)$, where $λ\in\F_q^*$, $-λ\notin g(\F_q)$, and $M$ is an $\F_p$-linearized permutation polynomial. We obtain three pairwise CCZ-inequivalent APN functions with boomerang uniformity one over $\F_{p^{15\ell}}$ for every $\ell\ge1$, six over $\F_{p^{120r}}$ for every $r\ge1$, and unbounded numbers of such classes in characteristic three. We also show that all our APN functions have the maximal possible algebraic degree $n(p-1)$. Finally, we exhibit both CCZ-equivalent and CCZ-inequivalent APN pairs with boomerang uniformity one at Hamming distance one.
Local turnpike property for a three-component mean field game system arising from a resource harvesting model

We study a three-component mean field game system arising from a resource harvesting model. It couples Hamilton--Jacobi and Fokker--Planck equations for the harvesters with a reaction-diffusion equation for the resource. The coupling is nonlocal in space and time. For standard second-order mean field game systems, exponential turnpike estimates are known under assumptions such as monotonicity of the coupling. For the present system, Kobeissi, Mazari-Fouquer, and Ruiz-Balet proved algebraic convergence to a stationary solution in a space--time averaged sense, but no exponential turnpike estimate has been obtained. We prove such an estimate near a stationary solution with strictly positive density components. Inspired by the relative entropy method, we add the relative entropy of the resource density to the standard energy for local turnpike estimates. In the time derivative of this modified energy, the nonlocal coupling terms cancel. The two key assumptions are coercivity of a quadratic form determined by the stationary resource density and smallness of the relative density perturbations in $L^\infty$. Under these assumptions, we bound the absolute value of the modified energy by two terms that decay exponentially away from the initial and terminal times. We derive weighted $L^2$ exponential turnpike estimates for the harvester density, the resource density, and the gradient of the value function. We give sufficient conditions for coercivity. For each fixed $T>0$, classical solutions satisfying these assumptions exist for initial and terminal data sufficiently close to the stationary solution. We extend the modified energy estimate to a more general reaction term under the corresponding assumptions.
Integral Compensation for Discrete-time Bearing-only Target Localization and Circumnavigation

This paper investigates the discrete-time control problem of driving an agent to localize and circumnavigate an unknown target at a prescribed radius using bearing measurements. Discretizing existing continuous-time circumnavigation controllers can introduce steady-state orbit bias, even at sampling rates that preserve stability. To eliminate the sampling-induced orbit bias, we propose an adaptive compensator for a circumnavigation controller formulated directly in discrete time. Driven by the estimated agent-to-target distance, the proposed compensator dynamically learns the geometric correction required to achieve the desired circumnavigation radius. Unlike existing static correction methods, neither the proposed controller nor the compensator update explicitly uses the sampling interval. Exponential convergence is rigorously established using Lyapunov-based analysis. Simulation results illustrate the performance of the proposed algorithms.
Directional weak mixing and directional Kronecker for $\Z^2$-actions
E. Arthur Robinson, Jr.; Ayşe A. Şahin

Let $T$ be a measure preserving $\Z^2$-action on a Lebesgue probability space $(X,μ)$ and let $L\subseteq\R^2$ be a $1$-dimensional subspace. For a rational subspace $L$, direction $L$ weak mixing corresponds to weak mixing for the measure preserving transformation $T^{\vv_0}$, where $\vv_0$ is a primitive vector in $\Z^2$ generating $L$. For an irrational direction $L$, we study two different definitions of direction $L$ weak mixing, and show that they are the same: ``Dynamical'' direction $L$ weak mixing is defined to be the absence of any direction $L$ Kronecker factors. These factors are defined in terms of almost periodicity along a finite width direction $L$ strip in $\Z^2$. ``Spectral'' direction $L$ weak mixing is defined as the absence of any direction $L^\perp$ line segments $I\subseteq\T^2$ with positive spectral measure. We also give a spectral characterization of the directional Kronecker property defined in \cite{liuxu}, and provide examples of $\Z^2$-actions $K$ that are direction $L$ Kronecker.
A Bayesian oriented exploration and reinforcement learning in continuous-time mean-variance portfolio optimization
Kexin Chen; Xiang Yu; Shanshan Zhao

We propose a new reinforcement learning (RL) framework for the continuous-time mean-variance portfolio optimization with unknown market parameters. To better reflect the impact of improved information of the unknown drift on the degree of exploration, we consider a novel randomization based on continuous-time stochastic filtering. Specifically, we construct a continuous-time analog to Thompson Sampling by treating the unknown drift as a random draw from a generalized sampling distribution parameterized by the filter's posterior mean and variance. The new learning objective measures the tradeoff between the wealth performance and the weighted KL divergence between the policy and the true Bayesian posterior, which transforms the classical feedback control into an information guided stochastic policy. As a result, the degree of exploration endogenously depends on the Reward-Biased Maximum Likelihood Estimation that decays with the shrinking filter's variance. This allows us to devise an efficient model-based learning algorithm in the mean-variance portfolio optimization with theoretical guarantee and superior learning performance.
Embeddings for Orlicz potential spaces with applications to mixed local-nonlocal problems

In this paper, we provide further insight into potential spaces within the nonstandard framework of Orlicz functions. More precisely, we establish continuous and compact embeddings of potential spaces in $\mathbb{R}^n$ into both unweighted and weighted Orlicz spaces. Special attention is devoted to the radial setting, for which compactness results are obtained through Strauss- and Ni-type inequalities. As an application, we prove the existence of positive radial solutions to a class of Henon-type problems involving both local and nonlocal contributions in the Orlicz framework.
Nonlinear stability and time-decay rates of planar rarefaction waves for the full compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system in $\mathbb{R}^3$
Renjun Duan; Feimin Huang; Rui Li; Lingda Xu

We prove the global-in-time nonlinear stability and establish explicit algebraic time-decay rates of planar rarefaction waves for the three-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system of an ideal polytropic gas in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Given a smooth initial rarefaction profile of small wave strength \(δ>0\), we first construct the corresponding global one-dimensional Navier-Stokes-Fourier solution \(U_b(t,x_1)\) and show that it converges toward the self-similar Euler rarefaction fan in \(L^\infty(\mathbb{R})\) at rate \((1+t)^{-12/25}\). For the three-dimensional Cauchy problem under small weighted $H^3(\mathbb{R}^3)$ perturbations with zero integral of mass, momentum, and total energy, we prove that there exists a unique global strong solution $U(t,x)$ converging toward $U_b(t,x_1)$ in $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3)$ at rate $(1+t)^{-11/25}$, with $\nabla(U-U_b)$ decaying in $H^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ at rate $(1+t)^{-11/25}$.
Rigid Lie Algebras from Semisimple Lie Algebras and Their Symplectic Modules

We consider two extensions associated with a nonzero finite-dimensional symplectic module $V$ over a complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{s}$, and study their rigidity. The toral extension adjoins a derivation acting as the identity on $V$ and trivially on $\mathfrak{s}$; the Heisenberg extension uses the invariant symplectic form on $V$ to define a central bracket. For the toral extension, we compute the first and second adjoint cohomology groups in terms of $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak{s}}(V)$, and obtain rigidity precisely when $V$ is irreducible. These results hold for arbitrary nonzero finite-dimensional modules. For the Heisenberg extension, we express the second adjoint cohomology as the kernel of a map combining the symplectic centralizer with an equivariant Jacobi map. A Killing-form argument shows that every multiplicity-free sum of irreducible symplectic modules gives an algebraically rigid Heisenberg extension. We also treat constructions with independent toral generators or Heisenberg centers. Repeated summands lead to explicit nonrigid examples, including a deformation to $\mathfrak{sl}_3$. The proofs use invariant cochains and recover several previously studied families.
Performance Analysis of Entanglement Swapping DV-QKD over MIMO FSO Channels

This paper studies multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) free-space optical (FSO) quantum communication systems employing polarization-encoded discrete-variable quantum key distribution (DV-QKD), based on entanglement swapping, with the goal of extending secure communications beyond the reach of a direct link. The FSO channels are subject to atmospheric absorption, diffraction, beam wander, pointing errors, and turbulence-induced fading, while background noise and detector imperfections degrade the performance. An eavesdropper controlling the channels and the relay is also considered. To analyze the performance of the considered system, both hops MIMO channels are decomposed into parallel spatial eigenchannels via singular value decomposition (SVD), photon loss is modeled using Kraus operators, and a threshold-detector model is developed for the relay. Based on these models, closed-form per-eigenchannel expressions for the relay gain are derived, which are then used to obtain expressions for the quantum bit error rate (QBER) and the secret key rate (SKR). Numerical results demonstrate that entanglement swapping maintains a low QBER over longer distances than direct transmission, extending the communication range beyond the noise-limited cutoff of the direct link, at the cost of a lower SKR at short distances. The crossover distance beyond which entanglement swapping prevails is determined mainly by the background noise and the detector technology, and it is demonstrated to increase with MIMO configurations. Moreover, the reach gain is shown to be maximized for a midpoint relay. Finally, since each swapping event requires a single-pair emission from both sources, a near-deterministic entangled-photon source is required, which spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources do not provide at practical key rates, whereas MIMO substantially relaxes this requirement.

Let $n\geq 2$ be an integer. Set $Γ_n=SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ (respectively $PSL_2(\mathbb{Z})$) for $n$ even (respectively for $n$ odd). Then $Γ_n$ acts on $\mathbb{Z}^n$ through the restriction of the linear action of $SL_2(\mathbb{R})$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$. We prove that that the von Neumann algebra $L(\mathbb{Z}^n\rtimes Γ_n)$ is a solid factor. This generalizes the case $n=2$ proved by N. Ozawa.
A 43-vertex 4-chromatic unit-distance graph in the plane with girth 5

We exhibit a set of 43 points in the Euclidean plane whose unit-distance graph has 83 edges, girth 5 and chromatic number 4. The smallest previously known 4-chromatic unit-distance graph of girth 5, due to Hochberg and O'Donnell (1996), has 45 vertices. The new graph is 4-critical, has trivial automorphism group, and has exactly 2n-3 edges; it is a Laman graph and its unit-distance realisation is infinitesimally rigid. The coordinates are algebraic numbers, specified as the unique real solution of an explicit system of 82 quadratic equations inside an explicit rational box. Every claim is certified by exact computation: existence and uniqueness of the realisation by a rational contraction-mapping certificate (independently re-checked with interval Krawczyk arithmetic), and non-3-colourability both by exhaustive search and by a DRAT proof verified with drat-trim.
A Prey-Predator Framework for Tumor-Immune Dynamics: Circuit-Based Modeling with Hilfer-Katugampola Fractional Derivatives

This study focuses on modeling tumor--immune interactions through a fractional-order prey--predator framework, where tumor cells act as prey and immune effector cells as predators. To capture the hereditary and memory effects inherent in biological systems, we employ the Hilfer--Katugampola fractional derivative, which flexibly interpolates between Riemann--Liouville and Caputo formulations. In addition, a circuit-based analogy is introduced to map tumor proliferation, immune regulation, and therapeutic interventions onto resistive, capacitive, and inductive elements, providing intuitive interpretation of the dynamics. Numerical simulations reveal that lower fractional orders lead to delayed oscillations, prolonged tumor persistence, and increased sensitivity to treatment strategies compared with classical integer-order models. A quantitative two-interval criterion for the Riemann hypothesis

We aim to study whether the Weil form can detect a zero of the Riemann zeta function away from the critical line using two functions with increasingly narrow, widely separated supports. We prove that the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality on every such pair at all sufficiently large separations, provided the component widths decrease subexponentially. We also express the cross term through prime powers in a moving multiplicative interval. The resulting criterion specifies a uniform arithmetic inequality whose proof would establish the Riemann hypothesis.
The $ν$-core label order and noncrossing partitions
We prove that the poset of $s$-noncrossing partitions is isomorphic to the core label order of the $ν$-Tamari lattice introduced by Préville-Ratelle and Viennot.

For every finite $q>2$, our lower bound gives a negative answer to the dimension-free question in Xu's \emph{JEMS} paper (2025) \cite[Problem~1.8(i)]{XuJEMS}, already for real scalar functions. The third order hypermetric $ρ(x,y,z)$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is given by the Euclidean distance of the point $(x,y,z)\in(\mathbb{R}^n)^3$ to the diagonal $Δ^{(3)}=\{(x,x,x):x\in\mathbb{R}^n\}$ of $(\mathbb{R}^n)^3$. In doing so, we obtain a fractional nonlocal version $\mathbb{D}^s(f,g)$, $0<s<1$, of the Dirichlet bilinear operator $\nabla f(x)\cdot\nabla g(x)$ which converges to this classical form when the fractional parameter approaches its endpoint $s=1$. Optimal rational spherical designs on the circle
Zhuo Cheng; Yeyao Hu; Deyu Yu

The minimum numbers of points in rational equal-weight spherical designs on the circle are $2304$, $4608$, $9216$, and $9216$ at strengths $4$, $5$, $6$, and $7$, respectively. We construct two nonisometric optimal designs at each strength. At arbitrary strength $t$, we obtain an explicit cardinality divisor $D_t$ with $\log D_t=(1/2+o(1))t\log t$. We consider matroid intersection under the minimum rank oracle model, in which two matroids are accessible only through an oracle that returns the minimum of the ranks of a given set in the two matroids. By Edmonds' theorem, this oracle determines the matroid intersection polytope, although it does not reveal the exchangeability graphs on which classical algorithms rely. We also give min-max theorems in terms of the minimum rank function via 1/3-submodularity, and present a strongly polynomial-time algorithm to compute an optimal dual solution.

This spectral bias is well documented, but it is much less clear which architectural choices mitigate it and which cannot. The port-Hamiltonian framework was built for mechanical and electrical systems, where the Hamiltonian is stored energy and the ports carry power. This review maps that spread. We classify each application by what its Hamiltonian really is: physical energy, a thermodynamic potential such as free energy or exergy, or an abstract storage function with no energetic meaning. The review keeps only sources whose bibliographic record we checked against Crossref. The picture that emerges is a continuum. Where a genuine thermodynamic potential exists, the theory is deep and constructive. Where the energy is borrowed, the framework still pays off through compositional interconnection and dissipation inequalities, but the work is younger and scattered. We close with a set of deliberately speculative research directions, including open port-Hamiltonian models of epidemics, opinion dynamics and supply chains, and learned port-Hamiltonian digital twins for structural health monitoring.

Relative greedy weights were introduced by Li and Liu in [19] as a measure of information leakage in coordinated two-party wire-tap channels of type II when the adversary follows a greedy strategy. The theorem splits naturally into two cases according to whether the quantity $D - 2ψ$ is non-zero or zero, with further subcases depending on whether the homothetic vectors are gradient or non-gradient. The theorem imposes no restrictions on $A(t)$, $g_{ij}$ or $V(x)$, and is therefore fully general and covariant. We apply the theorem to the time-dependent damped Duffing oscillator (DDO) in Euclidean space $E^{3}$ with $A(t) = e^{γt}$ and potential $V = \frac{1}{2}a\,r^{2} + \frac{% λ}{4}r^{4}$. For the damped harmonic oscillator ($λ= 0$) the theorem reproduces the classical Bateman invariant as a special case. For the anharmonic case we obtain a new exact time-dependent quadratic invariant, valid when the linear stiffness satisfies $a = 2γ^{2}/9$. Each invariant is verified explicitly by direct differentiation along the equations of motion. The new invariant provides a rare example of a global conservation law for a fully nonlinear dissipative system, and can be used for the integration and quantization of the DDO.
Error Estimates and Convergence Analysis for Learning Mechanism--AI Coupled Dynamical Systems
Pengfei Song; Yanni Xiao; Yuan Lou; Shuangshuang Yin

Mechanism--AI coupled dynamical systems retain known mechanisms while learning unknown dynamics from data. We study how neural approximation, numerical integration, finite observations, and optimization jointly affect the accuracy of this learning process. For time-dependent learned terms in a fixed compact admissible class, we derive a four-component objective error bound within an optimal control formulation. Explicit estimates are obtained for constrained ReLU approximation and Euler integration, with deterministic quadrature and random sampling treated separately. Under joint refinement, we establish $Γ$-convergence of the approximate objectives and show that approximate minimizers approach the continuous optimal set when the global optimization gaps vanish. We also derive conditional stability estimates for state-dependent learned terms. Numerical experiments with a susceptible--infected--recovered (SIR) model illustrate the analysis and show how solver resolution affects continuous-trajectory accuracy even when training losses are similar.
On naturality of cohomological support for small quantum groups

We apply the theory of hypersurface support by Negron and Pevtsova to prove the naturality of cohomological support of the small quantum Borel groups, with respect to restriction to Levi subalgebras. This in turn implies naturality of cohomological support of the small quantum groups for modules that lift to Lusztig's big quantum group, for instance tilting modules. This allows us to make the recent conditional classification of tensor ideals of abelian type in the category of such tilting modules unconditional.
Reconstructing Interacting Blood Flow and Wall Interface Deformation from Noisy Flow Data Using PirateNets
Han Zhang; Xue-Cheng Tai; Alessandro Veneziani; Raymond H. Chan

Blood flow and elastic vessel-wall motion interact with each other: fluid stress drives wall deformation, while the moving wall changes the domain in which blood flows. Given noisy flow images, we study the inverse problem of reconstructing the coupled, unsteady three-dimensional motions. We solve the reconstruction through Gauss--Seidel-type alternating fluid and geometry updates. For the fluid, we use physics-informed networks to recover velocity and pressure by fitting the observations while enforcing the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations on the moving domain, which is described by an arbitrary Lagrangian--Eulerian (ALE) map. For the geometry, a reference-domain correction and sequential registration recover the vessel shape and wall displacement. Interface traction continuity and an elastic momentum equation regularize the registration so that the recovered displacement is also physics-informed. The networks evaluate fields and physical residuals at sampled space--time points without remeshing the moving domain. Experiments on a converging channel and a patient-like aorta demonstrate reconstruction of flow and wall motion from noisy data. Ablation and parameter-sensitivity studies examine the role of structure regularization and imperfect physical coefficients. A further experiment with a three-element Windkessel outlet condition demonstrates how the framework accommodates a more physiologically realistic boundary setting.
A Goldbach-Type Problem for the Unitary Möbius Function

Let $g(n)=(-1)^{ω(n)}$, where $ω(n)$ denotes the number of distinct prime factors of $n$. We prove that, for every sufficiently large integer $N$, each ordered additive sign pattern $(g(a),g(N-a))=(s,t)$ occurs at least $N/(128(\log N)^3)$ times. We also prove that, for every $N\ge18$ and every $s,t\in\sgnset$, there is at least one integer $1\le a<N$ such that $(g(a),g(N-a))=(s,t)$. In addition, we establish a one-quarter asymptotic formula for almost all target integers. Finally, we discuss Goldbach-type problems for the ordinary Möbius function and formulate related questions.
Chuangqiang Hu; Stephen S. -T. Yau; Lishan Yu

We establish a generating trace formula for multicharacter ideal-type $L$-values associated with rank-one Drinfeld modules. For a sign-normalized Hayes module with free period lattice, the formula realizes the $L$-values at weights $n\equiv s\pmod{q^{°_\infty}-1}$ as a trace over the ordinary Hilbert class field. We further characterize the polynomials in the exponential variable $X$ arising in multicharacter lattice generating identities over arbitrary function rings. Their coefficients are given explicitly via the shtuka basis, which gives concrete control over their supports and degrees. This completely settles an open problem of Pellarin and Perkins: these polynomials are all constant if and only if $s<2q$. The results on coefficients apply to curves of arbitrary genus, infinite places of arbitrary degree, and nonprincipal period lattices.
Geometric Stochastic Dynamics and Fokker-Planck Equation on $\mathsf{T}\mathbb S^2$

This paper develops a geometric (coordinate-free) stochastic model of a controlled point mass evolving on the unit two-sphere $\mathbb S^2$, together with the Fokker-Planck equation governing the probability density of the resulting stochastic process. The state manifold is the tangent bundle $\mathsf{T}\mathbb S^2$. The Levi-Civita connection of the round metric is used to construct the horizontal-vertical splitting of $\mathsf{T}(\mathsf{T}\mathbb S^2)$ and to convert the intrinsic second-order dynamics of the system into a first-order controlled vector field on $\mathsf{T}\mathbb S^2$. Endowing the tangent bundle with the Sasaki metric then permits stochastic perturbations to be introduced intrinsically and independently in horizontal, i.e., position, and vertical, i.e., velocity, directions. The corresponding infinitesimal generator is obtained in horizontal-vertical Hessian form. The probability density is defined with respect to the Sasaki Riemannian volume measure. The Fokker-Planck equation is derived intrinsically in both Stratonovich and Itô forms. In the Itô representation, a globally defined horizontal-vertical diffusion tensor yields a compact double-divergence Fokker-Planck PDE. No coordinates or embedded Euclidean representation of the sphere dynamics are used in the development. Numerical simulations illustrate the stochastic motion of a controlled particle ensemble on $\mathbb S^2$ toward an antipodal target configuration.
A Zero-Free Sum of Cauchy Kernels with Positive Coefficients

We construct a zero-free meromorphic function \[ f(z)=\sum_n\frac{c_n}{z-a_n},\qquad c_n>0,\qquad |a_n|\to\infty,\qquad \sum_{a_n\ne0}\frac{c_n}{|a_n|}<\infty, \] thereby disproving the Clunie--Eremenko--Rossi conjecture. The construction starts from a product of two rotated Airy functions. The zeros of this product are shifted simultaneously so that all residues of $f$ are positive. The poles lie on the rays $e^{\pm iπ/3}[0,\infty)$. The resulting function has order and lower order $3/2$, and the sum of its residues in the disc $|z|\le r$ is asymptotic to $\frac{4}{3π}r^{3/4}$.
A Trajectory-Aware Domain-Decomposed Multispace Reduced Basis Preconditioner for Parametric Helmholtz Problems
An Ping; Zhichao Peng; Pengliang Yang

Repeated solutions of parametric Helmholtz problems arise in multi-query applications such as sensitivity analysis and uncertainty quantification. Classical preconditioned iterative solvers do not automatically reuse low-dimensional structures across parameters. Multispace reduced basis (MSRB) preconditioners can exploit such structures by constructing iteration-specific reduced order models (ROMs) from training data, but storing global iteration-dependent bases incurs substantial memory costs. Building on trajectory-aware MSRB training, we develop a domain-decomposed MSRB (DD-MSRB) preconditioner for parametric Helmholtz systems truncated by perfectly matched layers (PMLs). Within flexible GMRES, each reduced space is trained on inverse-action snapshots along the Krylov trajectories generated by the ROM-based preconditioners applied in preceding iterations. To reduce storage, problem-adapted spatial partitions exploit heterogeneous local snapshot compressibility across the physical interior and the PML. Local basis dimensions in each subdomain are determined greedily under a global snapshot-error budget to balance approximation accuracy and storage. The resulting hybrid solver applies DD-MSRB preconditioning during the initial iterations to capture dominant cross-parameter modes and then switches, when necessary, to a shifted-Laplacian preconditioner to reduce error components poorly represented by the reduced spaces. Numerical experiments on two-dimensional half-space propagation, elliptic-obstacle scattering, and three-dimensional waveguides demonstrate significant acceleration over the shifted-Laplacian baseline and substantial memory savings relative to global MSRB. For the largest waveguide system, with 11.0 million unknowns, DD-MSRB reduces deployed ROM storage by 44.9% and mean online solve time by 30.2% compared with global MSRB.
Local vanishing density of order $1$ and Divisor moments

We establish a general framework relating local vanishing densities of order $1$ to logarithmic growth of divisor moments on regular arithmetic curves. As applications, we recover classical divisor moment estimates for polynomial values and establish their function field analogue. Furthermore, under GRH, we obtain a result on divisor moments for polynomials in the Fourier coefficients of non-CM cuspidal eigenforms with trivial nebentypus and trivial inner twist. The Fourier coefficients need not be integers, and the polynomials need not be squarefree. Under additional analytic hypotheses, we also allow a Sato--Tate angle restriction.
GEAR: A GPU-Accelerated Global Solver for Bounded Continuous Nonlinear Programs via Linear Bound Propagation
Duo Zhou; Hesun Chen; Xiangru Zhong; Grani A. Hanasusanto; Huan Zhang

We present a novel GPU-accelerated global solver for constrained nonlinear programming (NLP) inspired by the efficient linear bound propagation framework in neural network (NN) verification. Existing work on NN verification, a problem that can be cast as feasibility detection for a nonlinear objective, demonstrated orders-of-magnitude speedups with the linear bound propagation-based framework when compared to traditional solvers. Extending this paradigm to global nonlinear programming requires addressing many challenges: a global constrained NLP solver must effectively exploit all, possibly unstructured, nonlinear constraints to improve the objective, whereas NN verification typically handles simple input box constraints over a well-structured NN and does not directly optimize an objective function. We address these challenges by fully exploiting the linear bounds produced by bound propagation: these linear bounds can be viewed as relaxations of nonlinear constraints and used to provide lower bounds, check infeasibility, and guide the search for a primal solution. In addition, we propose tighter linear relaxations for bilinear, quotient, and other commonly used nonlinear functions in NLP problems, and a projected augmented Lagrangian method tightly coupled to our dual solving procedure to produce primal solutions. Our method solves 421 of 505 bounded and continuous NLP problems in the GAMS and MINLPLib benchmarks under a 180-second limit, more than each of the six global solvers we compare with, including Gurobi and BARON (commercial), and SCIP (open-source). Sixteen of these problems are certified by none of the six global solvers; all of them contain exponential, logarithmic, or trigonometric terms, which are often challenging for traditional approaches. Project webpage is at https://verified-intelligence.github.io/GEAR.
A trace costs one quantifier: the exact complexity of perfect play in nonlocal games

Given a finite nonlocal game, can the players win with certainty? We prove that the existence of a perfect normal spatial strategy is $Σ^0_2$-complete, even when restricted to games of value one, so it cannot be decided even with an oracle for the halting problem. This is strictly harder than perfect play in the finite-dimensional and commuting-operator models, which are $Σ^0_1$-complete and $Π^0_1$-complete. Within the commuting model, the existence of a perfect normal strategy with a finite or semifinite von Neumann host is $Σ^0_2$-complete, whereas for every fixed type $\mathrm{III}_λ$ subtype it has the same $Π^0_1$-complete language as unrestricted commuting play. A trace thus costs one existential number quantifier: the hardness constructions force every perfect strategy to choose a finite clock period or a finite tree depth. Spatial $Σ^0_2$-completeness also holds when finite entanglement entropy is required, and both forms are formally verified in Lean. For every computable $0<α<1$, perfect spatial play with $\mathrm{Tr}\,h^α<\infty$ for the reduced density $h$ is $Σ^0_2$-complete as well; these conditions form a strict ladder between finite rank and finite entropy. We also prove $Σ^0_2$-completeness for one-shot zero-error communication with normal entanglement, and construct a finite channel with zero-error codes of a given size each of which needs infinite entanglement entropy.
Motivic generating functions and $L$-derivatives of cohomological automorphic representations

Forty years ago, Gross and Zagier proved a remarkable formula computing the central derivative of the Rankin--Selberg $L$-function of a cusp form $f$ of weight $2$ and a character of the class group of an imaginary quadratic field, satisfying the so-called Heegner condition, and deduce that the nonvanishing of the central derivative implies the nonvanishing of the corresponding Mordell--Weil rank. This formula was later generalized in various contexts and degrees, for example, by S. Zhang for $f$ of higher even weights; and by Yuan--Zhang--Zhang for $f$ a Hilbert cusp form of parallel weight $2$ over an arbitrary totally real field $F$ and $χ$ a Dirichlet character of an arbitrary CM extension $E/F$, allowing arbitrary ramification. In this article, we prove a Gross--Zagier type formula in the context of doubling method, for $f$ a Hilbert cusp form over $F$ and $χ$ a Hecke character of $E$ of general weights under a balancing condition, again allowing arbitrary ramification. Indeed, we even formulate a general conjecture which we call the motivic arithmetic inner product formula, for cohomological automorphic representations of $\mathrm{GL}_{2r}$ over $E$ of hermitian type of balanced weights.
Group-Conditional Conformal Risk Control: Exact Guarantees, Limits, and Overlapping Extensions

We study group-conditional conformal risk control (CRC) for disjoint and overlapping groups under bounded monotone losses. For disjoint groups, we establish exact finite-sample conditional risk control, two-sided bounds on the group-restricted risk, and fundamental limitations arising from local support and calibration-rank granularity. For overlapping groups, we study two exactly valid approaches: group-restricted calibration followed by union deployment, and direct calibration of the deployed prediction-set family. We characterize the union's limiting reconciliation gap, identify conditions for its disappearance, and establish sharp lower bounds for structured losses in specified product-form models. We also demonstrate a strict size advantage for direct calibration in an ordinal model. Experiments show that direct calibration can reduce prediction-set size, but its efficiency depends on group structure, loss type, and shape fitting. Results on historical diabetic-retinopathy scores further illustrate these tradeoffs. Overall, local support, reconciliation slack, and threshold heterogeneity determine efficiency, with neither approach uniformly dominating.

The Fast Tree Transform is a locally-aggregated transform defined for arbitrary graph geometries that generalizes both the Hadamard frequency transform and the Haar wavelet transform on the circle. The pure frequency part of the transform approximately diagonalizes the graph Laplacian; this fact makes it useful as a preconditioner in geometric optimization problems. The full transform provides an only slightly-redundant representation of signals on the graph that allows sparse representation of signals that include both edges and textures.
Zeroth-Order Langevin Dynamics for Stochastic Nonconvex Optimization: Curvature Regularization and Non-Asymptotic Guarantees

Zeroth-order methods provide a way to optimize stochastic nonconvex objectives using only noisy function evaluations. However, the smoothing inherent in their gradient estimators effectively modifies the objective being optimized. In particular, Gaussian smoothing with smoothing parameter $η>0$ induces, to leading order, an implicit Hessian-trace regularization, which motivates the study of the curvature-regularized objective of the form $f(x)+(η^2/2) tr(\nabla^2 f(x))$. We develop a non-asymptotic theory in the nonconvex setting for a class of algorithms called stochastic zeroth-order Langevin dynamics (ZOLD), which use only noisy function evaluations and do not have access to first- or higher-order derivative information, and derive excess-risk guarantees for the curvature-regularized objective. We first control the finite-time distribution of the ZOLD iterates in Wasserstein distance with respect to the Gibbs measure associated with the Gaussian-smoothed objective. An explicit coupling between the smoothing and inverse temperature parameters then quantifies the proximity of this measure to the Gibbs measure associated with the corresponding Hessian-trace-regularized objective. These distributional estimates in Wasserstein distance lead to excess-risk bounds for the curvature-regularized objective. Our analysis accommodates assumptions under which the stochastic function evaluations are allowed to have non-uniform dependence on the data stream. In addition, the constants in the non-asymptotic bounds do not rely on log-Sobolev or Poincaré inequalities as in prior zeroth-order Langevin analyses. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first non-asymptotic analysis of a zeroth-order Langevin method that simultaneously establishes excess-risk guarantees for a curvature-regularized objective and Wasserstein guarantees for the associated Gibbs measure in the nonconvex setting.
Xiaoyu Chen; Yujing Huang; Yingyan Zeng

Many scientific responses take values in Riemannian manifolds, with predictors that are scalar- and/or manifold-valued. A regression analysis in such settings must provide accurate prediction with hypothesis testing for individual coefficients. Yet no current manifold-regression framework accommodates both predictor types and enables per-coefficient hypothesis tests. We propose Riemannian Ordinary Least Squares (ROLS) as a tangent space conditional-mean model, which is the ordinary least squares (OLS) analogue for Riemannian manifolds. ROLS is well-defined under an explicit injectivity condition that keeps the logarithm maps single-valued, with cut-locus conditions for branch-sensitive cases outside it. Within the local geometric setting it admits a closed-form estimator, an $O(n^{-1})$ excess prediction-error bound with explicit curvature bias, and asymptotic $t$- and Wald tests for individual coefficients. With synthetic simulations and three real-data case studies, ROLS is shown to be competitive with the state-of-the-art baselines. In addition, the per-coefficient tests agree with effects reported in literature. We envision ROLS to be a standard tool for manifold-valued regression with coefficient-level inference to support scientific discovery, which can be interpreted in the same way as Euclidean OLS. The source code is available at https://github.com/XiaoyuChenPub/ROLS.
Uniqueness and stability of Appleton's solitons

We prove that Appleton's noncollapsed steady gradient Ricci solitons on complex line bundles over positive Kähler--Einstein manifolds are the unique such solitons arising from his metric ansatz. We then show that the four-dimensional examples on $O_{\mathbb{CP}^1}(-k)$, $k \geq 3$, are strictly linearly stable. By a result of Deruelle, this implies dynamical stability under the Ricci flow.
Lower Bounds Above $\sqrt{3}$ for Online Makespan Minimization on Four Identical Machines

For deterministic online makespan minimization, $m = 4$ identical machines is the smallest case whose optimal competitive ratio is open: it is known only to lie between $\sqrt{3} \approx 1.73205$ and $26/15 \approx 1.73333$. We prove a lower bound of $14383/8304 \approx 1.73206$ using a single branching layer, and refine the construction with a second, mirrored branching layer to obtain $14350/8283 \approx 1.73246$, closing about a third of the gap. Our constructions are the first branching adversaries for $m = 4$ machines, and the first explicit lower bounds for online makespan minimization in which the adversary presents jobs in non-monotone order of size.
An introduction to discrete dynamics in condensed sets: orbits, periodic loci, and arithmetic examples

We formulate discrete dynamics internally in the topos Cond of condensed sets. For an endomorphism $f\colon X\to X$, we construct orbit quotients, backward histories, preimage trees, and periodic loci as objects evaluated on profinite parameter spaces. The framework recovers global-section dynamics, fully faithfully embeds compact Hausdorff systems, characterizes the invertible extension, and is compatible with inverse limits. It organizes $p$-adic congruence towers and shows, for a Cantor-type non-Archimedean Julia set, that classical periodic points can be dense although the internal periodic locus is not isomorphic to the compact condensed Julia set.

Classical Bulgarian solitaire tracks only the sizes of the stacks. We ask how the lengths of its periodic orbits change when individual cards are distinguished. To study this question, we introduce four actions $T_1,T_2,T_3,T_4$ on partitions with labeled cells. The actions differ in whether the top or bottom cell is removed from each column and in the order in which the removed cells are arranged to form a new column. We determine the exact sizes of the periodic orbits for all four actions. The main work lies in the analysis of $T_2$, for which we develop a coloring algorithm on Ferrers diagrams. The coloring encodes the cycle structure of the permutation of the labels induced by one full period of the underlying partition.
High-order long-time stable methods for the forced incompressible Navier--Stokes equations
Fukeng Huang; Jie Shen; Xiaoming Wang

We present in this paper two scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) correction steps for constructing long-time stable schemes for the forced incompressible Navier--Stokes equations with no-slip boundary conditions. A main feature is that the same correction steps apply to any linear predictor satisfying the order and spatial regularity requirements in Assumption~P. Their construction and stability analysis are independent of the particular form of the predictor and require no energy estimate for it. The first correction uses a damped, shifted kinetic-energy variable to obtain a uniform-in-time $L^2$ bound in two and three dimensions, together with a weighted dissipation estimate. In two dimensions, the second correction combines a higher-energy auxiliary variable with a scalar relaxation to yield a uniform-in-time $H^1$ bound. Under the stated assumptions, these estimates hold on arbitrary positive time grids, without restrictions on step sizes or adjacent step ratios. We also derive eventual absorbing bounds; for the two-SAV scheme, these apply to the admissible initial class associated with fixed parameters. The generalized BDF schemes require one constant-coefficient Helmholtz solve per velocity component and one pressure Poisson solve per step; the second correction adds no field solve. Numerical experiments exhibit second-, third-, and fourth-order convergence for the tested BDF schemes and illustrate the long-time stability and efficiency of adaptive time stepping.
Extendability of general prime $K3$ surfaces without Gaussian maps and classification of prime Fano threefolds
Jayan Mukherjee; with an appendix written jointly with Anand Deopurkar

In arXiv:2409.03960 an approach to the question of extendability of projective varieties via degeneration to ribbons was introduced, and in arXiv:2503.12661 it was used to give a new proof of optimal results on the extendability of general non-prime $K3$ surfaces and the classification of non-prime Fano threefolds. In this article we treat the prime case. We give a new proof of the optimal results on the extendability of general prime $K3$ surfaces of every genus, of the classification of prime Fano threefolds of Picard rank one due to Fano, Iskovskikh and Mukai, and of the irreducibility of their Hilbert schemes. This involves degenerations of $K3$ surfaces to ribbons on embedded rational normal scrolls, called $K3$ carpets. We compute exactly the cohomology of the twisted normal bundle of these $K3$ carpets, instead of computing coranks of Gaussian maps of the canonical curve sections. The key challenge is to analyze the coboundary map of the sequence relating the normal bundle of the $K3$ carpet to the normal bundle of the scroll. We give a deformation theoretic interpretation of this map. Given such a $K3$ carpet and its hyperplane section, which is a canonical ribbon, we show that the coboundary map corresponds to the obstruction to lifting a first order deformation of the underlying scroll fixing the underlying rational normal curve to a first order deformation of the $K3$ carpet fixing the canonical ribbon. To compute the obstruction, we use a result on extensions of non-split ribbons on any curve to a unique $K$-trivial carpet in a canonical way.
Nonexistence of positive solutions stable outside a compact set for the Lane--Emden system in a half-space
Zetao Cheng; Long-Han Huang; Wenming Zou

We prove that, in every dimension and for all positive exponents, the Lane--Emden system in a half-space with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions admits no positive classical solution stable outside a compact set.
Birational Geometry of K-Moduli Spaces of Genus Four Curves
Kenneth Ascher; Kristin DeVleming; Hongyu Luo; Yuchen Liu; Junyan Zhao

We study the wall-crossings for K-moduli spaces of (3,3)-curves on $\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$. Together with the boundary polarized Calabi--Yau moduli space, these spaces interpolate between the GIT moduli space of (3,3)-curves and the Baily--Borel compactification of the moduli space of K3 surfaces arising as cyclic triple covers of $\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$ branched along such curves. As applications, we describe the corresponding birational models in the Hassett--Keel--Looijenga program and realize the K-moduli space of degree one del Pezzo surfaces through explicit wall-crossings.
Directional Ergodic Theorems, Ergodicity, and Weak mixing for $\mathbb Z^2$-actions
Chunlin Liu; Kairan Liu; Tao Yu

In this paper, we study Birkhoff and von Neumann type ergodic theorems for $\mathbb Z^2$-measure preserving systems along irrational directions. This leads us to a further investigation of directional ergodicity and weak mixing. Additionally, we show that our framework (dynamical definitions) is equivalent to the spectral definitions of directional ergodicity and weak mixing introduced by Robinson, Rosenblatt and Şahin \cite{RRS2023} for $\mathbb Z^2$-actions. We note that in their recent paper \cite{RS2026}, Robinson and Şahin established the equivalence between dynamical and spectral directional weak mixing for $\mathbb Z^2$-actions using an approach fundamentally different from the one employed in the present paper.
Sharp Logarithmic-Product Bounds for List Replicability of Sign Matrices

List replicability measures how many accurate hypotheses suffice to contain the output of a learning rule with arbitrarily high confidence. We prove that every nonempty class of $m$ binary concepts on $n$ domain points has list replicability at most $805\ln(2m)\ln(2n)$. This resolves the logarithmic-product conjecture of Blondal, Hatami, Hatami, Lalov, and Tretiak. Hanner matrices give lower bounds of the same order, for square matrices and for explicit families with unequal logarithmic aspect ratios. The upper bound is obtained by constructing nested acyclic sets in the faces of a cube. A critical-point estimate supplies highly connected regions, weighted cell attachments keep the sets compatible across faces, and a cubical carrier theorem converts them into accurate finite covers and learning rules. Appending one constant coordinate turns list replicability into an exact geometric quantity, the face width, and graph-orientation classes satisfy exact product formulas. In particular, there are explicit classes with list replicability $4k+1$ and equivariant index $3k$, so the additive gap between the two is unbounded. We also develop entropy-tilting and two-sided Gibbs constructions, give combinatorial upper bounds adapted to structured matrices, compute exact values on classical families, and study the index of Paley matrices.
Basis selection, universal sampling discretization, and sampling recovery
Feng Dai; Jiashu Ran; Vladimir N. Temlyakov

For every real $N$-dimensional subspace of $L_2$, we construct one orthonormal basis such that, for every $1\le v\le N$, at most $Cv\log(eN/v)$ positively weighted samples discretize the squared $L_2$ norm of all $v$-term combinations. Random rotations also give simultaneous weighted $L_p$ estimates and a sharp $C\log(eN)$ bound for the squared $L_2$ norm of the pointwise maximum. For prescribed coefficient classes, a change of measure yields sampling recovery estimates from $Cv\log^3(2v)$ samples under a lower Riesz inequality and a common square-integrable pointwise bound.
Discrete-Time Zero-Sum Markov Games with Control, Stopping, and State-Dependent Discounting

We study a discrete-time two-player zero-sum stochastic game with control and stopping, where both players can stop the game, the discount factors depends on the states, and the running and terminal rewards may be unbounded. A contraction argument for the constrained Shapley equation establishes the existence of the value and a Nash equilibrium consisting of stationary controls and stopping times. We further provides algorithms for approximating the value and computing an $\varepsilon$-Nash equilibrium. A numerical example with state-dependent discount factors illustrates the results.
Metric nefness of direct image sheaves under weakly semi-stable Kähler morphisms

We investigate the nefness of the direct image sheaves of relative adjoint bundles under weakly semi-stable Kähler morphisms between complex spaces. We show that the direct image sheaves are locally free and that their tautological line bundles are metrically nef, strengthening the previously known results on torsion-freeness and certain weak positivity.
Weighted Logarithm Laws in non-commutative Probability

We prove analogues of weighted laws of iterated logarithm and laws of logarithm for non-commutative martingales and independent random variables respectively. First we obtain a weighted LIL for non-commutative martingales, extending the sharp unweighted result of arXiv:2509.22037v2 to the case for polynomial weights, then by approximation to a broader class of functions. Then we proved a weighted law of logarithm for triangular array of weights and replacing the coefficient in the denominator by regularly varying functions with index $α$. We show that the normalised sums converge to 0 for $α> 1/2$ and for the case $α=1/2$, we obtain the sharp upper bound with constant $\sqrt{2}$.

Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a finite tensor category with exactly one isomorphism class of simple objects which are non-invertible. Semisimple tensor categories $\mathcal{D}$ with this property are called near-group categories, and have been studied by Evans, Gannon, Siehler and others. In this paper, we study such categories in the non-semisimple setting, with the additional assumption that the non-invertible simple object is projective. Specifically, we consider the case when $\mathcal{D}$ admits a fiber functor and has a unique semisimple abelian block (in the general case that $\D$ is not semisimple). We describe the structure of such categories and their corresponding Hopf algebras, and construct examples of such categories with a cyclic Picard group. We obtain additional results when the Frobenius-Perron dimension of the unique non-invertible simple object is a prime number.
Polynomial conjugacy invariants of pseudo-Anosov maps derived from train track representatives

We investigate two kinds of polynomials associated with pseudo-Anosov maps. Each kind consists of three polynomials that are conjugacy invariants of pseudo-Anosov mapping classes and these polynomials contain more information than pseudo-Anosov stretch factors. The first kind is defined by the train track representatives. The second kind is obtained from the first kind by incorporating additional data that encode the transitions among the unpunctured singularities of the invariant foliations. The Birman-Brinkmann-Kawamuro polynomials coincide with those of the second kind. As an application, we prove that the Birman-Brinkmann-Kawamuro polynomials are conjugacy invariants of pseudo-Anosov mapping classes which is also proved by Dodge-Kawamuro, independently.
How good are spline spaces for the Kolmogorov $n$-width of a Sobolev ball?

This paper studies the approximation power of polynomial splines on a uniform one-dimensional mesh. The quality of the best approximation of the unit ball of $H^{s}$ by an $n$-dimensional subspace, measured in the $L^{2}$ norm, is quantified by the sup-inf of that space: for each function in the Sobolev ball, take its minimal approximation error over the space, and then take the supremum of these errors over the ball. The infimum of this sup-inf over all $n$-dimensional spaces is the well-known Kolmogorov $n$-width $d_{n}$. Choosing the $n$-dimensional subspace to be the piecewise polynomial space of degree $k$ with smoothness $C^μ$ ($-1\leμ\le k-1$) gives our sup-inf $E$. The approximation accuracy of spline spaces is then examined by comparing $d_{n}$ and $E$. The two quantities are determined by two eigenvalue problems, through which we obtain a lower bound for $d_{n}$ and an upper bound for $E$. Under the restriction $k\ge s-1$, the upper bound for the error of the maximally smooth spline space ($μ=k-1$) is asymptotically equal to the lower bound for $d_n$, showing that uniform $B$-splines are asymptotically optimal among all $n$-dimensional spaces. For $μ<k-1$, we prove that $E/d_n$ is bounded below by a constant strictly larger than $1$, except when $k>s-1$ and $μ=k-2$ hold simultaneously. Simulating Nonlinear Resistive Networks using a Behavioral Splitting

An operator splitting method is developed for computing operating points of nonlinear resistive networks. Our behavioral formulation separates the device laws from Kirchhoff's laws and casts simulation as a zero-finding problem. Branch port resistances then provide a diagonal preconditioner for the relaxed Peaceman-Rachford iteration in scattering variables. Each iteration requires solving independent scalar equations and a linear system with a fixed weighted Laplacian matrix. Convergence is established for maximal monotone device laws when an operating point exists. Contractive branch reflections also yield a linear convergence bound independent of network topology. Numerical experiments on crossbar arrays illustrate the computational advantages.
Divide-and-Conquer is Tail- and Anomaly-Robust: Factor Model Estimation Without Moment Constraints

We study robust estimation of elliptical factor models with abnormal observations and without requiring the existence of any positive moments. Quenched large deviation estimates for skew product systems with the almost-sure fiber specification property

We establish quenched level-2 large deviation estimates for empirical measures of measurable skew products with compact metric fibers over an invertible ergodic measure-preserving transformation on a Polish space. Critical Branching Systems with General Lifetimes: Hunt Motions and Applications to Semilinear Equations

Vázquez Strong Maximum Principle and Compact Support Principle for singular and degenerate elliptical operators

In this paper, we present adaptations of the classical strong maximum principle and the compact support principle for a certain class of equations, with particular emphasis on the degeneracy of fully nonlinear operators and a new Vázquez-type condition on the nonhomogeneous term. The novelty of our approach lies in the framework of the problem: the coefficients of the operators are bounded, but we introduce a degeneracy depending on the power of the gradient of the solution. Moreover, the source term $f$ on the right-hand side of the equation is treated under a adapted and optimal integrability assumptions.
On the Vázquez Strong Maximum Principle for Linear and Nonlinear Elliptic Equations with Unbounded Coefficients and Optimal Conditions

In this paper, we present adaptations of the classical strong maximum principle for a certain class of equations, with particular emphasis on linear operators in non-divergence form and a new strategy to prove it. The novelty of our approach lies in the setting of the problem: the coefficients of the operators are unbounded, assumed to be merely integrable in the $L^{p,q}$-sense, and the source term $f$ on the right-hand side of the equation is treated under optimal integrability assumptions.

Gonzalez, Rossegger, and Turetsky introduced a spectrum-counting function $F(n)$ for the Scott complexities realized by $Π^{\mathrm{in}}_2$ theories with exactly $n$ countable models. They proved $7\leq F(4)\leq 8$ and left the exact value open. We prove $F(4)=8$. More precisely, we construct a $Π^{\mathrm{in}}_2$ sentence with exactly four countable models whose optimal Scott complexities are $Π^{\mathrm{in}}_2$, $Σ^{\mathrm{in}}_3$, $Π^{\mathrm{in}}_3$, and $d\text{-}Σ^{\mathrm{in}}_3$, one of each. First, in a small theory, a $Σ^{\mathrm{in}}_3$ Scott sentence forces a model to be prime over a finite tuple; after Morleyization the converse holds. Second, if a model realizes every complete finite-tuple type over the empty set, then every $Π^{\mathrm{in}}_3$ sentence true in it is true in the countable saturated model. These two principles force the four models into the four distinct Scott-complexity classes above.

We realize Hironaka's generalized lantern relations by lifting positive braid factorizations. For a nonpencil real line arrangement with no parallel lines, we construct a family of branched coverings on the regular fibers of a blown-up pencil of spheres. The motion of the branch points gives a factorization of a power of the full twist into least liftable powers of half-twists. The Artal-Carmona-Cogolludo-Marco Zariski pair gives two such factorizations of the same braid for a single simple branched covering of the disk. Their lifts are Hurwitz inequivalent even up to simultaneous conjugation by page homeomorphisms. The corresponding Milnor fibers fill the same planar contact three-manifold and have the same incidence matrix. They are homeomorphic and lie in distinct strong symplectic deformation classes.

The dimension conjecture in CR geometry is proved for an arbitrary real-analytic hypersurface. More precisely, we prove that the dimension of the algebra of infinitesimal holomorphic automorphisms of a germ of a holomorphically nondegenerate hypersurface in $\mathbb{C}^N$ in this class does not exceed $N^2+2N$. This number is exactly the corresponding dimension for any nondegenerate hyperquadric in the same ambient space. Moreover, equality holds if and only if the germ is equivalent to a hyperquadric.

Boundedness of a family implies boundedness of each member; in particular, boundedness of {T_emptyset,T_{3}} would imply that no Collatz orbit diverges. For {T_emptyset,T_{1}}, a rule depending only on x mod 32 has positive drift (10/17)log_2(9/8) for almost every 2-adic starting point. Thus almost all n have reachable sets containing values larger than n^1.05; residues modulo 2^L, L<=10, cannot prove unboundedness. Finally, we define unified maps in which valuations also determine the direction at odd inputs. The cases x=1 mod 4 govern their behavior: if they go down, every block is dominated by the corresponding Collatz map (and a census finds only the cycles (1), (2, 3) and (3, 5) with smallest element below 10^9); if they go up, the maps behave like T_S.
A metric characterization of free unitary quantum groups

Mobility Information Capacity of Multi-Robot Systems: Safety-Aware Maneuver Design

Multiple robots operating in shared workspaces must adjust their speed, direction, and trajectories to coordinate with one another and respond to changing tasks and disturbances. We further map workspace-boundary, inter-robot separation, and actuator chance constraints into coupled maneuver-covariance restrictions and derive conditions under which covariance optimization reduces to resource allocation across mobility modes. Finite joint maneuver codebooks are then constructed through individual risk screening and noise-whitened trajectory separation, with bounds linking sequence recovery error and achieved information to the capacity benchmarks. We analyze adaptive sampling stochastic model-based trust-region methods that build their models in random subspaces and use common random numbers (CRN) within an iteration, and obtain, within a STORM-type analysis, the first $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\varepsilon^{-4})$ bound on the number of function evaluations needed to reach $\varepsilon$-stationarity, both almost surely and in expectation. (2019). The bounds are obtained for two variants of a stochastic model-based trust-region method that differ in how the function evaluations used to measure progress are generated. To our knowledge, no STORM-type analysis has been able to accommodate the latter approach as the accuracy of an estimate at a point chosen from the samples cannot be assessed conditionally on the model; we overcome this with a probabilistic chaining argument.
Calculation and Recurrence Relations of the Determinants of the Hessenberg - Toeplitz Matrices

The determinant D(n) of a n x n Hessenberg - Toeplitz matrix is given as product of certain functions of its elements. A compact expression of D(n) is presented and recurrence relations involving determinants and matrix elements of the Hessenberg -Toeplitz matrices are found.
Costate-Conditioned Dynamic Programming for Parallel-in-Time Solution of Equality-Constrained Optimal Control Problems

When interior-point methods are applied to solve numerical trajectory optimisation problems, they spend most of their per-iteration time on a structured Newton--KKT system, associated to an equality-constrained linear-quadratic optimal control problem. Riccati-type algorithms exhibit linear complexity in the trajectory horizon. Parallel-in-time algorithms are able to reduce this to logaritmic complexity by distributing several subtrajectories over multiple cores and then stitch together the results by means of an associative scan. Existing exact formulations condition each subtrajectory on its terminal state. Each subproblem then carries the reachability to that terminal state explicitly as constraint rows. The associated reachability decision however is ill-conditioned for weakly actuated systems. In this work we condition each subtrajectory on the terminal costate instead. The resulting subproblems can now be computed by a free-end Riccati recursion without reachability carrying rows. This approach effectively compensates for the ill-conditioning of weakly actuated systems but requires additional bookkeeping with Lagrangian multipliers when stitching together the various subproblems. Numerically the method reproduces a direct solution of the primal-dual Newton-KKT system to $10^{-12}$ in relative terms, on a weakly controllable chain of masses, the accurracy rivals that of a sequential recursion, whereas terminal-state conditioning loses up to six digits or fails. Operation counts on a problem with 64 subtrajectories and a horizon of 4096 stages gives a speed-up of 26 compared with a sequential solve.
Memoryless BFGS on a nonsmooth convex function: two new results

We extend the analysis of Asl and Overton~\cite{AO2021} for memoryless BFGS (also known as L-BFGS-1) using an Armijo-Wolfe line search and applied to the nonsmooth convex function $f(x)=a|x^{(1)}|+\sum_{i=2}^n x^{(i)}$, where $n\ge2$ and $a \geq \sqrt{n-1}$. This function is unbounded below, so the method is successful if it generates function values diverging to $-\infty$, and fails otherwise. For scaled L-BFGS-1, we sharpen the sufficient condition for % az{convergence of the absolute normalized search directions} in Theorem~3.1 of failure in \cite{AO2021} from $a\ge2\sqrt{n-1}$ to $a\ge\sqrt{3(n-1)}$. For the unscaled version, we prove success for every $a$: either the method generates a direction along which no Armijo-Wolfe step exists, certifying unboundedness below, or its function values diverge to $-\infty$. Both results are consistent with the numerical experiments in \cite{AO2021}. Both proofs given here were derived with help from GPT 6 in discussions directed by the first author and corrected and rephrased afterward.
Convergence of Adaptive Least Squares Finite Element Methods

We consider a general class of operator equations $\mathcal B u=f$ where $\mathcal B:\mathbb U\to \mathbb L_2$ is a linear isomorphis from a Hilbert space $\mathbb U$ onto an ``$L_2$-type'' space $\mathbb L_2 = L_2(Ω;\mathbb R^q)$. This covers weak first order formulations of stationary elliptic boundary value problems, the Stokes system or systems for linear elasticity as well as space-time formulations of heat or wave equations. Since an $L_2$-residual is uniformly equivalent to the corresponding error in the trial space norm reliable and efficient computable a posteriori error bounds are for free. In contrast to a matured theory of classical adaptive finite element methods, estblishing linear convergence - and eventually optimal complexity - in a least squares setting seems to have remained open. To a large extent this is due to the fact that least squares error indicators do not exhibit any explicit dependence on local mesh-sizes. In this paper we propose a rather different approach to establish under which circumstances standard Dörfler-marking mesh refinement gives rise to linear convergence and rate optimality of adaptive least squares finite element methods as well. A central role is played by a new notion of {\em data-visibility} which is a structural property of the data rather than a smoothness condition.
Patrick Dendis; David L. Duncan; Timothy Tarter; Lior Weber; Colin Willette

A group action on a topological space induces an action on the space's representation variety. We determine the fixed point sets of this latter action for semifree group actions on surfaces and circle bundles over surfaces. We also discuss implications for mapping tori of periodic maps.
Full fillings at the accumulation point and triangular limits of almost toric diagrams

The ellipsoid embedding function of $M$ has an infinite staircase if it has infinitely many nonsmooth points. Cristofaro-Gardiner, Holm, Mandini, and Pires showed that these points must then accumulate at a solution of an explicit quadratic equation, and that at this accumulation point the ellipsoid embedding function agrees with the volume obstruction. We call this a full filling at the accumulation point, and study it in terms of almost toric fibrations. We show that if $M$ admits a sequence of almost toric base diagrams, each with a Delzant corner, converging nontrivially to a triangle, then $M$ has a full filling at its accumulation point. For the one-point blowups $H_b$ of $\mathbb{CP}^2$, we also prove the converse. As a consequence, $H_b$ has an infinite staircase if and only if it admits such a sequence converging to a triangle whose hypotenuse has irrational slope.

The only example known in even dimension, on six bits, was found from a quadratic APN function that is not itself a permutation, by Carlet--Charpin--Zinoviev (CCZ) equivalence. It is therefore natural to test APN functions for CCZ-equivalence to a permutation. This amounts to finding two complementary $n$-dimensional subspaces among the zeros of the Walsh transform, which lie in $\mathbb{F}_2^{2n}$. A known necessary condition only uses their projections to $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ and cannot decide every case. We give an exact test for functions whose Walsh supports are affine, including all quadratic functions. It reconstructs the subspaces from their projections, through searches for subspaces of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ and for constrained bilinear maps. On the benchmarked functions in dimension twelve, it lists them $39$ to $55$ times faster than the generic search of the commonly used sboxU library. With their result, our computations show that this holds for every even $n\le 24$. In dimension $18$ the necessary condition is satisfied, and the new test decides the case. Transport Less, Solve Faster: Exploiting sparsity in algorithm design for Unbalanced Optimal Transport

Let phi_m be the monic Chebyshev polynomial characterized by phi_m(t + t^-1) = t^m + t^-m. We study the geometric automorphism groups of the smooth projective models of y^n = phi_m(x) and y^p - y = phi_m(x). For every m >= 5, with p not dividing m in positive characteristic, we determine the projective stabilizer of the roots of phi_m together with infinity. For tame Kummer covers, we describe the normalizer of the cyclic deck group and compute it explicitly for m >= 6. It is the full group when m > 2n. We also establish finite jet stability, real-analytic dependence, and global $C^0$-stability of order $O(\varepsilon_F^{1/k})$. The microstructure of information through mean field learning interaction

We study how knowledge about partially observable model parameters is being created and propagated in large scale systems. Information is generated from observational signals whose dynamics depend endogenously on the learning history, the learning duration, the decisions and the related costs encountered by a continuum of decision makers. Such characteristics give rise to a new class of sequential testing problems in which there is continuous endogenous feedback. Adopting the classical approach of Shiryaev, we relate the problem to an optimal stopping one for the representative belief process, whose generator now depends on the evolving interactions. Considering a fixed point for the latter, we introduce a notion of mean field game and prove the existence of an equilibrium. Our arguments, which are based on a combination of pde and probabilistic techniques, involve a detailed analysis of the underlying variational inequality and the geometry, stability and continuity of the free boundaries.

In this paper, we exhibit both of these 4-periodicities as consequences of an isomorphism of two extraspecial groups of order 32.

Existing bilevel algorithms typically assume that the LL objective is available for evaluation, differentiation, or unrolling. However, this assumption can fail when the LL response is produced by a black-box solver, simulator, adversary, or learned predictor. In this paper, we study LL agnostic bilevel optimization, where the UL learner has access only to an approximate LL solution $\bar{\mathbf{y}}(\mathbf{x})$ and cannot query the LL objective, its gradients, Hessian/Jacobian information, or the procedure that generates the LL response. We study Turing instability in a closed Nutrient-Phytoplankton-Zooplankton-Detritus (NPZD) ecosystem model with nutrient recycling, formulated as a reaction-diffusion system without an explicit time-delay. The detritus compartment represents the biomass during the recycling process and acts to introduce a time delay in this process. Total biomass in the system is conserved, leading to a closed model. Although spatial diffusion typically promotes stability, our focus is on understanding how different diffusion rates for different species can destabilize steady states and give rise to spatial patterns. To address this, we first perform linear stability analysis to identify conditions under which Turing instability may occur. We then validate these theoretical predictions through numerical simulations. Our approach develops both intuition and rigorous analysis of how diffusion influences instabilities in the context of a conservative system, offering a comprehensive framework for understanding pattern formation in multi-species plankton ecosystems.
The Whitney Extension Problem in Carnot groups
Marjorie Drake; Arie Israel; Scott Zimmerman

Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a Carnot group, let $E \subset \mathbb{G}$ be compact, and suppose we are given a function $f: E \to \mathbb{R}$. The $C^1_H$ {\em Whitney Extension Problem} asks the following: what must be true about $f$ to guarantee that there exists a smooth, horizontal function $F \in C^1_H(\mathbb{G})$ extending $f$, i.e., there is some $F:\mathbb{G} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $F|_E = f|_E$ and $XF$ is continuous for every horizontal left invariant vector field $X$? We adapt the method of G. Glaeser and C. Fefferman to answer this question in this non-commutative setting. Moreover, we provide an alternative solution to the $C^1$ Whitney Extension Problem for horizontal curves in the Heisenberg group.
DisMUSE: An Efficient Distributed Singular-Spectrum-Based Optimization Approach with Theoretical Convergence Guarantee
Zhen Qin; Zhiyao Zhang; Yingbin Liang; Jia Liu
