We prove that for every countable group $Γ$, in the space of nonsingular actions by $Γ$, there is an action whose orbit under conjugation is dense. This is the nonsingular analogue of the result of Glasner, Thouvenot, and Weiss that every countable group $Γ$ is weak Rokhlin, i.e., there is a dense orbit in the space of probability measure preserving $Γ$-actions.
Isolated yet highly unstable 2D Euler equilibria
Alberto Enciso; Antonio J. Fernández; Marc Nualart

We construct steady solutions of the two-dimensional Euler equations on smooth annular domains that are isolated, modulo scaling, in the $L^\infty$ vorticity topology. They are highly unstable: any Yudovich trajectory remaining sufficiently close to such an equilibrium on an open time interval is a stationary multiple of it and, moreover, at fixed energy, enstrophy and circulations, distinct nearby trajectories cannot return even weakly to the equilibrium. Further, on any non-circular annulus, we show that this kind of isolated, highly unstable equilibria occurs arbitrarily close in the Yudovich norm to smooth equilibria which are themselves non-isolated.
Sharp isoperimetry in groups of polynomial growth

We study weighted edge boundary and outer vertex boundary on Cayley graphs of polynomial growth of degree $Q>1$. For every finite symmetric generating set, we prove that each exact isoperimetric profile satisfies $I(n)=c n^{(Q-1)/Q}+O(n^{(Q-1)/Q-β})$, where $β=1/(8Q^2)$. We identify the leading constant with the isoperimetric constant of a horizontal perimeter on the limiting Carnot group, after accounting for the counting density. Its integrand is a norm with polyhedral unit ball, determined by a convex minimization with one real variable for each coset of a torsion-free nilpotent subgroup. For every asymptotically minimizing sequence, we translate its vertex sets so that the characteristic functions of the associated rescaled regions are precompact in $L^1$. The limiting regions minimize continuum perimeter at fixed volume. The exact-cardinality estimate requires no regularity assumption on these regions. For virtually abelian groups, we prove a quantitative stability estimate using a discrete approximation to the Euclidean Wulff body. The relative symmetric difference from a translate is bounded by the square root of the sum of the relative boundary deficit and a cardinality error. We also characterize when bounded additive changes of Cayley metric preserve the leading vertex constant. Failure occurs already in rank two; we construct pairs with the same measured asymptotic cone whose leading constants have an unbounded ratio as the rank grows.
Asymptotic behavior of solutions to the critical $p$-Laplace equation near isolated singularities

In this paper, we study the asymptotic behavior of weak solutions to the following critical $p$-Laplace equation \[ -Δ_p u=u^{p^*-1}, \quad u\ge0 \quad\hbox{in }B_1\setminus\{0\}, \] where $Δ_pu=\diver(|\nabla u|^{p-2}\nabla u)$ is the classical $p$-Laplacian with $1<p<n$, $p^*=\frac{np}{n-p}$ is the Sobolev critical exponent and $B_1\setminus\{0\}\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ is the punctured unit ball. We develop a nonlinear potential-theoretic method to establish sharp upper bounds for solutions, without using the method of moving planes or moving spheres. Furthermore, we use Steiner symmetrization to study the radial symmetry of global singular solutions, and thereby classify all Fowler singular solutions. Finally, we prove that every local singular solution is asymptotic to a global Fowler singular solution.
Trace and Regularized Index of Callias Operators on Hyperbolic Space

Let $d \geq 3$ be odd. On hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^d$, we consider Callias-type operators, i.e. Dirac-Schrödinger operators of the form $D = ic \nabla + A$, where $c \nabla$ is the Dirac operator and $A$ a function with values in the self-adjoint operators, and provide an explicit formula for the iterated trace $\text{tr}_{L^2(\mathbb{H}^d,H)} \text{tr}_{S}( e^{-tD^*D} - e^{-tDD^*})$, $t>0$, that appears in the formulation of the Witten index. Thereby, the operator $D$ is not assumed to be Fredholm.
EDP-PI-DOSnet: An Energy Dissipation Preserving Neural Solver for Two-Phase Flow Problems
Jizu Huang; Yue Qian; Tao Zhou

Preserving the energy dissipation properties of gradient flow equations is important for the stability and reliability of numerical approximations, particularly in long-time simulations. In this paper, we propose a class of energy-dissipation-preserving physics-informed deep operator splitting networks (EDP-PI-DOSnets) for solving gradient flow equations. The proposed framework incorporates classical structure-preserving numerical schemes into neural network architectures, allowing the corresponding discrete energy dissipation laws to be preserved. In particular, suitable constraints are imposed on the convolution kernels to ensure that the learned discrete operators are symmetric and negative semidefinite. Furthermore, several network formulations are developed based on the Crank--Nicolson (CN), scalar auxiliary variable Crank--Nicolson (SAV/CN), and relaxed discrete variational derivative (R-DVD-1) schemes. Meanwhile, a physics-informed loss function based on the residuals of the governing equations is employed. Numerical experiments show that the predicted solutions are in good agreement with the reference solutions while satisfying the corresponding discrete energy dissipation laws. The results also suggest stable behavior during long-time recursive prediction and the potential applicability of the proposed framework to two-phase flow problems.
Kolmogorov Obstacle Problems: Euclidean Free Boundary Regularity under a Cone Condition
Junkee Jeon; Takwon Kim; Jehan Oh

We study obstacle problems for Kolmogorov-type operators that diffuse in one variable and transport in another. Such problems describe American options on running averages. Under a cone estimate, a strong monotonicity condition on the solution in the diffusive direction, we show that the free boundary is a graph in the diffusive direction with Hölder continuous first derivatives in the Euclidean sense, and that every free boundary point is regular. The key observation is that a Euclidean Lipschitz free boundary is flat at the intrinsic scale. For the American fixed-strike Asian option we verify the cone estimate, so that its exercise boundary has the same regularity.
Fluctuations of heat kernels and exit times on random graphs and application to the critical long-range percolation
Zherui Fan; Lu-Jing Huang; Takashi Kumagai

Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a graph equipped with random conductance. We give sufficient conditions for the Markov chain on $\mathcal{G}$ to exhibit large scale fluctuations in its on-diagonal heat kernel and in exit times. The conditions also imply non-tightness of the height process w.r.t. the quenched measure, while it is tight w.r.t. the annealed measure. As an application of the general theory, we prove large scale fluctuations for the simple random walk on $1$-dimensional critical long-range percolation.
Robust Bayes-like estimation of the distribution of a determinantal process

We consider the problem of estimating the distribution of a determinantal process (DP) on a measured space from the observation of $n$ independent copies of it. Our estimator is obtained by sampling from a $T$-posterior distribution associated with a suitable prior, and we establish non-asymptotic risk bounds for the Hellinger loss which hold with high probability. These bounds remain valid when the data are only independent rather than i.i.d., and when the model is misspecified, which makes the estimator robust, for instance, to the presence of a small fraction of outliers. For determinantal projection processes of rank $k$ whose kernels are associated with $k$-dimensional subspaces of a $D$-dimensional space, Haar priors on Grassmannians lead to a rate of order $\sqrt{k(D-k)\log n/n}$, and model selection extends this result to infinite-dimensional settings. For general DPs, we introduce priors based on the spectral decomposition of the kernel that combine uniform distributions on the eigenvalues with Haar measures on Stiefel manifolds. When the underlying space is finite with $N$ elements, we obtain a rate of order $N\sqrt{\log n/n}$, without any assumption on the kernel, and derive that the $2^{N}$ principal minors of the kernel can be estimated simultaneously. Finally, for translation-invariant DPs on the torus $\mathbb{T}^d$, we obtain rates that only depend on the smoothness of the kernel at the origin and that are adaptive with respect to it. Combined with a new lower bound on the Hellinger distance between such DPs, these rates also yield estimators of the kernel in $\mathbb{L}_2$.
The covariety of numerical semigroups with some prescribed pseudo-Frobenius numbers
William Giovanni Hernández-Yanes; José Carlos Rosales

If $S$ is a numerical semigroup, then we denote by $m(S)$, $F(S)$ and $\mathrm{PF}(S)$ its multiplicity, its Frobenius number and its set of pseudo-Frobenius numbers, respectively. Let $\mathcal P$ be a finite nonempty set of positive integers. In this paper, we prove that $\mathcal C(\mathcal P)=\{S\mid F(S)=\max(\mathcal P),\ \mathcal P\subseteq\mathrm{PF}(S)\}$ is a covariety. The associated tree provides algorithms to compute $\mathcal C(\mathcal P)$, its elements with a prescribed type or genus, and the set of numerical semigroups $S$ satisfying $\mathrm{PF}(S)=\mathcal P$. We show that every element of $\mathcal C(\mathcal P)$ has a unique minimal system of generators relative to $\mathcal C(\mathcal P)$, and we call its cardinality the $\mathcal C(\mathcal P)$-rank. Finally, we characterize the elements of $\mathcal C(\mathcal P)$ with $\mathcal C(\mathcal P)$-rank one.
Improved Approximation and Hardness Bounds for $β$-TSP
Paul Liu; Jack Spalding-Jamieson; Da Wei Zheng

The traveling salesman problem (TSP) asks for a minimum-length Hamiltonian cycle in a complete weighted graph. Its approximability depends on the edge lengths: unrestricted instances admit no constant-factor approximation unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$, metric instances admit Christofides' $3/2$-approximation, and fixed-dimensional Euclidean instances admit a PTAS. We study $β$-TSP, where the edge lengths satisfy $ \ell_{uw}\leqβ(\ell_{uv}+\ell_{vw}) \qquad \forall\,u,v,w\in V\ \text{pairwise distinct}, \quad β\in\left[\tfrac{1}{2},1\right]. $ The condition arises naturally in various settings, for example, when metric travel times are combined with positive service times at the vertices. The previous best approximation algorithm, due to Böckenhauer et al., ranges from $1$ at $β=1/2$ to $3/2$ as $β$ approaches $1$. We obtain a strictly better guarantee for every $1/2<β<1$ by combining two simple constructions whose guarantees counterbalance each other. We also improve the best known approximation hardness bound for every $1/2<β<1$.
Zak Phase, Pole--Zero Invariants and the Maslov Index of Bloch Cauchy Lines in One-Dimensional Periodic Media

The topological properties of the Bloch bands of a one-dimensional periodic medium are described either by the Berry--Zak phase or by the poles and zeros of the surface impedance. We show that both can be read from one geometric object: the line spanned by the field and its flux (the Cauchy data) at an inversion centre. For each band, this line turns as the quasi-momentum runs over the Brillouin zone. Its number of turns, the Maslov index, is fixed by the parities (even or odd) of the Bloch functions at the two band edges, and its parity is the Zak phase. In a gap, the Cauchy line of the solution decaying on one side rotates monotonically with the energy, and an interface state between two crystals is a crossing of two such lines. This gives the known criterion of at most one state per gap in terms of the same lines. Examples with a stratified medium show that the choice of inversion centre changes the interface spectrum. The last section discusses what is missing to extend the construction to higher dimension.
A 4-regular graph with 4/5 of its vertices satisfying the Šoltés property

The Wiener index $W(G)$ of a connected graph $G$ is the sum of distances between all unordered pairs of its vertices. A vertex $v$ is called a Šoltés vertex if $G-v$ is connected and $W(G-v)=W(G)$. Since the cycle $C_{11}$ is the only known graph in which every vertex is a Šoltés vertex, a natural problem is to construct other graphs with as large a proportion of such vertices as possible. We construct a $4$-regular graph with Šoltés fraction $4/5$, improving the previous value of $2/3$.
Inclusions and intersections of products of verbally prime $T$-ideals

We study inclusions and intersections of products of verbally prime $T$-ideals over a field of characteristic zero. Our main tool is a Vandermonde-type construction of graded polynomials with a uniformly bounded number of variables. Together with a reduction to finite exterior algebras, this construction yields separating polynomials that work uniformly under bounds on Grassmann envelope representations. We prove that, under these bounds, an intersection of $T$-ideals is contained in such a product only if one member is. This proves Berele's Conjecture~3 and, consequently, his Conjecture~1 \cite{Berele2012}. We also characterize inclusions between ordered products by an explicit combinatorial criterion, proving his Conjecture~2 and answering his Question~2 \cite{Berele2012}. These results characterize inclusions between arbitrary intersections of products of nonzero proper verbally prime $T$-ideals and show that every nonzero such intersection has a unique finite irredundant representation. As an application, we characterize finite quivers whose path algebras have the same polynomial identities as some, equivalently every, positive power of their arrow ideals.
Curves with absolutely irreducible Tate modules over $p$-adic fields

Over every number field, curves whose Jacobians have absolutely irreducible $\ell$-adic Tate modules exist in every positive genus and can be chosen hyperelliptic. Over $p$-adic fields, however, inertia and Frobenius can exclude entire genera. We classify the genera that occur for $\ell\ne p$ in terms of the residue characteristic and the cardinality of the residue field. For odd $p$, we also classify the genera occurring for hyperelliptic curves. These genera have relative density zero among those occurring for arbitrary curves, yielding Jacobians whose isogeny classes contain no hyperelliptic Jacobian. For odd $p$ and even residue degree, we obtain further restrictions on the genus when the curve itself is required to have potentially good reduction. Over number fields, we obtain uniform bounds from absolute irreducibility of the Tate module at two finite places of distinct residue characteristics different from $\ell$. The dimension of the abelian variety alone bounds the number of isomorphism classes in its isogeny class and the least degrees of isogenies between them.
Isomorphisms and representations of noncommutative function algebras
Marcel Scherer; Orr Shalit; Eli Shamovich; Mansi Suryawanshi

Let $V$ be a noncommutative (NC) variety in a NC operator ball. We study the dual operator algebra $H^\infty(V)$ of bounded NC functions on $V$, and the operator algebra $A(V)$ obtained as the closure of NC polynomials in $H^\infty(V)$. We identify the space of weak-$*$ continuous finite-dimensional representations of $H^\infty(V)$ as the similarity envelope $\widetilde{V}$ of $V$, and equip $\widetilde{V}$ with a metric which turns $\widetilde{V}$ into a complete invariant for $H^\infty(V)$, in the sense that $H^\infty(V)$ is weak-$*$ continuously isomorphic to $H^\infty(W)$ if and only if $\widetilde{V}$ and $\widetilde{W}$ are NC biholomorphic via a bi-Lipschitz map. The reduction to the linear case in the generality we work in depends on showing that the existence of maps implies the existence of origin-fixing maps, which we show using a novel ``two-circle trick" of independent interest. In the important case where the varieties are the full NC operator balls we find a striking rigidity phenomenon: if $A(B_E)$ and $A(B_F)$ are completely boundedly isomorphic then $E$ and $F$ are completely isometric. We also present a variety of examples illustrating the results and their sharpness, showing how several results from the literature fail to generalize to the setting studied here.
The exceptional set of Goldbach numbers among polynomial values
I. Althöfer; D. Chen; A. Perelli; J. Pintz

Let $ϕ$ be a fixed polynomial with integer coefficients, positive leading coefficient and degree $k\geq2$. We prove that the values $2ϕ(n)$, $1\leq n\leq N$, can be written as the sum of two primes, apart from at most $N^{α_k+o(1)}$ exceptional indices, where $α_k<1$. For quadratic polynomials the exponent is $1/2$, for cubic polynomials $5/8$, for quartic polynomials $3/4$, and for $k>4$ it is $1-1/(k+1)$. The proof combines a fourth-moment estimate over primes with mean-value estimates over arbitrary subsets of polynomial sequences.
Universal Decoding for Gaussian MIMO-ISI: Spherical Ensembles and Symmetric Neighborhoods

We construct a universal decoder for cyclic Gaussian multiple-input multiple-output channels with intersymbol interference and unknown channel taps and spatial noise covariance. Codewords are drawn independently and uniformly from a sphere of fixed total energy. Under stated bounds on frequency variation, the decoder attains the ensemble-average error exponent of informed maximum-likelihood decoding for fixed channels and channels with growing memory. We approximate the frequency response by a constant matrix within each frequency block. For this auxiliary channel, every matched log-likelihood is affine in a common sufficient statistic. At fixed received output, we compute the statistic density of an independent competitor. The decoder selects the candidate with the smallest statistic density, equivalently minimizing a weighted sum of residual log-determinants. The density and its support volume give an upper bound on the universal competitor probability. Affinity ensures that at least half of a suitable symmetric neighborhood of the transmitted statistic has matched likelihood no smaller than that of the transmitted word. Integrating a density lower bound over this half gives the matched competitor bound. These bounds establish equality of error exponents, which a Gaussian channel comparison transfers to the original channel. The same decoder attains the matched exponent for independent frequency blocks with prescribed energies satisfying the stated conditions. Approximation Algorithms for Right-Hand-Side Parametric Linear Programming Problems

Isomorphic classification of the coordinate algebras of the two-parameter braided quantum groups $\mathrm{SL}_2$

We classify, up to isomorphism, the coordinate algebras of the two-parameter braided quantum groups SL 2 .

We introduce an extension of Khovanov and Rozansky's categorification of the HOMFLY polynomial to arbitrary oriented tangles. Unlike previous such extensions, ours is invariant under the full suite of oriented Reidemeister moves, including the "misoriented" Reidemeister IIb. For oriented links $\mathcal{L}$, our construction recovers Khovanov and Rozansky's construction while removing the preliminary step of presenting $\mathcal{L}$ as a braid closure.
Anchored Iterative Decoding of Reed-Solomon Product Codes for High-Rate Magnetic Tape Storage

For a code $RS(256, 224)\times RS(175, 173)$ in a BSC we achieve post-decoding bit error rate (BER) of $10^{-20}$ at $\approx 5.3\times 10^{-3}$ raw BER while maintaining the common requirement to detect and correct 4 out of 32 dead tracks. The highest efficiency is achieved by performing an unlimited iterative decoder, which performs decoding iterations until no changes are made. We give an empirical analysis of the average number of iterations: below the raw BER of $5\times 10^{-3}$, four half-iterations are performed on average while improving substantially over a decoder that always performs 4 half-iterations. We provide a CPU implementation achieving 100-200 megabytes/s single-core throughput on a regular laptop and a design of a potential hybrid FPGA-CPU implementation of our decoder.

This paper addresses the birational geometry of three-dimensional algebraic varieties admitting a conic bundle structure. The central focus is on tetragonal transformations -- a special class of birational maps between standard conic bundles that are not fiberwise and play a key role in the birational geometry of such varieties.

We prove that the standard map $f_k(x,y)=(x+y+k\sin2πx,\,y+k\sin2πx)$ of the two-torus satisfies $\log(2πk+4)-2^{430}\le h_m(f_k)\le\log(2πk+4)$ for every $k\ge\exp(2^{50000})$, where $h_m$ is the metric entropy with respect to area. Positivity of $h_m(f_k)$ for all sufficiently large $k$, with a threshold that is not effective, was obtained in a recent preprint by OpenAI. We keep some of its architecture and follow it closely in about a third of the results. New here are an explicit covering argument for cancellations and a balance across scales at a fixed parameter, an inequality between mean shortfalls that replaces the compactness argument over limits of rescaled orbit geometries; together they yield the explicit constants and the entropy bound.

In this paper, we define a Drinfeld-type center for an associative crossed module and prove that it is canonically the internal category of an explicit crossed module constructed from Mac Lane's bimultiplications. The resulting center carries a canonical multiplicative lifting, which induces a natural strict braiding, establishing its correspondence to a braided crossed module. On the Motzkin-Straus theorem and clique number for k-uniform hypergraphs

In this paper, we establish a Motzkin-Straus type equality for k-uniform hypergraphs under certain conditions, which extends the classical Motzkin--Straus theorem for graphs. Using this equality, we present several spectral bounds for the clique number of k-uniform hypergraphs in terms of the spectral radii of the adjacency, signless Laplacian, and Laplacian tensors. On the existence of automorphisms acting expansively on the space of one-parameter subgroups of connected Lie groups

We study the action of automorphisms of $G$ on Sub$^p_G$, the closure of the set of all closed one-parameter subgroups of $G$ in Sub$_G$, in terms of expansivity. We show that a nontrivial connected Lie group $G$ with dim$(G)\geq 2$ does not admit any automorphism which acts expansively on Sub$^p_G$. A Structural Lower Bound for the Ramsey Number of the Petersen Graph

In this note, we investigate the diagonal Ramsey number of the Petersen graph, denoted by \(R(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{P})\). To the best of our knowledge, the dynamic survey \textit{Small Ramsey Numbers} (Revision \#18, 2026) records the lower bound as 19, established by Harborth and Krause. We construct a novel 2-coloring on the complete graph \(K_{20}\) that avoids any monochromatic Petersen graph. By defining the blue graph as the complement of the red graph, we utilize a specific join graph structure \(K_{9,9} \vee \overline{K_2}\). We rigorously prove its Petersen-free property, thereby improving the previously documented lower bound to \(R(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{P}) \ge 21\). Furthermore, we demonstrate the limit of this structural family by showing that the natural extension \(K_{9,9} \vee \overline{K_3}\) contains a Petersen subgraph.
Period bounds for Bergman kernel variation and the Suita defect

The periods of holomorphic differentials give an explicit lower bound for the curvature of Bergman evaluation matrices. We prove this bound along the Green sublevels of a smooth plane domain. For scalar evaluation at the Green pole, equality at one regular level holds precisely when that sublevel is simply connected. For complete jets at the Green pole, the matrices have continuous first derivatives, including at critical levels, and their logarithmic determinant defects are integrals of nonnegative curvature densities. A further estimate bounds the accumulated period energy by the determinant defect, with a constant independent of the jet order. On a multiply connected domain, all these defects vanish up to the first critical Green value and become strictly positive above it.
A scaled TW-PINN framework for soliton solutions of the Korteweg--de Vries equation
Seungwan Han; Jiaxi Gu; Daniel Olmos-Liceaga; Jae-Hun Jung

Accurate approximation of soliton solutions of the Korteweg--de Vries (KdV) equation remains challenging for physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) due to localized wave structures, high-order spatial derivatives, nonlinear interactions between solitons, and difficulties in long-time prediction. In this work, we address these challenges using a scaling PINN framework to approximate KdV soliton solutions. The framework transforms the governing equation into a normalized form, approximates its solution using a PINN solver, and reconstructs the solution in the original variables through inverse scaling. We introduce scaling transformations and PINN solvers tailored to one- and two-soliton problems. For the one-soliton case, we employ a PINN solver that incorporates a traveling-wave coordinate to capture soliton propagation. For the two-soliton case, we employ a two-step training procedure for the PINN solver. The first step learns the individual soliton profiles and estimates their propagation speeds, while the second step uses the estimated speeds to construct traveling-wave coordinates in the PINN solver and approximate the full two-soliton solution, including nonlinear interactions. We also introduce soliton-informed sampling (SIS), which places additional collocation points around the soliton trajectories. PH-Symb : Sparse symbolic identification of nonlinear port-Hamiltonian systems using Kolmogorov-Arnold networks
Achraf El Messaoudi; Karim Cherifi; Yann Le Gorrec; Yongxin Wu

The paper introduces PH-Symb, a novel symbolic structure-preserving identification method, that combines Kolmogorov Arnold networks and sparse regression to build explicit port-Hamiltonian (pH) models from data. Unlike other Machine Learning or neural pH approaches, PH-Symb recovers physically interpretable and explicit-symbolic components and enforces pH structure by construction. It also introduces a new normalization method that preserves the pH structure. It allows handling both identification from input-state-output (ISO) data and input-output (IO) data, and applications show it delivers interpretable models and lower errors than neural baselines on synthetic and real-world systems.
Unique ergodicity of systems of finite order and the density finite sums theorem in arbitrary abelian groups
Ethan Ackelsberg; Asgar Jamneshan; Or Shalom

Let $Γ$ be a countable abelian group and $k\geq 1$. We establish that every minimal topological $Γ$-system of order $k$ is uniquely ergodic. This result, which was previously only known for finitely generated groups for arbitrary $k$, answers a question of Glasner, Gutman, and Ye and yields the answer to multiple questions by Candela, González-Sánchez, and Szegedy. As applications of our dynamical results, we obtain the following combinatorial theorems. Let $A\subseteq Γ$ be a set of positive upper Banach density. Then there are infinite sets $B_1,\ldots, B_k\subseteq Γ$ such that $B_1+\dots+B_k\subseteq A$. Commuting Toeplitz and Little Hankel Operators on the Bidisk
Necessary and sufficient conditions are obtained for two Toeplitz operators and for a Toeplitz operator and a little Hankel operator to commute on the pluriharmonic Hardy space of the bidisk.
One complex metric and geometric adelic nefness

We prove that an arithmetic adelic line bundle on a smooth quasi-projective variety over a number field has nef geometric part if its prescribed continuous metric at one complex embedding has semipositive first Chern current. The proof constructs semiample approximations to every positive rational ample perturbation by boundary extension, multiplier ideals, and Nadel vanishing, followed by specialization and Galois descent. This gives geometric nefness of Gao--Zhang's canonical Gross--Schoen adelic line bundle.

Stieltjes's conjecture on Legendre polynomials asserts that no two distinct Legendre polynomials can share a nonzero root. This question is, surprisingly, connected to a number of disparate mathematical areas. From the point of view of spectral geometry, this question concerns zero-sets of spherical harmonics. A disk counterpart to the conjecture is a famous theorem of Siegel on nonexistence of nonzero common roots of Bessel functions, proved using transcendence theory. A weak version of the conjecture is implied by the dynamical Mordell--Lang conjecture. We prove, using a $2$-adic analytic approach à la Skolem, that for a root $α\neq 0$ of $P_l$ the set $\{n\in \mathbb{N}:\ P_n(α)=0\}$ has cardinality at most $2l$. In particular, this set is finite.

Finally, a short conditional-state description of the quantum source and field shows how a backreaction can introduce an additional phase and reduce interference visibility. The conditional-state overlap is represented by a central scalar--pseudoscalar element; preservation of the fluxoid sector alone does not guarantee unit coherence.

We determine the sharp constant in the weighted $L^2$ Bernstein inequality for coordinate derivatives on the unit ball with a Jacobi weight and the strengthened derivative factors introduced by Beberok and Xu. The constant is expressed in terms of the largest zeros of Jacobi polynomials, and all extremal polynomials are characterized explicitly. The proof uses an orthogonal polynomial decomposition that gives diagonal formulas for both the squared norm and the weighted derivative integral. We also obtain two-sided bounds for the sharp constant and determine its leading asymptotic behavior as the polynomial degree tends to infinity.

By diffeomorphism invariance, $DN(g\_0)^*$ takes values in divergence-free symmetric $2$-tensors, and in TT tensors if moreover $DN(g\_0)$ kills conformal directions. Such operators are local potentials, which we call machines: they produce smooth compactly supported tensors with the required property and, on closed manifolds, all of them up to a finite-dimensional space when their symbol is injective. On Einstein manifolds of every dimension, the linearised Bach tensor gives the operator $P$ of an earlier paper, which factorises on TT tensors into the massless and partially massless spin-$2$ operators; we also construct machines on Bach-flat, conformally flat and Ricci-parallel metrics. Replacing the diffeomorphisms of $M$ by those of the vacuum development, we obtain potentials, with a Fredholm property, for the linearised Einstein constraint equations on arbitrary spacelike hypersurfaces of Minkowski, de Sitter and anti-de Sitter spacetimes.
The enigma of locally Toeplitz matrices. I. Discrete Schrödinger operators with complex potential

Freezing the coefficients of a banded locally Toeplitz matrix gives a family of Toeplitz eigenvalue measures. Their average can fill a region of the complex plane even when the eigenvalues of the original matrices appear to follow curves. We conjecture that, when the above average has a sufficiently regular planar density, the limiting eigenvalue measure is its mother body. We prove it for a class of finite Dirichlet discrete Schrödinger operators with complex potential $V$ and a common real coefficient $α>0$ on the two adjacent diagonals. When $(\Im V)'>0$ and $V$ admits a suitable holomorphic extension, the limiting measure is supported on finitely many analytic arcs. Its logarithmic potential falls below that of the averaged measure by twice the least of four explicit actions. We obtain these actions from a four-term asymptotic expansion of the Dirichlet determinant. When $\Im V$ is not monotone, an exact transfer recursion gives a conditional extension. For a circular potential arc we verify the geometric switching condition, leaving non-resonance as the remaining hypothesis.
Higher Holonomy for Higher Lie Algebroid Connections on Graded Vector Bundles

We prove the existence of a Riemann--Hilbert $A_\infty$-functor from the curved dg-category of $\mathscr{A}$-connections on graded vector bundles, where $\mathscr{A}$ is a higher Lie algebroid, to the curved dg-category of $Π_\infty(\mathscr{A})$-connections on graded vector bundles, where $Π_\infty(\mathscr{A})$ is the homotopy groupoid of $\mathscr{A}$. Furthermore, for a graded vector bundle $E$, we introduce the notion of its higher general linear groupoid in such a way that $G$-connections on $E$, for a higher Lie groupoid $G$, become smooth functors from $G$ to the higher general linear groupoid of $E$. We combine this with the Riemann--Hilbert functor to define higher parallel transport functors for $\mathscr{A}$-connections. Finally, we use these functors to define the higher holonomy groups of $\mathscr{A}$-connections and endow them with the structure of augmented simplicial Lie groups.

Tensor-product splines mapped from a square to a disk-like domain form a discrete de Rham complex, but at the coordinate singularity the pushed-forward $0$-, $1$- and $2$-forms are discontinuous, unbounded and not square integrable. There exists a universal constant $\varepsilon_\ast>0$ such that $x_0$ is regular if, for some ball $B_R(x_0)\subsetΩ$ with $R>0$, \[ \frac1R\int_{B_R(x_0)}|\nabla u|^2\,dx \leq \varepsilon_\ast^2. \] The main difficulty is that the Dirichlet energy controls the velocity oscillation while its mean may be arbitrarily large. Subtracting the mean introduces a large constant drift into the perturbation equation. Moreover, smallness in $H^1$ alone is insufficient to close a direct nonlinear elliptic estimate in five dimensions. We overcome these difficulties through uniform Oseen estimates and a relative-energy comparison yielding quadratic improvement of the perturbation. As a consequence, the singular set has zero one-dimensional upper Minkowski content on every compact subset of $Ω$, and hence local upper Minkowski dimension at most one.

We show that for root-subgroup multiplication maps, dominance does not imply birationality. This gives a negative answer to a question of Fang, Fourier and Littelmann. Second, we exploit this characterization to formulate mixed-integer linear constraints on the discrete-time trajectories that allow for planning a trajectory whose piecewise polynomial interpolation satisfies the continuous-time STL formula. This paper proposes a novel controller for a double-integrator agent to track a moving target with bounded velocity on a hyperboloid $\mathbb{H}^n$. A splitting theorem for Einstein manifolds with symmetries

We prove that every negative-Einstein manifold with cocompact symmetries splits isometrically as a Riemannian product $H \times K$ with $H$ homogeneous and $K$ compact. This confirms a conjecture due to Böhm and Lafuente. As a consequence, we obtain a new proof of the 1975 Alekseevskii conjecture.

The purpose of this article is to study the convergence of a lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) for a simple diffusion equation. The LBM is proven to be stable and consistent in some sense, so that convergence results may be obtained. For every $n\ge3$ and $(n+1)/(n-1)<p<(n+2)/(n-2)$, we construct positive solutions of $Δu+u^p=0$ in the half-space with zero Dirichlet data away from the origin, the homogeneous singular profile there, and Poisson-kernel decay at infinity, resolving a question of del Pino--Musso--Pacard. Provable State Estimation with Recurrent Models

Despite their empirical success, recurrent models often lack formal guarantees on convergence and robustness. By framing RNNs as a time-discretization of continuous latent dynamical systems (Neural ODEs), we demonstrate that enforcing a contraction condition on the latent flow guarantees the existence of a smooth, injective map of the true physical state into the latent space. We study mesoscopic fluctuations of linear eigenvalue statistics for random $d$-regular graphs on $N$ vertices with fixed $d\ge 3$. Revisiting the approach developed by Dumitriu-Johnson-Pal-Paquette (2013) and Johnson (2015), we establish a mesoscopic central limit theorem in the bulk and identify its universal limiting variance. Our result applies to test functions with smooth compactly supported Fourier transforms and to a specific range of spectral scales $(\log N)^{-1}\llη\ll 1$. In particular, this case study allows the mesoscopic scale to tend to zero arbitrarily slowly.
Joint modelling of financial cost and carbon footprint in motor insurance claims: a BINAR(1) decision framework for circular auto parts adoption

Motor insurance claims management increasingly faces a dual objective: controlling claim costs while reducing greenhouse-gas emissions associated with vehicle repair decisions. This paper proposes a bivariate, discrete-time modelling framework that links the dynamics of financial claims and repair-related carbon footprint inspired by a BINAR(1) dependence structure, allowing for temporal persistence, cross-dependence and a positive/negative correlation between the two dimensions. Using externally sourced emission factors and cost information for replacement parts, we operationalise the carbon footprint of claims under two repair pathways: new parts versus circular-economy reused parts (PIEC). Results show that higher PIEC acceptance can simultaneously reduce expected emissions and average claim cost, and the magnitude of the joint benefit depends on the dependence structure and persistence captured by the BINAR(1) process. We consider totally irrational real n-by-m matrices and two conditions on their sequences of best approximations: (B) bounded successive height ratios and (C) bounded successive error ratios. Combining these bounds with known results, we determine the individual spectra of both exponents under (C), with and without the additional assumption (B). Boundary integral methods and shape reconstruction for periodic fluid--solid interfaces

This paper studies direct scattering by periodic fluid--solid interfaces and interface reconstruction from multifrequency near-field data. Using Helmholtz decomposition and quasi-periodic single-layer potentials, we formulate a coupled boundary integral system with the standard stress traction, establish its equivalence to the original fluid--solid transmission problem under suitable assumptions, and construct a corresponding Nyström discretization. For near-field observations at finitely many measurement points, we establish local Fréchet differentiability of the observation map with a quadratic remainder estimate. In the smooth setting, the derivative transmission problem and its boundary integral formulation are used to compute the observation Jacobian required for interface reconstruction. Elliptic units, derived Heegner classes and the p-adic Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer quotient of CM elliptic curves of rank two

In particular, this holds for all $ρ>1/N$, without any absolute-continuity assumption or arithmetic restriction on the digits or the contraction. At $ρ=1/N$, for commensurable digits, a frame measure exists if and only if $μ_{ρ,\mathscr D}$ is normalized Lebesgue measure on its attractor. Under a geometric accessibility condition, we derive explicit open-loop controls that drive the state into regions where the saturation takes prescribed values. For componentwise saturations, this condition holds generically with as few as two independent control directions. The controls require no state measurement and only partial knowledge of the dynamics, with no information on the structure of its nonlinear part. The resulting regressor is known in advance, and the unknown matrix is recovered exactly by a closed-form regression. Suitably chosen references then also enable exact identification of linearly parameterized (nonlinear) dynamics. In this paper, we propose a decomposition-based MPC method that reorders and reduces computations to shorten the delay between receiving a state measurement and applying the control input. Enhanced Informed Dynamic BP Decoding Scheduling Strategies for 5G NR LDPC Codes

We present an enhanced informed dynamic scheduling (IDS) strategy to avoid propagations of unreliable messages in the residual belief-propagation (RBP) algorithm for decoding low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes. On derandomizing the line-point low-degree test

Motivated by applications to minimal equicontinuous Cantor actions, which are characterized by such pairs, we characterize isometric *-algebra isomorphisms between such Hecke algebras by showing that they always arise as Koopman operators of homeomorphisms between the double coset spaces combined with the multiplication by some character. For $q\ge q_c$ there is none. We also show that, after removing the Gaussian factor, the profile has an angular limit shape $Φ$ in every mode, give an integral formula for its Kummer coefficients, prove that $Φ$ is real-analytic and is the uniform limit of the rescaled profiles, that $Φ/(η_1/|η|)$ is monotone along meridians, and that $Φ$ is proportional to $η_1/|η|$ if and only if $2α+q=1$. This paper compares various Rosenbrock and Rosenbrock W-methods. To achieve this, some methods implemented in the Julia package OrdinaryDiffEqRosenbrock.jl are selected and benchmarked using test examples. The test examples include stiff ODE problems as well as differential-algebraic equations. In addition to the already known methods, the new W-method Rodas4PW is introduced and included in the tests.

José Correa; Svenja M. Griesbach; Elfarouk Harb; Felix Hommelsheim; Reda Jlibene; Vasilis Livanos; Eilon Solan

In this note, we correct an error in the proof Theorem 1 of Comm. Math. Phys. 401 (2023), 2459-2482.

For weakly mixing systems, we establish a complete spectral characterization of two-sided $2$-nice recurrence via quadratic spectral functionals and Herglotz--Bochner duality, extending the theory to arbitrary integer polynomial configurations $\{0, p_1(n), p_2(n)\}$ with zero constant term and to actions of countable abelian groups. Furthermore, we uncover a fundamental structural phase transition at $k=3$: while $k=2$ recurrence is rigidly controlled by a quadratic spectral functional whose two-sided symmetrization eliminates all higher-degree cumulants, at $k=3$ fourth-order centered correlations survive symmetrization and can drive a strict recurrence deficit even when the quadratic spectral functional remains strictly positive. Using lacunary and multi-frequency Riesz products alongside uniform Wiener lemmas, we analyze the upper Banach density obstructions of negative spectral sets, establish partial partition regularity on the spectral cone, resolve an inverse Furstenberg correspondence problem of Rodríguez Martín for countable groups via Bernoulli product extensions, and characterize spectral $2$-nice ultrafilters in the Stone--Čech compactification $β\N$.
Elastic Wave Imaging via Kirchhoff Migration: Resolution Analysis and Inclusion Identification

We consider the inverse problem of determining the location, orientation, shape, and material parameters of a small elastic inclusion embedded in a homogeneous medium from full-aperture measurements of the scattered field. Using a small-volume expansion, we derive explicit leading-order expressions for four Kirchhoff migration imaging functionals, denoted by PP, PS, SP, and SS, corresponding to the four combinations of pressure (P) and shear (S) waves used for receiver- and source-side backpropagation. The resulting point-spread functions quantitatively characterize the resolution of each mode and show that the SS mode achieves the highest spatial resolution. For an elliptic inclusion, we show that the PP mode uniquely determines the elastic moment tensor (EMT) within the leading-order asymptotic model, thereby enabling the reconstruction of the material and geometric parameters of the inclusion. For a general small scatterer, the reconstruction may instead be interpreted as an effective elliptic representation determined by its leading-order EMT. For a disk, the parameter-identification problem is underdetermined; nevertheless, explicit upper and lower bounds on its volume are derived. We further analyze the model error arising from neglected cross-mode contributions when the distance from the center of the measurement configuration is not sufficiently large relative to the elastic wavelengths. Numerical experiments support the theoretical predictions and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed imaging and reconstruction methods.
Strong convergence rates for numerical approximations of the stochastic Burgers equation with additive rough noise

We establish strong convergence rates for a fully discrete method of the one-dimensional stochastic Burgers equation driven by additive rough noise. Using the Cole-Hopf transformation, the equation is converted into a linear stochastic heat equation, which is discretized by a spectral Galerkin method in space and an accelerated exponential Euler method in time. A numerical approximation of the original solution is then reconstructed through a regularized inverse Cole-Hopf transformation. The analysis combines strong Sobolev error estimates with the positivity and inverse-moment bounds for the transformed solution. For additive space-time white noise, the numerical method achieves mean-square convergence rates arbitrarily close to 1/2 in space and 1/4 in time. The rates are slower when the noises are rougher.
Formalization of Filter-Method Construction for Real Numbers in Coq

This paper presents a formalization for a theory of constructing real numbers using concepts related to filters. The formalization is implemented using the Coq proof assistant and is grounded in axiomatic set theory. The theory encompasses various notions such as filters, ultrafilters, principal ultrafilters, and arithmetical ultrafilters. A special filter, namely the non-principal arithmetical ultrafilter, whose existence requires the Continuum Hypothesis to be proven, is employed to establish several non-standard number sets: *N, *Z and *Q. The set of real numbers, R, is subsequently derived by equivalently classifying a specific subset of *Q. The entire theory is thoroughly formalized, with each detail verified to ensure rigor and precision. This work contributes a new selection of foundational materials for the formalization of mathematical theories.
Maximizing Reaction via Spatial Localization: The Reaction-Flux Landscape and Maximizing Sequences
Mohammad Yasir Feroz Khan; Bo Li

We continue our study of a PDE-constrained variational model for maximizing the total reaction flux by optimizing the spatial distribution of catalytic materials, such as enzymes. The total amount of enzyme is fixed, and the substrate concentration is governed by a reaction-diffusion equation with prescribed boundary values. We consider both linear and nonlinear Michaelis-Menten reaction kinetics. In previous work, we constructed a maximizing sequence, computed the first and second variations of the reaction functional, and established the nonexistence of local maximizers. Here, we conduct a more comprehensive analysis. We prove that the functional is strictly concave for linear kinetics but need not be concave or convex for nonlinear kinetics. We also show that no critical points exist. We then characterize maximizing sequences and identify all their possible limiting measures. Our analysis reveals the mechanism of reaction maximization through spatial localization: maximizing sequences concentrate enzymes near the portion of the boundary where the substrate concentration is largest. Moreover, the landscape of the functional defining the total reaction differs between the linear and nonlinear cases, a point less emphasized in applications. Consistent with existing biophysical studies, these findings motivate the development and analysis of regularized models.
Every IC-planar graph has weak-strict degeneracy at most 6
Zhen He; Yilong Li; Tao Wang; Xiaojing Yang

We prove that every IC-planar graph has weak-strict degeneracy at most $6$. Weak-strict degeneracy is the weak degeneracy of Bernshteyn and Lee plus one, so it bounds the coloring parameters controlled by weak degeneracy. In particular, every IC-planar graph is $6$-choosable, $6$-DP-colorable and $6$-paintable, which strengthens the theorem of Yang, Wang, Wang and Lih that IC-planar graphs are $6$-choosable. An IC-planar graph is a subgraph of a plane graph in which a set of pairwise vertex-disjoint inner $4$-faces, called marked faces, receive both diagonals. Our main tool is a Thomassen-type statement for such graphs: vertices of marked faces get one extra unit, except those in a prescribed independent set of boundary vertices. With no marked faces, this statement is exactly the theorem of Bernshteyn, Lee and Smith-Roberge that gives weak-strict degeneracy at most $5$ for planar graphs, so it contains both results. We prove it by a minimal-counterexample argument following Bernshteyn, Lee and Smith-Roberge. The new ingredients are a deletion rule that turns destroyed marked faces into ordinary edges, a pseudo-$2$-chord lemma for paths that use one diagonal, and a choice of orientation of the outer cycle that avoids a vertex of the independent set joined to two vertices of the prescribed boundary path.
Infinity operad pairs, higher distributivity and spectral Tambara functors

We introduce an $\infty$-categorical model of operad pairs and their associated bimonoidal categories. We study the related concepts such as cocartesian-cartesian operad pairs, algebra pairs and the Day convolution. Using the Day convolution for operad pairs, we can define distributive functors between a symmetric bimonoidal category and a cartesian closed monoidal category. As an application, we show that for a finite group $G$, the operadic distributive functors from $\mathrm{Span}(\mathsf{Fin}_G)$ to any cartesian closed monoidal category coincides with the distributive functors defined by the distributive diagram. Therefore, we show that the connective $G$-equivariant $\mathbb{E}_{\infty}$-ring spectra are equivalently the spectral $G$-Tambara functors.
Tom Goertzen; Abel Lacabanne; Daniel Tubbenhauer; Pedro Vaz
Using annular webs and Kazhdan-Lusztig mu-coefficients, we disprove Guralnick's absolute boundedness conjecture for first cohomology.
The Sparse-Complement Conjecture for Two Distinct Eigenvalues

For a graph $G$, let $q(G)$ be the minimum number of distinct eigenvalues of a real symmetric matrix whose off-diagonal zero--nonzero pattern is $G$. We prove that $q(G)=2$ whenever the complement $H=\overline G$ of a graph of order $n\ge3$ has at most $n-3$ edges, resolving the sparse-complement conjecture of Fallat and Mojallal. If $H$ contains a cycle, the proof constructs a nontrivial orthogonal projector with the strong spectral property and rank at most $|E(F)|-|V(F)|+4$, where $F$ is the union of the cyclic components of $H$. The construction combines faithful stress-free Gram representations, a one-coordinate lift for each excess core edge, exact orthogonal-frame completion, and a Stiefel-manifold pendant-extension argument.
Yuxuan Wang; Yu Sun; Bowen Li; Kangqiang Li

We study Byzantine-robust distributed sparse softmax regression in high-dimensional settings. We propose a communication-efficient distributed algorithm that employs robust aggregation methods---coordinate-wise trimmed mean and coordinate-wise median---to defend against Byzantine attacks. Under sub-Gaussian design assumptions with sparsity constraints, we establish that the distributed estimator achieves the convergence rate of $O_{P}(K^{\frac{5}{2}}\sqrt{s\log(Kd)/N})$ when the Byzantine fraction $α\asymp 1/\sqrt{m}$, matching the centralized oracle rate. Numerical experiments on synthetic data demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method.
A Smooth Equality Reformulation of Nonlinear Exponential Cone Optimization

Exponential cone optimization has received considerable attention in the modern literature, but studies involving nonlinear objective and constraint functions are still limited. This work can be seen as one of the first steps toward understanding nonlinear exponential cone optimization (NECO) problems. Here, we ask the question "Can smooth equality constraints replace nonlinear exponential cone constraints?". From a practical point of view, even squared slack reformulations in nonlinear programming introduce difficulties. However, such reformulations can be useful for studying optimality conditions. Motivated by this observation, in this work, we use a smooth surjective parameterization of the exponential cone to reformulate NECO as an equality-constrained nonlinear program (RNLP). We then analyze Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) and second-order optimality conditions for NECO through RNLP. Although feasibility is represented exactly, the KKT conditions for RNLP do not in general guarantee those for NECO. We characterize this correspondence through multiplier restrictions that are equivalent to a second-order condition involving only slack variables. We also establish an exact curvature identity showing that RNLP reproduces the sigma term of NECO without additional assumptions. Finally, we prove the relationships between second-order necessary and sufficient conditions for the two problems. We identify when RNLP can be used to rule out local minimizers of NECO or establish strict local optimality for NECO without explicitly evaluating the sigma term.
Group Invariance of Statistical Models and Associated Statistical Manifolds

We study the group invariance of a parameterized statistical model that is closed under push-forward sample transformations given by a group action. We prove that the group action on the sample space induces an isometric action on the associated statistical manifold. Furthermore, it preserves the Fisher-Rao metric as well as the Amari-Chentsov tensor. Moreover, we establish that this isometric action is compatible with equivariant and sufficient statistics in the spirit of the Hall-Wijsman-Ghosh generalized Stein's theorem. This compatibility leads to a novel reduction of the original group-invariant model, where its Fisher information loss is explicitly quantified via conditional expectation. As an application, we apply this framework to a generalized cardioid distribution in circular data analysis, illustrating how the reduced model facilitates estimation and hypothesis testing for relative parameters.
Cuspidal sections for varieties of arbitrary dimension

We define cuspidal sections for varieties of arbitrary dimension over fields of characteristic zero, extending the definition for curves by Grothendieck. Our notion of cuspidal sections is defined relative to a normal crossings compactification. We prove that the closure of the resulting set is independent of the choice of a compactification. For varieties iteratively constructed from fibrations, we compare our definition to an inductive notion of cuspidal sections, and discuss connections to the section conjecture of Grothendieck.
Slim Polygons, Hyperbolicity, and a new Quasi-Isometric Invariant

We introduce the slimness function, $\mathrm{Slim}_X(n)$, of a geodesic metric space, which records the maximal slimness of its geodesic polygons as a function of the number of sides. We study the large-scale behaviour of this function and its relation to hyperbolicity, growth function, and quasi-isometries. We first establish that the slimness function is a natural quasi-isometric invariant in the hyperbolic setting. We then obtain quantitative estimates for geodesic polygons in hyperbolic spaces and bounded-valency graphs. In particular, we show that sufficiently slow growth of the slimness function forces tree-like geometry. We also prove a decomposition result for trees of hyperbolic spaces. We show that for a finitely generated hyperbolic group $G$ there are only two possibilities: either $G$ is virtually free and $\operatorname{Slim}_G$ is bounded, or $\operatorname{Slim}_G(n)\simeq\log n$. Finally, we investigate the interaction between polygonal slimness and the growth of connected bounded-valency graphs. Combining the resulting estimates with large-scale dimension theory, we obtain criteria implying that an unbounded graph has asymptotic dimension one.
Quantitative group testing with a fixed shore: sharp asymptotics and exact formulas

We study adaptive quantitative group testing with one defective item in each of two disjoint sets. When one set has fixed size, we determine the leading term of the difference between the binary bound and the largest searchable opposite set size. The result extends to fixed unions of complete bipartite graphs and to positive weighted sums of the opposite set sizes. We determine exact eventual formulas when the fixed set has six, seven or eight items. The eight-item formula has a period-three correction. We explain this correction by optimizing the sizes of shared test pieces within fixed decision-tree prefixes. For each fixed finite family of such prefixes ending in star forests, the optimal deficit is eventually a rational polynomial plus a bounded periodic function. The asymptotic proofs are analytic; the exact formulas also use integer constructions and rational exclusion certificates.
Characterization of Attenuated V-Line Transform and Direct Reconstruction from Samples

The V-line transform (V-LT), a generalized Radon transform (RT), is widely used in Compton scattering imaging (CSI). The central mathematical problem of CSI is to reconstruct a function from its V-LT. Unlike V-LT, the attenuated V-line transform (AV-LT) accounts for the medium-induced loss of intensity, and has been demonstrated to improve image quality. The present paper makes two main contributions. (1) We establish the fundamental characterizations for AV-LT including operator properties ($L^2$-boundedness, operator norm etc.), a necessary and sufficient condition for the preservation of compact support, and sharp estimation of Sobolev smoothness. These characterizations remain unexplored, and they reveal essential differences among AV-LT, RT and V-LT. (2) We develop a direct reconstruction method based on AV-LT samples that does not require solving any equation. Our sampling formula gives exact reconstruction for band-limited functions. We also provide approximate reconstruction for functions in $H^s(\mathbb{R}^2)$ with $s>2$.
Claw-free minimal factor-critical and bicritical graphs
Huaibin Zhou; Mingyang Guo; Xiumei Wang

A graph $G$ is called $k$-factor-critical if $G-S$ has a perfect matching for every subset $S\subseteq V(G)$ with $|S|=k$, and is minimal if $G-e$ is not $k$-factor-critical for every edge $e$ of $G$. The cases $k=1$ and $k=2$ correspond to factor-critical and bicritical graphs, respectively. In this paper, we obtain complete structural characterizations of claw-free minimal factor-critical graphs and claw-free minimal bicritical graphs. The former is characterized by ear decompositions. For the latter, we first characterize the $3$-connected case using the theory of line graphs and then extend the characterization to the general case by a suitable $2$-sum operation.
Complete uniqueness for two-dimensional asymmetric incompressible jet flows

Alt, Caffarelli and Friedman established the existence of two-dimensional asymmetric incompressible jet flows in [Asymmetric jet flows. Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 35, 29--68, 1982]. In their formulation, the constant fluid speed $λ$ on the free boundaries and the downstream asymptotic angle $θ$ are selected as part of the solution. In this paper, we prove that the asymmetric jet is unique for a prescribed nozzle and mass flux. We first establish the strict vertical monotonicity of the stream function $u$ and introduce the partial hodograph coordinates $ξ=x$ and $η=u(x,y)$, which map every fluid domain onto the same fixed strip. Under this framework, each jet is characterized by a height function $y=h(ξ,η)$, which determines the vertical position along the streamline $u=η$ at horizontal coordinate $ξ$. By analyzing the difference between the height functions of two candidate jets on this strip, we derive an elliptic equation with Dirichlet conditions on the fixed walls and conormal conditions on the free boundaries. Combining these mixed boundary conditions with the asymptotic behaviors, we first establish the uniqueness of the free-boundary fluid speed $λ$. For the resulting common speed, a local perturbation of the height function near a nozzle endpoint, together with the maximum principle, proves that the two height functions must coincide. Inverting the partial hodograph transformation then establishes the uniqueness of the physical jet.
Hausdorff dimension of planar box-like self-affine sets with rotations
Antti Käenmäki; R. Dániel Prokaj; Károly Simon; Sascha Troscheit

We study the Hausdorff dimension of proximal planar self-affine sets whose defining maps have diagonal or anti-diagonal linear parts, with both types present. Such systems are irreducible but not strongly irreducible. Under a projective exponential separation condition, we show that the Hausdorff dimension equals the minimum of $2$ and the affinity dimension, thereby extending the dimension formula of Hochman--Rapaport to all proximal irreducible planar systems. When the affinity dimension is at most an explicit threshold determined by the Lyapunov exponents, the formula holds assuming only that there are no exact overlaps. Above the threshold, it holds under the strong open set condition. These dimension formulae are proved by approximation with finite diagonal subsystems. Assuming projective exponential separation, we also determine the pointwise dimensions of the coordinate projections of the equilibrium state. Below the threshold, the projections are not exact-dimensional: the pointwise dimension of each exists almost everywhere and takes exactly two values, each on a set of positive measure. At or above the threshold, both projections are exact-dimensional with dimension one.
Ore-degree conditions for matchings in uniform hypergraphs

Let $σ_r(\mathcal{H})$ be the minimum sum of vertex degrees over all nonedges of an $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal{H}$ on $n$ vertices. Balogh, Palmer and Raeisi conjectured that $n>2rs$ and $σ_r(\mathcal{H})>r[\binom{n-1}{r-1}-\binom{n-s}{r-1}]$ imply the existence of a matching of size $s$ in $\mathcal{H}$. We prove that, for every fixed $r\ge3$ and all sufficiently large $s$, $σ_r(\mathcal{H})>r[\binom{n-1}{r-1}-\binom{n-s}{r-1}]$ forces an $s$-matching whenever $n\ge rs+\lfloor(r-1)^{r-1}/r^{r-2}\rfloor$. A complete $r$-graph on $rs-1$ vertices together with $\lfloor(r-1)^{r-1}/r^{r-2}\rfloor$ isolated vertices shows that the vertex bound is sharp for all sufficiently large $s$. By adding new vertices to $\mathcal{H}$, retaining all its edges, and adding every $r$-set containing at least one new vertex as an edge, we also deduce that $n\ge rs+C$ suffices under the same degree condition for every $s\ge1$, where $C$ is a finite constant depending only on $r$. For $r=3$, we provide the explicit sufficient order $n\ge\lceil(7s+11)/2\rceil$ for $s\ge6$, together with bounds for $2\le s\le5$, establishing the conjecture in this uniformity. For $s=2$, we improve the known sufficient order $2r+2$ to $2r+1$ for every $r\ge3$ and show that this order is best possible.
Cable Knot Counterexamples to the All-Knot Volume Conjecture

Let $E$ be the figure-eight knot and let $V$ be the hyperbolic volume of its exterior. We study the reduced colored Jones polynomial at $q=e^{2πi/N}$ for the $(p,w)$-cable of the connected sum of $d\ge 2$ copies of $E$, where $w\ge 2$ and $p,w$ are coprime. The normalized logarithmic growth rate converges to the JSJ volume $dV$ along colors coprime to $2w$, and its upper limit along colors sharing a divisor with $w$ is at most $V$. Thus the $(1,2)$-cable of $E\#E$ violates the full-sequence volume limit for knots. The $(1,3)$-cable of the same companion shows that convergence can fail even along all odd colors. The separation comes from the multiples of $N$ in the exact cabling sum and a uniform first-derivative estimate for the other companion colors.
Fair Selection of Generalized Nash Equilibria: A Comparability Perspective
Sophie Hall; Heinrich H. Nax; Saverio Bolognani

Generalized Nash equilibrium (GNE) problems model self-interested agents coupled through their costs and shared constraints, and arise throughout control applications that allocate a scarce common resource. Such problems typically admit a continuum of equilibria, so any implementation must \emph{select} one. This selection is not neutral: it decides how the cost of the shared constraint is distributed among the agents, a decision often expected to be fair. The variational GNE (v-GNE), which charges all agents a uniform shadow price, is the conventional choice and is frequently advocated as fair. Through the lens of \emph{comparability} from social choice theory, we show that the GNE set itself requires no inter-agent comparability of costs, whereas the v-GNE implicitly assumes cardinal unit comparability, one of the stronger notions. We then introduce the fair GNE (f-GNE), which selects an equilibrium by explicitly optimizing a fairness metric matched to the comparability at hand, and give constructive routes to compute it for single-constraint and linear-quadratic games. An electric-vehicle charging game serves as a running example throughout this self-contained tutorial.
Equidistribution of Solution Gradients in Physics-Informed Neural Networks via Coordinate Transformations

Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) often struggle to approximate solutions with sharp gradients due to optimization difficulties and spectral bias. Motivated by the principle of gradient equidistribution from the stretching approach in grid generation, which redistributes solution gradients to reduce functional complexity, we propose Coordinate Transformation PINNs (CTPINNs), which incorporate learnable coordinate transformations to map the physical domain into a computational domain where the physical solutions become approximately affine, making them easier for neural networks to learn. We propose two constructions of the transformation: an explicit construction based on Majorants and an implicit construction based on invertable neural networks. Experimentally, the explicit construction can improve accuracy for PDEs with available explicit coordinate transformations, and the implicit construction can be combined with other advanced PINN models as an efficient plug-in module to improve performance across a range of challenging PDE benchmarks.

We show that $\mathrm{SL}(4,\mathbb{Z})$ contains an infinite family of Zariski-dense subgroups isomorphic to the fundamental group of a fixed closed hyperbolic $3$-manifold, which are pairwise noncommensurable up to conjugacy.
Resolvent-Diagonal Energy of Isospectral Jacobi Matrices

We study the minimum squared resolvent diagonal among Jacobi matrices with prescribed eigenvalues. For the zeros of $P_n^{(α,β)}$, we construct a canonical realization and bound its asymptotic cost against the optimum. Its rescaled inverse converges to the Green operator of a reflection-symmetric singular Schrödinger operator with Bessel-zero spectrum. A Green-coordinate identity places this construction and all finite realizations in the same density framework. Mass-constrained spectral problems then give computable lower bounds. The bounds meet at $α=1/2$, with optimal energy $2/15$, and have first-order contact with derivative $-13/75$. We classify the constrained extremal profiles and the three endpoint geometries of the canonical density. Two polynomial families with the same limiting edge spectrum have different limiting optimal energies. For Nesterov momentum $(s-1)/(s+1)$, the optimal leading endpoint Hessian-drift gain among nonnegative-link Jacobi realizations is $\sqrt{2}$ times the original gain. An explicit isospectral flow strictly improves the standard one-sided realization for $α>-1/2$, $α\ne1/2$.
Asymptotic stability of high-index saddle dynamics
Baoming Shi; Lei Zhang; Xiangcheng Zheng; Shangqin Zhu

High-index saddle dynamics (HiSD) has been extensively adopted to compute saddle points of arbitrary index, with various applications such as constructing solution landscapes of complex systems. In this work, we prove the asymptotic stability of various HiSD methods, including the idealized, perturbed, and coupled HiSD methods, as well as their momentum-accelerated variants. The analysis is Jacobian-free and thus compensates for the linear stability analysis in the literature. The results not only provide specific characterizations for the convergence rate and the basin of attraction, but also reveal intrinsic correlations among dynamics in the coupled HiSD. Theoretical results are substantiated by numerical experiments.
The dynamics through the first two Lagrange necks in the small-mass restricted three-body problem
Lei Liu; Pedro A. S. Salomão

We study the planar circular restricted three-body problem (PCR3BP) for sufficiently small mass ratios, from low energies to slightly above the second Lagrange value. We show that retrograde orbits around the primaries and Lyapunov orbits at the necks form the binding of a finite energy foliation. We construct these foliations using the theory of pseudoholomorphic curves in symplectizations developed by Hofer, Wysocki and Zehnder. Slightly above the second Lagrange value, the dynamics is transverse to families of disks bounded by the retrograde orbits, and cylinders connecting the retrograde orbits to the Lyapunov orbits, forming a $3-2-3-2$ foliation. The proof uses the rotating Kepler problem and Hill's lunar problem to control the singular limit as the mass ratio $μ\to 0$. As a consequence of the foliation, both Lyapunov orbits have infinitely many homoclinic orbits.
Induction instead of Feynman diagrams, L-functionals instead of Hilbert space

The main result of this paper is a construction of an inductive process that can replace Feynman diagrams. Combining this result with the notion of the L-functional, one can give an exposition of QED that does not suffer from infrared divergences
The existence of small defining polynomials for number fields, II

We prove that every number field of odd degree $n\geq 3$ and absolute discriminant $D$ has an integral defining polynomial whose coefficients are $O_n(D^{(n-1)/(2n-1)})$ in size. This strengthens, in odd-degree cases, the recently established bound of $O_n(D^{1/2})$ for all degrees $n$, which was conjectured in 1998 by Ruppert and is now known to be optimal in even degrees. More generally, we prove that this strengthened bound holds for all degree-$n$ fields having a real embedding and no subfield of index two. The proof makes use of the lattice shapes of the ring of integers and its trace dual, the inverse different. Assuming the quasi-Riemann hypothesis for Dedekind zeta functions, as recently announced by Cureton and Thorner, we obtain an exponent smaller than $1/2$ for every field with no index-two subfield, of any signature. In the case of primitive fields, we obtain the exponent $(n-1)/(2n)$. In particular, we prove that the optimal exponent for cubic fields is $1/3$.
Delaunay classification of positive singular solutions to the critical Lane--Emden system
Xia Huang; Yahui Jiang; Feng Zhou; Xianmei Zhou

We classify positive classical solutions of the Lane--Emden system \begin{align*} \begin{cases} -Δu=v^p & ~~\text{in }\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\},\\ -Δv=u^q &~~ \text{in }\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}, \end{cases} \end{align*} with a nonremovable singularity at $0$ (i.e., $\lim_{x\to0}u(x)=\lim_{x\to0}v(x)=+\infty$), where $n\ge3$ and $p,q>0$ satisfy \[ \frac1{p+1}+\frac1{q+1}=\frac{n-2}{n}. \] Without additional growth or integrability assumptions, we establish radial symmetry about the origin, strict radial decrease, and global two-sided power bounds for both components. Furthermore, every such solution can be written as \[ u(x)=|x|^{-α}U(\log|x|),\qquad v(x)=|x|^{-β}V(\log|x|), \] where $α=\frac{n}{q+1}$, $β=\frac{n}{p+1}$, and $(U,V)$ is either the positive equilibrium $(A,B)=((\fracαβ)^{\fracα{2}}, (\fracαβ)^{\fracβ{2}})$ or a positive nonconstant periodic solution of the associated Emden--Fowler system. These periodic solutions form a Delaunay family: for every $\varepsilon\in(0,A)$, there is a unique profile pair, up to translation in $t=\log|x|$, with $\min_{\mathbb{R}}U=\varepsilon$. The Hamiltonian energy provides an alternative parameter, decreasing continuously and strictly from zero to the equilibrium energy as $\varepsilon$ increases from $0$ to $A$. The common least period of the two components tends to infinity as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ and to the period of the linearized oscillation at $(A,B)$ as $\varepsilon\uparrow A$. The classification includes the case of a sublinear exponent.
Constrained Nested-Logit Pricing: An Exact Reformulation and Global Optimization Method

Sellers must price substitutable products while meeting operational requirements such as price limits and sales targets. Nested logit captures stronger substitution among similar products, but these requirements can undermine the structure used to solve unconstrained pricing problems. We develop an exact reformulation and a global optimization method for a fixed assortment with price bounds and weighted price caps. The key novelty is to concentrate the difficult interactions at the nest level while retaining convex optimization over individual products, without discretizing prices or approximating demand. This structure makes the number of nests, rather than products, govern the exponent in a conditional worst-case complexity bound. The method returns feasible prices together with a bound on how much profit could still be gained, allowing decision makers to assess solution quality even when computation stops early. Extensions cover purchase-probability bounds and price-order rules, with explicit accounts of their computational cost. In synthetic experiments, the method certifies solutions for assortments of up to 500 products with few nests. Projecting unconstrained prices onto the feasible set loses up to 32.60% of profit relative to direct constrained optimization, highlighting the value of jointly optimizing substitution and feasibility.
Infinitely many convex polytopes with dihedral angles bounded above by $π/2+δ$
Zhenkun Li; Jinmin Wang; Jing Yu
For every $δ>0$, we construct infinitely many pairwise combinatorially distinct convex three-dimensional polytopes whose dihedral angles are all less than $π/2+δ$.
Perfect Wave Transfer in Nonconformal Tomonaga-Luttinger Liquids

Perfect wave transfer (PWT) reproduces spatial reflection at a common finite time under a fixed Hamiltonian. We classify this process for open compact bosons and inhomogeneous Tomonaga--Luttinger liquids, distinguishing transfer of oscillator and neutral observables from transfer on the charged field algebra. In the single-charge model, the first two notions coincide. Global transfer additionally requires rephasing of the compact zero mode. For regular reflection-symmetric channels, exact oscillator transfer forces an odd multiple of the optical crossing time and a strictly ordered, parity-compatible spectrum differing from the conformal ladder at only finitely many levels. This spectral condition is also sufficient when the Robin boundary data induced by the physical profile are included. Requiring Neumann conditions after the Liouville transformation instead forces conformality. We construct an explicit, regular one-defect family for every $r>1/2$. Its transfer parameters are precisely the reduced fractions $r=p/q$ with odd numerator and denominator, with shortest transfer time $pL/v_0$. At the delay $3L/v_0$, the $r=3/5$ profile has numerical contrast $K_{\max}/K_{\min}\simeq 12.913$, compared with $81$ for $r=3$. Two independent conservative discretizations show second-order convergence on fixed mode bands. Occupation- and charge-constrained error estimates quantify robustness, while an exact homogeneous-chain calculation explains the $J^{2/3}$ resolved-band scale also observed in the engineered channels. These results provide a spectral design method and finite-device benchmarks for quadratic quantum channels. An interacting microscopic realization remains open.
Twisted Verlinde Formula for Finite Cyclic Orbifolds of Vertex Operator Algebras

Let $V$ be a simple, rational, $C_2$-cofinite and self-dual vertex operator algebra of CFT type, and let $G$ be a finite cyclic automorphism group of $V$. We establish a twisted Verlinde formula for cyclic groups of arbitrary finite order, expressing fusion coefficients among twisted $V$-modules in terms of the $S$-matrix in the orbifold theory. As an application, we compute fusion rules among twisted modules for the permutation orbifold $\left(V^{\otimes k}\right)^{\langle g\rangle}$ associated with a $k$-cycle $g=(1\,2\,\cdots\,k)$.
On optimal convergence rates for parametrized variational problems with applications to nonlocal models
Zhaolong Han; James Scott; Xiaochuan Tian

We develop an abstract variational framework for convergence rates of parametrized problems and their Galerkin approximations, with applications to nonlocal diffusion. The main objective is to quantify modeling and discretization errors in terms of the nonlocal horizon, the mesh size, the Sobolev regularity of the local solution, and the compatibility of boundary data. We establish error estimates in energy and $L^2$ norms and develop an adaptation of the Aubin--Nitsche argument that uses regularity of the limiting local dual problem. This approach yields improved $L^2$ estimates without requiring additional regularity of the nonlocal dual solutions, including for integrable kernels. We apply the framework to two constant-horizon nonlocal Laplacians with exterior boundary data and to heterogeneous localization models with classical Dirichlet, Neumann, and Robin conditions. The resulting estimates provide quantitative guarantees of asymptotic compatibility and improve existing error bounds under weaker regularity assumptions. Numerical experiments illustrate the convergence rates and examine the sharpness of the estimates.
Walsh Analysis in the Twenty-First Century: Convergence, Summability, Nonlinear Approximation, Universality, and Digital Applications

Walsh analysis connects ordered Fourier convergence, summability, nonlinear approximation, and universal representation through a common character algebra. This survey examines developments from 2000-2026 against their classical foundations. Binary kernel geometry explains Hardy-space losses and summability thresholds; interval and packet methods control spectral selection; localized blocks produce correction and universal representations with distinct coefficient and exceptional-set requirements. Selected proofs and counterexamples compare these mechanisms and identify where an implication needs an additional hypothesis. The same distinctions organize digital integration, sparse measurements, Boolean spectra, and generalized Walsh bases. Quantitative thresholds, source conventions, and published theorem pointers are collected in comparative tables.
