We develop a unified homology theory for directed partial orders (DPOs) and lattice-ordered positive cones on fields of characteristic zero. With the underlying field and its operations fixed, we define order?carrying spaces independently by topological conditions, establish a bijection with DPO positive cones, and characterize lattice orders by intersections of minimal open neighborhoods. A unified comparison theorem identifies graded Ext for region ideals with sheaf cohomology and multiplicative Tor with the reduced singular homology of truncated regions, giving a topological interpretation of the existence and preservation of reduced decompositions. We obtain canonical cohomological obstructions to lattice ordering, prove that a coefficient module for positive multiplication is flat if and only if the multiplier has a positive inverse, and show that every strict extension of positive cones on the same field produces a nonzero first Tor obstruction. Finally, we place the concrete lattice recently constructed by Bao-Zhang within this framework.
From the quantum group $U_{q^{1/2}}( {\widehat {\mathfrak{sl}}}_2 )$ to the Kronecker quantum cluster algebra
Junyuan Huang; Xueqing Chen; Ming Ding; Fan Xu

Let $\mathcal A_q$ be the Kronecker quantum cluster algebra with principal coefficients. We construct an explicit algebra homomorphism from the whole quantum group ${U_{q^{1/2}}}( {\widehat {\mathfrak{sl}_2}} )$ to $\mathcal A_q$, whose images together with either of the two frozen variables generate $\mathcal A_q$. As an application, we obtain algebra homomorphisms from the split $\imath$quantum groups of affine $\widehat {\mathfrak{sl}}_2$ to $\mathcal A_q$. Moreover, we explicitly determine the images of the positive and negative real and imaginary root vectors of ${U_{q^{1/2}}}( {\widehat {\mathfrak{sl}_2}} )$ in terms of quantum cluster variables.
Hopf-Galois Structures on Extensions Arising from Division Points on Elliptic Curves

We provide a general construction of infinite Hopf-Galois extensions from a direct system of finite Hopf-Galois extensions. We then apply this framework to extensions generated by division points on elliptic curves. Specifically, for a number field $K$ and an elliptic curve $E/K$ of rank at least $1$ with $P\in E(K)$ of infinite order, we consider for each integer $n\geq 2$ the extension $L_n=K(Q_n)$, where $Q_n\in E(\overline{K})$ is such that $nQ_n=P$. We show that the finite-level extensions $L_n/K$ need not be Hopf-Galois, and we give sufficient conditions for them to be so. We then prove that the infinite extension $L_\infty=\bigcup_{n\geq 2}L_n$ of $K$ is potentially Hopf-Galois, meaning it becomes Hopf-Galois after a finite extension of the base field.
Law-Dependent Poisson-Refresh Randomised Feedback Control for Stochastic Systems

This paper studies a continuous-time probabilistic control problem for stochastic systems in which the feedback law assigns a probability distribution over control inputs. The control is modelled as a law-dependent Poisson-refresh process: it is held constant between refresh times and resampled at Poisson times from a feedback rule depending on the current state and state law. The closed-loop system is therefore formulated as a jump--diffusion for the joint state--control process. The objective is to design the sampling rule by comparing the realised closed-loop system with a prescribed reference description. The cost separates two local terms: a relative-entropy penalty for the instantaneous refresh kernel and a state-side drift-mismatch cost. The state-side term is evaluated at the realised control value and is motivated by a frozen-control Girsanov identity. Under global Lipschitz, moment, and uniform ellipticity assumptions, we prove well-posedness of the closed loop and a dynamic programming principle on the joint state--control law space. For linear data and admissible mean-dependent affine-Gaussian refresh rules, the full joint law need not remain Gaussian, but the first and second moments of the joint state--control process close exactly. This yields a deterministic reduced control problem on moment space, with an explicit running cost, a reduced Hamiltonian, and a verification theorem.
A Polynomial Erdős-Pósa bound for Eulerian digraphs
Esther Galby; Roohani Sharma; Bart van der Steenhoven

In [Combinatorica 1996], Reed, Robertson, Seymour and Thomas proved Younger's conjecture dating back to 1973 that states that directed cycles have the Erdős-Pósa property. Specifically, they showed that every directed graph $D$ contains either $k$ arc-disjoint cycles or a set of at most $f(k)$ arcs that intersect every directed cycle. The function $f$, depending only on $k$, is however notoriously large--in fact, not even elementary. The first improvement on this function was only very recently provided by Hatzel, Kreutzer, Milani, and Muzi [FOCS 2024] who showed that $f$ can be taken to be an exponential tower of height $8$.
 In this work, we improve this function to $O(k^4)$ in the case where the digraph is Eulerian. This also answers an open question by Wahlström [Springer Monographs in Mathematics 2018] who asked explicitly when Eulerian digraphs have a polynomial Erdős-Pósa property.
 The only other known result about Erdős-Pósa on Eulerian digraphs is a result from Seymour [Combinatorica 1996] who showed that $f(k)=k$ when the Eulerian digraph admits a linkless embedding in 3-space, and such an equality is not possible for general Eulerian digraphs. We also complement our positive result, by showing that the result of Seymour cannot be extended to give a linear bound ($O(k)$) on general Eulerian digraphs, by showing that even on Eulerian digraphs the lower bound for the Erdős-Pósa property is $Ω(k \log k)$.
Existence of Lagrangian Mean Curvature Flow Singularities with Bounded Mean Curvature

In every dimension $n \ge 3$, we show there exist Lagrangian mean curvature flows that develop neck pinch singularities such that the mean curvature remains uniformly bounded. This follows from a related result that, under a structural assumption on the singularity formation, the mean curvature at small scales near the singularity can be bounded by the Lagrangian angle at outer scales with suitable weights. Applying this result to a subset of the finite-time Lagrangian mean curvature flow singularities constructed in the companion paper [arXiv:2607.03152] and the infinite-time Lagrangian mean curvature flow singularities constructed by Tsai, Wood, and the second-named author [arXiv:2401.02228] then gives examples of both finite-time and infinite-time singularity formation with uniformly bounded mean curvature.
Certified Collision Exclusion and an Unconditional Upper Bound $Λ<0.156821$ for the de Bruijn--Newman Constant

The de Bruijn--Newman constant $Λ$ is the transition time beyond which all zeros of the heat-deformed Riemann $ξ$-function are real. We develop a computer-assisted collision-exclusion method and obtain the bound $Λ<156821/10^6=0.156821$, in the normalisation of Polymath. The proof combines the published finite-height verification and the starting inequality $Λ\leq1/5$ with a compact-interior continuation theorem, five stable prime-polynomial Gram sources, certified moving-index recovery, a balanced real-jet transfer and a uniform Euler-product barrier at infinity. The resulting closed time-band exclusion, together with uniform remote reality, forces strictness at the proposed endpoint. The finite certificate uses 664,505 structural Fourier coefficients, 44,182 closed torus boxes, 184 separator moments and 17,385 separator rectangles. We isolate a Cauchy--Schwarz obstruction intrinsic to the four-prime source family, explaining the narrow feasibility margin of the certified endpoint. We state the proof-to-certificate interface and distinguish the present unconditional logical claim from other recent, as yet unrefereed, computational bounds.
From Continuum-Kinematics-Inspired Peridynamics to Simplicial Hyperelasticity

We develop a variational and functional-analytic framework for continuum-kinematics-inspired peridynamics with simultaneous nonlocal interactions among multiple points. We encode the finite-difference data of each interacting simplex in a simplicial deformation gradient. For nondegenerate simplices in three dimensions, the gradient, its cofactor, and its determinant encode the associated continuum-kinematics-inspired peridynamic line, area, and volume changes, respectively. This unified representation leads to a class of simplicial hyperelastic energies with general, possibly nonadditive, constitutive dependence on the affine deformation of an interacting simplex, thereby extending the original continuum-kinematics-inspired peridynamic framework.
 To describe interactions occurring at different scales and over different simplex geometries, we introduce radial- and shape-weighted nonlocal spaces. Their multipoint seminorms control two-point energies induced by the edge marginals of the interaction measure. This comparison yields nonlocal Poincaré inequalities and fractional Sobolev embeddings.
 We establish existence of equilibrium configurations by two complementary mechanisms. Particle-wise averaged convexity yields weak lower semicontinuity of the associated energy functionals. Under stronger assumptions on the edge marginals, fractional compactness gives existence for nonconvex energy densities. These results provide a mathematical foundation for simplicial and continuum-kinematics-inspired peridynamic models.
Sharp asymptotic stability of the IPM equation in $\mathbb{R}^2$ via isopycnal coordinates
Roberta Bianchini; Timothée Crin-Barat; Ling-Yun Shou; Shan Wang

We study the incompressible porous media (IPM) equation, a model describing the motion of a fluid with variable density through a porous medium under the action of gravity. We prove that the stably stratified state, in which heavier fluid lies below lighter fluid, is nonlinearly stable: small perturbations decay over time and the fluid returns to equilibrium. Our result holds in the sharp Sobolev setting $H^s(\mathbb R^2)$ for every $s>2$: this threshold cannot be improved, since the equation is ill-posed in $H^2(\mathbb R^2)$. This result follows from a proof of global well-posedness at critical Besov regularity, with smallness required only in a norm invariant under the natural scaling of the equation. We also prove optimal decay rates for suitably localized initial data.
 The main difficulty is that the stabilizing effect of stratification acts only in some directions, while the nonlinear transport acts in all of them. Reaching the sharp regularity threshold requires two main novelties. First, we rewrite the equation in \emph{isopycnal coordinates}, which follow the level sets of the density: in these coordinates the transport becomes one-dimensional, and the anisotropic stabilizing mechanism can be exploited at minimal regularity. Second, we establish new \emph{anisotropic commutator estimates} which allow us to control the remaining nonlinear terms. Finally, we show that the estimates obtained in isopycnal coordinates can be transferred back to the original variables.
Variational Splines and Generalized Gaussian Processes

Tikhonov regularization, kriging, and Gaussian-process regression share the same algorithm because, for a linear inverse problem with a Gaussian prior and Gaussian noise, the minimum-mean-square-error (MMSE) estimator is the solution of a regularized least-squares problem. We show that this equivalence survives the passage from vectors to generalized functions: the regularized least-squares estimators become generalized splines, and the Gaussian random vectors become generalized Gaussian processes (GGPs) on the dual of a nuclear space. A whitening operator $\mathrm{L}: \mathcal{S} \to L_2$ specifies both the native Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_\mathrm{L} \subset \mathcal{S}'$ of the splines and a family of GGPs, which solve a stochastic differential equation subject to boundary conditions. We prove that the Gaussian spaces of these processes are congruent to the core $\mathrm{L}^\ast(L_2)$ of the native space, and that their MMSE estimators from finitely many linear measurements are generalized splines. Our framework extends the classical correspondences of Kimeldorf-Wahba, Parzen and Kailath in two respects: our estimators form a broader class that includes generalized functions, and we give a proper Bayesian treatment of the case where the null space of $\mathrm{L}$ is non-trivial. The framework gives a precise meaning to statements such as ``fractional splines are the optimal estimators of fractional Brownian motion,'' and it provides a rigorous Bayesian formulation of infinite-dimensional linear inverse problems.
Separation Is a Riesz Energy: How Many Environments Does ICA Need?
Yuda Bi; Yubo Guo; Jiaxiao Cai; Xiaonai Li; Zhuolin Li; Vince D. Calhoun

How many environments and samples does it take to separate $d$ Gaussian sources whose variances change across environments? Each source has a signature, its vector of variances. The Riesz $2$-energy $E_j$ of source $j$ sums the inverse Fisher informations for rotating it towards other sources. With known whitening, we prove a worst-case squared-angle risk lower bound of order $E_j/(n+E_j)$ for orthogonal estimators at every $n$ and $d$. A quadratic pencil given the signatures attains $E_j/n$ up to a constant above a separation-dependent sample threshold, even with estimated whitening. For well-spread signatures at fixed $K$, the energy grows as $d^2$, $d\log d$ and $d$ for $K=2$, $3$ and $K\ge4$, respectively. A design with $K\asymp\log d$ and pairwise Fisher information bounded below by a constant makes $d\log d$ samples sufficient. The eigenvectors of a single fixed linear combination have an average first-order error coefficient of at least order $d^2$. Simulations up to $d=1000$ support the first-order predictions, and on task fMRI the energy helps rank split-half instability.
Calmness Modulus of Parameterized Convex Constraint Systems: Exact Closed-Form Formulas via Second-Order Admissibility

We resolve the open problem of deriving an exact, closed-form algebraic formula for the calmness modulus of $\mathcal{C}^2$ convex constrained feasible set mappings $\mathcal{F}(b) := \{ x \in \mathbb{R}^n \colon f_t(x) \le b_t, \, \forall t \in T \}$ under right-hand side perturbations at a given pair of the graph $(\bar{b}, \bar{x})$.
 First, under the condition $0_n \in \mathrm{int}\left(\mathrm{conv}\left\{ \nabla f_t(\bar{x}) ,\; t \in T(\bar{x}) \right\}\right)$, we prove that the calmness modulus coincides with the inverse distance from the origin to the boundary of the nominal subdifferential.
 Second, for general $\mathcal{C}^2$ convex systems where the previously mentioned interior condition does not hold, we introduce a second-order admissibility filtering over the active indexes. We show that this filtered family, $\mathcal{D}^0_2(\bar{x})$, yields an exact characterization of the calmness modulus relying solely on nominal data.

Random spherical eigenfunctions for the Lalplace-Beltrami operator are well understood and their local behavior, after renormalization, is described by Berry's random wave model. In this paper we construct a family of random fields on the sphere $\mathbb{S}^{3}$, identified with the group $SU(2)$, endowed with a sub-Riemannian structure. These fields are random eigenfunctions for the sub-Laplacian and they are constructed from matrix elements of unitary irreducible representations of $SU(2)$. We prove that the local behavior of such fields is the same as the Berry-Heisenberg random field on the Heisenberg group introduced in [10].

In this paper, we introduce the concepts of ~`\emph{rough weighted ideal-$τ$-convergence}' and ~`\emph{rough weighted ideal-$τ$-cluster point}' of a net in locally solid Riesz spaces. We also compare these concepts with key findings from the works of Lahiri $\&$ Das (2007/2008), Das (2012) and Aytar (2008), as follows:
 [(i):] The set of \emph{ideal-cluster points} of a sequence in a topological space is closed, 
[(ii):] The set of \emph{ideal-cluster points} of a net in a topological space is closed, [(iii):] The set of \emph{rough ideal-cluster points} of a sequence in a norm linear space is closed. 
 We demonstrate that, generally, the set of ~`\emph{rough weighted ideal-$τ$-cluster points}' of a net in a locally solid Riesz space may not satisfy the aforementioned results, which implies that it may not be closed. This suggests that this set exhibits new characteristics, which we will discuss here. Ultimately, our characterization demonstrates that these new concepts can help identify an ideal that is maximal and effectively represent any closed $τ$-neighborhood of $θ$ within these spaces.
Quasi-norms on $\mathbb{R}^d$: Characterization and Approximation by Conic Splines

We first show that a regularizer on $\mathbb{R}^d$ that is continuous, symmetric, and amplitude-equivariant is of the form $g=q^γ$ with $γ>0$, where $q$ is continuous and absolutely homogeneous; we call the set of such $q$ the CH class, whose convex members are the seminorms. Within the CH class, we single out two configurations of interest for regularization: the quasi-norms, which are exactly the positive-definite members of the family, and the quasi-seminorms with null space control, which are the composition of a quasi-norm with a linear map that sets the null space. We then propose a universal parametrization of the class by conic splines, the continuous functions that are linear on each cone of a polyhedral fan. Specifically, we show that the polyhedral CH functionals are exactly the symmetric non-negative conic splines, and that these admit a stable nodal representation in a basis of conic B-splines. Finally, we determine the rates of approximation: the conic spline interpolant converges at the second-order rate $h^2\asymp n^{-2/(d-1)}$, in the $L_\infty$-norm on the hyper-sphere when the angular profile is twice differentiable, and in the $L_1$-norm when its spherical Hessian variation is bounded, which covers the polyhedral members of the class. The rate is sharp, already for the Euclidean norm. The planar case is worked out in full, with the trigonometric hat functions as basis and an $\ell_1$-norm of second differences as regularity index.
Equilibrium webs and stability for arbitrary families of endomorphisms of projective spaces
Fabrizio Bianchi; Zhuchao Ji; Junyi Xie

We consider arbitrary holomorphic families of endomorphisms of a complex projective space. We prove that the existence of an equilibrium web implies the holomorphic motion of all repelling cycles contained in the Julia set, i.e., the support of the unique measure of maximal entropy. Together with previous results of Berteloot, Bianchi, Brévard, Buff, and Dupont, this completes the extension of the stability-bifurcation theory to arbitrary families of holomorphic endomorphisms. The same conclusions also hold for holomorphic families of polynomial-like maps of large topological degree.

We prove that every $C^1$ collapsed Anosov flow on a closed three-manifold with non-virtually-solvable fundamental group is accessible. No transitivity or nonwandering assumption is required, and the collapsing map need not satisfy the strong-collapse conditions. We also prove that every three-dimensional collapsed Anosov flow for which no positive iterate is a discretized Anosov flow is accessible.
Cross-Modal Semantic Successive Refinement for Generative Image Communication over Underwater Acoustic Channels
Xu Pei; Bin Wang; Guangxu Zhu; Yi Zhang; Haiyan Fan

Underwater acoustic communication faces challenges such as limited available bandwidth and complex channel environments, which impose demanding requirements on efficient image transmission and reliable reconstruction. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a generative image communication framework based on cross-modal semantic successive refinement. At the transmitter, text descriptions, compact bottleneck features, and visual side information compressed by residual vector quantization are transmitted. At the receiver, text and bottleneck features are first fused to predict a base estimate of the intermediate visual representation. The received RVQ indices are then used to recover supplementary visual information and perform residual correction, followed by image reconstruction using a one-step Pixel Mean Flow model. During training, a CLIP-based text-image semantic consistency constraint is introduced to preserve the semantic correspondence between generated results and the original text descriptions. During transmission, protection resources are allocated according to the importance of different information branches and RVQ quantization stages. Simulations using COCO 2017 images and measured underwater acoustic channel records from Watermark show that text and bottleneck features provide complementary semantic and structural conditions, RVQ visual side information further improves reconstruction quality, and layered unequal error protection helps improve recovery at low SNRs. Code-rate allocation experiments reveal a tradeoff between the reliability of fundamental conditions and visual-detail reconstruction under a limited visual-feature coding budget, providing guidance for allocating protection resources in underwater acoustic image transmission.
The Quantum Stochastic Limit for Non-Markovian Driving Processes

We express the stochastic limit (weak-coupling limit) of a quantum system interacting with its environment as the limit of solutions to a parametrized family of quantum stochastic differential equations (QSDEs). We prove the convergence of such solutions in the case where the driving processes may be non-Markovian and the system may be infinite-dimensional with unbounded Hamiltonian. We achieve this by imposing a particular condition on the n-point functions of the driving process which we verify for annihilation, creation, and gauge operators on a bosonic Fock space with sufficient mixing. Additionally, we include not only the usual fast-evolving system Hamiltonian which is averaged out in the limit, but also a slow-evolving system Hamiltonian which survives the limit. We also relax the requirement for the fast-evolving Hamiltonian to have a purely discrete spectrum allowing accumulation points under some circumstances. Moreover, our convergence mode for the processes is convergence of all time-centered n-point functions which is stronger than the typical semigroup convergence for the stochastic limit.
$C_2$-Cofiniteness of Permutation Orbifolds I: Relative $C_1$ Descent

We establish a relative $C_1$-cofiniteness criterion for $C_2$-cofiniteness of finite group orbifolds. For permutation actions on a simple, self contragredient, $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra of CFT type, it suffices to check a single relation for a derivative of the conformal vector in the Virasoro vertex operator algebra. This reduces the problem to a calculation depending only on the central charge and tensor degree. An exact calculation then proves cofiniteness for a family of nonsolvable permutation orbifolds without restricting the central charge.

We consider the 3-D rotating magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) equations. The combination of rotation and background magnetic field leads to the occurrence of dispersive magneto-Coriolis waves in the linearized equations. We establish a t ^{-1} decay estimate for waves with dispersion relation $σ$($ξ$) = $ξ$ \_3 h(|$ξ$|) under suitable assumptions on h, and show that this includes magneto-Coriolis waves. Then we apply these dispersive estimates to the nonlinear rotating MHD equations and obtain an improved lower bound on the lifespan of solutions.
Constructing Cospectral Hypergraphs Using Adjacency Preserving Permutations

In this paper, we use permutations of the vertices of hypergraphs that preserve their adjacency matrices defined in banerjee 2021. These permutations form a group which lies between the automorphism group and the full symmetric group $S_n$ where $n$ is the number of vertices. Using elements from that group which are not automorphisms, we construct cospectral non-isomorphic hypergraphs. We use hypergraph structure coming from finite projective planes to show existence of infinitely many families of such hypergraphs. Also this method is very specific to uniform hypergraphs with uniformity greater than or equal to 3, i.e not applicable to graphs.
Rational Torsion and Ramification Constraints on Odd Superelliptic Jacobians

Let C: y^d = f(x) be a smooth projective superelliptic curve over Q, where d >= 3 is odd, f(x) in Q[x] is separable of degree n >= 3, and gcd(d,n) = 1. Let J = Jac(C) be its Jacobian. We study the rational torsion subgroup J(Q)_tors through the interaction of ramification geometry, Galois actions, reduction at primes of good reduction, and the geometry of divisors. First, we describe the subgroup R_d contained in J[d] generated by the ramification-point differences and determine its Galois-invariant subgroup explicitly in terms of the sizes of the Galois orbits of the roots of f. This yields a precise description of the rational d-torsion classes arising from ramification, without assuming that they account for all of J(Q)[d]. Second, we establish criteria based on the orders of reduced Jacobians that can prove the vanishing of the full rational torsion subgroup. Finally, we derive geometric constraints on divisor classes represented by effective divisors of degree smaller than the genus, including a restriction arising when distinct effective divisors represent the same class. Explicit examples illustrate how the Galois-theoretic and reduction-theoretic methods can be combined to study rational torsion on odd superelliptic Jacobians.
Linear maps of $C^*$-algebras preserving norm parallelism
Chi-Kwong Li; Ming-Cheng Tsai; Ya-Shu Wang; Ngai-Ching Wong

Two elements $a,b$ in a normed space are parallel if $\|a+γb\|=\|a\|+\|b\|$ for some $|γ|=1$; they form a triangle equality attaining (TEA) pair if $\|a+b\|=\|a\|+\|b\|$. For finite-dimensional complex $C^*$-algebras other than $\mathbf M_2(\mathbb C)$ and $\mathbb C\oplus_\infty\mathbb C$, bijective linear maps on these algebras preserving parallel or TEA pairs are scalar multiples of isometries. For unital abelian algebras with spectra containing at least three points, preservation in both directions gives the same conclusion. We obtain corresponding results for type I factors, simple type I $C^*$-algebras, and unitarily invariant operator spaces under additional continuity and finite-rank hypotheses. All results for $C(X)$ and $B(H,K)$ hold over both real and complex fields.
Improving Hydrofoil Efficiency Through Simulation-Driven Design Optimization
Ante Sikirica; Ivana Lučin; Marta Alvir; Tin Matulja

Foil windsurfing is a sport in which competitors fine-tune their setup to optimize performance under varying environmental conditions. However, such adjustments are typically guided by intuition. This paper presents a methodology for improving hydrofoil design using computational fluid dynamics. First, structured light scanning was used to obtain the geometry of a conventional hydrofoil. Subsequently, five derived designs have been explored, inspired by advancements in airplane wing design. Following this, a preliminary design was selected, and a design of experiments approach was implemented. Generated simulation data were used to train a machine learning surrogate, which is ultimately used in the multi-objective design optimization. While the surrogate-based approach yielded promising results, it was limited to exploring a restricted set of design parameters. To overcome this constraint, additional improvements were attained through adjoint optimization, demonstrating that comparable performance can be achieved with a distinctly different hydrofoil design. Finally, the conventional design was refined through adjoint optimization. Notably, adjoint optimization yielded a 15% increase in efficiency. The results suggest that both proposed approaches can produce novel hydrofoil designs capable of outperforming the original configuration under specific conditions; however, due to its inherent flexibility, the adjoint approach with realistic constraints offers more freedom in the design exploration process.
Fano's Inequality and Channel Capacity in the Individual-Sequence Regime

We derive an individual-sequence analogue of Fano's inequality, replacing entropy by Lempel--Ziv (LZ) complexity and probability of error by empirical error frequency. In the setting considered, an arbitrary encoder maps a message to a channel input sequence $\{x_t\}$, the channel maps the input to an output $\{y_t\}$ in a completely arbitrary manner, and a block finite-state decoder produces an estimate of the channel input from the output. The individual-sequence Fano inequality lower-bounds the empirical symbol-error frequency in terms of the LZ complexity of the channel input conditioned on the channel output. This leads to a channel coding converse: reliable communication at a given rate is possible only if that rate does not exceed the individual-sequence LZ channel capacity, defined as the LZ mutual information maximized over channel inputs and minimized (worst-case) over a noise set. We also prove a matching achievability theorem for the class of \emph{symbol-wise invertible} channels, in which the channel output at each time $t$ is $y_t = f(x_t, v_t)$, $v_t$ being a `noise' variable, and $f(\cdot,v)$ is a bijection for every fixed $v$. This class includes group-additive channels $y_t = x_t \oplus v_t$ studied by Feder and coworkers. For such a channel, any rate below the LZ capacity is achievable with vanishing per-message error frequency, simultaneously for every $v^n$ in a given noise set $\mathcal{N}$, provided $\mathcal{N}$ is closed under block permutations; this condition is satisfied by any noise set that depends on $v^n$ only via its type class with respect to such blocks. The achievability uses a universal decoder that requires no knowledge of the channel and no feedback.
A Galois-type Springer theorem for hermitian and generalized quadratic forms

We prove that anisotropy of nonsingular hermitian and skew-hermitian forms over central simple algebras with involution is preserved under scalar extension to every finite Galois extension of odd degree coprime to the index of the algebra. In characteristic two, the same conclusion holds for generalized quadratic forms over algebras with involution of the first kind, with no nonsingularity assumption on their polar forms. The main tool is an isometry-level descent theorem. For a cyclic extension of odd prime degree, every anisotropic nonsingular form over a division algebra with involution, of rank smaller than the extension degree and with Galois-invariant isometry class, descends to an anisotropic form over the base field. Unlike descent results for Witt classes, this theorem descends the form itself. A bounded-rank reduction, based on injectivity of the Witt-group restriction map, derives the cyclic anisotropy theorem from this descent result; a regularization argument removes the nonsingularity assumption on polar forms in characteristic two, and the Feit-Thompson theorem extends the result to arbitrary finite Galois extensions of odd degree.
Optimal Error Estimates With Polynomial Dependence on $ε^{-1}$ for Mixed Finite Element Methods of the Cahn-Hilliard-Navier-Stokes System
Haijun Gao; Xi Li; Xiaoli Li

In this paper, we analyze a first-order convex-splitting mixed finite element scheme for the Cahn--Hilliard--Navier--Stokes system, tracking explicitly how the error constants depend on the interface width $ε$. Due to the strong nonlinear coupling inherent in the CHNS system and the singular dependence of the Cahn--Hilliard equation on $ε$, conventional energy-based analyzes often lead to severe dependence of the error constants on $ε^{-1}$, and may even result in exponential growth. Such dependence significantly limits the applicability of the resulting error estimates in the small-interfacial-thickness regime. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a robust parameter error analysis framework with respect to interfacial thickness $ε$. In particular, by introducing $H^{-1}$ approximation properties for the Ritz projection and the Ritz and Stokes quasi-projection operators, together with spectral-type estimates for the discrete perturbed Cahn--Hilliard operator, we effectively control the singular terms arising from the interfacial thickness parameter in the error analysis. Compared with the classical results, which address only the Allen-Cahn or Cahn-Hilliard equation, we adopt a three-term discrete Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality analysis technique and achieve a substantial reduction in the degree of polynomial dependence for the coupled system. Numerical experiments are presented to verify the effectiveness of the theoretical results and to demonstrate the robustness of the method for different parameters of interfacial thickness.
Koszul duality and homotopy algebras for operads over quivers

For a quiver $Q$, we introduce and study $Q$-operads (or operads over $Q$), defined as a special sort of $\mathbf{fc}$-multicategories or virtual double categories, in which the directions of the arrows of $Q$ encode the permitted input orderings. In this higher operadic framework, we construct the bar--cobar adjunction and develop a theory of Koszul duality and homotopy algebras, together with compatibility results under changes of quiver. We treat dg categories and their left modules, right modules, and bimodules as algebras over quiver-operads. We prove that these operads are Koszul and that their resolutions govern the corresponding $A_\infty$ categories and modules. We also categorify Sagave's notion of derived $A_\infty$ algebras and introduce modules over derived $A_\infty$ algebras and categories. Finally, we explain that restriction along a folding of quivers constructs diagonal $A_\infty$ bimodules, while extension along an inclusion of quivers realizes two-sided bar models of derived tensor products.
Flux-Matched Poisson Iteration for Generated Jacobian Equations: Local Convergence and Spectral Galerkin Approximation

We develop a flux-matched Poisson iteration for solving generated Jacobian equations with second boundary conditions. In each step, it solves a fixed shifted Poisson problem with a Neumann-type boundary condition. Near a smooth regular solution with positive $C^{1,1}$ densities, we prove that the iteration has local geometric convergence in $C^{2,α}$ on smooth connected Riemannian domains. The iteration is then discretized using a spectral Galerkin method, with local convergence proved for the Fourier-Jacobi scheme on spherical caps. Optical numerical experiments support these estimates and demonstrate useful imaging performance beyond the local convergence theory.
CARM: Conformal Adaptive Risk Masking for Reliable Scientific Super-Resolution
Guangtao Zhang; Haonan Wu; Junxuan Gao; Zhengyang Liu; Zhaoxi Zeng; Zhihao Li; Jianguo Huang; Zhiqiang Liu

Deep learning-based super-resolution (SR) can reconstruct fine-scale Earth-observation fields from coarse observations, but reconstruction accuracy alone does not provide a calibrated rule for identifying reliable spatial regions. Conformal Mask Calibration (CMC), built on conformal risk control, converts a spatial uncertainty score into a trust mask and controls the expected worst-case local distortion under exchangeability. However, its fixed threshold can become miscalibrated in Earth-observation streams affected by seasonality and episodic events. We propose $\textit{CARM}$ (Conformal Adaptive Risk Masking), a statistical framework for adaptive spatial risk control under temporal distribution shift. CARM maintains experts with heterogeneous update rates and aggregates their threshold proposals online using an asymmetric surrogate loss, balancing rapid adaptation to distribution changes against stability during relatively stationary periods. All updates are causal and use only mature feedback available after a fixed delay, allowing CARM to operate with any SR model that provides a spatial uncertainty score. We prove that the time-averaged mask-conditioned risk converges to at most $α$ at an $O(1/T)$ rate, without distributional assumptions and for any choice of aggregation weights across experts. On a daily South China Sea chlorophyll-$\textit{a}$ SR stream, CARM reduces the empirical violation rate from $43.49\%$ to $9.38\%$ and the moving-average exceedance frequency from $47.29\%$ to $1.22\%$ at $α=0.10$, while retaining a non-trivial trusted region. Experiments on ERA5 wind and OSTIA sea-surface temperature further show consistent relative improvements across multiple SR backbones.
Hadamard configurations and sharp cubic-period bounds for stealth in dimensions 10, 11, and 12

We construct explicit, nonlattice periodic point configurations in dimensions $10$, $11$ and $12$ with stealth center density $1/24$ and unit-density stealth radius $2\cdot24^{-1/n}$. These values exceed those of duals of the current record lattice packings, without claiming to exceed all possible lattices. The construction uses the $24$ sign rows of an order-$12$ Hadamard matrix and their antipodes, projected onto $n$ coordinates. For an arbitrary, not necessarily binary, equally weighted motif with marked period $2\mathbb{Z}^n$, we prove a sharp $2n$-point lower bound for a raw stealth radius at least one and classify equality by antipodal Hadamard configurations. We deduce bounded-complexity optimality, sharp optimality among binary motifs in dimensions $10$--$12$, and local maximality under simultaneous perturbations of the motif and the marked period shape. A divisibility argument excludes ordinary equally weighted periodic formal duals. Statements are confined to their indicated classes; no global optimality among arbitrary-period configurations is asserted.

Extending a result of Thomassen, we prove that for every choice of positive integers $K\geq k$ there exist a $K$-strong digraph which has two disjoint sets $S,T$ each of size $k$ so that the only linkage from $S$ to $T$ in $D$ is the one whose existence follows from Menger's theorem.
The Convergence Rate of Accelerated Proximal Gradient Methods with General Inertial Term for Convex Composite Multiobjective Optimization

We study accelerated proximal gradient methods with general stepsizes for convex composite multiobjective optimization, where each objective is a smooth convex term plus a proper closed convex term and the proximal subproblem keeps a separate offset for each objective. For a two-parameter root momentum rule with trajectory-dependent coefficients, we construct a new energy function and establish an energy identity. This yields sharper convergence guarantees: boundedness, weighted square summability of the displacements, a merit-function rate of $o(k^{-2})$, and displacement decay of $o(k^{-1})$ whenever the first parameter converges to a value in $(0,1)$; the second parameter need not converge or have bounded total variation. At the critical value $α=3$, we obtain $u_0(x^N)\le \frac{2\ell R}{N(N+3)},$ together with $O(1/N)$ displacement decay, square summability, and weak Pareto convergence. The remaining little-$o$ question at $α=3$ is reduced to the vanishing of a nonnegative critical energy. For $1<α<3$, we prove the rate $O(N^{-(α-1)})$, and for every $α>0$ we obtain $u_0(x^k)\to0$, $F_i(x^k)\to c_i$, and $\sum_k D_k/k<\infty$. A JOS1 experiment numerically validates the predicted little-$o$ separation and the rate behavior.
A Viscous Cascade Construction of Nonunique Leray--Hopf Solutions to the Unforced 3D Navier--Stokes Equations
Thomas Y. Hou; Xiang Qin; Peicong Song; Wenhan Zhang

We construct a nonzero divergence-free initial velocity on $\mathbb{R}^3$ and a continuum of pairwise distinct suitable Leray--Hopf solutions of the unforced three-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations on a common time interval. The initial datum is axisymmetric, smooth away from the origin, and belongs to every $L^{\mathfrak q}$ with $1\leq \mathfrak q<3$, but not to $L^3$. All the solutions attain this datum strongly in $L^2$, are smooth at positive times, and satisfy both the global and local energy equalities through time zero. The same family belongs simultaneously to every $L^{\mathfrak p}_tL^{\mathfrak q}_x$ with $1\leq \mathfrak p\leq\infty$, $2\leq \mathfrak q\leq\infty$, and $2/\mathfrak p+3/\mathfrak q>1$. The same solutions also belong to the critical Lorentz space $L^\infty_tL^{3,\infty}_x$. This endpoint is sharp for uniqueness in the Leray--Hopf class within the Lorentz scale.
 The proof is entirely analytic and uses a cascade through geometrically separated Gaussian swirls. We establish growth for the time-dependent viscous linearization and determine the sign of its complete quadratic stress, including the interaction of the reference velocity with the second variation. The integrated stress generates a controlled perturbation at the next larger spatial scale. At each finite cutoff, a prescribed terminal coordinate selects an initial perturbation whose physical $L^2$ norm tends to zero as the cutoff is removed. Uniform energy, moment, and transfer estimates yield the common strong initial trace while preserving a nonzero observable at a fixed positive time.
Reconstruction and well-posedness of an inverse coefficient problem for a diffusion equation
Siyu Cen; Bangti Jin; Yavar Kian; Zhi Zhou

In this work, we investigate the inverse coefficient problem of determining an unknown coefficient in a diffusion equation from a single boundary flux measurement. More precisely, assuming that the domain is cylindrical, we develop a unified theoretical and numerical framework for the stable reconstruction of a space-time-dependent coefficient, by reformulating the inverse problem as a nonlinear equation. The inherent nonlinearity of the problem is transferred to an auxiliary nonlinear equation, enabling the application of techniques and concepts from nonlinear analysis. By combining representation formulas with regularity properties of solutions to diffusion equations, we extend to nonlinear inverse problems an approach that has so far been restricted to linear ones. The theoretical reconstruction procedure is complemented by a numerical analysis of the proposed method, including convergence and error estimates, as well as numerical experiments. The proposed reconstruction algorithm is directly inspired by the theoretical framework.
Geodesic Transversal of Hypercube and Butterfly networks
R. Prabha; B. Sandhiya; Paul Manuel

A geodesic $P$ of a connected graph $G(V,E)$ is called a maximal geodesic if there exists no geodesic $P'$ in $G$ that contains $P$ as its sub-path. The geodesic transversal problem determines a subset $S\subseteq V(G)$ such that every possible maximal geodesic of $G$ includes at least one vertex of $S$. Such a set with minimum number of elements is called a gt-set and its cardinality is the gt-number of $G$. In this paper, we establish a general result, called the Geodesic Transversal lemma which provides a lower bound for the gt-number of an arbitrary graph $G$ in terms of the gt-number of its induced subgraphs. Using this lemma, we determine the gt-number of Butterfly and Hypercube networks.
Taylor Dupuy; Alon Levy; Thomas Tucker; Zhuoran Wang

We prove that a finite surjective post-critically finite self-map of a variety in characteristic zero remains post-critically finite on every preperiodic integral effective divisor after passing to its periodic image with its return map. Iterating this result proves PCF all the way down. A detailed report on AI usage is contained in the manuscript.
Compatible Condensation and Generalized Gauging: Marked Transport and Wall Interchange

We formulate condensation compatible with a specified separable generalized gauging operation in a unitary (2 + 1)-dimensional defect realization. Compatibility is a coherent reversible crossing of the full condensate algebra, retaining charged channels and the marked condensation interface. The resulting composite network determines the transported condensate, the induced operation, and a commuting square of specified walls. For connected gauging data, compatibility admits a central matching description that retains the transported condensate and its algebra identification on the specified wall. The specified unit may absorb a nontrivial parent anyon algebra; strong connectedness appears only as the transparent-unit specialization. We distinguish original vacuum insertions, vacuum branches after unit absorption, and the full vacuum algebra of the final phase, and we prove a complete Higgs criterion that incorporates the parent algebra absorbed by the specified unit. In the toric-code example of a non-invertible subgroup gauging we classify the compatible condensations for the fixed operation, exhibit two inequivalent crossings of the same parent condensate that lead to different final phases, and analyse a pure condensation operation in which the specified unit absorbs the parent electric condensate and produces additional final vacuum operators. The transparent-unit case recovers reverse-condensation transport and the vacuum-overlap formula, and the three complete Higgs conditions appear as a corollary of the general criterion.
Constrained minimization problem and unbounded dynamics for the four-dimensional Klein-Gordon-Schrödinger System
Masaru Hamano; Hiroaki Kikuchi; Kenta Tomioka

In this paper, we study the Klein-Gordon-Schrodinger system in four spatial dimensions. We consider a constrained minimization problem associated with the corresponding stationary system and establish the existence of a positive radial minimizer. We further investigate the asymptotic behavior and qualitative properties of minimizers. As an application, we analyze the dynamics of solutions with initial data in a potential well and prove that such solutions either blow up in finite time or exhibit unbounded growth in the energy norm as time tends to infinity. Since the minimizers lie on the boundary of the potential well, we also establish the strong instability of the associated standing waves.
Neighbourhood second Zagreb matrix of graphs: spectral radius bounds and extremal graphs

Let $G$ be a connected graph on at least two vertices, and let $δ(i)$ be the sum of the degrees of the neighbours of a vertex $i$. The \emph{neighbourhood second Zagreb matrix} $\NF(G)$ has $(i,j)$-entry $δ(i)δ(j)$ if $i\sim j$ and $0$ otherwise; its spectral radius is denoted by $\rNF(G)$. We prove that $\rNF(G)\geρ(G)^{5}$, where $ρ(G)$ is the adjacency spectral radius, with equality if and only if $G$ is regular or bipartite semiregular, and we use this to show that the same graphs are exactly the extremal graphs of a Berman--Zhang--type upper bound. We sharpen the estimates $\demin^{2}ρ(G)\le\rNF(G)\le\demax^{2}ρ(G)$ by means of the extreme edge weights of $\NF(G)$, give sharp upper bounds in terms of the maximum degree $\dmax$, the maximum neighbourhood degree sum $\demax$, the size $m$ and the clique number $ω(G)$, and determine the extremal graphs for bipartite graphs and trees. For every connected unicyclic graph $G$ of order $n\ge3$ we prove $32=\rNF(C_n)\le\rNF(G)\le\rNF(\Sp n)$, where $\Sp n$ is the triangle with $n-3$ pendant edges at one vertex, with equality only for $C_n$ and only for $\Sp n$, respectively. Finally, we give bounds in terms of the first Zagreb index and for the neighbourhood second Zagreb energy; for lower energy bounds, the extremal graphs are described completely.

In this paper, we investigate the superposition of two minimal Darboux transformations in Euclidean three-space. A four-dimensional permutability diagram for transformations of isothermic surfaces yields the common minimal transform for distinct nonzero parameters and an explicit formula for its Gauss map. This formula determines the planar ends over regular umbilic-free points of the seed: an end is embedded when the two transformed Gauss maps coincide away from the seed value and has multiplicity 3 when all three values coincide. We illustrate this criterion with the Enneper surface and the catenoid. For the catenoid, suitable parameters give complete surfaces of finite total curvature, and we determine the numbers and multiplicities of their planar ends from the parameters and initial values. In the family with multiplicity-3 ends, the remaining initial-value parameter realizes, up to rotation, the López--Ros deformation.
On the Cameron-Praeger conjecture for Steiner 6-designs
Ximin Wang; Zheng Huang; Weijun Liu

A long-standing and far-reaching conjecture of Cameron and Praeger (1993) asserts that no non-trivial block-transitive $6$-$(v,k,λ)$ designs exist. Huber (2010) reduced the Steiner case ($λ=1$) to a single infinite family of possible exceptions, where the automorphism group is $G=\PGaL(2,p^e)$ acting on the points of the projective line, with $p\in\{2,3\}$ and $e$ an odd prime power. In this paper, we resolve this final case. By combining orbit-stabiliser analysis for the action of specific involutions in $\PGaL(2,p^e)$ with the modular arithmetic constraints derived from the design parameters, we prove that no such Steiner 6-designs can exist for any admissible $q$. This completes the proof that the Cameron-Praeger conjecture is true for the important case of non-trivial Steiner 6-designs.
Descriptor representations of geometric port-Hamiltonian systems on Hilbert spaces

We establish conversions in both directions between geometric and descriptor representations of linear port-Hamiltonian systems on infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. For the geometric-to-descriptor conversion, we represent the possibly multivalued inverse Dirac relation by a skew-adjoint operator on enlarged Hilbert spaces, retaining the original operator-domain restrictions. The construction accommodates internal and external ports. We show that the conversions preserve trajectories and the power balance. An incompressible Kelvin--Voigt solid illustrates the results.
Odd and even fake quadrics isogenous to a product
Fabrizio Catanese; JongHae Keum; Do Geun Kim; Kyoung-Seog Lee

A $\mathbb{Q}$-homology quadric is a smooth compact complex surface which has the same $\mathbb{Q}$-homology as a quadric surface, that is, the product of two $2$-dimensional spheres. It is called fake if it is minimal and not rational. Among them are the fake quadrics which are isogenous to a product of complex curves. In this paper, we determine the parity of the intersection forms of all fake quadrics isogenous to a product of unmixed type. In particular, we show that there are fake quadrics with odd intersection forms.

Andrews and Newman \cite{andrewsnewmanI} introduced and studied ``mex,'' function for an integer partition $λ$ of a positive integer $n$. The related function $σ^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ was subsequently defined, and its generating function and other properties have been studied by several authors. In this article, for a positive integer $\ell \geq 2$, we define the minimal excludant of an $\ell$-regular partition $λ$ of a positive integer $n$. We then define $σ_\ell^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$, the sum of the minimal excludants over all $\ell$-regular partitions of $n$, and obtain explicit generating functions for $σ_\ell^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ in the cases $\ell = 2$ and $\ell = 3$, expressed as eta-quotients. We prove that the sequence $σ_\ell^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ is weakly increasing for every $\ell$, and we obtain Hardy--Ramanujan type asymptotic formulas for $σ_2^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ and $σ_3^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ as $n \to \infty$. Additionally, we completely determine the parity of $σ_2^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$, showing that it is odd precisely at generalized pentagonal numbers, and we use this characterization to compute the density of $n$ for which $σ_2^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ is odd versus even. Finally, for $σ_3^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$, we prove that it is odd infinitely often, and we establish a quantitative lower bound, showing that the number of such $n$ up to $X$ grows at least like $\log \log X$.

Wilker-type properties record how a compact set can be split along a binary open cover, and they are precisely the continuity conditions for the union operation on open lattices, governing the topology of power and function spaces. We give a unified treatment of the four properties $\W$, $\Ww$, $\Wi$ and $\Win$. We prove that $\Wi$ and $\Win$ are hereditary for arbitrary subspaces, whereas $\W$ and $\Ww$ are hereditary only for closed subspaces; all four are preserved by continuous retracts, and $\Ww$, $\Wi$, $\Win$ are finitely additive over topological sums. For KC-spaces $\Ww$ and $\Wi$ coincide, and spaces whose compact subspaces are Hausdorff belong to $\Win$. Using Kovár's compact KC-space $M_0$ and its variant $\QQ^{+}$, we obtain countably infinite compact KC-spaces in $\Wi\setminus\W$, showing $\Wi$ is strictly weaker than $\W$. Conversely, we construct compact $T_1$ spaces whose product fails $\Ww$, proving the classes $\Ww$ and $\Wi$ are not reflective. We further show Vietoris constructions need not preserve $\Wi$, and prove that $\Ok(M_0)\cong \Ck(M_0,\Sier)$ is not sober and fails property~$S$. Open problems are collected at the end.
Exact Transport-Information Correspondence for Distribution-Adaptive Discretization

Discretization of continuous probability distributions is an operation on the sample space, and the structure induced by this operation cannot generally be determined solely from information geometry. In our recent work on unavoidable canonical nonlinearity (UCN), we established a non-arbitrary connection between the transport cost associated with discretization and the information-geometric indistinguishability of continuous probability distributions. Through the transport-information correspondence, the UCN quantify the information-theoretic cost due to discretization as the expected Kullback-Leibler divergence between nearby continuous distributions associated with the discretization geometry. In the original UCN construction, discretization is implemented by transporting the probability mass within each cell to its geometric centroid. The resulting transport-information correspondence, however, is derived under specific conditions involving the cell geometry, spatial coverage, and the vanishing-cell-scale limit. In this work, we introduce an alternative local-map discretization scheme in which the probability mass within each cell is transported to its own probability-weighted centroid. This change in the representative-point selection enables an exact expression for the transport cost of each cell in terms of the covariance matrix of its conditional probability distribution and the Fisher metric of the underlying continuous family. We establish an exact correspondence between the resulting transport cost and the expectation of the associated Fisher-induced quadratic form, without requiring uniform cell geometry, complete coverage of the sample space, or an infinitesimal cell-scale limit. The proposed construction thus generalizes the transport-information correspondence to finite-scale discretization using arbitrary collections of non-overlapping bounded convex sets.
Non-admissible smooth irreducible representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ for totally ramified extensions $F/\mathbb{Q}_p$

Let $p\geq 5$, and let $F/\mathbb{Q}_p$ be a nontrivial finite totally ramified extension. We construct a non-admissible smooth irreducible representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$. The construction uses representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathcal{O}_F)$ on which the first principal congruence subgroup acts nontrivially, together with a deformation of a diagram indexed by $\mathbb{Z}$.

In his famous ``testamentary letter'' Galois formulated several results without proof. Among them he claimed --- here we express it in modern terms --- that the projective special linear group $PSL(2,p)$ has a subgroup of index $p$ only for $p\le 11$. Nowadays this result is seen as a corollary of the complete enumeration of all subgroups of $PSL(2,p)$ obtained by Gierster in 1881. In this paper we attempt to give a proof that uses only methods available to Galois.
Poissonian Pair Correlation and Discrepancy Rates
Bo Tan; Zhen Zhang; Qing-Long Zhou

We prove the existence of a sequence in $[0,1)$ with Poissonian pair correlation (PPC) and optimal-order star discrepancy $D_N^*=O((\log N)/N)$, and further give a deterministic construction by applying a conditional-expectation rule to a nested dyadic random model. We also show that PPC imposes no universal discrepancy decay rate: for every positive sequence $ρ_N\to0$, there exists a PPC sequence with $D_N^*/ρ_N\to\infty$. Under suitable regularity and growth assumptions, we realize prescribed discrepancy asymptotics, including $D_N^*\sim c_βN^{-β}$ for every $0<β<1$, with $c_β>0$. We further construct a PPC sequence satisfying $D_N^*\asymp(\log N)/N$ for all sufficiently large $N$.
Can a self-sustaining chemical network emerge due to just a few catalysts?

Understanding how self-sustaining chemical reaction networks can emerge from simple molecules is an important question in chemical approaches to the origin of life. Reflexively autocatalytic and food-generated (RAF) sets provide a mathematical framework for investigating this question. This line of research goes back to the early work of Kauffman on autocatalytic reaction networks and was subsequently developed through the probabilistic framework of Mossel and Steel. Further contributions by Hordijk, Steel, and collaborators extended the theory to more heterogeneous forms of catalysis, including reaction-dependent probabilities or power-law distributions of catalytic activity. We introduce a stochastic model that combines heterogeneous molecular catalytic activity with reaction-dependent molecule-reaction compatibility. By assigning random catalytic weights to molecules and incorporating compatibility through an explicit formulation of catalysis probabilities, our model provides a concrete and flexible setting that captures both sources of heterogeneity while remaining mathematically tractable.
 We establish novel and general criteria for RAF formation and nonformation. We further demonstrate that classical phase-transition criteria need not remain valid in the presence of reaction-dependent catalysis. For heavy-tailed catalytic weights, we identify and rigorously quantify an additional phase transition. In models with finite-mean catalytic weights, RAF formation and nonformation are governed by a catalytic intensity parameter. For infinite-mean weights, however, we show that RAFs may emerge with probability tending to one even when the catalytic intensity parameter tends to zero.
The Cone Fixing the Reals of $\mathrm{HOD}^{M_{2n}(x)}$

For a cone of reals $x$, the reals of $\mathrm{HOD}^{L[x]}$ are precisely the reals in $Q_3$, or equivalently, the set of reals in $M_1$, the minimal proper class mouse with a Woodin cardinal. We show that if $z$ is any real coding $M_1|δ^{+M_1}$, then $z$ is the base of such a cone (so $M_1^{\#}$ is such a base). We also establish a kind of optimality for this result, by identifying a real $x$ such that $M_1\subseteq L[x]$ but $\mathbb{R}\cap\mathrm{HOD}^{L[x]}\not\subseteq M_1$, although there is a base for the cone in a generic extension of $L[x]$. We prove an analogous result for the reals of $\mathrm{HOD}^{M_{n}(x)}$ for even $n$, as well as an analogous optimality result which holds for all $n$.
Toward Shifted symplectic Chiralization: Deformation of Courant Algebroids

We study the chiralization of Poisson--Lie theory through graded symplectic geometry. We compare Courant deformations and classical $r$- and $R$-matrix constructions, obtaining integrable hierarchies and free field realizations. We give a variational description of the obstruction to Lie conformal bialgebra compatibility and recover Liberati's obstruction in the Virasoro case. We also introduce a vertex bialgebra analogue of quantized universal enveloping algebras and construct explicit quantizations to all orders of Cartan type Lie conformal bialgebra structures on $\operatorname{Cur}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$. These results contribute to the first author's broader programme of developing shifted symplectic chiralization as a geometric method for constructing chiral analogues of Poisson-Lie structures via $n$-shifted symplectic geometry, and exploring its connections with AKSZ theory and quantization.
Capelli Operators and the Bernstein-Sato polynomials of Minors

For every ideal of minors of a generic complex matrix, we determine all roots and their multiplicities in the Bernstein-Sato polynomial. These roots lie in explicit rational intervals indexed by the rank strata. Every nonintegral root is simple, whereas the multiplicity of each integral root equals the number of labels producing that root. We deduce the strong motivic monodromy conjecture, including the inequality relating pole orders to root multiplicities; for minors of size $r$, the largest possible root multiplicity over all matrix dimensions is $\lfloor\sqrt{4r-1}\rfloor$.
 Keywords. Bernstein-Sato polynomial, determinantal ideal, root multiplicities, strong monodromy conjecture.
Quantum Adiabatic Theorem under Wiener Noise: Maximal Mean-Square Estimates
A. M. H. H. Caldera; R. P. K. De Silva; K. K. W. A. S. Kumara; B. P. W. Fernando

We derive maximal mean-square adiabatic estimates for finite-dimensional stochastic Schrödinger equations with Hamiltonian-proportional Wiener noise. For deterministic $C^2$ Hamiltonians whose eigenvalues have constant multiplicities and do not cross on $[0,1]$, we construct a unitary stochastic adiabatic intertwiner driven by the same Wiener process as the exact propagator. A commutator argument, Itô calculus, and Doob's maximal inequality yield an explicit bound for the expected supremum of their squared operator-norm difference on a selected initial eigenspace. Under uniform coefficient bounds, the physical noise scaling $α=σT^{-γ}$, where $T$ is the total evolution time and $σ\geq0$ and $γ\geq0$ are fixed, gives maximal mean-square error $O(T^{-2}+σ^4T^{-4γ}+σ^2T^{-(2γ+1)})$. Consequently, adiabatic convergence holds for every $γ>0$ as $T\to\infty$, while $γ\geq1/2$ recovers the deterministic $O(T^{-1})$ bound for the root-mean-square maximal error. For fixed nonzero physical noise amplitude, the estimate leaves convergence unresolved.
Attraction-Ranking Mismatch in Out-of-Distribution Detection: Theory and Evidence from Hamiltonian Feature Dynamics

Attracting features toward learned in-distribution (ID) regions is an intuitive strategy for out-of-distribution (OOD) detection, but does such attraction improve detection? We investigate this question using class-conditioned Hamiltonian dynamics as a controlled testbed and identify an attraction-ranking mismatch: improving individual class-affinity scores need not improve the relative ordering of ID and OOD samples. Our analysis separates misalignment between the driving field and the detection score from ranking failure that persists even when they are aligned. An exact AUROC decomposition and a local boundary analysis identify relative score changes at the ID-OOD ranking boundary as the source of first-order AUROC change under regularity conditions. Experiments demonstrate that a score-aligned rule can improve performance on a held-out source validation split yet consistently degrade it after transfer, even without a single winning-class change. A separate perturbation study finds that near-boundary relative score changes track the direction of small AUROC changes in the tested settings. Finally, centroid approximation and shared scales connect the zero-step score to a static centroid family that includes the existing CTM detector. Together, these results explain why class attraction is insufficient to justify feature refinement and motivate evaluating its effect on the ranking boundary.
Finiteness of Non-decomposable Critically Frustrated Signed Graphs

A signed graph $(G,σ)$ is a graph $G$ with a signature $σ$ labeling each edge with a positive or negative sign. Two signatures of $G$ are switching equivalent if one is obtained from the other by sequentially changing the signs of all edges in an edge-cut. The frustration index of a signed graph $(G, σ)$ is the minimum number of negative edges among all signatures switching equivalent to $σ$. A signed graph is critically $k$-frustrated if it has frustration index $k$, and the removal of any edge decreases its frustration index. A critically $k$-frustrated signed graph is prime if it is irreducible and contains no two edge-disjoint negative cycles. Steffen and Naserasr et al. asked if there are only finitely many prime critically $k$-frustrated signed graphs for any positive integer $k$. The cases $k\leq 3$ were proved to be true by Cappello et al., and later, the cases $k=4$ and $5$ were verified by Z. Wang. In this paper, the author proves the conjecture by a topological argument.
The Maximum Principle and Optimal Gradient Estimates of Solutions to the Insulated Conductivity Problem

We study the insulated conductivity problem with two unit spherical inclusions embedded in a bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $n\ge3$. The gradient of solutions may blow up as the distance between the two inclusions goes to zero. We introduce bispherical coordinates and expand the solution in spherical harmonics. Then we use the maximum principle to give a new proof of the optimal gradient estimate obtained by Dong-Li-Yang.
The integral Chow rings of $\mathcal A_3$ and $\mathcal M_3$

Over $\mathbb C$, we compute the integral Chow ring of $\mathcal A_3$, the moduli stack of principally polarized abelian threefolds. Along the way, we compute the integral Chow ring of $\mathcal M_3$, the moduli stack of smooth genus-three curves. The ring $\CH(\mathcal A_3)$ is generated by the Chern classes of the Hodge bundle, along with three classes supported on the locus of decomposable abelian varieties, subject to 16 relations. The ring $\CH(\mathcal M_3)$ is generated by the Chern classes of the Hodge bundle, with five relations. In particular, we find that the top Chern class of the Hodge bundle, $λ_3$, has order 504 on $\mathcal A_3$ and 252 on $\mathcal M_3$. For $\mathcal A_3$, this removes the factor of 4 from the bound $252\mid\operatorname{ord}(λ_3)\mid 1008$ of Ekedahl and van der Geer.
Geometric Multigrid Preconditioners for conforming Finite Element Methods on Arbitrarily Agglomerated Meshes

Geometric multigrid methods for conforming finite element discretisations classically require a nested mesh hierarchy, forcing coarse meshes to be conforming, which is unsuitable for general domains. In order to eliminate this geometric constraint, we introduce and analyse a family of multilevel auxiliary space preconditioners. At the first level, a conforming Lagrangian discretisation on a fine simplicial mesh is preconditioned by a non-conforming polytopal discretisation posed on an arbitrarily agglomerated coarse mesh. At the subsequent levels, the coarse problem is solved by a geometric multigrid method for that polytopal discretisation on further agglomerated meshes, so that the whole hierarchy is generated from the fine mesh by agglomeration alone. We consider two polytopal discretisations, a symmetric interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin method and a hybrid high-order method. The prolongation operator at the first level is an element-wise interpolation onto the fine mesh followed by nodal averaging, preceded in the hybrid high-order case by a local potential reconstruction. For point-Jacobi and vertex-star patch additive Schwarz smoothers, we prove that the condition number of the preconditioned system is bounded by $O((H/h)^3)$, where $H/h$ is the coarsening ratio, and by $O((H/h)^2)$ for the DG variant with penalty proportional to $H/h$. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions, on structured and unstructured meshes with agglomerates generated by automatic clustering algorithms, confirm the robustness of the preconditioners.
Long-memory Hermite functional processes in functional time series spectral asymptotics
M. C. Düker; P. Zoubouloglou; M. D. Ruiz-Medina

Functional Non-Central Limit Theorems (NCLTs) are derived, in the functional spectral domain (see RuizMedina, 2022), for square integrable transformations, mapping an H_{1}-valued Gaussian stationary functional sequence into a nonlinear H_{2}-valued sequence, where H_{1} and H_{2} are separable Hilbert spaces. Linear and nonlinear operator-based scalings are considered, leading to different limit LRD Hermite functional processes. Under bounded linear operator scalings, an infinite-dimensional version of Theorem 5.3.1 in Pipiras and Taqqu (2017) is obtained, involving a functional reduction theorem, extending Theorem 5.3.3 in Pipiras and Taqqu (2017). Alternatively, when an operator-valued exponent based nonlinear scaling is applied, we pay attention to the LRD dominant set at each active output direction, in the leading chaos. Both scaling scenarios allow the derivation of NCLTs under similar settings of conditions.
How Unbalanced Must a Latin Rectangle Be?

We view a $k\times n$ Latin rectangle as $n$ points in the grid $[n]^k$. Each symbol gives one point, whose coordinates are the columns it occupies. The rectangle is balanced when these points are pairwise equidistant in the $\ell_1$ metric. Its imbalance measures the distance from this ideal. We study the minimum imbalance from three sides. Constructively, we use a simulated annealing that moves symbols within rows and only penalises column clashes. Against the reference table of Voboril et al. (2025), it improves 33 of the 51 non-square values for $8\le n\le 13$, by up to 39.4%, and matches the rest. A cheap invariant, the row group, certifies that none of the 33 new rectangles is isotopic to rows of a group table, so the earlier column-swapping local search cannot reach any of them. Exactly, a computer-assisted branch and bound proves that the minimum imbalance of a $3\times 9$ rectangle is $56$. Díaz et al. found this value, but its optimality was open. A sharper pruning bound, derived from the identity $I=2\sum(d-t)^+$, reduces the search tree by a factor of $2.4$ to $3.3$ on the instances with $k\ge3$ that we solve. Asymptotically, the minimum imbalance is $Θ(n^3)$ for every fixed $k$. A pigeonhole argument gives a lower constant of order $k\,4^{-k}$, and random rectangles give an upper constant of order $\sqrt k$. For $k=2$, the limit of $\min I/n^3$ exists, a permuton attains it, and it lies between $4/375$ and $0.1196$. Perfect balance is an $\ell_1$-equilateral problem, so it forces $k=Ω(n/\log n)$ rows. For $2\times n$ rectangles, single two-minute annealing runs improve five of the seven six-hour MIP upper bounds for $14\le n\le 20$. Finally, the Lean 4 kernel checks every rectangle reported in this paper against a 74-line specification that imports only Lean's core library. We also prove the pigeonhole lower bound in Lean with Mathlib.
The enhanced polylogarithm conjecture in weight two for imaginary quadratic fields

Zagier's polylogarithm conjecture predicts that special values of Dedekind zeta functions can be expressed in terms of polylogarithms at algebraic arguments. For imaginary quadratic fields, Zagier and Gangl refined it by lifting both sides to complex values modulo rational multiples of a power of $2πi$. In previous work, the author extended their enhanced zeta values from ideal classes to ray classes by means of the Shintani $L$-function of two variables and formulated the enhanced polylogarithm conjecture for ray classes. In this article, we prove this conjecture in weight two. More precisely, we establish a Galois-equivariant equality between the enhanced partial zeta values of ray classes and the enhanced dilogarithms of elements of the rational Bloch groups of the corresponding ray class fields. These elements are constructed explicitly, starting from the Eisenstein class of Doran and Kerr on the square of a CM elliptic curve and contracting it with the graphs of complex multiplication.
Failure of superharmonicity near an isolated singularity of the critical biharmonic equation
Juncheng Wei; Hui Yang; Ronghao Yang

Let $n\ge5$ and $u$ be a positive singular solution of $Δ^2u=u^{(n+4)/(n-4)}$ in a punctured ball. A long-standing question is where or not $ -Δu>0$ in the punctured ball. In this paper we show that the answer is negative. More precisely we construct a positive singular solution whose singularity at the origin is nonremovable, while its lower limit there is zero. On a normal subspace, $-Δu$ converges to a strictly negative constant. The spherical minimum has order $r^β$, where $2<β<4$, and the spherical Harnack ratio is unbounded. The proof uses balanced planar polygons, finitely many exterior parameters and a countable gluing construction.
Coherent configuration on 3-uniform hypergraph over strongly regular graph

This paper investigates coherent configurations on 3-uniform hypergraphs constructed from strongly regular graphs. We establish that the hypergraph preserves the automorphism group of the original graph and induces a nonhomogeneous Schurian coherent configuration. Using the case of Petersen graph, we obtain a configuration with two fibers and thirteen basic relations. We further determine their valencies and nonzero intersection numbers, together with the corresponding adjacency matrix multiplication identities.
Linear adaptive variable time step schemes for the anisotropic phase field dendritic crystal growth model

In this paper, we propose a class of efficient, linear and decoupled adaptive variable time step schemes for the anisotropic phase field dendritic crystal growth model. The main difficulty is twofold: the gradient dependent anisotropic coefficient and the strongly nonlinear terms make unconditional energy stability difficult to achieve, and on nonuniform meshes the discrete energy dissipation law, which is straightforward to establish on uniform meshes, has to be reestablished under varying step sizes. To overcome these difficulties, two linear stabilizers and a time dependent auxiliary variable with relaxation are introduced and incorporated into a second-order generalized BDF-type operator, with the spatial derivatives discretized by the Fourier spectral method. The proposed schemes are energy stable for arbitrary positive adjacent step ratios, so that no restriction on the step ratio is imposed, and only two linear equations together with a few algebraic equations, which are solved independently in Fourier space, need to be solved at each time step. Moreover, the schemes are naturally compatible with energy based time adaptive strategies. The associated adaptive strategy reduces the number of time steps by $24.6\%$--$86.6\%$ in comparison with uniform time stepping, and numerical experiments on fourfold and sixfold dendritic growth in two dimensions and on three-dimensional growth confirm the accuracy, efficiency and stability of the proposed schemes.

In this article, we introduce Borel--Moore and uniformly finite versions of magnitude homology and path homology for locally finite graphs by allowing possibly infinite chains subject to local finiteness and boundedness conditions. In both settings, we construct magnitude--path spectral sequences extending the spectral sequence studied by the author. Their E^1-pages are given by the corresponding magnitude homologies, their E^2-pages contain the corresponding path homologies on the p-axis, and they converge to coarse homology and uniformly finite homology, respectively, in the sense of Nowak--Yu. Moreover, the E^{r+1}-page is invariant under r- homotopy, whereas the homology to which the spectral sequence converges is invariant under coarse equivalence. Thus the spectral sequences interpolate between small-scale and large-scale geometry.
 We also show that the Borel--Moore and uniformly finite magnitude homologies are products and restricted products, respectively, of ordinary magnitude homology groups with a fixed initial point. Hence the E^1-page is assembled from pointwise magnitude-homological data, providing a mechanism for combining local information into global large-scale invariants. As applications, we establish Mayer--Vietoris sequences for magnitude homology, path homology, the associated spectral-sequence pages, and coarse and uniformly finite homology. We also show that diagonality of ordinary magnitude homology implies degeneration at the E^2-page, yielding isomorphisms between path homology and the corresponding coarse homology. Finally, we discuss applications to Cayley graphs of graph products, including right-angled Artin groups and right-angled Coxeter groups.
Ray-Tracing-Based Dynamic Channel Sounding With Autoregressive Wi-Fi CSI Prediction
Lyutianyang Zhang; Yixin Ying; Liu Cao; Vanlin Sathya; Jinke Ren; Shuguang Cui

Channel sounding in Wi-Fi multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems must balance channel state information (CSI) accuracy against CSI acquisition overhead. Device mobility causes channel aging, while autoregressive CSI prediction introduces errors that accumulate over sounding intervals. However, standardized statistical channel models cannot fully capture the environment-specific channel dynamics encountered in physical artificial intelligence (AI) applications, motivating the use of Sionna-based ray tracing to evaluate CSI prediction under device mobility and evolving propagation geometry. This paper develops a dynamic sounding framework that integrates autoregressive CSI prediction with signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR)-constrained interval selection. A Transformer with rotary position embedding that converts device positions into CSI sequences predicts CSI across multiple subcarriers for beamforming updates between sounding exchanges. We formulate sounding-interval selection as a predicted average-throughput maximization problem under per-stream SINR lower-bound constraints, including CSI acquisition and processing overhead. A prediction-error perturbation analysis provides the SINR bounds, and cumulative-sum enumeration globally solves the finite single-variable problem. Actual SINR feasibility holds whenever the prediction errors satisfy the bounds. Ray-tracing experiments assess channel prediction, trajectory transfer, and autoregressive prediction errors. In single-STA Wi-Fi 7 link-level simulations, predicted-CSI beamforming improves mean goodput by 67.3%, 112.7%, and 119.1% over stale CSI for linear, circular, and cosine trajectories, respectively.
Exact $3$-Adic Periods of Symmetric Dellac Numbers and Their Polynomial Extensions

The odd and even symmetric Dellac numbers are the specializations $a_n=f_n(0)$ and $e_n=f_n(1)$ of the Randrianarivony--Zeng family $f_n(s)=2^{-n}D_n(s)$. Using a finite Stieltjes-fraction truncation, we establish the sharp congruence $v_3(a_n)=1$ for $n\ge2$ and obtain explicit congruences modulo $81$ for both sequences. We also establish universal eventual periodicity modulo arbitrary positive integers. For every integer $s\ge0$ and $k\ge1$, we give and analyse formulas for the \emph{least} eventual period of $f_n(s)$ modulo $3^k$ and its \emph{least starting index}.
