The result uses a random snapshot update and counts all full-gradient computations. No new algorithm or rate is claimed.
Chordality of Enhanced Power Graphs of Finite Simple Groups: A Resolution of a Conjecture

The \emph{enhanced power graph} $\PE(G)$ of a finite group $G$ has vertex set $G$, two elements being adjacent if and only if they generate a cyclic subgroup. We determine the finite simple groups $G$ for which $\PE(G)$ is chordal: they are the cyclic groups of prime order, $\Alt(7)$, $\PSL_2(q)$ ($q\ge4$), $\Sz(q)$ ($q=2^{2n+1}\ge8$) and $\PSL_3(4)$. This answers an open problem of Bubboloni, Fumagalli and Praeger \cite{BFP}. We also prove that for every finite group $G$, if the power graph $P(G)$ is a cograph (resp.\ chordal) then so is $\PE(G)$; the cograph case is a conjecture of Bubboloni, Fumagalli and Praeger \cite{BFP}.
Fibrewise Real-Analytic Landsberg Metrics in Dimension at Least Four Are Berwald

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold of dimension $n\ge4$, and let $F$ be a smooth, strongly convex Landsberg metric, regular on the entire slit tangent bundle. We prove that $F$ is Berwald if, at each fixed base point, the Minkowski norm is real-analytic on the entire slit tangent space. The proof rests on two analytic rigidity theorems for a single Minkowski space. The first asserts that, in dimension at least $3$, a real-analytic Minkowski norm whose Hessian metric is flat is induced by an inner product. The second asserts that, in dimension at least $4$, the Hessian metric of a real-analytic Minkowski norm is flat if the entire indicatrix carries a nonzero smooth symmetric quartic form satisfying a twisted Codazzi equation. The quartic form need not be real-analytic, and the second theorem is proved independently of the first. Applying these results to the angular Berwald quartic form shows that the metric is Riemannian on the open set of base points on whose fibres the Berwald curvature is not identically zero. Since every Riemannian metric is Berwald, this set must be empty. No analytic structure, compactness or completeness of the base manifold is assumed, and the metric need not be reversible.
Factoriality of Mixed $q$-Gaussian Algebras at the Boundary

For arbitrary index set $I$, we determine the center and characterize factoriality for mixed $q$-Gaussian von Neumann algebras $Γ_Q(\cH_\R)$ associated with real symmetric matrices $Q=(q_{ij})_{i,j\in I}$ satisfying $|q_{ij}|\le1$ through the strict graph we introduced in this article. Two vertices $i$ and $j$ of $I$ are joined by an edge in the strict graph if and only if $|q_{ij}|<1$. Let $S$ denote its isolated vertices. We prove that $Γ_Q(\cH_\R)$ is a factor if and only if $q_{ii}=-1$ for every $i\in S$, no two-vertex component $\{a,b\}$ satisfies $q_{aa}=q_{bb}=-1$, and no nonempty finite subset $A\subseteq S$ satisfies $\prod_{j\in A\setminus \{k\}}q_{jk}=1$ for every $k\in I$. We also determine the laws of some central elements.
Dissipative Hamiltonian representations of linear evolution equations

We investigate explicit and implicit dissipative Hamiltonian representations of generators of strongly continuous semigroups on real or complex Hilbert spaces. For a prescribed positive definite selfadjoint energy operator $H$ satisfying $\operatorname{dom}(A)\subset\operatorname{dom}(H)$, we show that the Lyapunov dissipation inequality is equivalent to an exact factorization $A=DH$, where $D$ can be chosen maximally dissipative. For bounded $H$, the criterion also yields an implicit representation. We further study energy constructions based on closed intertwiners and output trajectories, distinguishing contractive energy-space dynamics from operator factorizations on the original state space. Examples illustrate the roles of noncoercivity, unboundedness, and domain compatibility.

Erdős and Gyárfás conjectured that every graph with minimum degree at least three contains a power-of-two-length cycle. We prove every Cayley graph of odd order satisfies the conjecture. As a corollary, we find that Cayley graphs of finite nilpotent groups satisfy the conjecture as well.
Martino Borello; Martin Scotti; Lune Vila

Intersecting codes are codes in which any two nonzero codewords share a common nonzero coordinate, and they have been extensively studied due to their applications in communication theory, cryptography, and combinatorics. Recently, geometric interpretations have provided new insights into intersecting codes, both in the Hamming metric and, more recently, in the rank metric for linear codes. In this paper, we introduce and study matrix rank-metric intersecting codes. By defining the support of a matrix as its row space, we extend the notion of intersecting codes to the matrix rank-metric setting. Using the slice space associated with the generator tensor of a rank-metric code, we derive a geometric characterization that is equivalent to the intersecting property. This characterization generalizes the known results for linear rank-metric intersecting codes and highlights both analogies and differences with the linear case. In particular, it yields bounds on the parameters of intersecting codes, one of which is sharp and differs from the one in the linear case, together with first constructions. We then consider codes that are closed under multiplication, i.e. matrix algebras. In this setting, the intersecting property can be read off from the algebraic structure, namely the Jacobson radical and the socle. This provides a simple and flexible way to construct many intersecting codes, including codes that do not satisfy the classical sufficient condition on the minimum distance.
The Maximum Second Zagreb Spectral Radius of Trees, Unicyclic Graphs and Bicyclic Graphs

The second Zagreb matrix of a graph $G$ is $Z(G)=D(G)A(G)D(G)$, where $D(G)$ and $A(G)$ are the degree matrix and the adjacency matrix of $G$. For many degree-based weighted adjacency matrices, the trees, unicyclic graphs and bicyclic graphs with the largest spectral radius have a vertex adjacent to all others, and Mei et al. conjectured this for every such matrix on unicyclic graphs. Jiang et al. showed that $Z(G)$ is a counterexample. We prove that, for $q\in\{0,1,2\}$ and every $n\ge4$, the connected graph of order $n$ and cyclomatic number $q$ maximizing the spectral radius of $Z(G)$ is unique, and is obtained from two adjacent vertices with $q$ common neighbours by attaching $n-q-2$ pendent vertices to them as evenly as possible. The only exceptions are the star for $q=0$ and $n\le7$, and the triangle with one pendent vertex at each vertex for $q=1$ and $n=6$. This confirms a conjecture of Jiang et al.\ and all three parts of a conjecture of Shen and Shan for this matrix, with best possible thresholds on $n$. For $n\ge8$, the maximum value is $\lfloor (n+q)^2/4\rfloor+(n+q)/2+7q-2+O(1/n)$, whereas the star gives only $(n-1)^{3/2}$. A key tool is a determinant criterion that reduces spectral comparisons to sign conditions on explicit polynomials.
Singular sets of homogeneous Dirichlet heat flows at large time

We study homogeneous Dirichlet heat flows for real symmetric, uniformly elliptic divergence-form operators. We establish quantitative stability of singular sets near homogeneous harmonic polynomials and eigenfunctions. Based on these, in the smooth coefficient case, we prove the spatial singular set at sufficiently large time is codimension-two and has a uniform measure upper bound independent of time. However, this codimension-two property fails in the Lipschitz coefficient case. On a three-dimensional ball, we construct a fixed self-adjoint operator and a heat flow consisting of two eigenmodes whose singular sets contain two-dimensional disks at a sequence of times tending to infinity.
From Random Advection to Transport Noise and the LU Framework for the Navier--Stokes Equations
Arnaud Debussche; Bérenger Hug; Etienne Mémin

We consider the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations in a smooth bounded domain in dimension two or three, with Dirichlet boundary conditions, when the velocity is advected by a rapidly varying stationary Markov process $\eps^{-1}m(t/\eps^2)$. The fast field may be spatially inhomogeneous. We prove that, when $\eps\to0$, the laws of the large-scale velocities are tight and that their limit points are martingale solutions of the stochastic Navier--Stokes equations with transport noise in the form of the location uncertainty framework. The limiting equation contains in particular a noise which is described in terms of the covariance of the fast advection. Under a symmetry assumption on the temporal correlations of the fast field, the noise is Stratonovich and an advection by the Itô--Stokes drift appears. The proof relies on perturbed test functions, which we use both for the uniform energy bounds and for the identification of the limit. We have to adapt this method and add the Stokes operator to the Poisson equation associated to the fast advection in order to use fewer regularity assumptions and obtain correctors which satisfy the boundary conditions.
A Wolpert Theorem for shearing coordinates

A theorem from Wolpert bounds the Weil--Petersson distance from a hyperbolic surface to a maximally noded surface in terms of the lengths of the underlying pants decomposition. We prove analogues for punctured surfaces both in terms of the lambda-lengths and in terms of the shearing coordinates of an ideal triangulation.
Pin-Hsian Lee; Peng-Ting Lin; Meng-Tsung Tsai; Ting-An Wu

The Nash-Williams--Tutte theorem characterizes the existence of $k$ edge-disjoint spanning trees by a condition on every vertex partition. We prove that, for simple graphs, the same condition guarantees $k$ edge-disjoint spanning trees, each of diameter $O(n/δ)$ and with $O((n/δ)\log(δ+1))$ internal vertices, where $n$ is the number of vertices and $δ$ is the minimum degree. Both bounds hold simultaneously for every tree, with absolute implicit constants independent of $k$, and each is asymptotically optimal in general. Our proof is constructive and yields a randomized algorithm with expected running time $\tilde{O}(n^5)$. We derive applications to short edge-disjoint routes and weak linkages, small Steiner trees, and survivable networks with short paths. The joint bounds also yield low-diameter spanning Eulerian subgraphs and short tours for postman and general routing problems.
A Short Proof and Generalization of the Rainbow Cycle Theorem and Improved Bounds for Binary Even-Query LCCs

A \emph{rainbow cycle} in a list-edge-colored graph is a cycle where no color appears more than once. We give a short and simple proof of a result of [ABSZZ] showing that a properly edge-colored $n$-vertex graph with average degree $Ω(\log n\log\log n)$ always contains a rainbow cycle, and generalize it to weighted graphs with edges list colored with list size at most $\ell$ and where the total weight of all edges containing a given color $i$ incident to a vertex is at most $Δ$, showing that $Ω_\ell(Δ\log n\log\log n)$ average degree guarantees a rainbow cycle. Using the reduction of [AG26] and the new generalized rainbow cycle theorem, we prove that for $r\geq 3$, every binary linear $r$-query locally correctable code $E:\mathbb{F}_2^k\rightarrow \mathbb{F}_2^n$ satisfies $k\leq \tilde{O}(n^{1-2/(r-1)})$ by showing a rainbow analogue of the odd $r$-LDC lower bounds of [BHKL25,JM25], closing the gap between the best known lower bounds for odd- and even-query binary linear $r$-LCCs.
Curvature Estimates and Prescribed Curvature Problems for Sum Hessian Equations on Star-Shaped Hypersurfaces
Dongjing Ma; Peihe Wang; Hua Zhu

Let $M$ be a closed star-shaped hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ and let $η=Hg-h$ be the first Newton transformation of its second fundamental form. For a fixed constant $α>0$ and $2\le k\le n-1$, we study the prescribed sum Hessian curvature equation \[ σ_k(λ(η))+ασ_{k-1}(λ(η))=f(X,ν). \] Under the natural admissibility condition \[ λ(η)\inΓ_{k-1}\cap \{λ:σ_k(λ)+ασ_{k-1}(λ)>0\}, \] we establish a global curvature estimate for closed star-shaped solutions with a general positive right-hand side depending on the position vector and the unit normal. A key point is that the sum Hessian operator is nonhomogeneous; the resulting lower-order term in the maximum-principle calculation is controlled by a partial curvature estimate. We also use the augmented-variable identity \[ σ_k(λ)+ασ_{k-1}(λ) =σ_k(λ_1,\ldots,λ_n,α) \] to recover the relevant ellipticity and concavity properties. As an application of the a priori estimates, we prove existence and uniqueness for the corresponding prescribed curvature problem under suitable spherical barrier and radial monotonicity assumptions.
A Unified Isoparametric Moving Mesh PDE Method for P1 and Q1 Elements with Certified Local Nonsingularity

We develop a unified isoparametric moving mesh partial differential equation (MMPDE) method for $P_1$ simplicial and $Q_1$ tensor-product elements, including elements on embedded surfaces. Mesh movement follows a prescribed symmetric positive-definite metric through equidistribution and alignment. For $Q_1$ elements, we prove that bounded, exactly integrated adaptation energy prevents local Jacobian rank loss on a fixed finite mesh at sharp critical exponents. The result also gives local full-rank preservation for embedded bilinear surface elements. A complete physical-coordinate gradient accounts for metric variation at moving quadrature points. For the discrete MMPDE, we use whole-element validity tests and develop sufficient Bernstein certificates for trilinear hexahedra. An explicit positive-margin bound on each fixed stage is provided by an optional certificate barrier. Numerical examples illustrate metric-driven movement on one-dimensional, planar, volume, and graph-surface meshes. Limitations of pointwise hexahedral Jacobian sampling are also presented.
Finite Spectral Depth Controls Gaussian Entrance Rank and Avoidance of the First Gradient-Flow Saddle

Matrix factorization provides a simple model for studying the training dynamics of neural networks. Recent studies of gradient flow under small initialization have analyzed how trajectories escape from a neighborhood of the origin and approach their first nonzero stationary point. In this paper, we study continuous-time dynamics that applies a finite number of Newton-Schulz iterations to the normalized matrix gradient (Muon). We show that the number of Newton-Schulz steps can change the rank selected during the early stages of training and allow the resulting trajectory to bypass the first nonzero stationary point approached by gradient flow. Under an additional residual-inertia condition, we prove that bypass occurs for all sufficiently large finite Newton-Schulz depths and provide an explicit sufficient threshold. We also construct an example in which the bypass threshold is four.
The integer spectrum of a superintegrable quantum field theory

In our previous article CMP 407 (2026) 131, we explored the rich algebraic structures arising from a specific quantum many-body Hamiltonian quartic in the bosonic creation-annihilation operators. This Hamiltonian originated from the works of Gérard and Grellier on classical turbulent energy transfer in a Lax-integrable setting, and its quantum version respects hierarchies of polynomial conservation laws all of which possess purely integer spectra, as does the Hamiltonian itself. The latter feature, known from numerical studies, has previously remained unproved. Here, we present an elementary solution of the quantum Gérard-Grellier Hamiltonian. The eigenstates are labelled by partitions and the corresponding eigenvalues admit simple explicit expressions in terms of the principal hook lengths. The key ingredient in this construction is a specific basis we introduce, inspired by the classical multisoliton coherent states, in which the Hamiltonian is upper-triangular. The expressions for the eigenvalues then immediately follow, while the full eigenbasis can be recovered via a Gram-Schmidt procedure.
The APN Property of Two Families of functions over $\F_{2^{n}}$ from the Switching Construction
Chenmiao Shi; Longjiang Qu; Kangquan Li

Let $m\geq5$ be odd with $3\nmid m$. Helleseth, Ichanska, and Kaleyski \cite{HIK} conjectured that two norm-perturbed Budaghyan--Helleseth--Kaleyski functions $F_2,F_3$ over $\F_{2^{2m}}$ are APN. In this paper, we prove this conjecture. First, by using the basis $(1,β)$ of $\F_{2^{2m}}$ over $\F_{2^m}$, we show that $F_2$ and $F_3$ are EA-equivalent to two functions $\mathcal G_1$ and $\mathcal G_0$, respectively. Their derivatives can be written as two trace equations for a matrix $P\in\mathrm{GL}(2,\F_{2^m})$. We then prove that these two equations have no solution. The proof uses only identities over finite fields, the characteristic polynomial of a $2\times2$ matrix, and elementary properties of Frobenius automorphisms. The repeated-root case and all parity cases are considered separately. It follows that the derivative of each function has kernel of size two in every nonzero direction, and hence both $F_2$ and $F_3$ are APN for every admissible $m$.
Rate-dependent gradient flows of integral currents via varicurrents
Antonín Češík; Malte Kampschulte; Filip Rindler

Motivated by the analysis of recent models of dislocation motion in crystalline materials, this work introduces space-time varicurrents, a form of Young measures over integral currents, to describe their evolutions with rate-dependent dissipation potentials. This addresses the problem that rate-dependent versions of the (rate-independent) space-time variation suffer from a lack of lower semicontinuity with respect to the natural weak topology. This causes a dynamical relaxation to occur by means of infinitely fine oscillations. Varicurrents retain a description of this ``microstructure'' (in space-time) and, based on this theory, we are able to establish the existence of solutions to a rate-dependent gradient flow. This is in contrast to the classical formulation using integral currents, which does not have a solution in general.

Hecke operators can be used to relate characters of rational conformal field theories with different central charges, but it has remained a mystery how to interpret these relations physically. We offer a simple explanation in terms of self-duality under asymmetric orbifolds. Self-dual orbifolds also give more general identities beyond the familiar Harvey-Wu construction, which we illustrate through examples.
Almost primes in short intervals and averages of long Dirichlet polynomial approximations to $(ζ'/ζ)^{k}$
Siegfred Baluyot; John Brian Conrey; Ayesha Irfan; Nina C. Snaith

We study the asymptotic behaviour of the mean square of long truncations of the Dirichlet series for $\bigl(ζ'/ζ\bigr)^{k}$ on the critical line; we establish the connection between this problem and the short-interval variance of the convoluted von Mangoldt function $Λ^{*k}$ in short intervals and in arithmetic progressions. Under a shifted moments conjecture and the Riemann Hypothesis (RH), we prove that the short-interval variance leading coefficient is the derivative of the mean-square leading coefficient. A unitary trace-sum average governs the variance of sums of $Λ^{*k}$ over monic polynomials in $\mathbb F_q[T]$; we denote its leading coefficient by $δ_k(c)$, where the total trace degree and matrix size grow with a fixed ratio $c$. Under a weaker shifted moments conjecture and RH, we recover this $δ_k(c)$ as the leading coefficient of the variance of short-interval sums of $Λ^{*k}$ over the integers. It is the counterpart of $γ_k(c)$, the piecewise polynomial from the variance of divisor sums, with the Dirichlet coefficients of $ζ(s)^k$ replaced by those of $\bigl(-ζ'/ζ\bigr)^k$.
Two-Player Zero-Sum Hybrid Games with Set-Valued Dynamics
Santiago J. Leudo; Francesco Ferrante; Ricardo G. Sanfelice

In this paper, we formulate a two-player zero-sum game under dynamic constraints defined in terms of a hybrid inclusion. The game consists of a min-max problem involving a cost functional that depends on the actions and corresponding (potentially non-unique) solutions, defined as functions of hybrid time and, hence, can flow or jump. We present sufficient conditions given in terms of Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs-like equations to establish a bound and to exactly evaluate the worst-case cost under the optimal strategy. Under additional conditions, we show that the proposed optimal state-feedback laws render a set of interest pre-asymptotically stable for the resulting hybrid closed-loop system. The results are illustrated in an application with sporadic jumps and linear quadratic hybrid dynamics.
Basic Reproductive Numbers in Host-Parasite Systems with Demographic Bistability
Carli Peterson; Erika Gallo; Christopher Kribs

The basic reproductive number, $\mathcal{R}_0$, is widely used to determine whether an infectious disease can persist in a population. However, its interpretation may become unclear when the underlying disease-free demographic dynamics exhibit multiple types of stable attractors. In this study, we investigate how demographic bistability between fixed points and periodic cycles affects the calculation and interpretation of $\mathcal{R}_0$. We consider two discrete-time host-parasite models with infection: a tick-host model motivated by Borrelia burgdorferi transmission and a Nicholson-Bailey host-parasitoid model with intraspecific competition and infection. For each model, we calculate reproductive numbers associated with different disease-free attractors using the next-generation operator method and compare their invasion thresholds. In the tick-host model, the reproduction number calculated on the stable demographic cycle differs from that calculated at the positive coexistence fixed point, resulting in parameter regions where infection can invade at one demographic attractor but not the other. In contrast, in the host-parasitoid model, the host-driven invasion threshold is necessarily the same at the positive coexistence fixed point and on the host-only periodic cycles. These contrasting results demonstrate that demographic bistability alone does not necessarily produce attractor-dependent invasion thresholds. Rather, the effect of demographic dynamics on invasion depends on the structure of pathogen transmission. In particular, a complete host--vector--host transmission pathway can allow differences between demographic attractors to alter the invasion threshold. Our results emphasize the importance of considering both demographic dynamics and transmission structure when interpreting $\mathcal{R}_0$ in populations with multiple stable disease-free states.
Algebraic ellipticity of double covers of $(\mathbf P^1)^3$
Alexander Dvorsky; Shulim Kaliman; Mikhail Zaidenberg

We show that every smooth complex double cover of $(\mathbf P^1)^3$ branched along a smooth divisor of tridegree $(2,2,2)$ is algebraically Gromov elliptic. These irrational Fano threefolds form Mori--Mukai family 3-1 and have anticanonical genus seven and Picard rank three. Their three coordinate projections define degree-four del Pezzo fibrations. Each threefold also admits a dominant rational map of degree two from $\mathbf P^3$.
The obstacle problem for fractional heat equations with memory
Félix del Teso; Fernando Quirós; Julio D. Rossi

We study the obstacle problem for the evolution equation $\partial_t^αu+(-Δ)^s u=0$ in the whole space $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $\partial_t^α$ with $α\in(0,1)$ is the Caputo derivative in time and $(-Δ)^s$ with $s\in(0,1]$ is the fractional Laplacian in space ($s<1$) or the classical Laplacian ($s=1$). We prove that the problem has at most one bounded viscosity solution, and we obtain existence as the limit of an explicit monotone finite-difference scheme, which combines the L1 discretization of the Caputo derivative with powers of the discrete Laplacian. The scheme is also used to establish regularity estimates in space and time. We then study the large-time behaviour: solutions converge, along subsequences, to stationary solutions, and we identify the limit when the initial datum coincides with the obstacle (the minimal stationary solution) or has a limit $c_*$ at infinity. In the latter case the dimension plays a role, as a consequence of the recurrence of the underlying process: the limit is the unique stationary solution with limit $c_*$ at infinity if $d>2s$, and a constant (the maximum between $c_*$ and the supremum of the obstacle) if $d\le2s$. Numerical experiments in one dimension, based on an explicit stationary solution, illustrate the convergence of the scheme and the relaxation towards the stationary profile.
Substantially Improved Rate and Distance for Addressable Transversal Phase Gates
Bujiao Wu; Tongyin Lin; Bin Cheng

An important ingredient in fault-tolerant quantum computation is asymptotically good codes with fully addressable transversal non-Clifford gates. Existing constructions, however, provide only small explicit guarantees for rate and relative distance. Here, we substantially improve these guarantees for fully addressable transversal phase gates at every fixed level $h\ge3$ of the Clifford hierarchy, using a cyclic encoding beyond the binary CSS framework. The encoding separates logical phase control from the joint design of rate and distance, enabling two constructions with different computational costs. A deterministic polynomial-time algebraic-geometric construction gives a common asymptotic lower bound of $52/(675h)$ on both quantities. A counting argument gives an exponential-time construction with exact verification, improving this bound by a factor of approximately $2.86$. We further establish a universal upper bound for codes supporting fully addressable transversal single-qubit phase gates. Within our cyclic encoding framework, we obtain a stronger upper bound that is approximately $1.28$ times the lower bound achieved by our exponential-time construction. As concrete examples, we construct codes with $48$ and $90$ physical qubits supporting fully addressable transversal $T$ gates. These results narrow the gap between achievable code parameters and addressability bounds, providing quantitative targets for further improvements in efficient code constructions.
Gervasio Figueroa; Joel Kuperman; Pedro Sánchez Terraf

We prove that there is no sequence $\{ X_n \}_{n\inω}$ such that for all $n$, there is an injection from $\mathcal{P}(X_{n+1})$ to $X_n$ under a restricted set of axioms that conforms to the "working mathematician's" intuition (excluding Choice, Replacement, and Foundation). We also show such a sequence cannot be defined using a formula either. More precisely, it is inconsistent with Zermelo set theory minus Infinity to have a formula $Φ(\cdot,\cdot)$ such that for each $n\inω$ there are $X$ and $Y$ with $Φ(n,X)$, $Φ(n+1,Y)$, and $\mathcal{P}(Y)$ being injectable into $X$. We finally show that the theorem fails if we allow infinitely many definitions, one for each term of the sequence, by using Hamkins, Linetsky, and Reitz's pointwise definable extensions of countable models of ZFC.
Distributionally Robust Dynamic Inventory Control: Automatic Recovery under Martingale Demand
Jianzhi Leng; Daniel Zhuoyu Long; Lun Ran; Chi Xie

Problem definition: We study dynamic inventory control for battery-swapping stations that combine central replenishment with automatic local recovery. Central replenishment improves immediate battery availability but reduces the depleted-battery pool available for subsequent recovery, creating an intertemporal trade-off. Managing this trade-off is particularly challenging when historical demand data are limited and future demand is uncertain and temporally dependent. Methodology/results: We develop a time-consistent distributionally robust dynamic program under martingale demand ambiguity, using the latest observed demand as the next conditional mean without requiring a fully specified demand distribution. We establish an optimal order-up-to policy for every finite horizon and identify two critical recovery rates governing replenishment decisions. Under a regular penalty condition, we derive explicit finite-horizon policies and worst-case demand distributions, showing that sufficiently strong automatic recovery makes central replenishment unnecessary in nonterminal periods. Extensions to submartingale and supermartingale demand reveal contrasting behaviors, including eventual full-capacity replenishment under upward ambiguity and recovery-induced positive replenishment under downward ambiguity. Managerial implications: Numerical experiments demonstrate that the robust policy is particularly competitive when demand is highly dispersed and historical information is limited, whereas its advantage diminishes when demand becomes more predictable or the conditional-mean assumption becomes less reliable. Our findings also reveal that greater reliance on local recovery may compromise service availability, highlighting the importance of jointly considering demand information, recovery capability, and service requirements when making replenishment decisions.
Arithmetic product theorems on self-similar sets of uniqueness and homogeneous Moran sets
Yan-Song Fu; Xu-Guang Wang; Meng Zhu

Varjú and Yu have given a complete description of non-singleton self-similar sets of uniqueness on the real line $\mathbb R$. In this paper, we first prove an arithmetic product theorem for self-similar $U$-sets $E:$ if $F\subset\mathbb R$ is compact, then $F\cdot E$ is an $M_0$-set if and only if $F$ is uncountable. We next show that this conclusion remains valid for bounded integer-based homogeneous Moran sets. As an application, for every $s\in(0,1]$, there exists a bounded integer-based homogeneous Moran set of uniqueness $K$ such that $\dim_H K=s$ and the self-product $K\cdot K$ is an $M_0$-set. In sharp contrast, for every $s\in[0,1/2]$ we can construct an unbounded integer-based homogeneous Moran $U$-set $E$ with $\dim_H E=s$ such that both $E$ and $E\cdot E$ are $U$-sets, and $1/2$ is the optimal threshold for $U$-sets to be closed under the arithmetic self-product. Moreover, we show that if $E\subset[0,1]$ is a compact set whose self-product $E\cdot E$ is contained in an $H$-set, then $\underline\dim_B E\le1/2$.
Deep Neural Operator Learning for stochastic heat equations and applications
Hengrong Du; Qi Feng; Weinan Wang

In this paper, we establish a universal approximation theorem for solution operators of semilinear stochastic heat equations in spatial dimension \(d\ge2\), extending deep neural operator approximation results to SPDEs with distribution-valued Gaussian forcing. A smooth Fourier cutoff reduces the forcing to finitely many measurements, while Besov and Schauder estimates control the resulting solution error. The finite-dimensional solution map is then approximated by ReLU branch networks together with grid-based trunk functions, yielding explicit bounds on the numbers of forcing measurements and trunk functions and approximation in every finite stochastic moment. For linear equations, the reduction coincides with truncation of the first Wiener chaos. Lastly, as an application, we prove a high-probability local-in-time approximation theorem for stochastic Navier--Stokes equations, with finite measurements of both the initial condition and forcing and an explicit sensing rate.
A constraint dissolving method for generally constrained optimization over a nonconvex set
Pengjie Liu; Haonan Shen; Xiaoxi Jia

This manuscript studies a constraint dissolving method for solving optimization problems with general constraints, comprising an abstract constraint G(x) \in C and a potentially nonconvex geometric constraint x \in D, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first constraint dissolving type method applicable to this general setting. More specifically, we introduce an auxiliary variable s to decouple G(x) \in C into G(x) = s and s \in C, and construct the constraint dissolving mapping acting jointly on both variables. We then propose a penalty-based constraint dissolving method, in which the penalty parameter is updated adaptively according to the feasibility error. Under mild conditions, every accumulation point is Mordukhovich-stationary. Anal., 288(3): Paper No. 110733, 23, 2025].

In this paper, continuing this story, we apply the same method, but consider distinct partitions. In particular, let $q_F(m)$ denote the number of ways of writing $m$ as the sum of distinct Fibonacci numbers. Yan-Zhu (arXiv:2605.31477) showed the compactness of complete Riemannian manifolds with non-negative Ricci curvature and uniformly convex boundary. In this paper, we give an alternative proof of this compactness theorem.

In five space dimensions, these equations admit infinitely many self-similar solutions with an increasing number of unstable modes. It was observed numerically in [1] that all excited profiles share the least unstable eigenvalue $λ=5$. The proof builds on an interplay between microlocal analysis and algebraic geometry. We also describe the generic sets through algebraic conditions.
Inverse powers and 2-adic properties of binary 3 x 3 matrices associated with the Tribonacci sequence

Finally, we provide a classification of 3 x 3 matrices associated with the Tribonacci recurrence via similarity over Q.

Matrix-weighted $Z$-spaces and tent spaces:characterizations, duality and interpolation
Tengfei Bai; Pengfei Guo; Jingshi Xu

Let $α\in\mathbb R$, $0<p<\infty$, $0<q,r\le\infty$, and $W$ be a matrix $\mathcal A_p$ weight on ${\mathbb R}^n$. We introduce the matrix-weighted $Z$-spaces $Z^{p,q,r}_α(W)$ and tent spaces $T^{p,q,r}_α(W)$ on the upper half-space and establish their characterizations using reducing operators. We then characterize homogeneous matrix-weighted Besov and Triebel--Lizorkin spaces in terms of the corresponding $Z$-spaces and tent spaces, respectively, using Schwartz kernels satisfying Tauberian and finite moment conditions. Furthermore, we establish duality for the matrix-weighted $Z$-spaces and tent spaces and obtain real and complex interpolation results for these spaces and the associated homogeneous matrix-weighted Besov and Triebel--Lizorkin spaces.
Four problems about the irreducible determined $T_0$-topologies

We answer four questions on irreducible determined $T_0$-topologies and a related question on monotone determined topologies posed by Xu, Yang and Luo (Topology Appl.\ 382 (2026), 109762). For every $T_0$ topology $τ$, the family $τ_r$ used to define its irreducible-derived topology is already a topology and preserves all nonempty irreducible subsets and their closures. Consequently, the least irreducible determined refinement is obtained in one step: $τ_r=\rd(τ)=\Rd(τ)$. For an arbitrary poset $P$, we describe the weakest order-compatible irreducible determined topology $ρ(P)$ using Dedekind--MacNeille cuts and a finite-cover condition involving principal lower sets. The Scott space of the binary-prefix domain provides a common counterexample to saturated heredity for irreducible determined spaces and monotone determined spaces: its maximal-point subspace is Cantor space. We also describe $ρ(P)$-closure by iterating an irreducible-cut operator, characterize Scott continuity of this operator, and give an example requiring two applications of the cut operator. A finite-decomposition condition extends the topology and closure-preservation results to general subset systems. For the Rudin and well-filtered determined systems, we exhibit a common $T_1$ example whose first and second derived topologies are the co-countable and discrete topologies, respectively. Thus the first derived topology need not be determined by the same subset system.
Asymptotic Optimality of $cμ$-Rule for LLM Inference Scheduling under Memory Constraint
Zhenghao Li; Shengbo Wang; Nian Si

Large language model (LLM) inference, the process by which a pre-trained model receives an input prompt and generates output tokens sequentially, has become increasingly important with the widespread deployment of LLM-based applications. As inference workloads continue to scale, GPU memory has emerged as a critical bottleneck: the long input prompts and generation sequences common in agentic and reasoning workloads lead to substantial key-value (KV) cache usage. In this paper, we study the resulting online scheduling problem from a queueing perspective. Requests arrive stochastically with heterogeneous prompt and output lengths, undergo prefill and autoregressive decode, and compete for a finite KV-cache capacity. Unlike classical queueing models, the duration of a processing step depends on both prefill computation and KV-cache I/O, so service capacity is jointly determined by computation, memory access, and memory occupancy. We develop a fluid model that reduces the system to a multiclass single-server queue with effective service rates capturing computation, memory access, and memory capacity. This fluid analysis yields a $cμ$ priority rule, where the effective service rate $μ$ is jointly determined by computational speed, memory bandwidth, and memory capacity. We prove that this rule minimizes cumulative holding cost in the fluid model and, for a finite workload, also minimizes completion time and maximizes full-run output-token throughput. We then construct a feasible scheduling policy for the original finite system and prove that its scaled dynamics converge to the optimal fluid policy. Finally, experiments on a real LLM serving engine using an NVIDIA H800 show that practical implementations of the proposed priority rule substantially reduce average latency while maintaining high throughput relative to existing scheduling policies.
Pushforwards of lc pairs under morphisms to abelian varieties

Let $f$ be a morphism from a log canonical pair $(X,Δ)$ to an abelian variety $A$ and $D\sim_{\mathbb Q}m(K_X+Δ)$ a Cartier divisor on $X$ with $m>1$ a rational number. We prove that $f_*\mathcal{O}_X(D)$ is globally generated after pullback by an isogeny. Our methods involve birational geometry, mixed Hodge modules and singular Hermitian metrics with the minimal extension property. Moreover, we provide simple counterexamples where the above result fails for plt pairs when $m=1$ and where the existence of Chen--Jiang decompositions fails for plt pairs for any $m\ge1$.
Generic factorizations and alternating direction method for fixed-rank approximation of matrix polynomials
Sweta Das; Andrii Dmytryshyn; Froilán M. Dopico; Mårten Gulliksson

We present an algorithm for approximating a given matrix polynomial of degree $d$ by a matrix polynomial of prescribed rank and degree at most $d$. The method builds on recent advances in the theory of generic eigenstructures and factorizations of matrix polynomials with bounded rank and degree. We also give a specialized treatment of the case of matrix pencils (degree one matrix polynomials), motivated by its particular theoretical and practical importance. Lastly, numerical experiments are reported to assess the performance of the proposed approach and to compare it with existing methods.
Construction of New Complete Complementary Codes Using Extended Boolean Functions and Permutations

Complete complementary code (CCC) is a crucial component in the design and optimization of modern wireless communication systems, particularly in addressing challenges related to interference, spectral efficiency, and signal quality. The design of CCCs is an active area of research, as it directly impacts the number of users that can be supported interference-free in the system. In the literature, CCC constructions are restricted by a set size smaller than the sequence length. In this paper, we introduce a novel construction method for CCCs based on the extended Boolean functions (EBF) that overcome existing restrictions by including a set size bigger than the sequence length. Further, the proposed construction uses functions which are new in literature and provide us with new CCCs. This is also the very first construction where row PMEPR is also bounded by $n$ for a set size in the form of power of $n$.
Regularity of geodesics in the spaces of convex and plurisubharmonic functions III

In this note, we study the regularity of solutions to the geodesic equation in the space of plurisubharmonic functions in a general Reinhardt domain. Our findings resolve a problem left open from our previous note [AD26].
Hidden Symmetries of the Kepler Problem and Jacobi's Theorem
Alejandro Moreno Díaz; Juan B. Sancho de Salas

We present a geometric derivation of the hidden symmetries of the Kepler problem, combining a duality for central-force systems, obtained by interchanging positions and velocities, with a generalized form of Jacobi's theorem. Applied to the dual Kepler problem, this theorem identifies Kepler hodographs of prescribed energy with geodesics of a metric of constant curvature. After adjoining one point at infinity, the resulting geometry is complete. Its Killing vector fields induce a finite-dimensional Lie algebra of infinitesimal symmetries on the corresponding energy hypersurface. The distinguished point at infinity determines a canonical decomposition of the Killing algebra into two vector subspaces, whose associated Noether invariants recover angular momentum and the Runge-Lenz vector.
Space--time Runge approximation for weakly viscous nonlocal waves and identification of coefficients

We study very weak solutions and Runge approximation for weakly viscous nonlocal wave equations with elastic term $(-Δ)^su$ and dissipative term $(-Δ)^r\partial_tu$, where $0\leq r<s$. For time-dependent potentials satisfying a smallness condition, we establish a transposition theory for sources in the dual of the natural space--time energy space. Under explicit nonlocality and nonresonance assumptions, we prove Runge approximation in $L^2(0,T;\widetilde H^s(Ω))$ and in $L^2(0,T;\widetilde H^s(Ω)) \cap H^1_0(0,T;\widetilde H^r(Ω))$. As an application, partial exterior Dirichlet-to-Neumann measurements uniquely determine a bounded, nonnegative, time-dependent coefficient in the nonlinear velocity damping term $q|\partial_tu|^{p-2}\partial_tu$ for $0<r<s$ and $2<p\leq 2+4r/n$. The proof establishes the small-amplitude response by energy estimates, weighted $L^p$ monotonicity convergence, and a linear Green identity, then applies adjoint Runge approximation followed by a forward velocity approximation in $L^2$. No smallness or positive lower bound is imposed on the nonlinear damping coefficient.
Weakly viscous nonlocal wave equations: forward theory, Lebesgue Runge approximation, and inverse problems

We study forward and inverse problems for weakly viscous nonlocal wave equations with elastic term $(-Δ)^s u$ and dissipative term $(-Δ)^r\partial_tu$, where $0\leq r<s$. For time-dependent potentials in suitable $L^\infty(0,T;L^p(Ω))$ classes, we establish finite energy well-posedness, strong continuity in time, and an energy identity by parabolic regularization and time-regularization arguments. Under explicit nonlocality and nonresonance assumptions on the fractional orders, we prove Runge approximation in $L^2(0,T;\widetilde H^r(Ω))$ and hence in $L^2(Ω\times(0,T))$. As an application, partial exterior Dirichlet-to-Neumann measurements uniquely determine the potential in all three exponent regimes of the Runge theorem, including integer elastic orders with noninteger dissipative orders. The recovery argument combines equality of solutions with the same exterior input, unique continuation or the entanglement principle, and a single Lebesgue-space Runge approximation. It applies to the full admissible potential class, without spatial boundedness, sign, or smallness assumptions.
On the Onsager--Machlup functional of the infinite-dimensional angular central Gaussian distribution and related measures
Hefin Lambley; T. J. Sullivan; Sam Taylor

The Onsager--Machlup functional of a probability measure is a generalisation of the negative logarithm of the probability density function, defined precisely using the ratios of masses of balls in the limit of vanishing radius. It plays an important role in several areas of applied mathematics because its minimisers can be understood as modes of the measure. We show that the Onsager--Machlup functional of the angular central Gaussian measure on the unit sphere of an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space---i.e., the radial projection of a centred Gaussian measure with covariance operator $C$---is constant on the finite-dimensional sphere spanned by the eigenvectors of leading eigenvalue under $C$, and takes the value $+\infty$ elsewhere. We discuss the consequences of this extreme concentration of mass for maximum a posteriori estimation in Bayesian inverse problems with an angular central Gaussian prior.
On the Haagerup Vertex Operator Algebras
Chongying Dong; Xiangyu Jiao; Feng Xu

Three constructions of vertex operator algebras realizing the Haagerup center were announced independently and almost simultaneously. The relations between these constructions are studied in this paper. The generators are expressed in a common lattice basis for $E_6\oplus A_2$. It is proved that the constructions of Riesen and Huang give isomorphic vertex operator algebras, and that this algebra and the algebra constructed by Jiao have isomorphic fixed point subalgebras under automorphisms of order two. The isomorphisms are given explicitly on generators. The common fixed point subalgebra contains the parafermion vertex operator algebras $K(\mathfrak{sl}_2,3)$ and $K(\mathfrak{sl}_2,13)$. A general rationality criterion for unitary vertex operator algebras is given in terms of positive linear combinations of conformal vectors and is applied to these constructions. The two vertex operator algebras are simple current extensions of the common fixed point subalgebra and have equivalent module categories as ribbon categories. The equivalence follows from decomposition with respect to a nondegenerate pointed subcategory with four simple objects in the module category of the common fixed point subalgebra. It is also proved that the conformal nets associated with these unitary vertex operator algebras are completely rational.
Relative Tate-Shafarevich kernel of a reductive group over a global field

We describe an algorithm and a computer program computing the relative Tate-Shafarevich kernel $Sha^S(K,G)$ of a reductive group $G$ over a global field $K$ with respect to a finite set $S$ of places of $K$ containing no archimedean places. We assume that we know the algebraic fundamental group $Λ=π_1^{alg}(G)$ together with the action on it of the Galois group $Θ=Gal(L/K)$, where $L/K$ is a finite Galois extension with no real places such that $Gal(K^s/L)$ acts trivially on $Λ$. We also assume that we know the decomposition subgroups $Θ_v\subseteq Θ$ for all places $v$ in $S$, and all non-cyclic decomposition subgroups $Θ_v$ for $v$ outside $S$. Under certain conditions, we compute the set $Sha^S(K,G)$ also when $S$ contains archimedean places.

We give a counting formula for the coefficients $a\in\F_{p^h}$ for which $x^{2n}+ax^n+1$ is irreducible in $\F_{p^h}[x;σ]$, for arbitrary positive integers $n$ and $h$, where $σ(a)=a^p$ and $p$ is an arbitrary prime power. The proof reduces the problem to quadratic reduced norms, establishes a uniformity statement for every Frobenius generator, and counts the remaining coefficients by Möbius inversion.
Unbounded total mean curvature with prescribed boundary metric

Bär has shown that a fixed boundary metric and a scalar-curvature lower bound do not generally bound total mean curvature from above. We extend this unboundedness to every smooth compact connected manifold of dimension $n\ge3$ with nonempty boundary and every prescribed boundary metric, using scalar-flat metrics. While Bär's examples use warped products, our construction uses a nonzero cubic variation of total mean curvature near a flat product, followed by localization and conformal correction. We also construct arbitrarily $C^k$-small perturbations of the flat torical half-cylinder with nonnegative scalar curvature, unchanged boundary metric, an exact product end, and positive total boundary mean curvature.
Real-analytic functional calculus and strictly real Banach algebras

We use real-analytic functional calculus to show that the envelope of the algebra of $m$-variable polynomials with real coefficients, with respect to the class of strictly real Banach algebras, is isomorphic to the algebra of real-valued analytic functions on $\mathbb{R}^m$.
Increasing stability for the inverse potential problem of the fractional Helmholtz equation
Dong Qiu; Xiang Xu; Yue Zhao

This paper is concerned with the inverse potential scattering problem for the three-dimensional fractional Helmholtz equation. For every $0<α<1$, we establish an increasing stability of determining the potential function from multifrequency exterior measurements of the scattered field. The stability consists of a Lipschitz data discrepancy and a logarithmic remainder that decreases when the upper measured wavenumber increases. The key ingredient in the analysis is to construct appropriate geometric optics solutions, which relate the X-ray transform of the potential to the measured fields. As a consequence, the stability is derived by applying analytic continuation. Two-dimensional numerical examples with noisy near-field data illustrate the benefit of enlarging the measured frequency band for three representative fractional orders.
Analytical properties of the principal clamped transmission eigenpair for a planar region
Haoran Qi; Isaac Harris; Andreas Kleefeld

This paper investigates the analytical properties of the principal eigenpair for the clamped transmission eigenvalue problem, which arises in the context of biharmonic (i.e. flexural wave) scattering by a clamped planar obstacle. By deriving a suitable Rayleigh quotient, we provide rigorous proofs for several fundamental properties that were previously only observed through numerical experiments. One of the results we have shown here is that the first eigenvalue is monotone decreasing with respect to the domain. Furthermore, we prove that the corresponding eigenfunction is of a single sign, a property analogous to the principal eigenfunction of the Dirichlet eigenvalues of the Laplacian. Another key result is a Faber--Krahn type inequality, establishing that the disk minimizes the principal eigenvalue among all domains of a given measure. The theoretical results are supported by a comprehensive numerical investigation.
Stochastic interpretation of the Water Waves equations

The aim of this article is to derive a stochastic interpretation of the Water Waves equations, based on the location uncertainty principle (LU). Next, these equations are used to infer simpler models from scaling limits, such as the Saint-Venant, Boussinesq and Serre-Green-Naghdi ones. Once adapted to the stochastic setting, these models have been successfully implemented numerically, and we show several experiments to assess their properties -- for example the breaking of the wave symmetry, and the influence of time correlated noises.
An oscillation result for slightly perturbed trigonometric series
We establish that any nontrivial anharmonic Fourier series with exponents quadratically close to the positive integers changes sign on each interval of length 2$π$.
Profinite approach to S-adic shift spaces II: Invertible directive sequences
Jorge Almeida; Alfredo Costa; Herman Goulet-Ouellet

This paper is the second in a series about (relatively) free profinite semigroups and S-adic representations of minimal shifts. The first installment introduced the key notions of profinite images and saturating properties. The present paper examines the relationship between relative invertibility conditions (on a directive sequence) and charging properties (of a shift). The main result shows that the two properties are equivalent under mild conditions. Moreover, charging properties are shown to be equivalent to density of subgroups generated by return words in relatively free profinite groups. The main result can then be used to deduce purely discrete statements about subgroups generated by return words in relatively free groups. We also highlight applications of the main result to the study of maximal bifix decoding, following earlier work by the second author. Finally, we establish some results on the effect of direct images on charging properties and explain how to apply these results to the case of episturmian shifts.
Finding Integer Roots of Polynomials in Nearly Optimal Time

Let $f\in\mathbb Z[x]$ be a polynomial of degree $n$ with integer coefficients of absolute value less than $2^b$. Using Pan's approximate factorization theorem, we give a deterministic algorithm that finds all distinct integer roots of $f$ in $\widetilde O(nb)$ bit operations. This matches the bit size of the input up to logarithmic factors and does not require $f$ to be square-free. Since we were unable to verify parts of the running time analysis of Pan's theorem, we also give a self-contained deterministic algorithm with running time $\widetilde O(nb+\min(n,b)^3b^2)$, which is $\widetilde O(nb)$ whenever $b\leq n^{1/4}$. This answers a question of Harvey and Hittmeir (2022), who asked whether integer roots can be found deterministically in quasilinear time, conditionally on Pan's theorem, and unconditionally for $b\leq n^{1/4}$. The fastest previous deterministic algorithm, due to Nir, takes $\widetilde O(n^{3/2}b)$ bit operations and works only for square-free polynomials. Instead of $p$-adic lifting, we combine approximate complex root finding with exact polynomial evaluation. We first approximate the complex roots of the polynomial formed by the top $\min(n,b)+1$ coefficients of $f$. Every integer root $r$ of $f$ with $|r|\geq 2$ lies within distance $2$ of some complex root of this truncated polynomial. Rounding the real parts of the approximate roots therefore gives a list of $O(\min(n,b))$ candidate integers that is guaranteed to contain all integer roots of $f$. Although a single candidate can have up to $b$ bits, a bound via the Mahler measure shows that the bit lengths of all candidates sum to $O(b)$. This allows us to test all candidates by exact multipoint evaluation in $\widetilde O(nb)$ bit operations.
Local resolution of the second log-Fitting ideal

Logarithmic Fitting ideals encode the complexity of the corresponding morphisms in a natural and intrinsic way, and their principalisation offers a new perspective on problems such as the resolution of cotangent sheaves and the monomialisation of morphisms. In this paper, we give a local resolution theorem for log-rank adapted morphisms: after finite sequences of smooth local blow-ups, the first two log-Fitting ideals \mathcal{F}\_{n--1}(σ) and \mathcal{F}\_{n--2}(σ) become principal monomial ideals.
A Discontinuous Galerkin Framework for Efficient Simulation of Cyclic Voltammetry Models
Assionvi Hove Kouevi; Debora Campos de Faria; Can Evren Yarman; Gabriel J. Lord

We develop a numerical framework to efficiently simulate the cyclic voltammetry models based on discontinuous Galerkin (DG) spatial discretization combined with linearly implicit Euler time integration. The method is applied to two electrochemical mechanisms: a heterogeneous electron-transfer (ET) reaction and an electron-transfer reaction coupled with a catalytic chemical step (EC'). The governing time-dependent reaction-diffusion equations are expressed in dimensionless form and discretized in space using locally defined orthonormal Legendre polynomial basis functions. This discretization leads to a system of ordinary differential equations that is subsequently advanced in time using the linearly implicit Euler method. The resulting solver, denoted $\text{DG}_{\text{Impl}}$, is evaluated through numerical experiments and compared with MATLAB's $pdepe$ solver in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. The numerical results demonstrate the convergence of $\text{DG}_{\text{Impl}}$ with respect to spatial and temporal discretizations and show that the method accurately reproduces the voltammetric responses of both ET and EC' mechanisms. For a prescribed relative error, $\text{DG}_{\text{Impl}}$ requires less computational time than $pdepe$ in the numerical experiments considered. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed DG formulation for the forward simulation of cyclic voltammetry models and provide a numerical foundation for subsequent adjoint-based parameter-estimation and inverse-problem formulations.
Approximating Distributions on Vertex Degrees in Random Hypergraphs via Stein's Method
Xianghe Zhu; Wenkai Xu; Gesine Reinert

Complex data are increasingly represented as hypergraphs. We establish bounds for approximating joint vertex-degree distributions by independent multivariate Poisson and correlated normal distributions in hypergraph models with independent hyperedges. We discuss the approximation of the distribution under different density regimes which are further supported by simulation studies.
Glauber Dynamics for Sampling Colorings: Rapid Mixing above $(1+1/\mathrm{e})Δ$ via Hidden Hard-Core Models

We show that for every $γ>0$ and every sufficiently large $Δ$, the Glauber dynamics for proper $q$-colorings of any $n$-vertex graph of maximum degree $Δ$ has spectral gap $Ω_γ(1/n)$, and hence mixing time $O_γ(n^2\log q)$, whenever $q\ge(1+1/\mathrm{e}+γ)Δ$. Our proof establishes a Bochner-type inequality by exploiting the spectral gaps of hard-core models hidden in the color classes. The constant $1+1/\mathrm{e}\approx1.368$ comes from the uniqueness threshold $\approx\mathrm{e}/Δ$ of the hard-core model on the infinite $Δ$-regular tree.
Characterization of Integral Transforms for Hilbert Space-Valued Functions

The aim of this paper is to characterize the Fourier transform of functions taking values in a separable Hilbert space $\Hi$ and defined on locally compact abelian groups. Inspired by Krukowskis characterization of integral transforms on locally compact abelian groups, we establish characterizations of the Fourier, Laplace, and cosine transforms for separable Hilbert space-valued functions on locally compact abelian groups. Furthermore, we obtain a characterization of the group Fourier transform on the Heisenberg group.
Rate-Distortion-Perception Tradeoff for Vector Gaussian Sources with Limited Common Randomness: Exact Characterization and Approximate Universality
Wentao Wang; Shuo Shao; Ruibin Li; Jingjing Qian; Jun Chen; Bin Xia

The distortion-rate-common randomness-perception (DRCP) theory characterizes how limited common randomness (CR) improves reconstruction fidelity under perceptual constraints, thereby providing an information-theoretic foundation for generative compression. In this paper, we characterize the DRCP tradeoff for vector Gaussian sources with limited CR under the squared-error distortion measure and the squared Wasserstein-2 perception measure. Specifically, we first establish a generalized reverse waterfilling characterization of globally optimal allocations. Second, we derive an analytical upper bound on the DRCP function through sequential greedy allocation of rate and CR. For fixed rate and CR budgets, the resulting representation is independent of the perception threshold. Finally, we establish its approximate universality through uniform performance guarantees: the achievable distortion exceeds the optimal distortion by at most $2ρ^*\approx0.2897$ times the total source variance, whereas the optimal-to-greedy distortion ratio is at least $η^*\approx0.7517$.
Two-block paths in oriented graphs under the Ore-type condition
Ke Zhao; Jia Zhou; Yunshu Gao

Stein conjectured that for every positive integer $k$, every oriented graph with minimum semi-degree greater than $k/2$ contains every oriented path of length $k$ [Springer Optim.Appl. 165 (2020), 459--486]. For directed paths this is a classical result of Jackson (1981). The two-block case of the conjecture was established by Chen, Hou and Zhou (2025). In this paper we prove the two-block analogue of Jackson's theorem. For all positive integers $s$ and $r$, let $P(s,r)$ be the oriented path consisting of two directed paths of lengths $s$ and $r$ with a common terminal vertex, and let $Q(s,r)$ be its reverse. We show that for all $K\ge3$ and all $s,r\ge1$ with $s+r\le K$, every oriented graph $D$ with $δ(D)\ge K$ and $d_D^+(u)+d_D^-(v)\ge K-1$ for every ordered pair of distinct vertices $(u,v)\notin A(D)$ contains both $P(s,r)$ and $Q(s,r)$. Our result is the two-block analogue of Jackson's theorem, and it extends the two-block result of Chen, Hou and Zhou. The proof iterates a shift of the terminal vertex of a longest path.
A Relative Telescope-Type Conjecture: Support and Generation in Half-Bounded Derived Categories

Let $R$ be a commutative noetherian ring. We ask whether complexes with finitely generated cohomology and a fixed support can be generated by relatively compact objects, using coproducts which exist in the half-bounded derived category. We prove that $\mathbf D^+_{\mathrm{fg},W}(R)=\operatorname{Loc}_{\mathrm{ex}}(\mathbf D^b_{\mathrm{fg},W}(R))$ whenever $W\subseteq\operatorname{Spec} R$ is specialization closed and has finite dimension. The same equality holds for every specialization-closed subset of $\operatorname{Spec} B$ when $B$ is a finite-type algebra over a noetherian domain $A$ of finite character and either $A$ or $B$ is regular. These equalities classify the thick Hom-submodules closed under existing coproducts. We also prove the corresponding bounded-above statement from the support results of Matsui--Takahashi. For an arbitrary noetherian ring, the bounded-below generation conjecture reduces to torsion complexes over quotient domains, with their support unchanged. Finally, over a regular noetherian domain of infinite dimension, we give a bounded-below object which is generated by bounded objects with the same support but has no bounded-below representative by finitely generated modules. The comparison functor from the bounded-below derived category of finite modules is therefore neither full nor essentially surjective.
Resolvent comparison for Hermitian block matrices and Kelmans transformations
Xianhao Meng; Zhijun Xu; Zhiyuan Zhang

A Kelmans transformation increases or preserves the largest eigenvalue of a symmetric nonnegative matrix. We determine when this comparison holds for Hermitian block extensions with a fixed coupling and an arbitrary common complementary block. An orthogonal change of basis and Schur complementation give an exact formula for the compressed resolvent difference as a difference of two rank-one matrices. This formula characterizes admissible coupling subspaces by proportionality of projected resolvent vectors. Polynomial coefficient kernels describe all such subspaces, and cyclic subspaces give dimension bounds and a maximum-dimension result for a two-block family. We also prove a general block comparison theorem and give monotonicity and equality criteria for nonnegative rank-one couplings. Applications concern graph joins, complex attachments, and Hermitian adjacency matrices.
Lower Bounds for Adaptive Relaxed Locally Decodable Codes via the Capped Horvitz--Thompson Estimator
Guy Goldberg; Tom Gur; Sidhant Saraogi

We prove a nearly optimal lower bound on the blocklength of general relaxed locally decodable codes (RLDCs), extending the result of [GGS26] to nonlinear encodings and adaptive decoders with two-sided error. Namely, we show that any $q$-query RLDC $C\colon \{0,1\}^k \to \{0,1\}^n$ must satisfy $n = k^{1+Ω(1/q)}$, closely matching the upper bound of $n = k^{1+O(1/q)}$ by Ben-Sasson, Goldreich, Harsha, Sudan, and Vadhan (STOC 2004). Our proof reduces showing RLDC lower bounds to estimating the output distribution of adaptive decoders. To this end, we introduce a capped Horvitz--Thompson estimator with uniformly bounded discrete derivatives on the $p$-biased cube. We establish its concentration of measure via self-bounding inequalities and control the downward bias induced by capping through a spreadness argument.
Online packing of the three largest trees

For every $n\ge4$, arbitrary trees of orders $n,n-1,n-2$ can be packed into $K_n$ online, in decreasing order of size: each tree must be embedded before the next is revealed, and earlier embeddings cannot be changed. This strengthens the classical three-tree packing theorem of Hobbs, Bourgeois and Kasiraj (1987). In particular, the second tree is embedded without knowing the third, and the resulting pair of copies can be extended to accommodate every possible third tree. Our strategy is to embed the first two trees so that their union is $2$-degenerate. We prove that the complement of every $2$-degenerate graph on $n$ vertices contains every tree of order $n-2$, which guarantees the final move. The main ingredient is an embedding lemma for spiders whose center must occupy a prescribed vertex having degree at most two in the forbidden graph. We then extend this lemma to arbitrary trees by induction.
Lorentz-Invariant Measure for Path Integrals in the Future Cone
Vladimir V. Belokurov; Vsevolod V. Chistiakov; Klavdiia A. Lursmanashvili; Evgeniy T. Shavgulidze

We construct a measure on continuous paths in the future cone of two-dimensional space that is invariant under the orthochronous Lorentz group and quasi-invariant under the action of the diffeomorphism group. We use the proposed measure to obtain the fundamental solution of the heat equation. The result agrees with the expression obtained by other methods.
Uniform boundary observability for periodic wave equations with low frequency exponent $4/3$

We study boundary observability for Dirichlet wave equations with symmetric, periodic coefficients in bounded $C^{2,1}$ domains of dimension $d\ge2$. We establish two-sided observability estimates, uniform in the oscillation scale $\varepsilon$, for initial data generated by eigenfunctions with eigenvalues at most $δ\varepsilon^{-4/3}$ with some small factor $δ$. The proof reduces wave observability to boundary gradient estimates for narrow spectral clusters. These estimates are obtained using a second-order expansion and a uniform commutator estimate for harmonic extension in boundary layers.
Effective results in representation theory of reductive groups over local fields
Avraham Aizenbud; Dmitry Gourevitch; David Kazhdan; Eitan Sayag

We prove effective versions of several classical results in representation theory of reductive groups over non-Archimedean local fields of arbitrary characteristic. More specifically, we deal with the support of matrix coefficients of cuspidal representations and the recursions satisfied by matrix coefficients of representations of finite length. We provide effective generation results for irreducible representations. Finally, we study the effective smoothness of characters on the set of regular semi-simple elements.
Benjamin Merlin Bumpus; Guilherme C. M. Gomes; Laura Larios-Jones; Will J. Turner

Tree decompositions describe large graphs as gluings of smaller component parts. Here we study their categorical duals, tree co-decompositions, which construct large graphs via fibered products of small constituent parts. Co-decompositions are compressed representations of graphs or relational structures: the decomposed object can be exponentially larger than the space required to specify the co-decomposition. Our main contribution is an algorithmic meta-theorem for first order logic: given only a co-decomposition of a $σ$-structure $G$ with $b$ bags, each of size at most $w$ and an FO sentence $ϕ$, there is an algorithm which, without ever constructing or inspecting $G$, operates on the co-decomposition and determines whether $G \models ϕ$ in time $f_σ(w,|φ|)\cdot b$. We pair this algorithm with structural results on tree co-width, including its relationship to tree-width and a separation from twin-width. Furthermore, we characterize bounded path co-width using a graph grammar. In contrast to our logical meta-theorem, we prove that $(s,t)$-Path becomes NP-hard on co-decomposition inputs. These results demonstrate how categorical constructions can enable efficient computation on exponentially compressed structures.
Long-time behaviour and bifurcation analysis of a non-reciprocal two-species aggregation-diffusion system on the torus

A two-species aggregation-diffusion system on the one-dimensional torus with antisymmetric cross-interactions modeling pursuit-evasion dynamics is studied. The self-interaction strength is used as a bifurcation parameter, and the linear stability of the homogeneous state is characterized by Fourier analysis. It is shown that non-reciprocal coupling enlarges the stability region. In a symmetric diffusion setting, exponential convergence to the homogeneous state is established for sufficiently weak self-interactions by means of an entropy argument, with a decay condition independent of the cross-interaction strength. Under suitable nondegeneracy and spectral assumptions, the first loss of stability is shown to occur through a Hopf bifurcation associated with a single spatial Fourier mode. A branch of time-periodic patterns is thereby obtained, along which the two species oscillate with a fixed phase difference. An explicit formula for the cubic Hopf coefficient is derived, and an essential dependence of the direction and stability of the bifurcating branch on the second spatial harmonic is identified. Local convexity obstructions for bounded realizations of Teichmüller space

We prove that $\partial D$ has no locally convex boundary patch containing a complex $(n-1)$-dimensional manifold through each of its points. Together with known constructions of C*-diagonals in the stably finite setting by Xin Li, this shows that every classifiable C*-algebra (in the sense of the Elliott classification programme) has a C*-diagonal. Futhermore, to characterize the performance benefit of joint decoding, we further derive numerical and closed-form achievability bounds for the two-user Gaussian MAC under joint nearest-neighbor (JNN) decoding. Additive energy, Freiman's lemma, and an edge-isoperimetric problem on the boolean cube

The limiting interface measure satisfies Brakke's inequality, and its normal velocity equals the sum of its mean curvature and the normal projection of the fluid velocity.
Isolated symplectic singularities admitting symplectic resolutions

We give a proof that an isolated algebraic symplectic singularity of dimension $2n\ge 4$ admitting a projective symplectic resolution is analytically isomorphic to the minimal nilpotent orbit closure in $\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}$ at the origin.
Weighted orbits of hypercyclic vectors on F-spaces

We characterize the scalar sequences for which weighted hypercyclicity always implies ordinary hypercyclicity: their nonzero values must be bounded and bounded away from zero. We revisit the classical spectral problem for the Laplace-Beltrami and Laplace-Bochner operators on complex Grassmannians. Together, these approaches provide a more explicit picture of the spectral geometry of Grassmannians and clarify the relation between harmonics, Young diagrams, magnetic bundles, and Laplacian spectra.
Changxin Yang; Jianwei Shi; Zhongyi Zhu

Distributed statistical learning has recently attracted significant attention owing to its computational efficiency and scalability in large-scale systems. However, the non-smooth quantile loss poses substantial challenges to the development of efficient decentralized algorithms for quantile regression. Existing methods may either suffer from slow convergence or rely on smoothing-based approximations that require additional stringent assumptions, particularly in high-dimensional settings. To address these issues, we propose a decentralized framework that integrates gradient tracking with iterative hard thresholding for sparse quantile estimation. The proposed method avoids smoothing approximations and relaxes the initialization requirement. Theoretically, we show that the proposed algorithm achieves linear convergence under stated regularity conditions and that the resulting estimator attains the same order of statistical accuracy as its centralized counterpart. We further develop a decentralized information criterion for selecting the working sparsity level and establish support screening guarantees. Numerical experiments and a real-data study illustrate the finite-sample performance of the proposed method.

Using the incidence correspondence between $X$ and $M$, we construct a family $\mathcal E$ of objects in the Kuznetsov component $\operatorname{Ku}(X)$. For a very general point of the trivector divisor corresponding to discriminant $24$, we also construct an integral Hodge isometry between the full Mukai lattices of $\operatorname{Ku}(X)$ and the associated twisted K3 surface.

This paper proposes and examines a completely discrete discontinuous Galerkin finite element scheme to approximate the solution of a class of strongly damped wave equations with uniform exponential decay property. Subsequently, a fully discrete scheme is developed and analyzed. Using suitable energy techniques, the consistency between the decay properties of the continuous and discrete systems is demonstrated. Moreover, error estimates that preserve the uniform decay property are highlights of this paper. Finally, several numerical experiments are performed to confirm the theoretical convergence results, verify the predicted decay behavior, and investigate the influence of model parameters on stability and computational accuracy.

For odd $p$ the groups are new: they adapt OpenAI's direct-finiteness construction with a signed cancellation, found first by S. V. Ivanov and independently by us, via an exact solution of a colour-balance problem and a Perron certificate. As far as we know, they are the first torsion-free counterexamples to direct finiteness and to the idempotent conjecture in odd characteristic. We propose a new estimator of low-frequency skewness (monthly) that exploits high-frequency data (5 min) through a direct functional mapping consisting of layers of Convolutional Neural Networks followed by Multi Layer Perceptrons. Monte Carlo experiments involving stochastic volatility models, with and without jumps, show that the estimator reduces finite-sample bias relative to existing realized-skewness estimators and remains accurate under model misspecification. Empirically, our estimator exhibits temporal stability and delivers cross-sectional performance in actual skewness-sorted portfolios. We characterize the finite-sample bias of conventional plug-in skewness estimators and establish risk consistency properties of the proposed NN estimator under standard regularity conditions.
Continuized Quasar-Convex Acceleration via an Unbiased Finite-Mixing Network Oracle

CQA-Net keeps a common state, mixes local rows for finitely many rounds, and disseminates one uniformly selected row; its oracle is unbiased at every mixing depth, so incomplete averaging affects only the variance. A walking token removes dissemination, the shared clock, and the shared root, and an importance weight keeps it unbiased on fixed graphs. On the IQC and SRG Frameworks: Equivalences and Converse Results

Integral quadratic constraints (IQCs) and scaled relative graphs (SRGs) are two prominent frameworks for analyzing feedback systems. Although both frameworks are rooted in the same graph separation principle, a general characterization of their relationship has remained unavailable. This paper establishes conditions under which the IQC- and SRG frameworks are equivalent. To this end, we introduce two new classes of systems, termed disjunctive and conjunctive systems, which are respectively characterized by unions and intersections of quadratic input-output constraints. Under structural assumptions, we prove equivalence between the IQC and SRG frameworks for these system classes. By exploiting this equivalence, we develop novel IQC- and SRG-based converse stability results for linear and nonlinear systems. Full spectrum reuse with a common waveform generates mutual interference that couples the two functionalities. Communication performance is characterised through downlink queues whose service rates are governed by the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) via the Shannon capacity. Sensing performance is captured by a Kalman filter (KF) whose measurement noise covariance depends on the sensing SINR, yielding a non-classical state-dependent filtering problem. We define system-level performance metrics under the Palm distribution of the base station process and prove the consistency of their empirical estimators. We then prove that, for a typical base station, communication and sensing metrics are associated, so that operating regimes favourable to one functionality tend to benefit the other. The proof combines the monotonicity of the queue and filter recursions in the configuration of interferers with the Harris--FKG inequality for Poisson functionals. We also show that the excess association ratio of the two interference levels decays as the inverse of the network density. Simulations based on a ray-tracing channel model corroborate the analysis.
Nonlinear Darcy Laws for Generalized Newtonian Fluids with Orlicz Growth and Oscillating Navier Slip in Periodic Porous Media

We study the periodic homogenization of a stationary generalized Navier--Stokes system in a periodically perforated domain $Ω\subset\mathbb R^N$, $N\in\{2,3\}$, with a heterogeneous bulk stress of general Orlicz growth and an oscillating nonlinear Navier friction law on the pore walls, both at the Darcy scale. The proof relies on a uniform Orlicz--Korn inequality, a Darcy-scaled two-scale trace theorem and a coupled bulk--surface Minty argument.

Starting from a fully three dimensional model of finite viscoelasticity in the Kelvin-Voigt rheology, we derive a bending model for thin, viscoelastic rods. For this, we utilize a formulation of the model as a time-dependent metric gradient flow and pass to the limit by establishing convergence of curves of maximal slope using $Γ$-convergence. A posteriori, we relate the metric gradient flow limits to gradient flows in Hilbert spaces and discuss their properties. In contrast to previous results, where limit deformations are infinitesimal, in the bending regime, we deal with large rotations. This prevents us from using an additive ansatz for the construction of recovery sequences. Instead, we adapt from a previous result by the authors a multiplicative ansatz for elastoplastic Cosserat rods to the viscoelastic setting. For regularization purposes, we consider strain gradient terms in the three dimensional model that vanish in the limit.
Finiteness properties of centralisers in $\mathrm{Out}(F_N)$ and automorphisms of free-by-cyclic groups

Let $F$ be a finitely generated free group. We prove that the centraliser of any element of $\mathrm{Out}(F)$ or $\mathrm{Aut}(F)$ is of type $\rm{VF}$. We also prove that the (outer) automorphism group of any free-by-cyclic group $M=F\rtimes_φ\mathbb{Z}$ is of type $\rm{VF}$, and so are the McCool subgroups of $\mathrm{Out}(M)$. This relies on the construction of a new $\mathrm{Out}(M)$-invariant splitting of $M$, that enables us to reduce the proof of the above statements to the case where the outer class of $φ$ has finite order.
