As a generalization of ordinary $m$-positivity, sequential $m$-positivity is defined by the hyperbolicity cones of successive directional derivatives of the determinant. We formulate a generalized mixed Hodge--Riemann conjecture for this condition and prove several cases beyond the scalar inequalities supplied by hyperbolicity. We prove strict strong positivity for good prefixes with at most three repeated blocks after the first factor. We also consider weak $m$-positivity which corresponds to the pointwise subsolution condition for the complex $m$-Hessian equation. In this setting, we prove the Hodge--Riemann relations for $p\neq q$ and in several diagonal cases, and show that the associated power map induces a pointwise diffeomorphism onto the cone of positive $(d-1,d-1)$-forms. Using Dinh and Nguyên's $L^2$ globalization method, we pass from the pointwise relations to cohomology classes on compact Kähler manifolds. Finally, we propose conjectures on a numerical criterion for sequential $m$-positive classes and on the solvability of the generalized $m$-Hessian equation.
Verena Bögelein; Naian Liao; Calvin Stanko
Under a minimal tail condition, local weak solutions to a class of nonlinear nonlocal parabolic equations modeled on the fractional heat equation possess continuous spatial derivatives.

Consider the hyperbolic Gaussian analytic function (GAF) \begin{equation*} F_{\mathbb{D}}(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty }ξ_{n}z^{n},\qquad |z|<1, \end{equation*} where the $ξ_{n}$ are independent standard complex Gaussian variables. Peres-Virág theorem tells that the distribution of the zeros of $F_{\mathbb{D}}(z)$ is provided by a Determinantal Point Process (DPP). We prove that $F_{\mathbb{D}}(z)$ is the only GAF whose zeros are determinantal with a Hermitian kernel, up to multiplication by a zero-free holomorphic function and a one-to-one holomorphic change of variable, with a \ non-degeneracy condition imposed to exclude trivial cases. The proof identifies a geometric property of GAF's with (local) determinantal zeros: the metric defined by the first intensity must have constant curvature $-4$.
The kinetic Kato square root problem

We solve the kinetic Kato square root problem for the whole-space Kolmogorov operator $$H_A=\partial_t-X\cdot\nabla_Y-\operatorname{div}_X(A\nabla_X)$$ on \(\mathrm L^2\) with Lebesgue measure, where \(A\) is a bounded measurable complex uniformly accretive matrix depending on all variables. We define its realization through a sesquilinear form and identify the square-root domains of the resulting maximal accretive operator and its adjoint with the intrinsic Sobolev space defined by one velocity derivative and half a derivative along the transport flow. The homogeneous norm equivalences depend only on the dimension and the coefficient bounds. The energy also controls a position derivative of order one third. The proof uses second-order resolvents and localized affine testing. A regularized transport symmetrizer gives hidden coercivity, while comparison with a positive Rockland operator supplies intrinsic smoothing. Commutator and dyadic approximation estimates remove the smoothing before a Carleson argument is applied. We also obtain uniform shifted square-root estimates and bounded velocity, transport and position Riesz transforms.
Diagonal Equivalence in State Space Models: Characterization, Retrieval Rank, and Selective Extensions

We classify real and complex state-space models (SSMs) with linear transitions, distinguishing fixed-basis diagonal equivalence from input-output equivalence and tracking coefficient-conditioning windows under coordinate changes. We characterize diagonal equivalence through commuting transition families whose members are diagonalizable over the chosen field. With time-shared token-local matrix maps, we identify this class's state-mediated kernels with unnormalized scalar-mode linear attention with multiplicative masks. Mamba 3's multiple-input, multiple-output (MIMO) construction lifts one value per local interface; SSD-MIMO routes independent values for local retrieval rank above one. HybridMamba combines Mamba 1's per-coordinate decay, Mamba 2-style heads and Mamba 3's complex rotations and two-endpoint writes, mixing real and rotating state blocks with different decay laws. They recover Mamba 1-3 single-input, single-output (SISO) configurations as exact special cases. On five large H100 bfloat16 workloads, our fused GPU kernels improve geometric-mean training time over official Mamba 1/3 in matched SISO recoveries, with Mamba 2 near parity at SSM-core scope. Memory tradeoffs depend on the baseline and metric: saved-for-backward versus peak allocation. In small-model multi-token recall experiments, both designs outperform Mamba 1-3 on the hardest tier; higher routing ranks perform best in gated or phase-diverse configurations. In single-seed language models with about 500M parameters, both improve on Mamba 1/2 in test loss at 2B tokens, but the routing gains do not translate into lower language-model loss. Our best configurations approach Mamba 3 SISO through 10B tokens while remaining behind it and Mamba 3 MIMO in language-model loss.
Non-simple Arrangements of Lines and Pseudolines with Many Triangles

We study affine arrangements of an even number $n$ of lines and pseudolines with many triangles. For simple ones, Blanc's bound limits the number of triangular faces to $\lfloor n(n-5/2)/3\rfloor$. Adapting the Bartholdi-Blanc-Loisel doubling to the even case, we construct an infinite series of arrangements of $n=6\cdot2^t+2$ ($8,14,26,50,\ldots$) straight lines with two triple points and $(n(n-5/2)+1)/3$ triangles, one more than the simple bound allows. We obtain exhaustive enumerations of triangle-maximal pseudoline arrangements, simple or not, for even $n\le12$. For $n=6,8,10,12,14$ the maximum number of triangles, for both lines and pseudolines, is $7,15,25,38,54$; for $n=8,12,14$ every optimal arrangement has multiple points. All optimal arrangements for even $n\le12$ are realizable by straight lines, except two arrangements of 10 pseudolines, which are not stretchable. For the odd value $n=11$, no arrangement with $33$ triangles exists even with multiple points. We also obtain even arrangements by adding a line to odd ones. For $n\equiv2\pmod 6$ this again gives one triangle more than the simple bound, in pseudolines up to $n=44$ and in straight lines for $n=20$ and $n=32$. Doubling these pseudoline arrangements gives members of the series $18\cdot2^t+2$ and $30\cdot2^t+2$ with the same excess, up to $n=146$ and $n=242$, respectively; those with $n=38$ and $n=74$ are realizable by straight lines. These results lead us to conjecture that an arrangement of an even number $n$ of pseudolines has at most $\lfloor n(n-2)/3\rfloor-\lfloor n/6\rfloor$ triangles.
Xiang Ji; Tiancheng Xu; Wensheng Yu

Mordell's problem asks for the largest product of squared pairwise distances among $n$ points in the complex plane with a prescribed sum of squared distances from the origin. When this sum equals $n$, the maximum for $2\le n\le5$ is known to be $n^n$, attained precisely by the $n$th roots of unity up to rotation and relabeling. For $n\ge6$, Chalk showed that a regular polygon together with its center gives a larger product than the regular $n$-gon. We prove that for $6\le n\le9$ the maximum is $(n-1)^{n-1}r_n^{n(n-1)}$, where $r_n=\sqrt{n/(n-1)}$. Up to the same symmetries, the unique maximizer consists of the origin and the vertices of a regular $(n-1)$-gon of radius $r_n$. For six points, algebraic elimination reduces the proof to an exact comparison of stationary values. For seven points, we compare all twelve classes in a published classification of equilibria. For eight and nine points, rigorous interval arithmetic establishes an inequality for every admissible pair. Summing over pairs gives the sharp global bound, and the equality conditions determine the configuration. An explicit ten-point comparison and a known instability result together exclude Chalk's configuration for every $n\ge10$. For each $n$ from two through eight, Mordell's problem and the minimum-diameter problem studied by Bateman and Erdős have a common optimal configuration.
Pairs of quadrics in eleven variables over number fields

A nested version of the $δ$-method is developed for number fields $K/\QQ$ and is used to establish an asymptotic formula for the number of $K$-rational points of bounded height on non-singular complete intersections of two quadrics in $\PP^{n-1}_K$, when $n\geqslant11$.

A $\textit{diamond}$ is a graph obtained by removing an edge from the complete graph on four vertices. A graph is $\{P_7, \text{diamond}\}$-$\textit{free}$ if it contains no induced subgraph isomorphic to a seven-vertex path or a diamond. Schiermeyer (2020) asked whether there is a constant $c$ such that $χ(G)\leqω(G)+c$ for every $\{P_7, \text{diamond}\}$-free graph $G$. We answer this question affirmatively by proving $χ(G) \leq ω(G)+3$. Moreover, the bound is optimal.
The Nuclear Dimension of Extensions and Graph $C^*$-Algebras
Samuel Evington; Gregory Faurot; Christopher Schafhauser

We prove that the nuclear dimension of any graph $C^*$-algebra is at most two, and we compute the exact value of the nuclear dimension for a large class of graph $C^*$-algebras. In particular, this class covers all graphs with Condition (K). Our methods --- based on Szabó's recent $KK$-uniqueness theorem --- provide a unified approach to computing the nuclear dimension of various extensions. This includes the nuclear dimension of the Toeplitz algebra (first computed by Brake--Winter) and that of the Cuntz--Toeplitz algebras (first computed by Easo et al).

Given $A,B\in B\left(H\right)_{+}$, we consider the existence and uniqueness of a positive operator $C\in B\left(H\right)_{+}$ such that \[ \left(I+mA+nB+mnC\right)^{-1}=\int_{\left[0,1\right]^{2}}s^{m}t^{n}dE\left(s,t\right),\quad m,n\geq0, \] for a positive operator-valued measure $E$. This is a joint Hausdorff moment problem. Without $C$, it holds if and only if $AB=BA$. In dimension two we give a complete criterion for noncommuting pairs. In higher finite dimensions, nonexistence is generic. Under certain spectral and cyclicity assumptions, we obtain a necessary and sufficient condition on arbitrary Hilbert spaces. The completion is unique in this case. We also classify these pairs up to unitary equivalence. The class includes irreducible infinite-dimensional examples, even with continuous spectrum.
Finite-horizon Optimal Consumption and Investment with Costly Income Adjustment

We study optimal consumption and investment for an investor who receives labor income until a fixed retirement date, can raise the income rate irreversibly at a constant price per unit of income flow, and cannot borrow against future income. A pathwise argument shows that no income is purchased during a final period before retirement whose length depends only on the interest rate and the price. Before this period the dual problem has two free boundaries: a lower one generated by the borrowing constraint and an upper one, at which income is purchased, that escapes to infinity as the final period begins. The analysis of this problem is our main mathematical contribution. During the final period it is a single obstacle problem, which we solve, together with the regularity of its free boundary, by established methods. Before that period a partial hodograph transformation straightens both free boundaries and turns the problem into a quasilinear parabolic equation with oblique boundary conditions on a fixed interval. Comparison principles, explicit barriers and regularity theory for quasilinear equations then give existence, uniqueness and smoothness. Transforming back and gluing the two constructions yields global regularity: both free boundaries are infinitely differentiable and the value function is a classical solution at every positive wealth level. A dual budget process verifies optimality. We also derive coupled Volterra integral equations for the free boundaries, prove exponential convergence to the perpetual problem under a scalar condition, and find numerically a purchase threshold that is U-shaped in the time to retirement.

This book develops a digital formulation of finite group theory, in which every finite group of order $N$ is represented as the alphabet $\{0,1,\dots,N-1\}$ endowed with the transported group product. Multiplication, inversion and related structure are written explicitly as integer operations on labels. The foundations treat digit functions, codes of permutations and $r$-ary operators, finite magmas, and constructions of laws from diagrams. Classical parts of finite group theory, including conjugacy classes, stabiliser chains and characters, are recast as identities between digits of codes. The book gives explicit digital laws for all groups of order at most 32, the finite quotients of the 17 plane and 230 space crystallographic groups, the symmetric and alternating groups, the finite simple groups of Lie type, and all 26 sporadic groups. For most sporadic groups the laws are obtained by chain constructions; for the Baby Monster and the Monster they are computed structurally from the 196884-dimensional representation and evaluated with the mmgroup package. The accompanying software archive reproduces the laws, tables and worked examples as verifiable integer data.
Singular evolution of Gaussian measures under energy-critical and supercritical nonlinear Schrödinger equations

We consider a family of nonlinear Schrödinger equations with odd-power nonlinearities and fractional dispersion in an energy-critical/supercritical regime. For a family of Gaussian measures supported on high-regularity spaces, we show that the flow immediately evolves these measures to ones that are mutually singular with respect to their initial distributions. In the cubic case, the threshold for singularity exactly corresponds to the energy scaling for the equation. In particular, we establish singular evolution of Gaussian measures under the flow of the energy-critical cubic NLS on the 4-dimensional torus.
Higher Groupoids of Gauge Potentials in Higher Gauge Theories admitting Weights

We construct an explicit small model for the $\infty$-groupoid of null-concordances of higher gauge curvatures by algorithmically trivializing their nonlinear Bianchi identities. More precisely, for a finite-type Sullivan minimal Bianchi algebra equipped with positive integer weights, we organize weighted potentials and higher gauge parameters at each fixed curvature into an $\infty$-groupoid whose gauge transformations are linear in the parameters. We prove that this model is naturally equivalent to the $\infty$-groupoid of null-concordances through an intermediate total-form model, with explicit projection and section maps and simplicial homotopies. When nonempty, its connected components form a torsor for the degree-zero cohomology of an associated weighted gauge complex, and its higher homotopy groups are computed by the higher cohomology of this complex.
Perturbation Analysis of Gravitational Collapse of Gaseous Stars in the Pressureless Euler-Poisson System

The compressible Euler-Poisson system describes the full evolutionary processes of inviscid compressible gases, including compression, expansion, fluid motion, equilibrium states and gravitational collapse, under the combined effects of self-gravitation, pressure and inertial forces. It constitutes the fundamental macroscopic mathematical model for describing stellar structures, nebular evolution and gravitational collapse of gaseous celestial bodies. The system comprises mass conservation, momentum conservation, energy conservation laws coupled with the Poisson equation. Following the research in \cite{huang2022}, this paper investigates the quantitative relations among the relative perturbation amplitude of initial velocity, critical time and collapse time for gaseous stars undergoing gravitational collapse within the framework of the pressureless Euler-Poisson system. The closed-form formulas are verified against direct numerical integration, the accuracy of the asymptotic power law is quantified, and the relation between the two time scales is examined.

A monomial square form is a polynomial $F=\sum_{i=1}^k M_i^2$, where $M_1,\ldots,M_k$ are pairwise distinct squarefree monomials $\ne1$. We consider the problem of which of these forms are universal, i.e.\ represent every positive integer. We consider three classes of such forms:\\ (1) Forms $M_1^2+M_2^2+M_3^2+M_4^2$ ($k=4$),\\ (2) Forms $M_1^2+\ldots +M_5^2$ ($k=5$) in at most 5 variables,\\ (3) Forms where the monomials are products of consecutive variables of a fixed length:\\ $P_{m,d}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{d}(x_ix_{i+1}\cdots x_{i+m-1})^2,$ and its circular version\\ $C_{m,d}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}(x_ix_{i+1}\cdots x_{i+m-1})^2\quad(n=m+d-1,\ x_{i+n}=x_i).$ We classify which of these are universal, possibly universal, or conditionally universal on a conjecture on the form $x^2+4y^2+5z^2$. This ternary form appears repeatedly and seems to play a central role. For forms (1), we also show that a form is universal if and only if it represents 14, 15, 29 and 9591 (partially conditional on $x^2+4y^2+5z^2$).
Resilient Cell-Free MIMO ISAC Under Uncertainties: An Impairment-Aware Graph Neural Network Framework
Oways Alsoloh; Robert-Jeron Reifert; Aymen Khaleel; Stefan Roth; Aydin Sezgin

Beamforming designs for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) in cell-free multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems face the challenge to stay reliable under uncertainties from both channel state information (CSI) as well as clutter. To this end, this paper proposes an impairment-aware heterogeneous graph neural network (GNN) framework for beamforming that obtains the CSI error level and the clutter covariance as edge features, which enables a single trained model to adapt to both impairments. In particular, the GNN is trained on a low quantile of the minimum user rate with a clutter-aware signal-to-clutter-plus-noise ratio, balanced by a normalized Tchebycheff scalarization. Simulation results show that the proposed GNN framework outperforms the considered baselines in sensing-only and communication-only settings. Depending on the operating point, a single GNN model attains approximately 97\% of each baseline's rate while serving both functionalities at once. The model further generalizes to unseen CSI error levels and clutter counts and renders the ISAC system resilient.
Deep Reinforcement Learning for BD-RIS-Assisted Multi-UAV RSMA Communications
Aamer Mohamed Huroon; Ali A. Nasir; Daniel B. da Costa

Beyond-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (BD-RISs) extend conventional diagonal RISs by allowing controllable coupling among reflecting elements. This flexibility is attractive for aerial networks, where unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) face rapidly varying channels and strict power limits. In this paper, we study a hybrid BD-RIS-assisted multi-UAV rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) downlink, in which UAVs within favourable BD-RIS coverage use both direct and BD-RIS-aided links, whereas the remaining UAVs are served through direct links only. We formulate a network sum-rate maximization problem that jointly optimizes UAV trajectories, RSMA common-rate allocation, beamforming, BD-RIS scattering matrices, and UAV-BD-RIS association. The resulting mixed-integer non-convex problem is solved by using deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm, equipped with a constraint-preserving action layer that generates reciprocal and lossless BD-RIS responses in closed form and handles the binary association inside the environment transition. Simulation results, averaged over three training seeds under a physically consistent channel model with blocked direct links near the BD-RISs, show that the proposed design attains a sum rate comparable to SAC and higher than twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient ( TD3), proximal policy optimization (PPO), and deep Q-network (DQN), exceeds per-slot alternating optimization with fixed trajectories at about 1/65 of its per-slot runtime, and benefits mainly from RSMA, while the additional BD-RIS gain is modest.
Hotplug Coded Caching: Uncoded versus Row-Wise Coded Placements

In the hotplug coded caching model, $K$ users fill their caches of size $M$ as a function of $N$ files, but only an unknown subset of $A\leq K$ users is active in the delivery phase. In all regimes where the optimal hotplug tradeoff is known, it depends only on $A$, not on $K$; whether this holds in general is open. We show that: (i) Under uncoded placement, YMA delivery with MAN placement, where offline users are assigned the demands of active users, is optimal. Hence, offline users cause a strict load penalty at intermediate memory sizes, while the MAN placement is optimal for every number of active users; (ii) Under row-wise placement (RWP), where each cache is a function of the user's own row of each file, every classical scheme can be embedded in a Reed-Solomon code. The resulting hotplug scheme has the tradeoff of the classical model with $A$ users, for every $A\leq K$: there is no load penalty, but the placement depends on $K$. We then derive a converse for RWP, which shows that: (a) for $2\leq N\leq A$, the scheme of Gomez-Vilardebo (GV) is RWP optimal for $AM\leq N/(N-1)$, which settles the RWP tradeoff for $N=2$; (b) YMA is RWP optimal at $AM=N$; and (c) for $N=A=3$, GV is RWP optimal for $M\leq 1$. Hence, the Reed-Solomon embeddings of these schemes are optimal among embedded RWP schemes.
Topological triviality of exact Lagrangian Cobordisms

Inspired by the rigidity of exact Lagrangian submanifolds, a conjecture by P.~Biran and O.~Cornea asks if a simple exact Lagrangian cobordism $W$ in a tame exact symplectic manifold is always ``symplectically trivial'' (i.e. the Lagrangian suspension of an Hamiltonian isotopy). In this short note, we prove a topological version of this conjecture~: if the cobordism has dimension at least $6$, it is always topologically trivial. This extends a previous work of Lara Suarez who reduced the question to proving an injectivity result among fundamental groups.
On Higher Order Elliptic Differential Operators

In this note we examine the positive preserving properties, or the lack thereof, for Green's operators of elliptic differential operators on smooth, closed Riemannian manifolds. We will obtain the existence of elliptic differential operators on closed manifolds whose lowest eigenvalue is not simple, and the existence of a large family of elliptic differential operators on closed manifolds that only have signed eigenfunctions associated with the lowest eigenvalue. That is, we will see that there is both "good news" and "bad news" when one studies the positivity preserving properties of Green's operators associated with higher order elliptic differential operators on smooth, closed Riemannian manifolds and the eigenproblem for higher order elliptic differential operators on smooth, closed Riemannian manifolds.
Positive integral points on Mordell-Schinzel surfaces
Antoine de Saint Germain; Robin Zhang

We apply the theory of generalised cluster algebras to classify the finiteness of positive integral points on the class of log K3 surfaces defined by $xyz = G(x,y)$ where $G$ has positive coefficients. We furthermore establish results on Zariski density, number of orbits and asymptotic growth of such points. These provide a Diophantine realisation of the finite-affine-indefinite trichotomy of rank-two root systems.
A Cooperative Game-Theoretic Framework for Real-Time Deviation Settlement in Local Energy Communities
Angel M. González-Rueda; Iago Núñez Lugilde; Jose L. Crespo-Vazquez; Tarek Alskaif

This paper proposes a cooperative game-theoretical framework for the financial settlement of real-time deviations in Community-Based Local Energy Markets (CB-LEMs). The real-time settlement process is modeled as a transferable-utility cooperative game, and the resulting Real-Time Local Energy Market (RTLEM) game is shown to be superadditive and balanced. We analyze two game-theoretical allocation mechanisms, the Shapley value and the nucleolus, and evaluate their efficiency, individual rationality, coalitional rationality, and temporal-aggregation properties. We subsequently compare these mechanisms with a settlement rule based on proportional imbalance responsibility. The three mechanisms are efficient and individually rational, but only the nucleolus is guaranteed to satisfy coalitional rationality for every RTLEM instance. The proposed framework is demonstrated using real-world data from a residential energy community in Amsterdam, showing the trade-offs among the three allocation mechanisms in terms of surplus distribution, coalitional stability, interpretability, and computational requirements.
The computational capacity of the Logistic family

Viewing computing machines as symbolic dynamical systems is a powerful idea which has led to many important results. However, the standard setting of symbolic Turing dynamics is not well suited for studying questions of typicality, genericity, or robustness. Such natural questions, for example, as "what is the computational power of a typical computer program?", "how common is poly-time computability", or "how common is universal computation among all algorithms?" require a different approach. In this paper we develop a suitable general framework of viewing families of dynamical systems as computing devices. We study a specific class of such devices given by the logistic family, and give the answers to the above questions in this setting.
Limiting properties of Hermitian-Einstein metrics under variation of the Kähler class

We study the behaviour of Hermitian-Einstein metrics on a holomorphic vector bundle over a compact Kähler manifold, as the underlying Kähler metric varies and its Kähler class changes. In particular, if the bundle stops being stable at some point, the Hermitian-Einstein metrics blow up, and their rescaling can be used to construct a destabilizing subsheaf, following the argument of Uhlenbeck and Yau. Furthermore, we study the behaviour of Chern connections of these metrics, and show, that after passing to a subsequence, and applying suitable gauge transforms these connections converge, and identify the blow-up locus of their Uhlenbeck limit.
Stochastic Homogenization of Schrödinger Equations with Exponentially Mixing Sub-Gaussian Potentials

We study the stochastic Schrödinger equation $ i\partial_t u_{\varepsilon} = H_{\varepsilon} u_{\varepsilon} $ with $ H_{\varepsilon} = -Δ+ V(x/\varepsilon) $, where V is a stationary ergodic sub-Gaussian field with exponential mixing. We establish the optimal algebraic error rate $ \varepsilon^{d/2} $ in $ L^2(Ω; L^2_x) $ for every $ d\ge1 $, prove it sharp by a matching lower bound when $ \widehat{R}(0)>0 $, and upgrade the convergence of Zhang--Bal from convergence in probability to almost sure convergence. We further establish a Gaussian fluctuation central limit theorem with explicit covariance. The limiting fluctuation satisfies $ i\partial_t \mathcal{G} = (-Δ+ \bar{V})\mathcal{G} + \sqrt{\widehat R(0)}\,\dot W(t,x) $, a linear random Schrödinger equation driven by additive space-time white noise, where $ \bar{V} = \mathbb{E}[V] $ is the effective potential.
Low-rank corrections to a shared reference Jacobian for GPU-parallel AC $N\!-\!1$ contingency analysis
Marc Hunkemöller; Nico Westerbeck; Joost van Dijk; Lars Schewe; Dirk Witthaut

Contingency analysis repeatedly solves the power-flow equations under many single-element outages, an increasingly demanding workload as operating margins tighten and renewable variability grows. Graphics processing units (GPUs) are attractive for this task, but a change in topology alters the sparsity pattern of the Jacobian, preventing the uniform batched factorization on which efficient GPU solvers rely. This paper presents a GPU-parallel Newton--Raphson solver for $N\!-\!1$ contingency analysis that separates the change in operating state from the change in topology. A single reference Jacobian is inverted once and reused across all contingencies. Each topology change is expressed as a low-rank Woodbury correction, while the residual state-dependent perturbation is handled by an inner iterative solve, a truncated Neumann series or the biconjugate gradient stabilized method. We analyze the spectral radius and condition number of the resulting iteration matrices and show that the reference Jacobian is an effective preconditioner. On transmission-scale benchmarks, the method attains per-topology solve times competitive with an optimized 80-core central processing unit baseline, with the low-rank correction accounting for approximately 1--2\% of the workload. This makes GPU-parallel $N\!-\!1$ contingency analysis feasible at transmission scale without per-topology refactorization.
Strong Borel-Cantelli laws and clusters of visits for random intermittent maps

Near the neutral fixed point of an intermittent map, a single entrance into a small target can be followed by a long run of consecutive visits, so the number of visits need not follow its mean. We study targets $[0,u_n]$ for iid random compositions of Liverani-Saussol-Vaienti maps with a bounded parameter law that is regularly varying at its minimum $α\in(0,1)$; this includes a single map. For $u_n=cn^{-g}L(n)$, where $c>0$, $0<g\leq1$ and $L$ is slowly varying, the visit count is almost surely asymptotic to its mean if and only if $\sum_n n^{-1}(nu_n)^{-(1-α)/α}<\infty$. Under the stationary law, the count divided by its mean converges to one in $L^1$ exactly when $nu_n\to\infty$. Thus clusters of visits separate these two modes of convergence.
Fluid Antenna Array-Enabled Near-Field ISAC: Joint Port Position Optimization and Transmit Beamforming Design
Wangqi Shi; Zhentian Zhang; Hao Jiang; Zaichen Zhang; Kin-Fai Tong

Fluid antenna systems (FASs) have shown that activating a single port from a densely packed antenna array can yield spatial diversity comparable to that of tens of independent antennas, a property that has substantially improved communication reliability and efficiency. The fluid antenna array (FAA) extends this concept to multi-port configurations while avoiding complex multi-dimensional spatial correlation, and offers significant geometrical flexibility under a finite aperture and a limited port budget. These attributes motivate environment-adaptive array geometry for sensing in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. Although this flexibility enables adaptive array geometries that exploit near-field distance-angle information, improving multi-parameter target estimation under communication and deployment constraints remains challenging. In this paper, we propose a planar FAA-assisted near-field ISAC framework for multiuser communication and target sensing. Specifically, we derive the Fisher information matrix (FIM) and the corresponding Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) for the joint estimation of target range, zenith angle, azimuth angle, and radial velocity. Based on the derived CRB, we jointly optimize the FAA port positions and transmit beamforming to improve sensing accuracy while satisfying communication signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR), transmit power, and physical deployment constraints. To solve the resulting non-convex problem, we develop a two-stage alternating optimization algorithm, in which transmit beamforming is optimized through semidefinite relaxation (SDR), while FAA port positions are successively optimized through discrete search and continuous refinement. Simulation results indicate that the proposed algorithm achieves favorable sensing performance while maintaining a reasonable computational cost.
Local limit Theorem for Directed polymers in a random environment in the full weak disorder regime

For directed polymers in random environment, we provide a short and mostly self-contained proof of the local limit theorem in the full weak disorder phase, including the critical inverse temperature $β_c$. That is, the point-to-point partition function is well approximated by the product of two independent point-to-line partition functions (one starting from each endpoint of the system) multiplied by the simple random walk transition kernel. The approximation is valid in the $L^p$ sense for an optimal range of $p$. The result is new at $β=β_c$ and for $p>2$, and in all cases the proof is significantly simpler, technically and conceptually, than what can be found in the literature. As a consequence of the result we establish an invariance principle for the polymer measure with fixed end-point, valid for all $β\in [0,β_c]$.
Computational performance versus numerical accuracy in the acoustic terms of weakly-compressible SPH
Giuseppe Bilotta; Alireza Zarei; Roberta Cristofaro; Alexis Hérault; Élie Saikali; Morteza Derakhti

Accurate computation of the acoustic terms in weakly-compressible SPH, including the equation of state, its inverse, and the evaluation of the local speed of sound, is essential to ensure energy conservation, robust solid boundary conditions, and correct open boundary behavior. In the classic Cole's equation of state, using values of the polytropic constant $γ\ne 1$ can lead to significant precision loss, particularly when computations are performed in single precision, as is common in GPU implementations. We extend here our previous results on the optimal choice of state variable by introducing a new higher-precision form for all three acoustic terms, denoted \texttt{explog}, and assess its numerical accuracy and computational performance across a variety of devices and test cases. We find that the new form evaluates the acoustic terms with a maximum ULP of~2 for arguments less than $0.125$, and has higher errors in less than 1\% of the arguments larger than the threshold. Combined with a rewritten expression of the pressure at solid boundary particles in the ``dummy'' model, it provides consistently more accurate results, maintaining deviations from the reference pressure profile to below 2\%, even in presence of a rough bottom terrain. Computationally, the new formulation is also faster than the naive one on GPU, and only marginally slower on CPU.
Fischer-Burmeister-based Multiplier Dynamics in Inequality-Constrained Optimization

We study proportional-integral multiplier feedback for inequality-constrained optimization using the Fischer-Burmeister complementarity residual. We construct explicit dynamics and characterize gain-dependent stability and convergence rates. For a single active constraint, we derive exact local stability and decay-rate conditions, including a tradeoff between continuous-time convergence and discretization costs. For strongly convex objectives with affine constraints, we establish global convergence and characterize geometric conditions for uniform exponential stability. Numerical experiments compare feedback structures and computational costs.
On local spectra of classical distance-regular graphs with $b = 2$

Using a combination of spectral techniques and combinatorial counts, we prove a number of non-existence results for putative distance-regular graphs with classical parameters, focusing on the case $b=2$. Among those, the case $(d,b,α,β)=(d,2,1,2^d-2)$ passed all known feasibility conditions and required a deeper combinatorial analysis, from which nonexistence has been derived whenever $d \ge 9$. In doing so, we constructed a new family of regular graphs with four distinct eigenvalues which would have been local graphs in such a distance-regular graph.
Symmetry, uniqueness and nondegeneracy of positive solutions of the Choquard equation
Song Fan; Gui-Dong Li; Jianjun Zhang

We study positive solutions \(Q\in H^1(\mathbb R^N)\) of \[-ΔQ+Q=(I_α*Q^p)Q^{p-1},\] where \(I_α\) is the Riesz potential of order \(α\), \(N\ge1\), \(0<α<N\), \(p>1+α/N\), and \((N-2)p<N+α\). We prove that every such solution is radially symmetric and strictly decreasing about some point. For \(p\ge2\), we establish uniqueness up to translations and show that the real linearized operator has Morse index one and kernel spanned by \(\partial_1Q,\ldots,\partial_NQ\). The symmetry proof uses the method of moving planes. Uniqueness follows from nondegeneracy and compactness through a continuation argument.
Information Limits for Stable Reduction of Coupled Diffusion Systems

Eliminating an unresolved diffusion field from a coupled parabolic system produces an operator-valued memory term and a contribution from the hidden initial state. We study whether a reduced prediction of the retained field meets a prescribed tolerance. For known hidden initial data, the discarded response, damped by diffusion and transmitted through the coupling, gives an upper error bound; an auxiliary diffusion problem supplies a lower bound. Rigorous discretisation bounds then yield tests that accept, reject or remain undecided. If the discarded initial state is known only through a norm bound, the minimum worst-case error equals that bound multiplied by the time-uniform gain from the missing state to the retained trajectory. Our main result encloses this infinite-dimensional gain using a finite spectral Galerkin evolution, its residual in the full equations and an explicit diffusion tail. The enclosure converges without compactness or smallness of the coupling. Strict comparisons of the optimal radius with a tolerance have finite certificates if all endpoint quantities admit arbitrarily accurate rigorous enclosures. Multiplication-coupling examples with infinitely many dynamically coupled modes illustrate both settings, including explicit finite-element error budgets.
Propositional Dynamic Logic with Program Costs

We introduce $\mathbb{N}\mathtt{PDL}$, a resource-aware variant of Propositional Dynamic Logic ($\mathtt{PDL}$) capable of accounting for program costs measured by natural numbers (such as time or space in the sense of computability theory). In this framework, programs correspond to transition systems weighted by extended natural numbers, and the syntax of our logic includes formulas expressing which properties are reachable by program executions within specific cost constraints. First, we explain how the standard program constructs of non-deterministic choice, sequential composition, iteration, and tests are interpreted in this weighted setting and establish the validity of their corresponding reduction axioms. Using an appropriate adaptation of the (Fischer-Ladner) filtration technique, we proceed to prove decidability and completeness for $\mathbb{N}\mathtt{PDL}$ as our main results. We furthermore provide upper and lower complexity bounds for this logic using translations between standard $\mathtt{PDL}$ and $\mathbb{N}\mathtt{PDL}$.
On blow-up for the cut-off Boltzmann equation with very hard potentials
Ning Jiang; Feng Shao; Dongyi Wei; Zhifei Zhang; Kai Zhou

We construct smooth, strictly positive solutions of the three-dimensional cut-off Boltzmann equation with very hard potentials whose densities become unbounded in finite time. A main ingredient is a new velocity weight that is Gaussian on a ball and has a polynomial tail of fixed order. We establish coercive estimates for the linearized collision operator and bilinear estimates for the collision term, with constants independent of the radius of the Gaussian region. Combining these weighted estimates with an imploding solution of the compressible Euler equations, we develop an energy framework that controls the Boltzmann solution up to the blow-up time. The initial data agree with a constant Maxwellian outside a bounded spatial region and have finite relative entropy.
Operator Fejér--Riesz Theorems with Gaps and Degree Bounds

Let $K$ be a nonempty compact semialgebraic subset of the real line, and let $S$ be a saturated scalar description of $K$. We prove that every hermitian polynomial with bounded-operator coefficients that is positive semidefinite on $K$ belongs to the operator quadratic module generated by $S$. We also show that if such a polynomial has degree at most $\tt{d}$, then it admits a certificate of weighted degree at most $\tt{d}+c_S$, where $c_S$ depends only on $S$, not on the polynomial or the coefficient Hilbert space. In contrast to the scalar case, where natural preorderings admit the degree bound $\tt{d}$ independently of $K$, we show that no uniform additive constant exists for natural matrix preorderings. We construct quadratic $2\times2$ matrix polynomials positive semidefinite on unions of two intervals whose minimum certificate degrees in the corresponding natural preorderings diverge as one interval shrinks to a point, while the gap length remains bounded below. Conversely, we establish uniform bounds of the form $\tt{d}+C$ for families of interval unions contained in a fixed compact interval when interval lengths and gap lengths have uniform positive lower bounds. Our proofs develop two techniques that may be of independent interest. First, a quadratic reduction principle represents arbitrary-degree operator polynomials as compressions of quadratic ones on enlarged Hilbert spaces. A perturbation argument and the closedness of truncated operator quadratic modules then extend uniform degree bounds from the quadratic case to arbitrary degrees with linear degree bounds of slope $1$. Second, a rank-one symmetric matrix pencil transfers positivity on interval unions to $[0,1]$, where the operator Fejér--Riesz theorem yields certificates.
Full-Rank Constructions of Explicit Lossless Expanders and Good Small-Set qLTCs
Yali Aharon-Holzman; Michael Ilan; Assaf Reiner; Amnon Ta-Shma

We construct explicit two-sided lossless expanders whose binary adjacency matrices have full rank, and use them to obtain explicit asymptotically good quantum LDPC codes whose specified X- and Z-check matrices have full row rank and satisfy small-set soundness, or confinement, on a linear range. Our lossless expanders are a variant of those of Hsieh, Lubotzky, Mohanty, Reiner, and Zhang, with a free action of a finite 2-group. Under such an action, injectivity and surjectivity of the adjacency matrix are detected on a fixed-size matrix indexed by vertex orbits. Adding a sparse factor to the gadget at the middle vertices of a single type then enforces full rank, with a controlled loss in expansion. To obtain the 2-group action, we observe that reducing the generators of the Lubotzky-Phillips-Sarnak Ramanujan graphs modulo powers of 2, instead of modulo an odd prime, gives Ramanujan Cayley graphs on finite 2-groups. This construction may be of independent interest. Plugging two such expanders into the balanced product of Lin and Hsieh gives the quantum codes, since full rank of the input graphs is inherited by the check matrices. Our construction supplies the code family sought by Hong, Guo, and Lucas. Applying their analysis, within their framework and under their dynamical assumptions, gives quantum memories whose free-energy density is analytic at every positive temperature and whose guaranteed lifetime is $exp(Ω(N))$ at sufficiently low fixed positive temperature, where N is the blocklength. This improves the previously guaranteed stretched-exponential timescale.
High-order fractional linear differential equations do not describe stochastic processes with finite state space

The replacement of the classical derivative in the governing equation of a continuous-time Markov process with finite state space by a fractional derivative of arbitrary order $α>1$ produces solutions that are mathematically incompatible with the theory of stochastic processes.

In receding-horizon games, self-interested players repeatedly solve a finite-horizon generalized Nash equilibrium problem (GNEP) and apply its first-stage actions. Ensuring stability of the resulting closed-loop system, however, is a challenging task that requires careful design of the players' strategies or additional constraints. We propose a stability filter that minimally modifies the variational equilibrium of the finite-horizon GNEP to enforce a prescribed decrease of a quadratic Lyapunov function. For receding-horizon games with linear dynamics, quadratic costs, and polyhedral coupling input constraints, whose associated GNEP is strongly monotone, we show that a filter always exists such that a closed-loop equilibrium exists, the filter is always feasible, does not intervene when the equilibrium already satisfies the decrease condition, and that renders the closed loop globally exponentially stable. Moreover, the filtered strategy is an $ε$-generalized Nash equilibrium, with $epsilon$ vanishing exponentially along closed-loop trajectories.
Corona and Gleason problems for certain Banach spaces of holomorphic functions

We use a combination of the classical dead-end space method and the interpolation (by bounded holomorphic functions) method to affirmatively solve Corona and Gleason problems for familiar Banach spaces of holomorphic functions such as (Besov-)Lipschitz spaces of holomorphic functions on bounded symmetric domains (including the unit ball and polydisc) in $\mathbb{C}^n$, holomorphic mean (Besov-)Lipschitz spaces, (Besov-)Hardy-Sobolev spaces and some special classes of holomorphic mixed-norm (Bergman) spaces (including weighted Bergman spaces) as well as some special classes of holomorphic (mean) Besov-Lipschitz spaces on the unit ball in $\mathbb{C}^n$. Indeed, we extend our recent work on both problems for holomorphic Lipschitz algebras.
Efficient Numerical Evaluation of Arbitrary High-order Partial Derivatives via Algebraic Decomposition

Computing high-order partial derivatives of multivariate functions is often computationally and memory intensive. This paper addresses this problem via an algebraic approach. High-order partial derivatives of a multivariate function are expressed as linear combinations of univariate directional derivatives, which are computationally friendly. The coefficients and direction vectors are determined by the Waring decomposition of monomials, so that the number of univariate directional derivatives in the representation is minimized. Numerical experiments confirm the efficiency of the proposed method.
On some positivity properties of the Riemann $Ξ$ function

We prove strict log-concavity of the positive functions $Θ$ and $Λ$ with one-sided and bilateral Laplace transforms $1/ξ(\tfrac12+\sqrt s)$ and $1/Ξ$, respectively, where $Ξ(z)=ξ(\tfrac12+iz)$. For either function, log-concavity is the Pólya frequency property of order two (PF$_2$). Without assuming the Riemann hypothesis (RH), but using its published verification up to height about $3\cdot10^{12}$, we further prove that both densities are PF$_{k_*}$ for $k_*=1\,810\,540\,931\,075$. The proof views $Θ$ as a small signed perturbation of a density that is PF of every order, with an error bound independent of the order, so the numerical check reduces to scalar inequalities. Since $Λ$ is a Gaussian mixture of $Θ$, it inherits the same order. Conversely, a pole obstruction shows that if either density is PF$_k$, then every zeta zero lower than the $(k+2)$-nd lies on the critical line. Finally, we prove that if RH holds up to height $T>\tfrac12$, then $Ξ$ satisfies the generalized Laguerre inequalities $L_n[Ξ](x)\ge0$ of every order $n$ for $|x|\le T-\tfrac12$, extending the case $n=1$ of Csordas, Ruttan and Varga (1991).
Frank-Wolfe is Approximate Broximal Gradient Descent

We show that the Frank-Wolfe method is an approximation of Broximal Gradient Descent (BroxGD), and hence of the ball-proximal method. For constrained minimization, the ball-proximal method minimizes the objective over the intersection of the feasible set with a ball around the current iterate. Linearizing the objective gives BroxGD, but the intersection can remain difficult to handle even when linear minimization over the feasible set alone is cheap. We therefore replace the intersection by a smaller copy of the feasible set, obtained by shrinking it toward the current iterate so that it lies inside the ball. Minimizing the linear model over this smaller set gives exactly Frank-Wolfe, with the shrinking factor as its step size. We examine what this approximation preserves and what it can lose. For smooth convex objectives on compact convex sets, Frank-Wolfe retains a linear-model decrease guarantee that gives it and BroxGD a common convergence proof, recovering the classical $O(1/k)$ bound. Among compact convex regions inside the ball chosen before the gradient is known, the smaller copy is the smallest that preserves the same linear-model decrease guarantee. Nevertheless, Frank-Wolfe can achieve much less linear-model decrease than BroxGD at the same radius. A simplex example illustrates the sparsity gained by restricting the region, while a family of triangles shows how Frank-Wolfe can lose the distance decrease guaranteed by BroxGD. We also give a computable test for recovering the distance guarantee and a refinement procedure that terminates after finitely many oracle calls on polytopes.

We study singularities of separation coordinates for geodesic flows of real-analytic two-dimensional (pseudo-)Riemannian metrics. We obtain a complete local classification of these singularities using the Nijenhuis operator associated with a quadratic first integral. The singular set is locally a smooth curve, an isolated point, or two transversely intersecting curves. We also show that orthogonal separation near one point of an analytic disk extends to a quadratic first integral on the entire disk and provide explicit separation coordinates near singularities.

We study real zeros of completed modular L-functions and the determination of cusp forms by their periods. Using Chebyshev systems and the Riemann-Roch theorem, we obtain bounds for real zeros, counted with multiplicity, and rank estimates for evaluation maps in terms of the dimensions of cusp-form spaces and the genera of modular curves. These estimates give criteria for finite families of periods to determine a cusp form and yield explicit dual bases in cases where the relevant quotient curves have genus zero. We also bound the dimensions of rational spans of eigenform periods.
Buildings governed by twisted Bruhat orders

This paper introduces the notion of a twisted building associated to a Coxeter system and an initial section of a reflection order. These are pairs of buildings and a map between them which depends on a twisted Bruhat order. It is proved that projection maps exist between components and that the common apartment property holds for a suitable notion of an apartment, generalising what is known for twin buildings. Several well-known examples are given, including a family of twisted buildings associated to an affine building and its façades.
Periodic KPP equations in hyperbolic space

We study Fisher-KPP equations on hyperbolic space with reactions periodic in a Busemann coordinate or in the distance from a point or a geodesic. We determine spectral thresholds for extinction and persistence, including critical extinction from $L^2$ data, and characterize the signed speeds of horospherical fronts. In the hyperbolic plane, we construct a smooth periodic reaction admitting a positive stationary solution that decays away from a geodesic, and determine the spreading speed along the geodesic. For constant linear growth, we obtain logarithmic level positions with bounded error for balls, horoballs and geodesic tubes.
Resolution Is Not Accessibility: Coupled Minimax Risk for Reduced Statistical Experiments
Yuzhao Zhu; Jiahui Shao; Dongqi Liu; Xiaoxiao Hu

A reduced experiment can have vanishing minimax risk yet lose arbitrarily much precision relative to full observation. We determine when growing reductions preserve target-specific minimax precision, their exact cost, and which omissions can remain without increasing that cost. For Gaussian sequence reductions, we give necessary and sufficient criteria for bounded relative risk and losslessness. With parameter-dependent information, sampling difficulty and unresolved target variation draw on the same parameter budget. We prove that the exact global asymptotic minimax risk is the maximum scalar interval-decision risk over their jointly attainable frontier under a Sobolev constraint. This identity shows that positive ambiguity at the inverse-square-root sample-size scale can preserve the full-observation minimax constant. Under the corresponding full-experiment risk match, a sharp boundary criterion determines when critical-order resolution suffices for losslessness. A quadratic Poisson budget yields an exact threshold and quadratic risk onset under a stated information condition. Across Poisson power budgets, separate-maxima planning incurs a diverging asymptotic coordinate-budget factor near full precision, both with a positive lossless threshold and with zero threshold but higher-order risk onset. Finite-sample calculations and conditional medical-data and classifier audits distinguish the effects of observation coverage and repeated measurement.

We revisit the classical Siegel-Shidlovskii method in transcendental number theory from a new perspective, in which functional relations play a central role. Within a single self-contained framework, we recover the foundational results in the theory of E-functions, including the Siegel-Shidlovskii theorem, Beukers' lifting theorem, and Andr{é}'s theorem on the singularities of the minimal differential operator annihilating an E-function. Notably, the latter is obtained without any recourse to the theory of Gfunctions. This unified approach also allows us to resolve a problem posed by Shidlovskii: we obtain a general algebraic independence measure extending the classical Siegel-Lang measure to an arbitrary algebraically independent family of E-values. We also provide a short elementary proof of a second theorem of Andr{é}, which has become an important tool in the theory of Efunctions and concerns the primality of the specialization, at a regular point, of the ideal of functional relations of a vector of E-functions satisfying a differential system.
Representations of Bound Quivers over $\mathbb{F}_1$ and Hall Algebras

Representations of quivers over the virtual field $\mathbb{F}_1$ can be naturally extended to bound quivers with monomial and commutativity relations. In this paper, we introduce and study the Hall algebra $\mathcal{H}_{\mathbb{F}_1}(Q,I)$ for a bound quiver $(Q,I)$ equipped with such relations. As in the quiver setting, $\mathcal{H}_{\mathbb{F}_1}(Q,I)$ is a graded, connected, and cocommutative bialgebra, and the free subgroup generated by all indecomposable representations forms a Lie subalgebra. We study $\mathcal{H}_{\mathbb{F}_1}(Q,I)$ in detail for two special classes of bound quivers: Nakayama bound quivers and gentle one-cycle bound quivers. In both cases, we prove that for any triple $L, M, N$ of $\mathbb{F}_1$-representations over $(Q,I)$, the Hall number $g_{N,L}^M$ coincides with the evaluation of the corresponding Hall polynomial $ϕ_{N,L}^M(t)$ at $t=1$. Consequently, there exists a canonical isomorphism between $\mathcal{H}_{\mathbb{F}_1}(Q,I)$ and the degenerate Hall algebra $\mathcal{H}_1(Q,I)$, justifying Tits's $\mathbb{F}_1$-philosophy in these settings.
Antidiagonal and square averages for amenable groups

We prove that, for commuting unitary representations $U,V$ of a countable amenable group $G$, the averages $$ D_F=\frac1{|F|}\sum_{g\in F}U_g^*V_g $$ have a common selfadjoint weak operator limit along all left and right \Folner{} sequences, with strong* convergence along two-sided sequences. This answers Bergelson's question on commuting actions. For any unitary representation $π$, we also prove that $A_F=|F|^{-1}\sum_{g\in F}π(g^2)$ converges strongly along right \Folner{} sequences to a selfadjoint central operator supported on the finite type~I part of $π(G)''$; the adjoints $A_F^*$ converge strongly along left \Folner{} sequences. This settles the convergence question for square averages posed by Bergelson and Rodríguez-Martín. For measure-preserving actions of finitely generated amenable or countable virtually FC groups, we obtain $$ \lim_n\frac1{|F_n|}\sum_{g\in F_n}μ(A\cap T_{g^2}A)>0 \qquad\text{whenever }μ(A)>0. $$ For each $\varepsilon>0$, the set $\{g:μ(A\cap T_{g^2}A)>μ(A)^2-\varepsilon\}$ meets every Bohr neighborhood of the identity in a set of positive lower density, uniformly over \Folner{} sequences. These intersections are also left and right IP$^*$ for virtually FC groups. We construct a unitary representation $π$ of a locally finite nilpotent group and a weakly mixing vector $f$ for which $\{g:\text{Re}\langleπ(g^2)f,f\rangle>-\varepsilon\}$ has upper Banach density zero for small $\varepsilon>0$. We also give a weakly mixing action of a two-generated solvable group for which the IP$^*$ conclusion fails. The recurrence results yield product sets $BB$ inside difference sets, with $B$ of positive upper density.
Customizing Wireless Channels via Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces: Feasibility, Fundamental Limits, and Constructive Design
Xiyuan Liu; Qingqing Wu; Guangji Chen; Yuxuan Chen; Wen Chen

By adjusting their reflection coefficients, intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRSs) can reshape the channels between a base station (BS) and user equipment (UE). Existing studies mainly optimize IRS phase-shifts for communication objectives, leaving the physical attainability of prescribed IRS-reflected channels largely unexplored. This paper investigates channel customization with a phase-only IRS under three progressively relaxed criteria. Observing that the customization mean-squared error (MSE) has the same mathematical form as the signal MSE of a point-to-point multiple-input multiple-output system, we construct a counterpart problem to characterize individual singular-coordinate gain limits and the condition for attaining the amplitude-matching upper bound. To address multi-stream phase conflicts, we analyze principal contribution area (PCA) overlap and derive sufficient array-size conditions for disjoint PCAs under a specified focused-vector construction with parallel uniform linear arrays. We also derive necessary conditions from the two propagation links' singular values and an array-size restriction under the parallel-array Fresnel model. Both the restriction and the construction involve the BS--IRS array-size product. Numerical results show that jointly selecting right singular vectors and IRS phase-shifts reduces mean customization MSE, whereas gains exceeding propagation spectral limits cannot be realized exactly. These results provide design guidance and highlight spectral limits of phase-only IRS channel customization.
Uniqueness and shape of simplex ground states for aggregation--diffusion energies with mild repulsion

We study global minimizers in $\mathbb{R}^d$ of the free energy $\mathcal{E}_κ=\mathcal{W}+κ\mathcal{U}$, where $\mathcal{W}$ is a power-law interaction energy with mild repulsion and $\mathcal{U}$ is the porous-medium internal energy with exponent $m>1$. In a range of exponents that we call the strict simplex regime, results of Lim--McCann and Davies--Lim--McCann show that $\mathcal{W}$ is minimized, uniquely up to rigid motions, by equal point masses at the vertices of a regular unit $d$-simplex. Diffusion excludes such atomic minimizers for every $κ>0$. We prove that uniqueness nevertheless persists: for every fixed $m>1$ and all sufficiently small $κ>0$, the free energy has a unique global minimizer up to rigid motions. After a suitable rigid motion, this minimizer is invariant under every symmetry of the simplex, and its support splits into $d+1$ clusters near the vertices, each of mass exactly $1/(d+1)$; in particular, it is not radially symmetric when $d\geq2$. The clusters have width of order $κ^{1/(d(m-1)+2)}$, which is also the exact order of the quadratic Wasserstein distance from the minimizer to the atomic simplex measure. Rescaled at this scale, the clusters converge in $L^1$ and $L^\infty$ to explicit Barenblatt-type profiles supported on ellipsoids determined by the Hessian of the simplex potential. For $d\geq2$ these ellipsoids are spheroids flattened along the directions of the vertices; when the repulsive exponent exceeds two, their aspect ratio equals $(d+1)^{-1/2}$, independently of all other parameters. At the endpoint $(4,2)$ of this regime in dimensions $d\geq2$, where the zero-diffusion minimizer is not unique, we show instead that vanishing diffusion selects the uniform spherical shell.
A Universal Policy Wrapper With Guarantees
Georgiy Malaniya; Anton Bolychev; Pavel Osinenko

Many control tasks require driving the system into a prescribed goal set and subsequently keeping it there. The considered setting assumes that a working controller is available that provably reaches and maintains the goal, albeit with suboptimal performance. This controller is referred to as the fallback policy. Conversely, although state-of-the-art reinforcement-learning (RL) algorithms can discover policies with impressive empirical performance, the neural networks at their core act as opaque black boxes learned through data-driven exploration and, as such, provide no theoretical mechanism to guarantee that the system will ever reach---and stay within---the prescribed goal set. This article presents CALF-Wrapper, a method that combines the fallback policy with a pretrained RL base policy and uses the critic estimate associated with the base policy to select between them during deployment. The theoretical analysis establishes that CALF-Wrapper inherits the goal-reaching property of the fallback policy under the stated assumptions and provides probability bounds for the settling time and the maximum distance from the goal set over a prescribed time interval. The experimental study evaluates CALF-Wrapper in four simulated control environments of different complexity. Comparisons include the base policy, fallback policy, and constrained reinforcement-learning methods formulated for the same objective. Sensitivity and ablation studies provide direct hyperparameter recommendations. The experiments show how CALF-Wrapper can provide effective task performance while attaining the maximum possible observed goal-reaching rate. CALF-Wrapper requires no additional dynamics model, online learning, or constrained optimization during execution.
Fundamental solutions to Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck equations with unbounded lower order terms

We continue the study of fundamental solutions for equations involving Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck operators with rough local or non-local diffusions. Here we consider possibly unbounded lower order terms, such as drifts and potentials. We prove existence and uniqueness of weak solutions and of an appropriate notion of fundamental solution for a wide class of kinetic equations. This is based on kinetic transfer of regularity and anisotropic embeddings.
Stability and exact extremal colourings for the Alon--Frankl--Lovász bound
Tianhong Kan; Hongliang Lu; Feihong Yuan

The Alon--Frankl--Lovász theorem states that every $q$-colouring of the edges of the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices contains a monochromatic matching of size $\lfloor(n+q-1)/(r+q-1)\rfloor$. For fixed uniformity $r$ and number of colours $q$, we prove a stability theorem: every colouring whose largest monochromatic matching has size at most $n/(r+q-1)+o(n)$ differs from a threshold extremal colouring on only $o(n^r)$ edges. We also give a necessary and sufficient structural characterization of all extremal colourings for sufficiently large $n$. The proofs combine rigidity of fractional covering weights with an extension argument for prescribed matchings. These results answer, for sufficiently large orders, the stability and extremal-colouring questions posed by Gishboliner, Glock, Michaeli and Sgueglia.
A Reilly approach to weighted curvature integral inequalities in hyperbolic space

We establish a polarized weighted Reilly identity and an exact deficit decomposition for weighted curvature integrals $I_j=\int_ΣVE_j~\mathrm{d}μ$ in hyperbolic space, where $V=\cosh r$ and $E_j$ is the normalized $j$th mean curvature. For compact domains with smooth connected boundary, these yield $I_k^2\geq I_{k-1}I_{k+1}$ under intrinsic sub-staticity at $k=1$ and static convexity with $κ\inΓ_k\cap\overlineΓ_{k+1}$ for $2\leq k\leq n-1$, with equality precisely for geodesic balls. Under $h\geq0$ and $Vh-V_νg\geq0$, log-concavity and a Euclidean mixed-volume representation recover the centered-ball comparisons conjectured by Hu and Li \cite[Conjecture~1.1]{HuLi}, allowing the weight center to lie outside the domain. Equality in these comparisons holds precisely for balls centered at the weight center.
Optimal L^2 Error Estimates for CSLDG Ideal Numerical Solutions in Time-Dependent Compressible Periodic Flows

We study the characteristic Galerkin-type semi-Lagrangian discontinuous finite element (CSLDG) method for conservative linear transport equations. When the characteristic maps and upstream regions are exact, each update of the ideal CSLDG scheme is equivalent to exact conservative transport of the current numerical solution followed by L^2 projection onto the background DG space. The conventional estimate obtained by accumulating projection errors over successive time steps loses one order when Δt\asymp h, but this loss does not represent the actual accuracy of the scheme. For smooth velocity fields \A(\x,t) on a common periodic lattice, we construct local correctors used only in the analysis on uniform Cartesian meshes, assuming that Δt/h is fixed and that every component of the local Courant vector remains uniformly separated from the integers throughout the space-time domain. We prove strict contraction of the reference-cell transport-projection operator on the zero-mean polynomial space, establish uniform solvability of the corrector equation and Lipschitz estimates with respect to its parameter, and control the difference between the exact flow map and a local frozen translation through weak integral moments. This yields a one-step residual of order O(h^{K+2}), and, while retaining the step-by-step update and the standard L^2-projected initial data, gives, for the P^K approximation, an optimal O(h^{K+1}) error bound. The velocity may depend on both space and time, and incompressibility is not required. An appendix extends the analysis to a compact-support setting, in which the velocity field and the solution need not share a common spatial period.
Pollutant Concentration Reconstruction in Porous Media from Localized Measurements
Adel Blouza; Siyu Cen; Yavar Kian

Reliable environmental monitoring and groundwater protection heavily rely on the ability to reconstruct full pollutant concentration fields from sparse, partial field measurements. In porous media, dissolved contaminants are transported by groundwater flow while undergoing hydrodynamic dispersion and complex chemical or biological reactions. To address practical contamination challenges, this work investigates the reconstruction of pollutant distributions using water samples collected at discrete locations in unsaturated or saturated soils via sampling tubes equipped with ceramic tips. While these suction samplers provide critical local data, they inherently capture only a fraction of the subsurface environment, leaving wide areas unmonitored. Motivated by this real-world monitoring procedure, we propose steady and time-dependent advection-diffusion-reaction models to simulate contaminant transport. Our main contribution is a generalized unique continuation result demonstrating that, under appropriate physical and mathematical assumptions, two concentration fields coinciding on a non-empty observation region must match throughout the entire space-time domain, even when originating from different source configurations. We investigate this problem from both theoretical and numerical perspectives, backing our mathematical uniqueness results with numerical simulations that validate the efficiency and practical utility of our approach. The theoretical proofs combine regularity properties away from source singularities with unique-continuation principles for parabolic and elliptic partial differential equations, providing a robust framework for environmental risk assessment and site remediation.
McKean-Vlasov flights without moments: well-posedness, propagation of chaos and a critical threshold for law-dependent jumps

We study McKean-Vlasov equations driven by an isotropic $2s$-stable L{é}vy noise, $s\in(0,1)$, whose solutions may have no finite mean, with coefficients that are Lipschitz with respect to a bounded Wasserstein-type distance. When the jump noise is additive, we prove strong well-posedness for every initial law and every $s$, without any moment assumption, and propagation of chaos at the rate $N^{-1/2}$ for kernel interactions. When the size of the jumps depends on the law, we prove the same results for $s>1/2$, and we show by an example that uniqueness fails for every $s<1/2$. The value $s=1/2$ thus separates well-posedness from non-uniqueness; the critical case itself remains open. These results answer, for stable noise, the question of uniqueness without moments raised by Jourdain, M{é}l{é}ard and Woyczy{ń}ski and by Cavallazzi.
Density and distribution of quotients associated with Goldring's $w$-function

For primes $p,q,r$ that are not all equal, let $n=pqr$ and define Goldring's $w$-function by $w(n)=P(p+q)P(p+r)P(q+r)$, where $P(a)$ denotes the largest prime factor of $a$. In this paper, we resolve three problems of Chen, Shi and Wu. As $n\to\infty$ through such products, the sets of finite limit points of $P(w(n))/P(n)$ and $w(n)/n$ are $[0,1]$ and $[0,\infty)$, respectively. The same conclusions hold when $n$ is restricted either to $p^2q$ with distinct primes $p,q$ or to squarefree products of three primes. Nevertheless, on each of these three sets, the proportion of integers $n\le X$ satisfying $P(w(n))/P(n)>α$ tends to zero as $X\to\infty$, for every fixed $α>0$. We also determine the complete set of finite joint limit points of the two quotients for $n=p^2q$ with $p\ne q$.
Quasimorphisms and bounded cohomology of transformation groups of nonorientable surfaces

Let $N_g$ be a closed connected nonorientable surface of genus $g\ge1$, let $ω$ be a smooth positive density, and let $μ$ be a good measure. In this paper we generalize the Gambaudo--Ghys construction using homogeneous quasimorphisms on the central quotients of the braid groups of $N_g$. We prove injectivity of this map for density-preserving diffeomorphisms. For $g\ge2$ and quasimorphisms vanishing on the disc braid group, we obtain an injective map to $C^0$-continuous homogeneous quasimorphisms on $Homeo_0(N_g,μ)$. We also obtain undistortion criteria in $Homeo_0(N_g)$ and $Diff_0(N_g)$. For $g=1,2$ and every $d\ge2$, we prove $$ \dim\overline H_b^d(Homeo_0(N_g,μ))=\infty,\qquad \dim\overline{EH}_b^d(Diff_0(N_g,ω))=\infty. $$ Moreover, $\overline{EH}_b^d(Homeo_0(N_2,μ))$ is infinite dimensional in every positive even degree $d$. Here $\overline{H}_b^d$ and $\overline{EH}_b^d$ denote reduced bounded cohomology and reduced exact bounded cohomology, respectively.
Characterization of the boundary zero set of stable polynomials in $\mathbb B_2$

Given a polynomial $p\in \mathbb{C}[z,w]$ whose zeros lie outside the unit ball $\mathbb{B}_2$ of $\mathbb{C}^2,$ we study its local Weierstrass polynomial--obtained via the Weierstrass Preparation Theorem--and provide a strong version of the Nash curve selection lemma. These results lead to a characterization of the intersection of the zero set of $p$ with the unit sphere: $\mathcal{Z}(p)\cap\mathbb{S}_{2}.$
Compressed Multiscale Kernel Collocation and Physics-Informed Kernel Learning for Elliptic BVPs
Sara Avesani; Manel Babay; Angela Kunoth; Michael Multerer

Kernel collocation is a meshfree method for partial differential equations whose accuracy depends on the smoothness of the kernel and of the solution. For globally supported kernels, however, the collocation matrices are dense and severely ill-conditioned. We address both issues by combining a multiscale collocation scheme with samplets, a multiresolution basis of discrete signed measures with vanishing moments. In the samplet basis, the collocation matrix has only O(N log N) relevant entries, while the multiscale scheme adapts the kernel width to the spacing of the points on every level. Since the differential operator scales the equations at the interior points differently from those at the boundary points, the rescaling alone does not bound the condition number of the level systems. We therefore solve them by a Schur-complement reduction that is invariant under this scaling. For noisy data, we consider physics-informed kernel learning, which replaces the collocation system by a regularized least-squares fit. We show that it reduces to collocation as the regularization vanishes, and we solve it by a deflated conjugate gradient method that reuses the Schur-complement reduction. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions, with exact and noisy boundary data, show that the method handles significantly more points than dense collocation.
The anelastic approximation and convergence rate for the compressible Navier-Stokes equations with ill-prepared data in bounded domains

We justify the anelastic approximation and establish a convergence rate for local strong solutions to the isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations in a three-dimensional bounded domain, with ill-prepared initial data and vorticity-slip boundary conditions. When the Mach and Froude numbers vanish at the same rate $ε$, the system converges to an anelastic system with nonconstant hydrostatic density. Compared with the incompressible limit, the balance between singular pressure and gravity generates a variable-coefficient acoustic operator and additional commutators. To overcome these difficulties, we introduce the pressure perturbation adapted to the hydrostatic balance and establish weighted acoustic and vorticity estimates, yielding uniform-in-$ε$ estimates. We then use the weighted Helmholtz decomposition and time-averaging technique to prove the strong convergence of solenoidal component of the momentum and obtain an error bound controlled by $ε$ and the initial error in the projected momentum. Our analysis reveals the weighted cancellation mechanism that applies to singular limits around a class of nonconstant equilibria.
On knotted self expanders of the mean curvature flow in $\R^3$
In this article we produce many examples of knotted self expanders. For example, there is an expander isotopic to a trefoil knot with three half cylinders attached.
Graph splitting algorithms for inconsistent feasibility problems
Rubén Campoy; César López-Pastor; David Torregrosa-Belén

In this work, we study graph splitting algorithms for feasibility problems involving closed and convex sets whose intersection may be empty. We characterize their minimal displacement vector, which is known to be the limit of the differences between successive iterates, in terms of a least-squares problem measuring disagreement between the sets according to the graph structure. We then specialize to closed affine subspaces, proving strong convergence of the shadow sequence to a solution of such a least-squares problem whenever one exists. Our analysis extends classical Douglas-Rachford results on best approximation pairs to graph splitting algorithms.
Efficient Detailed Scheduling of Multiproduct Pipelines using Action-Decoupled Deep Reinforcement Learning
Kai Shao; Ling Jian; Liming Liu; Serguey V. Bogomolov; Xinmin Wang

Multiproduct pipelines transport refined products to delivery stations in sequential batches, and their detailed scheduling must meet market demand while respecting nonlinear hydraulic constraints. Retaining the full hydraulic nonlinearity yields a mixed-integer nonlinear program that is computationally intractable, while the linearization commonly adopted for solver-based optimization degrades hydraulic accuracy without resolving the heavy computational burden. This paper develops an action-decoupled proximal policy optimization (PPO) framework that efficiently produces detailed schedules while preserving hydraulic fidelity. The scheduling process is cast as a semi-Markov decision process (SMDP) with flexible action durations. To handle the discrete-continuous hybrid action space, a cascaded dual-actor architecture decouples the discrete operating duration from the continuous flow decisions, eliminating the gradient interference that destabilizes conventional coupled-action policies and thereby yielding high-quality schedules far more efficiently. Validated on a real-world multiproduct pipeline in China and benchmarked against a single-actor baseline and a linearized MILP solved by Gurobi, the proposed framework achieves delivery accuracy close to the exact optimum while substantially improving flow rate stability and substantially reducing solution time.
Sharp Injective Norm Bounds for Inhomogeneous Gaussian Tensors and Sparse Extensions

We study the Euclidean injective norm of inhomogeneous random tensors with independent entries. For Gaussian tensors, we establish optimal two-sided bounds for the expected norm, with constants depending only on the tensor order. These bounds describe the interplay between variance accumulation along fibres and the contribution of the largest individual entries. In the matrix case, our result is consistent with the characterizations in~\cite{LVHY18}. We then extend the analysis to sparse Gaussian tensors with arbitrary amplitudes and activation probabilities. The expected norm is characterized by the expected largest absolute entry and the largest fibre standard deviation after truncating amplitudes at this scale. Our proofs combine geometric chaining with estimates for averaging over the random support.
When Is Tracking Affordable? A Movement-Budget Feasibility Threshold for Dynamic Regret

Dynamic regret measures an online learner against a moving comparator, and standard analyses assume the learner may move freely at every round. We study what happens when it may not: the learner is given a hard budget $S$ on its total movement $\sum_t \|x_t - x_{t-1}\|$. Our main result is that a movement budget creates a feasibility barrier. On a domain of diameter $D$ with $G$-Lipschitz convex losses, for every comparator path length $P_T \in [D, DT]$ we exhibit a deterministic adversary that forces $R_d = Ω(GDT)$ on every budget-feasible algorithm whenever $S \le c P_T$ for a universal constant $c>0$. This barrier is caused by the budget rather than by a volatile environment: for fixed $D$, it applies when $P_T = o(T)$, where the unconstrained minimax rate $Θ(G\sqrt{D(D+P_T)T})$ is sublinear, so the same instances are learnable with an unbounded budget and unlearnable without one. Conversely, projected online gradient descent with a budget-aware step size is budget-feasible and attains $o(GDT)$ once $S = ω(D + P_T)$. Thus the critical movement scale is $D+P_T$: linear regret is unavoidable below a sufficiently small constant multiple of $P_T$, while sublinear regret is achievable when $S/(D+P_T)\to\infty$ in the learnable regime.
